Name: John Bambrook
Question: What would happen if a small child bumped into Darth Vader or Darth Sidious?
Answer: Darth Vader and Darth Sidious have both bumped into small children, when they have been on their dark side rampages. During the great Jedi purge, directly after the Clone Wars, Darth Vader was with his legion of stormtroopers on the now Imperial held Wookiee home world of Kashyyyk. Amidst the chaotic battle, Vader encounters a straggler. Jedi knight, Kento Marek. Slaying Kento in a lightsaber duel, Vader and his men proceed to continue their purge when Vader discovered a small boy. The boy was Kento Marek’s son. Galen Marek. This now orphaned child displayed such raw and unprecedented talent in the force, that he easily force snatched Vader’s crimson lightsaber straight from his hand. Vader was so impressed with this small boy’s connection to the force, that he abducted him and took him as his secret apprentice. Trained for years in the dark side at the hands of one of the cruelest masters, young Galen was dubbed Starkiller. He went on to defy his former dark master and paid for it with his life. Darth Sidious, whilst apprenticing to Darth Plagueis, was on Dathomir when a Nightsister approached him with her infant child. In a bid to grant her son a better life with a supreme being, she turned him over to Sidious. She sensed his dark authority as soon as she gazed at him across a marketplace. Sidious, knowing about these Dathomirian witches’ uncanny dark side abilities, had Maul trained in the dark side on Mustafar, far away from the eyes of the Jedi. Trained as a fledgling Sith assassin, Maul went on in time to become one of the most deadly dark side opponents that any Jedi would hesitate to engage in combat. In summary, when two of the greatest Sith lords to ever live encounter small children, they sometimes end up becoming galactic monsters feared by all who hear their names. Question: Was Obi-Wan ever able to visit Yoda on Dagobah during his exile?
Answer: Not physically. In Revenge of the Sith, after the execution of Order 66, Obi-Wan tells Bail Organa and Yoda that he will watch over Luke on Tatooine, whilst Bail will take Leia to Alderaan. After revealing that Qui-Gon Jinn had ‘become one with the force’ Yoda tells Kenobi that he will teach him how to communicate with his former master. But he never meant that he would pop over for a visit or anything. Yoda was hiding on Dagobah because it was so rich in the force, especially the darkside. Using the darkside as a shield he hid unawares to Palpatine and the Empire. To leave would jeopardise everything. If the Sith discovered both of the Jedis hiding locations it would be game over. Kenobi knew likewise, and didn't want to draw attention to his movements, especially on Tatooine,.but he couldn't leave Luke unattended. Yoda could commune to Kenobi through the force, which was sufficient enough. They didn't want to risk the future of the Jedi Order just by visiting one another, especially while they were public enemy number one. It would have to be in the event of a life or death situation that Kenobi would even contemplate visiting Master Yoda at his swampy hideout.

Question: Could the Sith troopers in TROS be clones?
Answer: The Sith Troopers were not clones. When the Empire came to an end after Operation Cinder the remnants of the Imperial officers and stormtroopers went to live on Exegol. Palpatines plan was to revive his Empire hidden away on the shady planet. The Sith Troopers were children of the Empire, and also children from the Sith Eternal occultists who already resided on Exegol. The planet was safely hidden in the Unknown Regions of space, and virtually impossible for anyone to locate without a Sith Wayfinder. The children of these two factions would go on to becoming the Sith Troopers. While they had no connection to the force they were completely loyal to the Sith, and to Palpatine. Because the Sith occultists ruled the planet of Exegol Palpatine had thousands upon thousands of children to conscript into his Final Order. The children were raised to worship the Sith, and to be diehards fanatical to Palpatines cause. Their devotion to Palpatine was without question, unwavering and totally loyal,..unlike the officers and troops of the Empire and First Order. Both respectively didn't rely on clones, and neither did Palpatines Final Order and the Sith Troopers. Instead Palpatine refined the work of the Kaminoan scientists pertaining to brain conditioning, and through the use of these techniques they managed to totally suppress the free will of the Sith Troopers. Palpatine did this via way of.. Because Palpatine finally worked out how to completely control his troops through brain manipulation he didn't need to use clones. His former Imperial staff, and the Sith Occultists, would provide him with enough soldiers, and through the work of his own scientists and the legacy of the Kaminoans he had an army unquestionably loyal to him. Source; Sith troopers:Wookiepedia

Question: You're a Separatist commander at the end of the Clone Wars and you want to desert, you're part of a small planetary defence fleet far from the main conflicts and have a single Lukrehulk Battleship under your command. What do you do?
Answer: I'd be doing the same thing as the Separatist droid general Kalani did on the planet Agamar, and he survived for 17 years after the Clone Wars and beyond. This was because Kalani refused the droid shutdown command issued by Darth Sidious, and believed it was a Republic trap. Being a super tactical droid he deduced that the wars end was imminent, and that the Republic would resort to trickery against the Separatist forces. The last order he recieved before the droid shutdown command was from Count Dooku. Previously he had been stationed on Onderon, to support a civil war resulting in Separatist favour. Because of the need for support Kalani was awaiting further instructions when the call came in to shut down the droid armies of the Separatist Alliance;..himself included. Instead he rescinded the order to his forces and awaited on aboard his DH-Omni support vessel for the next 17 years. I'd do what Kalani did, but he had a substantially larger vessel than the Lucrehulk Battleship presented in this scenario. Nonetheless, it has adequate room for enough supplies to begin anew somewhere,..far from the eyes of the emerging Empire. I'd take those who shared the same ideals as myself and set a course to a planet similar to Agamar; somewhere that will hide us from any interest from the Empire. Then because of my loyal droid crew I would source materials to keep them sustainable for the ongoing future. Then I would devise a contingency order in the event of the Empire showing up, and just kick back like Kalani.

Question: Besides Darth Plagueis, are there any other ancient Sith Lords you believe would have had a significant impact if they had lived longer?
Answer: Yeah,..Darth Plagueis’ master. Darth Tenebrous. Why? Because this guy was concocting a plan far more wicked than his apprentice Plagueis, and if he had lived longer it would definitely have brought about the end to the Jedi Order once and for all. That's a fairly significant impact. Before his apprentice Darth Plagueis snapped his neck, finally killing him, Darth Tenebrous was calling all the shots. He came to believe that the force was an energy source of unlimited power, just waiting for him to harness it. He was obsessed with shaping the future to his will, and he and his former master had once experimented with a very fascinating and debilitating virus. Tenebrous and his master tried to create a virus that specifically targeted the Jedi, and would ultimately sever their connection to the force. This project was eventually deemed a failure after years of experimentation. But had Tenebrous survived his final encounter with his treacherous Muun apprentice things could have been vastly different in the Star Wars Universe as we know it. If Tenebrous emerged triumphant against Darth Plagueis, and refined the diabolical Jedi virus, he would have effectively wiped out the Jedi Order. Without the force to guide them, and assist them in battle, the Jedi would be left completely vulnerable to attack from the Sith. Tenebrous would have achieved what his Sith forebears could only contemplate, and ascend to becoming the most powerful Sith Lord that ever reigned. But Darth Tenebrous didn't completely adhere to the darkside tradition of ‘The Rule of Two’, and had another apprentice besides Darth Plagueis. At some point after he took on Plagueis as a five year old apprentice Tenebrous secretly took on another apprentice; Darth Venamis. Venamis was a fellow Bith, and Tenebrous taught him similarly to Plagueis. Tenebrous wasn't afraid to break Darth Banes antiquated rule. If Tenebrous was willing to break the rule of two once,..then he could do it again. Tenebrous could use Venamis to recruit more Sith acolytes to their higher cause, and muster a powerful army to defeat the Jedi. Without their former connection to the force they would crumble underneath Darth Tenebrous and his legions of Sith warriors…and the Jedi would be no more. Tenebrous’ virus would be the first step in erasing the Jedi now, and for all ages to come. They couldn't even revive the Jedi Order, or train new recruits,..and would eventually fade away into obscurity. Palpatine made the galaxy believe the Jedi were extinct in under two decades, despite many still living in hiding. Tenebrous would erase their entire memory in two or three generations, and with no hope for a revival. The galaxy would be ruled by the Sith, and they would return the Sith Order to its once former glory. Palpatine could only dream about what Darth Tenebrous could have achieved;..had the Bith lived longer than he did.

Question: Which Star Wars character most needs a standalone film?
Answer: Sheev Palpatine. He's one of the most integral and powerful characters in the entire Star Wars Saga, yet we know next to nothing about his early childhood and teenage years. We know that he was from Naboo, and was born into the noble houses among Theeds capital. We know he became the Senator for Naboo, eventually representing over 30 worlds once he became Supreme Chancellor for the Galactic Republic. We know he was a Sith Lord, trained by Darth Plagueis, and went on to have such powerful apprentices as Darth Maul, Count Dooku and the great Darth Vader. But by the time the events of episode I, The Phantom Menace begin, Palpatine is already 52..having been born in 84 BBY. This is why it would be great to see Palpatine in a standalone movie that documents his life from when he was a child,..all the way through to adulthood. In Legends material, Darth Plagueis by James Luceno, we are given a rare glimpse into the life of a young Sheev Palpatine. We learn from the story that when Sheev was a boy he was very manipulative, cruel and highly intelligent,..and aware that he had powers which he hid from his family and the world; especially his father Cosigna. His early life in the capital of Naboo was spent in the lap of luxury,..yet Palpatine still yearned to become so much more. He had a very turbulent and chaotic relationship with his father, living in the expectation that he would become important Naboo nobility. He frequently butted heads with his father, and it was when Cosigna forbade him to see his new friend, Hego Damask, that Sheev crossed the line. Unbeknownst to everyone his new friend was a Sith Lord, Darth Plagueis, and after Plagueis manipulated Palpatine into killing his family..Palpatine had no choice but to become a Sith. It would be this period in his life that would make for a fantastic standalone movie or series. Watching young Palpatine train under Darth Plagueis, and delve into the secrets of the darkside would be far more fascinating than some of the storylines getting around out there in the SWU. We would see Sheev learn of his hidden powers, and explore the more intricate aspects of the Sith Lords and their secretive Order,..see how the Sith manipulate individuals and governments across the galaxy,..see how they use knowledge holocrons and ancient texts full of unseen darkside lore,..and how they continually plot against the Jedi and the Republic. It would be the perfect opportunity to showcase everything darkside related, and bring it from the realms of Legends into current Canon lore.

Question: Why did The Galactic Empire hate aliens?
Answer: Because the Empires racist views were actually a bigger part of Emperor Palpatines evil plans. When Palpatine was devising his scheme for intergalactic domination he realised he would need someone trustworthy to oversee the ruling of the Empires vast military operations. Even before the fall of the Republic Palpatine was actively keeping his eye on a future candidate. This is when he started to gain the confidence and trust of Captain Wilhuff Tarkin. Tarkin had a very humanocentric view on the way he operated and selected his officers and troops. This very speciesist tendency of Tarkins served Palpatine when he rose to power, because it helped the new Emperor feed his war machine with soldiers. Specieism was a powerful tool for Palpatine, because he used it stir up conflict and xenophobia. This made racist humans flock to be recuited because of what the Empires ideals represented. The Stormtroopers were 99% human, as was a requirement to enlist with the Empire, yet on occasion Palpatine did employ aliens in his ranks such as Grand Admiral Thrawn, and members of the Imperial Inquisitorious. But it was Tarkins humanocentric view, along with his self titled doctrine, that fueled racist loyalties within the Empire;..soldiers that inherently hated any other race not human. If you remember when Han and Luke are dressed as stormtroopers on the Death Star, pretending to escort Chewie to the detention block, the Imperial officer that first noticed Chewie said… And also when Princess Leia referred to Chewie as a “walking carpet”. These comments were aligned with speciesism, but on the second occasion it was from a Rebel Alliance representative instead of an Imperial. Regardless of the princesses comment this is just proof that racism exists everywhere,..no matter what galaxy you're from, or what side of the fence you sit on. The speciesism of the Empire helped keep a sense of order through its racist tendencies. The Stormtroopers believed that they were superior to all the other alien races, and because their Empire backed up their skewed sentiments it fueled their own ideals. Even when we watch Rebels, Kenobi and The Mandalorian we get a sense that the bulk of the stormtroopers are just “alien hating” clods, fueling each others redneck views. This played right into Palpatines hands because the guy controlling his militaries perpetuated the same ideals. Palpatine himself wasn't speciesist but he used it keep a firm stronghold on power. Even when the Empire came to power Tarkins homeworld of Eriadu “legitimised the enslavement of non humans”*. We seen this bigoted stance sadly happen again on Kashyyyk. If the Wookiees were humans they most likely wouldn't have been cruelly enslaved and persecuted. The Empires treatment of the Wookiees was especially cruel under their reign, as they traded Wookiee slaves and allowed the Trandoshan slavers to freely hunt them without consequence. Specieism was one of the Empires cruelest tools. This wouldn't have happened with droids,..who are indiscriminate of race, colour or species. *Source; Speciesism; Wookiepedia.

Question: How were Emperor Palpatine and Lord Vader still alive during "A New Hope" despite being on an exploding space station?
Answer: Because neither of them were on the first Death Star when Luke Skywalker blew it to pieces. The Emperor wasn't there because he was personally overseeing the dissolution of the Imperial Senate on Coruscant, and Lord Vader was blown clear of the explosion moments before it was destroyed by the Rebel Alliance. We hear Tarkin mention previously in the film that the Imperial Senate has been dissolved. Palpatine wasn't on the Death Star because he was officiating, and expediting the process. Once the senate was dissolved it gave him ultimate power as a dictator, and freed him up to use his new toy. Vader was trying to stop the Rebels from destroying the battle station when his wingman was hit, propelling him into Vaders TIE Advanced. This sent him careering off course, which inadvertently saved his life.

Question: What if Grievous guards killed Anakin and Obi-Wan during the opening of ROTS?
Answer: Grievous’ guards!! If this was the case then those Magnaguards would be mass produced overnight..after the Separatist Alliance spread word about their incredible victory. It would also destroy Palpatines plans to make Anakin his new apprentice, and leave the door open for Dooku to make his move. But most of all..it would really anger Grievous knowing that one of his “droid” bodyguards accomplished what he could not. Regardless, it would be a sad day for the Republic and the Jedi Order, after losing two of their greatest champions. After the death of Skywalker and Kenobi aboard the ‘Invisible Hand’ the Chancellors plans would be severely hindered. He would lose the apprentice he had been grooming for years, and have to make do with retaining Dooku for the meantime. Order 66 wouldn't be tremendously affected, but he wouldn't have Anakin to march on the Temple and quickly snuff out the Jedi on Coruscant. He would still have to contend with Masters Windu and Yoda once his plans came into effect, and have to solely rely on the Clones without Anakins assistance. He would have to orchestrate another way back to the surface of Coruscant, after the Separatist command ship plummets onto the surface of the planet. Dooku would be most satisfied knowing that both Skywalker and Kenobi were no more, and that he still remained in control of the Confederacy of Independent Systems and the Separatist Alliance armies. But for Sidious and the Jedi Order this would be a nightmare. Palpatine would never have ‘the chosen one’ for himself, and be stuck with Dooku until he found another naive apprentice. The Jedi would be down two of their finest generals, but most of all be left reeling after the sudden tragic loss. Sidious may even push forward Order 66,..but ultimately he will defeat the Jedi. He could just make up a story, and say that Skywalker and Kenobi revealed a Jedi plot to take over the galaxy, and that it was Count Dooku who killed them,..in turn revealing that himself and the CIS wanted peace between themselves and the Republic. He could execute Order 66, snuff out the Jedi, have Dooku kill Grievous and enforce the droid shutdown command. He could use this excuse to merge the Republic and the CIS into the Galactic Empire, and proceed forward with his plans, but ultimately he would have to deal with Dooku. Every event after ROTS would be vastly different to what we know. Padme probably survives, along with the twins, and goes to the ‘Lake Country’ she mentioned earlier to Anakin, ..or goes completely into hiding after Palpatine rises to power. With no Vader to enforce the will of the Emperor Palpatine is left in a predicament;..kill Dooku and replace him, or keep him on..and risk treason. Who knows if Dooku would be successful in a bid to destroy his master, and rule in his place. There are so many things that will change after the deaths of Skywalker and Kenobi, but it would be a much sadder galaxy with the loss of Obi-Wan Kenobi for sure.

Question: What is something about Star Wars that always irked you?
Answer: Yodas lightsaber. Not the lightsaber itself, but the glaring discrepancy of continuity pertaining to its fate. After Yoda has his epic duel with Palpatine in the Senate Building his lightsaber was lost during the battle. This was 2002. Now here's where it gets a little hazy, until Grogu refuses it from Luke Skywalker in chapter 6 of The Book of Boba Fett. After the duel in the Senate Building it was stated that in Star Wars:Complete Locations, 2016, that somehow it ended up being stored in a box in Yodas hut on Dagobah. This is by the time the events of The Empire Strikes Back commence. But then a year later in 2017, the Darth Vader #1 comic shows it being destroyed in a ceremony officiated by Mas Amedda, with Palpatine and Vader watching from above. This is when it was stated by Lucasfilm that Yoda probably had a few lightsabers in his time,.. …and then to put an end to the long standing discrepancy they try to end it five years later in the comic Crimson Reign, issue #3. Here it is ultimately stated that it is was only “one” of Yodas lightsabers that was destroyed by Mas Amedda in the lightsaber burning ceremony of '17. Yodas lightsaber was very first introduced in 1999s Episode I, Visual dictionary,..then we see Yoda use it in Episode II against Dooku,..then it takes well over two decades for its fate to be definitively ascertained. Even then, the lightsaber that Luke offers Grogu is just his second one, and not the one from Revenge of the Sith. This just irks me because of how long it took to be rectified,..and now people can just... ”Oh,..do you know how Maz Kanata got one of Luke Skywalkers lightsabers in The Force Awakens?”

Question: What are your favorite details in the Star Wars movies that most people miss?
Answer: Here's some details cleverly hidden in plain sight during the Star Wars movies. During The Force Awakens we see a pink and white astromech droid in the background of a Resistance base. R2-KT pays homage to Katie Johnson, whose community project to build the droid to lift her spirits during brain cancer warmed hearts globally. R2-KT is also seen in the The Clone Wars animated series, as part of an elite droid unit sent behind enemy lines. Speaking of droids, IG-88 who was seen with the other bounty hunters during The Empire Strikes Back, is also seen in pieces on Cloud City, and also used for bar props in Chalmuns Cantina during A New Hope. The IG droids iconic head is actually a combustion chamber of a Rolls Royce Derwent mk9 engine. The front seats in the Millennium Falcon are also recycled car parts, being from a Porshe 928, and the rear seats are fighter pilot ejection seats from a real life aircraft. When Vader is redeemed in Return of the Jedi, and Luke is getting him to the Imperial shuttle to evacuate you can hear blaster shots ringing out on board the second Death Star. There were no other Rebel forces on the battle station, suggesting that because of the limited number of escape pods the Stormtroopers or Imperial officers were executing other stormtroopers or Imperials in a bid to control the escape pods or ships. This is actually quite harrowing and terrifying if you stop to think about it for a moment. James Bond actor Daniel Craig had a cameo role in The Force Awakens. He is the actor playing the First Order stormtrooper in the holding cell with Rey, when she uses the force to mind trick 007 into removing her restraints, and leaving his weapon behind when he leaves the room. Rumours initially suggested he was the stormtrooper that took on Finn after the destruction of Maz Kanatas castle on Tokodana. During the Battle of Coruscant in Revenge of the Sith, Obi-Wan and Anakin fly past an exploding Separatist ship. As the space debris collides with the Republic Star Destroyer you can see that one of the pieces is actually a kitchen sink! In The Clone Wars we can see a Picasso inspired piece of artwork of Duchess Satine Kryze. When Maul takes over Mandalore he steals this piece of artwork and takes it to the Nightsister Temple on Dathomir. Years later during events of the Rebels animted series we see that Maul has defaced the Duchess’ painting with blood, and on the wall has also scrawled in blood the word ‘Kenobi’ in Mandalorian. This is an insight into the twisted mind of Maul in his pursuit to inflict tremendous pain upon Kenobi. Also in the animated series The Clone Wars we see Wat Tambor of the Techno Union assume control of the planet Ryloth. In his sacking and plundering of Ryloths riches and treasures we see his minions load something familiar onto a Separatist transport. Upon closer inspection we can see that it's the Ark of the Covenant from Lucas’ other successful movie, Raiders of the Lost Ark. Apparently the dangerous relic, that ends up being stored in an Area-51 type facilty on Earth, has its origins rooted in the Star Wars Universe. In episode I The Phantom Menace we can see an EVA Pod from Stanley Kubricks 2001:A Space Odyssey hidden amongst scrap parts. George Lucas was such a huge fan of Kubricks work that to pay homage to his idol he put one of the EVA Pods in the background of Wattos Junk Shop on Tatooine. In The Last Jedi Luke Skywalker fools everyone on the planet Crait into believing that he is actually there in person. It was actually an illusion, as we all seen but one sure way to tell that he wasn't there was due to the fact that his holo/astral projection left no footprints on the salt covered surface of the planet. Finally,..during the Rebel Alliance X-wing attack on Galen Ersos Imperial complex on Eadu we see something that happens so fast…that if you blink you'll miss it. When Chirrut Imwe fires his lucky shot at an Imperial TIE Fighter the ship goes hurtling back into the Imperial facility, exploding on impact. If you slow this scene down you can see the TIE Fighter pilot smash through the windshield of the exploding ship..and go hurtling through the small opening of the outposts window! This one you can pause and watch for yourself.

Question: What motivated General Grievous and why did he decide on supporting Palpatine in conquering the Galaxy?
Answer: General Grievous was motivated by the same thing that fuels and motivates Darth Vader,..hatred. Grievous was an enforcer for the Intergalactic Banking Clan right before he took up Dooku's offer to be Supreme Marshall Commander of the Separatist Droid Armies. Power and vengeance were his after that, as he unleashed his full fury upon Republic forces and the Jedi. The Jedi were responsible for the deaths of untold thousands of his people, when they previously sided with the generations old enemy of the Kaleesh..the Yam’rii. From that point on Grievous made ‘improvements’ to his body in the quest to be able to take on the Jedi personally. These cybernetic improvements allowed him to fight the Jedi head to head, but a shuttle crash that the Count orchestrated cemented his future with Dooku and the Sith. Palpatine just viewed Grievous as a weapon, a tool for his greater plans…and a disposable pawn. But he viewed him as someone highly capable of leading the droid armies. Grievous only supported Palpatine through Dooku, as Dooku was the head of state for the Confederacy of Independent Systems. He didn't directly report to Palpatine until Dooku lost his head during the Battle of Coruscant. When referring to Palpatine, Dooku would call him “my master”, so Grievous knew that his boss answered to another boss. He even refers to him as Darth Sidious in Revenge of the Sith. When Palpatine ordered Grievous to move the Separatist leaders to the Mustafar system he was just following the chain of command,..being his dead bosses boss giving the orders now! Grievous knew that if Darth Sidious won the war,..which Sidious told him personally was nearly at an end, he would have his vengeance and final victory over the Jedi. Grievous wanted what the Separatist Alliance wanted; what his new master wanted. Which was the permanent eradication of the Jedi Order and their Republic. He just never assumed that the guy calling the shots was just using him in a meticulously orchestrated war, designed to give him control of the galaxy after the Clone Wars finally wrapped up. If he survived Kenobi on Utapau I highly doubt that he would have followed along with the droid shutdown command from Mustafar. Without the support and might of the battle droids and Separatist war ships he didn't have any support to back him up, so shutting them down wouldn't be in his best interests. At this point he would definitely exchange words with Darth Sidious.

Question: How many different types of aliens are there in Star Wars? What do they look like, and what do they call themselves?
Answer: There are more than 20 million known sentient species recorded in the Star Wars Universe. It's a far cry from when we hear C-3P0 mention that he can converse in over six million forms of alien communication.. Many different species cohabitated on single planets, like the Mon Cala and the Quarren who both live on the planet Mon Calamari. On Tatooine for example we have the Jawas and the Sandpeople both residing on Tatooine,..and again on Endors moon we have Ewoks, Yazzums and Goraxes. Each species has evolved over untold millenia, both physically and technologically, and have distinct traits, features and abilities in all their weird and wonderful cultures. Some different races have had to adapt and evolve to survive on their respective worlds. For example, the Kaminoans homeworld used to be land based until an ancient cataclysm forced them to live in domed cities high above the waves of their new ocean world. The same thing happened on Tatooine, where once lush forests and oceans existed, but similarly a great cataclysm transformed the planet into a scorched, sandy rock. The Jawas and the Sandpeople had to adapt to survive the harsh desert climates, resulting in their thick protective clothing and head gear to accommodate the rough conditions. There's no possible way I could name all the species, and describe them in graphic detail, given the more than 20 million species. We have species from Aqualish to Zabraks, Chiss to Hutts, and Trandoshans to Wookiees. Some species are kind and benevolent, such as Bith, Alena and Ortolans who are very welcoming and friendly as an overall species. But then we have species such as Collicoids, Trandoshans, Amani and Karkarodons which are very hostile, violent and mistrusting of outsiders. Many are humanoid in appearance, but there are multitudes of alien species that look extremely bizarre in appearance to us humans. Collicoids and Yamrii for instance, are very insectoid in appearance,.. ..and serpentine looking species such as the Thisspiasians and Anacondans; who appear as gigantic snake like beings.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How many Mandalorians would it take to defeat General Grievous (Star Wars)?
Answer: Remember that time when General Grievous casually managed to capture three of the most powerful individuals in the entire Star Wars Universe; Sheev Palpatine, Anakin Skywalker and..Kenobi? On that occasion Grievous just decided to use his brains a bit more, and utilise the ray shields aboard the Invisible Hand. He was more intelligent than most gave him credit for. Grievous was no idiot, and he was more than a match for Mandalorian warriors despite them wearing Beskar armour. He had reinvented himself physically as a Jedi killing maelstrom of death and fear, and had many trophies of dead Jedi at his hidden fortress on Vasseks moon. Mandalorian warriors would prove far easier quarry for him to slay,..than the bothersome Jedi. When we see the Son of Dathomir comics it is painfully obvious that you would need quite a lot of Mandalorian warriors to ultimately defeat General Grievous. He literally rips through more than half a dozen Mandalorians loyal to Maul, tearing and clawing them apart in a blur of horrifying carnage. He effortlessly does this all whilst relishing in his actions,..and not once uses his lightsabers to kill them on that particular occasion. These guys were no pushovers neither, being Mandalorian Super Commandos with years of experience under their belts. To defeat Grievous with Mandalorians you're probably going to have to bring 50 minimum to ensure a victory against the general. But even then you're sending many straight to their graves. Another interesting point here is that General Grievous is able to rip apart the Mandalorians beskar armour like a clonetroopers plastoid armour,..leaving it shattered and destroyed.

Question: In a fight, who would win between a single Clone Trooper and an ARC Trooper?
Answer: Unless it is some really exceptional Clone Trooper the ARC Trooper is going to win this situation hands down. ARC Troopers were chosen from the most elite Clone troopers in the Grand Army of the Republic, and underwent extensive training in the special forces branch of the army. When clonetroopers were first developed by Kaminoans, it was Jango Fett himself who trained troops in the first batch. His impressive tutelage of the clones was passed down through their training, and these elite soldiers were chosen to undertake the most difficult and dangerous missions in the name of the Republic. Advanced Recon Commandos from this point on were selected for their incredible heroics and skills during a battle or campaign. The title was a coveted rank for members in the regular clone army, with many a clone trooper aspiring to become promoted to an ARC Trooper. An ARC troopers dual DC-17 blaster pistols would make short work of a ‘reg’, as ARC troops trained extensively to be ambidextrous with the pistol,..and far better shots when it came to accuracy and speed. They had their own unique armour set, with more components than a regular clonetrooper,..and extensive survival equipment including a knife and an ascension cable. They were considered the best soldiers in the Grand Army of the Republic, and their reputations preceeded them for very good reason. They were sent on missions and assignments more suited to them, and those which standard clonetroopers would find extremely challenging to accomplish. A standard rank-and-file clonetrooper wouldn't stand a chance against a seasoned ARC trooper,..unless he was supremely exceptional in that he may possess more of Jango Fetts extraordinary abilities than the standard clonetrooper.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How do Star Wars restrooms account for the various ways aliens might excrete? Have Star wars restrooms ever been shown in media?
Answer: In both Star Wars Rebels and The Mandalorian we see a restroom and a toilet, otherwise known as a refresher in the Star Wars Universe. In Rebels we see Wedge Antilles go to use the the refresher after finishing a mission. The droid AP-5 wanted to continue a discussion with him and followed Wedge into what looked like a toilet, where Wedge went to use the urinal. Needless to say Wedge wasn't impressed with AP-5s bathroom etiquette, but we did get to see a glimpse at the toilet or bathroom in the SWU for one of the first times. In The Mandalorian, during the very first episode we see a refresher aboard Din Djarins bounty hunter vessel, The RazorCrest. Djarin had captured a Mithrol bounty at a local bar, and once in space the shifty Mithrol requested to use the refresher. If you look closely you'll see that it's got everything to accommodate for different alien species, with various tubes and pipes going to the on board septic tank. It's very similar to a real life space shuttles restroom facilities, especially being equipped for zero gravity toilet situations of varying degrees. In other forms of SW media, like the comics for example, we see refreshers in situations like on board an Imperial vessel, and on another occasion where Han and Chewie ended up trapped in the Millennium Falcons restroom.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What was Emperor Palpatine's reason for hating the Jedi? Was there any indication of him having positive feelings towards them?
Answer: He hated the Jedi because they upheld the light side of the force, which was in direct opposition of his alignment. The dark side and the light side are two vastly different philosophies, and the Siths ultimate goal is to wipe the Jedi from the galaxy. The Jedi stood in the way of the Sith, and Palpatine hated them for interfering with his plans. He viewed them as narrow minded hypocrites who opposed the tremendous power he wielded. Once he began apprenticing under Darth Plagueis he began to follow in the footsteps of his ancient predecessor Darth Bane. As such he was taught to hate the Jedi, to despise and hate them as the sworn enemy of the Sith. As he poured through the archives of Sith literature he would have noted all the deaths of Sith Lords at the hands of the treacherous Jedi. This would have instilled a deep hatred towards the Jedi and their entire order. Everything they ever believed in was a lie according to the Sith, designed for themselves to hold the monopoly on galactic power. But it was this power that Darth Sidious sought to usurp, twist and manipulate to his own desires. Besides when Palpatine tells Anakin that the Jedi and the Sith are similar in almost every way..I can't recall one occasion, event or single piece of literature that ever indicated that Palpatine had positive feelings towards the Jedi. The only positive emotions that he felt in regards to the Jedi was when he killed them gleefully, and plotted their destruction. In the Legends novel, Darth Plagueis, the Sith send the dead body of Jedi to the Temple in a cruel sneer to the Order, and used to freely walk around the outside of the Temple using the force to hide their presence from the Jedi. Palpatines reason for hating the Jedi is the same reason why his master hated them, and his master before him, and so on;..simply because they are Jedi.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Was Palpatine afraid of Yoda before their fight during Order 66, or was he confident he would win their duel?
Answer: Palpatine never thought that Yoda would show up in his senatorial office because he thought that he was dealt with on Kashyyyk. Instead, when Yoda arrives and knocks out Palpatines Royal Guards he looks at Master Yoda with a degree of suprise on his face. Learning Yoda survived did not deter Palpatine from immediately attacking him, and by the looks of things Yoda wasn't quite prepared for Sidious’ initial assault of Force Lightning. As Yoda lays there stunned Palpatine laughs over his motionless form, and displays his supreme overconfidence in besting his “little green friend”. Palpatine was no fool, and knew that if he took on the Grand Master of the Jedi it would be a worthy fight,..and that he could personally relish in his long savoured victory. But Yoda recovers quickly,..and this is when Palpatines overconfidence quickly fades away. After Yoda hurls him flying across the room, toppling into his chair, Palpatine tries to flee but Yoda forces his hand. Palpatine believed that he could just use the force to defeat Yoda, but when Yoda recovers and challenges him to a lightsaber duel, Palpatine has no choice but to whip out his lightsaber. But at this point Palpatine could still summon hordes of clonetroopers to his aid…but still refuses. Sidious wanted to defeat Yoda personally, and savoured the confrontation he had probably dreamed of;..but just assumed Commander Gree would have finished off Yoda for him. He was confident he would win, which he ultimately did..but there were moments a shred of doubt may have crossed his mind. Yet throughout their duel Sidious doesn't summon clones to help him, nor does Mas Amedda, who departed moments before the confrontation erupted. This is a clear indicator that Sidious expected to win without assistance, because after all,..why would the most powerful being in the galaxy need help from some clones on the day of his greatest triumph?

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What motivated Palpatine to become a Sith Lord? Was it for power or was he born into it?
Answer: Palpatine was always motivated by greed and the attainment of power. His family were practically Naboo nobility, and House Palpatine had a very well to do reputation that young Sheev was always reminded to uphold, by his father Cosigna. Life for him was spent in the lap of luxury, and he was educated at the finest schools that Theed had to offer. He was a privileged, entitled, cocky little trust fund kid, who craved more and more the older he got. His father even covered up a speeder accident that Palpatine caused. He knew he had powers, but he hid them from everyone;..especially his father. He knew he would be ostracised and shunned because he was different, and so kept it secret from the galaxy. Until he was noticed by an individual known as Hego Damask. Hego was head of Damask Holdings, a very influential financial corporation which he used to advance his hidden agenda. Hego was actually a Sith Lord known as Darth Plagueis, and during his manipulation of Naboo he came to notice young Sheev Palpatine. Through getting to know the young man he learned that Palpatine wanted power above everything else. He wanted to be a leader, and not a follower..and expressed his inner desires to his new found friend. In turn Hego manipulated Palpatine, and made him believe that his father was holding him back;..stopping him from becoming everything that he was destined to become. Then he manoeuvred Palpatine into a position where he had no other choice but to accept Hegos help. Palpatine had become so angry and disillusioned at his father, especially when he forbade his son from seeing Hego Damask again. Palpatine was seething with anger and when Cosigna took the entire Palpatine family aboard their starcruiser he crossed the point of no return. He slaughtered his entire family with his bare hands, and used the force to rip them to pieces. Plagueis knew he would come to him for help, and when he did he revealed himself as a Sith Lord. Then made him an offer that he couldn't refuse. He offered for Palpatine to join him, and become his apprentice. Palpatine didn't have much of a choice; either take up Darth Plagueis on his offer, or possibly spend the rest of his life in a prison cell. Palpatine wasn't born into it, he was chosen by a Sith Lord to become something much, much more.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is the cruelest way a Jedi has defeated a villain in Star Wars?
Answer: Even though Admiral Trench had been a continual thorn in the Republics side the way Anakin Skywalker killed him was unusually cruel. Keep in mind that at this point in time Anakin was only months away from completely succumbing to the darkside, and towards the end of the war was the most conflicting time in his life. Skywalker was justified in killing an enemy combatant, who had laid waste to many a Republic vessel and life throughout the war,..but his handling of Trench seemed satisfying for him. Firstly he eliminates all of Trenchs droids, then finally has the Harch Admiral dead to rights. He could have dealt with this so very differently, but chose to ignore his heart and abandon his principles. He could have easily subdued Trench, but instead chose to mercilessly kill him without any concern. This highlights Anakins descent into darkness, and how unhinged he was actually becoming. Trench basically pleads for his life, and Skywalker cruelly severs three of his arms with his saber. Trench thought that because Skywalker was a Jedi he wouldn't kill him,..and tells him as such to his face. But Skywalker angrily exclaims that he doesn't harbour the same weakness as other Jedis,..and after Trench tries to defend himself Skywalker angrily skewers the Admiral to death. He then watches the life quickly drain from the Harchs eyes. Then he saunters off throwing a casual one-liner as he acts like it was just another trivial formality of the day. The last thing he gleefully says to Trenchs lifeless corpse is “It's been fun Admiral.” With an emphasis on the word ‘fun’.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How does R2-D2 roll across sand, mud, and debris filled forest floors in the universe with what appears to be wheels not even more than an inch in diameter?
Answer: It may appear that underneath R2-D2s three legs he is rolling on wheels, but this is a common mistake because,..well, how often do you get the chance to see underneath his feet? R2-D2 doesn't utilise wheels when moving because they're actually not wheels. He is fitted with three motorised, all terrain treads that propel him around on any surface. This explains how the astromech can manoeuvre freely in rocky, sandy, muddy and harsh terrains the galaxy over. On Dagobah his all terrain treads proved very convenient as he made his way around the swamps and jungles of the planet. On Tatooine his treads allowed him to roll effortlessly over the rocks and sands of the desert planet, although I think he would share his former masters distaste for the sand found on the scorched world. In the event that he couldn't traverse over the land he was also fitted with twin rocket boosters hidden in his left and right leg compartments, giving him the ability of flight. Source; The Force Awakens:The Visual Dictionary

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Is it possible for Yoda to defeat General Grievous without using his lightsaber?
Answer: Yes. If General Grievous was fully armed, spinning his four lightsabers..coming at Yoda with the full intent on eviscerating him..then I strongly believe that Master Yoda would defeat the good general within moments of engaging him. Yoda was no fool, and recognised General Grievous for what he was. He was completely aware that the general only wielded Jedi weapons, and did not possess a Jedis connection to the force. This actually made Grievous weaker in Yodas mind, and there would have been more than a few ways that Yoda could have dealt with the wayward warrior. Yodas greatest weapon was his ability to use the force in grandiose style. He could levitate X-Wings from swamps, send massive stone slabs flying and completely freeze an individual to the spot using force grab. General Grievous can rant and rave all he wants, and unleash a terrible fury that few Jedi could withstand: but Yoda isn't going to entertain the generals posturing. To defeat General Grievous without a lightsaber would be relatively easy for Grievous, as Grand Master Yoda can just hold and suspend the general in mid air…and decide his fate on a whim. He could just force crush him with a wave of his wrist, or unleash electric judgement and fry his cybernetic circuits. Or just suspend Grievous to the floor, and use the force to levitate his lightsaber up to the generals neck, and…

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is the cruelest thing a Star Wars character has done?
Answer: Once upon a time,..in a little village on the backwater world of Raydonia two strangers came calling. Maul had only been restored by Mother Talzin back on Dathomir, thanks to his brother Savage. Now he only had one thing on his mind. Revenge. For 10 years he languished on Lotho Minor, consumed by his revenge against the one man who took everything from him;..Kenobi. But it was how he was going to lure his nemesis to come to him that made the next thing Maul did one of the cruelest acts in Star Wars. After his explanation to Savage the two began to ruthlessly slaughter all the men, women and children who had begun to gather near their starship. At some point during this carnage Maul assembled some of the remaining survivors and recorded one of the most disturbing holo messages seen. He personally calls out Obi-Wan Kenobi and tells him to come to Raydonia alone..or he will spill more blood. Then Maul callously beheads the Raydonians. He did this just to draw out Kenobi to his location to punish him on his own terms. He seen the excited children come to greet him and his brother when they touched down. He knew that he was going to indiscriminately, inhumanely, and without conscience kill everyone in the village; and he did it with glee knowing that it would affect Kenobi. After confronting Kenobi he also went on a ramble about how sadistically he was going to mutilate the Jedi. I found this scene to be more disturbing because of the fact it was in a so called ‘childrens cartoon’.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Was Grievous aware of his cyborg status and that he was not born as a cyborg?
Answer: Of course he was aware of his cyborg status, and also fully aware that he was once Qymaen Jai Sheelal: former warlord and general of Kaleesh. After his hatred towards the Jedi festered Grievous gradually submitted to cybernetic “improvements”, which he believed made him powerful enough to take on the Jedi. This process was deliberate, gradual and very painful. Over time he began to replace organic body parts with extensive cybernetic upgrades, like his arms and legs for instance. He was working as an enforcer for the Intergalactic Banking Clan on Muunilist when his skills earned the attention of Count Dooku and Darth Sidious. Grievous had been improving his physical body by replacing it with droid equivalents. His mind was obsessed on slaying Jedi, and he was losing more and more of his original form. Through cybernetics he had become powerful enough to engage a Jedi Master, but at a terrible cost. But after the Sith needed a general to lead their armies in the upcoming Clone Wars Grievous became the ultimate choice. His fate was sealed when Dooku orchestrated a shuttle crash, nearly destroying what remained of his organic form. Geonosian scientists and medical droids seen to his final transformation into his duranium body, complete with final upgrades. The Sith had ultimately granted his wish to become the ultimate Jedi killing machine. In his new cybernetic form it had integrated sensors that allowed him to touch and feel the world around him. But the Geonosians did tamper with sections of Grievous brain, to sharpen his reflexes and focus his intelligence. The Geonosians modified areas of his organic brain to suppress former memories. But Grievous’ memory of his past was intact to the point that he remembered that he personally made the intentional choice to become a cyborg. He tells this to his personal medical droid EV-A4-D. He modelled his new body after his original Kaleesh form, even down to a new replica of his old Kaleesh war mask. He also paid homage to his former life by way of life size statues, depicting himself going through several transformations. But it was Dooku and the Geonosians who just expedited his wishes, after the shuttle crash they deliberately planned. That detail would have been deliberately wiped from his memory for obvious security purposes.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How would Palpatine have controlled Vader if he hadn't been damaged and ended up in the suit?
Answer: Leverage and fear. These are the methods Palpatine would use to control Vader, just as he did the Empire for nearly a quarter of a century. Fear was Palpatines greatest control method. When the Empire was in its infancy Palpatine had Grand Moff Tarkin devise his self titled doctrine of control; the Tarkin Doctrine, aka The Doctrine of Fear. This was a theory that used leverage and fear to rule the galaxy, and to be kept in check with the planet destroying Death Star. The way Palpatine controlled Vader was no different. The leverage he had over him was a suit that Palpatine designed himself, that somewhat restrained Vader from his full potential. The fear that Palpatine held over Vader was his power. As a Sith Lord he had taught Vader everything that he knows, and Vader was aware that Palpatine had secrets. He feared what the Emperor was holding back, and he feared a direct confrontation with him. After witnessing and personally feeling the Emperors wrath before, Vader had genuine cause to fear his master. Vader lashed out at the Emperor right after recieving his new suit, but that was about the only time he fully tried. But Palpatine would have expected a reaction like this, especially after delivering the bad news about Padme. Every other occasion the Emperor shut him down, and only feared what Vader could do if he reached his full potential. The suit ensured that Vader couldn't reach his full physical potential, and restricted his movements. It also ensured that Vader couldn't unleash force lightning because of his extensive prosthetics. But how would the master control his student if the student was never physically ruined on Mustafar? Palpatine would have to find something to hold over Vader. Something that Vader cared about; or more to the point..something that Vader feared to lose. Like every power hungry Sith Vader feared to lose his power, but that wouldn't suffice in controlling him. Darth Vader at full uninhibited potential would be a nightmare for Sidious to deal with, but Vader had weaknesses. One such weakness was his naivety. He almost blindly believed in what Palpatine told him, but that wouldn't be enough alone to control him. Anything short of controlling the midichlorians, or some kind of extremely potent Sith Alchemy, wouldn't be enough to rein in his powerful apprentice. But in Legends Palpatine did have a means to control wayward apprentices. In the video game series, The Force Unleashed, in one of the alternative (evil) endings Palpatine gains control of Vaders secret apprentice via another suit, called Sith Stalker armour. This armour was constructed to be grafted to the wearer, and reduced them to Palpatines puppet. But this was only seen in Starkillers vision, and ultimately this is just swapping one suit for the other. So unless Palpatine can somehow conjure up the best mind trick on Vader, his undamaged apprentice is going to be one of the hardest individuals in the entire galaxy to control. Then again, Palpatine could just use the same technology we see in The Mandalorian, which is called a Mindflayer; otherwise known as the Six-O-Two Mitigator. This was a type of device that used an electrical current to mentally recalibrate your brain. But even its highest setting may not be enough to control Vader.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: In Star Wars, if you are a commander of a stormtrooper unit in a battle, what would be some inspiring and motivational speech you would give to your fellow troopers to move forward in battle?
Answer: “Loyal soldiers of the 501st Legion. I stand here before you with an impossible task. But you all have proven to me time and time again that the word ‘impossible’ simply is not part of your vocabulary. This commitment,..this focus,..and this sheer will to prove yourselves to your Emperor has not gone unforgotten. The Emperor himself praises you to the highest degree, and I salute the men before me for your brave and courageous actions,..that have ensured Imperial victories in countless engagements across my Empire. You have bought peace and stability to our planets stretching to the farthest regions of the stars. You have brought safety to a galaxy that needed saving from itself,..and you have brought order to the lawless. Today is no different, only you face an enemy with far vaster numbers, but this is no reason to forget why you are here. You are here to guarantee a victory for your Emperor, and a win for the Empire. Put aside any lingering doubts that you may harbour, and draw upon your anger and your hatred. Use them to fuel your rage, and feed your fury. Crush the enemy and annihilate them with extreme prejudice,..rip these cowards from their hiding places and show them what fear looks like. With the full might of the Empire against your back, and with myself personally leading the frontal assault..you can not fail. Make them suffer, make them bleed, make them grieve,..and make them regret not bowing down before your leader, your ruler,..your Emperor. Take up arms, ready yourselves..and prepare for battle! For in a few hours you will be rejoicing amongst the carnage and ruin of your victory, and I will be there to salute your triumph. Now wipe them out;..all of them.”

Name: John Bambrook
Question: In Star Wars, what would happen if Palpatine was unexpectedly assassinated?
Answer: For the sake of the answer I'll respond as if Palpatine was Emperor. Now if Palpatine was unexpectedly assassinated by an unknown assailant his death would create a power vacuum in the Star Wars Universe. Normally, immediately after his death the Imperial Moffs would assume control of the regional distrcts within the Empires territories. Procedure would then dictate that the Imperial Senate would have to re-elect a new Emperor, but Palpatine had contingency measures in place in the event of his death. One such contingency plan was Operation Cinder;..which was devised by Palpatine to punish the Galactic Empire for not preventing his death. No matter what the Imperial hierarchy did in its vain attempt to retain control of the galaxy Palpatines contingency would still come into effect. Operation Cinder was the codename for an orbital bombardment campaign, that was relayed through sentinel messengers to Imperial officers loyal to Palpatine. Upon receiving said messages the operation would commence with orbital satellites bombarding a designated planets surface with a powerful, climate disrupting laser weapon. Essentially the satellites combined power resulted in a planet killing superweapon. The effects of the weapon created extreme heat waves across a planet, and ultimately boiled its oceans; resulting in either a dead or dieing planet. Palpatine deemed that if the leadership of his Empire could not protect his life then they didn't deserve to rule in his place after his death. Only in this situation Operation Cinder is successful, but there's no Palpatine to revive the Empire on Exegol. If Palpatines assassin doesn't kill him immediately then the Sith Lord may have time to transfer his essence into a clone body on Exegol, in which case his hidden agenda of reestablishing the Empire, by way of the First and Final Order, will still happen;…unless his surviving apprentice Darth Vader has anything to say about it.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What do psychopaths think of Emperor Palpatine?
Answer: One of the 20th centurys most prolific serial killers, Jeffery Dahmer, gave a prison interview some time after 1992 about his thoughts on certain topics. Movie villains superheroes became a topic of discussion. From there all sorts of rumours began to swirl about Dahmer and Star Wars, but it was a forensic psychiatrist who worked out the truth in his own sessions with the serial killer. Park Dietz was a respected forensic psychiatrist that testified at Dahmers trial in 1992. The below text is an excerpt by Dietz from Jeffery Dahmers criminal trial.. Dahmer actually compared himself to Emperor Palpatine in interviews with prison psychiatrists and officials. But of the rumours surrounding Dahmer and Star Wars there was one where reports said he wanted to “build a temple from his victims skulls, where he could sit and absorb a spiritual force or power”,.. ..and Dahmer himself said that he went out and bought yellow tinted sunglasses, when he was stalking victims in nightclubs,..to give him that “Emperor look”. Jeffery Dahmer was convicted on the killing and dismemberment of 17 males between 1978 and 1991. He was beaten to death by fellow inmate Chistopher Scarver on November 28th in 1994,..after serving less than two years into his sentence. Source; Wikipedia; Jeffery Dahmer, and Goat Magazine 1st August, 2019, Andrew P Street.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did Darth Sidious learn from Darth Plagueis?
Answer: For more than 40 years Palpatine apprenticed to the most powerful being in the galaxy, Darth Plagueis. During this time he learned the ways of the darkside, including; how to construct a lightsaber, saber dueling, how to control the force and use its abilities,..and even helped his master with his experiments related to midichlorian manipulation. Plagueis taught Palpatine how to harness his rage and anger, and trained him on inhospitable worlds such as Mygeeto and Mustafar. It was Plagueis himself who taught Sidious to let go of his inhibitions and embrace the darkside. He taught him to cast away the notions of morals and ethics for the greater good of their cause, and to face his fears. After Palpatine murdered his entire family, and their security detail aboard his fathers starcruiser, he first went to Plagueis. This is where Plagueis covered it up, making it look like an accident, and revealed that he was a Sith Lord. From that day onwards Palpatine continually learned from his master up until he murdered him. But it was after Palpatine had killed his former master that we truly see what Sidious thought about his master. We also got to see his opinion on Plagueis’ teachings and more in the Book of Sith:Secrets of the Darkside. It is a compendium of 6 legendary Sith texts, including a scientific journal by Darth Plagueis, and Darth Sidious’ own manifesto on his rise to power. Here Sidious has scribbled his own thoughts on the pages, and we gleam a very fascinating insight to his character, and what he learned from his master. Sidious talks about how the prophecy of the chosen one will never come true,..how he agreed with his master on certain topics, and how Plagueis was the first to influence the midichlorians. He also mentions how he will never chose a successor, and that Darth Banes legacy will end with him. Source; Book of Sith;Secrets of the Darkside, Daniel Wallace 2012.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Has anyone besides Maul used two sabers in a fight like he did against Qui Gon Jinn? If so, who were they and when did it happen?
Answer: I'll give one example of when this happened. Jedi General Pong Krell went rogue during the Battle of Umbara during the Clone Wars in 20 BBY. He cut down members of the 501st with utter disregard for their lives, and with a cruelty that made him one of the most hated characters in the saga. Krell was appointed command of the 501st after their regular assigned general, Anakin Skywalker, was called back to Coruscant on a pressing matter. Unbeknownst to everyone was the fact that Krell wanted to become Count Dookus apprentice, and wanted to gain his attention and praises for massacring Republic troops on Umbara. He had turned to the darkside long before his treachery against the Republic. In his secret quest Krell was discovered to be a traitor by Captain Rex and the 501st, and he even tried to execute troopers Jesse and Hardcase for saving the day. After being uncovered by the clones he unleashed his devastating fury upon members of the the 501st. Krell wielded two twin bladed lightsabers with malicious intent, and cut through the clones like a whirling dervish of obliteration;..and with utter cruelty and disregard. Unlike Maul Krell had two twin bladed lightsabers, and another set of arms, which probably made him more ferocious than Maul in his fighting abilities. It appeared from watching him slaughter the clones that he actually enjoyed it. Needless to say that he was ultimately captured by the clones and preemptively executed by Dogma, who had once praised Krell. The former Jedi died on Umbara in his holding cell, but not before displaying a devastating demonstration in the efficiency of a twin bladed lightsaber.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Was Count Dooku afraid of Qui-Gon Jinn because he may have been a better duelist?
Answer: He wasn't afraid of Qui-Gon for his dueling skills as Dooku was even considered the best swordsman of the day. Dooku respected Qui-Gon as his second apprentice, and for the time they spent together as teacher and pupil. Dooku became a Jedi Master somewhere between 82 BBY to 78 BBY, and had no need to fear Qui-Gon being a better duelist. It was in 68 BBY that Dooku took Qui-Gon as his apprentice, and from there the two developed a very strong bond. He was always praising Qui-Gon for his insight and his honesty, and when Dooku first took padawan Jinn around the Temple, and into the Jedi library Jinn was the one who was first drawn to a holocron containing Jedi prophecies. After years of training together both of them had the same mindset to act against the Jedi High Council if they didn't like one of their decisions, and in 49 BBY Qui-Gon went through his trials and became a master himself. Dooku was impressed and happy at his students achievement. He never once feared him as a duelist. After Qui-Gon finished his apprentice to Dooku the two kept in touch, and when Qui-Gon took young Kenobi as his padawan Jinn spoke very highly of him to his former master. In 32 BBY Dookus faith in the Order was rocked so hard that he became completely disillusioned with them. The actual tipping point for Dooku was when he learned that Qui-Gon had been killed by Maul, a Sith Lord that Jinn first discovered. He lamented over his former pupils death, and reflected on it afterwards at The Great Tree. This place held significance for the two because when Qui-Gon was a new apprentice to him they used to go there. Qui-Gon was born on Coruscant and for him trees were foreign, so Dooku and him would reflect on the rest of the galaxy there together. His death saddened Dooku to the point where he left the Order. Killing Master Yaddle just sealed the deal.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Can you name any friendly Droids in the Star Wars universe besides R2-D2, C-3PO, and BB-8?
Answer: There's a ton of friendly droids in the SWU besides our favourites like R2-D2, C-3P0 and BB-8. There are so many I can't name them all here,..so I'll name as many as I can think of. C1-10P..otherwise known as Chopper of Phoenix Squadron.. AP-5..who was an Imperial protocol droid who ended up working for the Rebel Alliance.. K2-SO..who also used to be an Imperial droid.. IG11..who was an IG series bounty hunter droid who ended up sacrificing himself to save his friends.. TC-14..who was a protocol droid just like C-3P0 only female in designation.. NED-B..who was a loader droid sympathetic to the Rebels.. R5-D4 (and pretty well every astromech and protocol droid not owned by villains).. 2-1B..which is a Rebel Alliance medical droid.. FX-7..which is also a Rebel medical droid.. AZI-3..who was a Kaminoan medical droid.. L3-37..who was Lando Calrissians personal droid and pilot.. B1-05106..who was a Separatist B1 Battle droid turned Republic sympathiser after developing a conscience.. D-0..one of BB-8s little friends.. PIT droids..responsible for maintenence and repairs on different items from starships to a pod racer.. EMW Midwife droid..used in the delivery of infants.. Professor Huyang..an ancient droid proficient in the art of lightsaber creation.. WA-7..a waitress droid.. BO-N1..a Droid Spa attendant.. D-Squad, consisting of R2-D2, QT-KT, U9-C4, M5-BZ, and WAC-47,.. ..and without going on and on any more,..the Gonk droid, which was responsible for bringing much needed power supplies to the galaxys needs.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Were there any individuals who fought for both sides in the Clone Wars?
Answer: There was one individual who fought for both sides in the Clone Wars, and he was least likely candidate that you would assume;..a B1 Battle droid! Designated B1-05106, this battle droid was damaged by Kenobis blaster deflection straight to his head, and suddenly developed a conscience! During the Battle of Horain B1-05106 , who was fighting with the battle droids against Republic forces, suddenly copped a blaster bolt to his head. Somehow the damage to his head short circuited his processor, and when he recovered he felt conflicted by what he was witnessing. After realising that the Jedi and the clones were being outnumbered by droids he decided to join the Republic, and took up arms against his former droid brothers. He saluted Kenobi and Rex, and instantly jumped into the fray. His new found prowess was most impressive, with B1-05106 kicking another B1s head straight off, and proceeding to rip its arm off. Then he turns on the droids, and uses the dismembered arm to beat them senseless! From his defection to the Republic, and his battle field heroics, he earned the nickname ‘Bats’, and he appeared to be more combat tactical and intelligent after his mishap. He could even duel wield twin blasters with impressive accuracy, to the point where even Captain Rex compliments him for his efforts. He helped Republic forces retreat, was captured by the Separatists only to bust out, commission a Separatist tank…and cause general mayhem for his former droid companions. He rescued his new found allies, and returned to Coruscant to be adopted into the Grand Army of the Republic. When Skywalker was introduced to him by Rex and Kenobi they came to the conclusion that a “droid spy”, sympathetic to the Republic, would prove useful on future missions. He even pleaded with Anakin to recieve his own personal lightsaber! What a team player! Source; Star Wars Adventures, 2017, ‘Roger Roger’

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Which Star Wars battle Droid class do you prefer and why?
Answer: I prefer the Droidekas, aka Destroyer Droids. Manufactured by the Colicoid Creation Nest on Colla IV, these rolling, shielded droids were one of the greatest challenges for a Jedi to face during the Clone Wars. At 1.83 meters tall they were an imposing sight on the battlefield, and combined with their two twin blaster cannons proved highly effective against the Jedi and the clones. But their greatest advantage over the enemy was their deflector shield, and the ability to “transform into a ball shape for high speed rolling”. These two features of the Droidekas often made defeating them a near impossible task, until Republic forces worked out that a forward distraction, followed by a rear assault, was effective in destroying the Destroyer Droids. They proved to be one of the CIS's most effective battle droids against the Grand Army of the Republic, and were responsible for thousands of clone casualties during the war. A Droidekas deflector shield, powered by an on board generator, rendered the clones blasters, and the Jedis lightsabers pretty much useless. They had a very furious attitude towards eliminating the enemy with extreme prejudice, which was something that they got from their creators..the vicious Collicoids. I prefer the Droidekas because of their origins. A Droidekas three legged stance is engineered by the Collicoids to resemble their likeness. Standing at over 2 metres tall, and covered in an extremely durable layer of armour the Collicoids were brutal insectoid carnivores from the planet Colla IV, and first began manufacturing the Droidekas for the Trade Federation;.. before ultimately winning the contract with the Confederacy of Independent Systems. The Collicoids were most known throughout the SWU for their “completely emotionless and murderous ways”, and their exotic technology that was mostly foreign to the Republic. They were a very hostile, warmongering species that could roll much like their droid counterpart, and were vicious in their frenzied attacks. When they designed droids in their likeness they had inadvertently created battle droids that would change the war drastically. In exchange for shipments of Droidekas to fuel the Separatist war machine the Collicoids accepted payments in the form of…exotic meats. This must have delighted some of the Neimoidians of the Trade Federation like Nute Gunray, seeing as how he recieved batches of extremely deadly war droids in exchange for some goods from the butcher! Source; Wookiepedia-Droideka, and Collicoids.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is a unique species in the Star Wars Canon that you wish was more popular?
Answer: The Mikkians. We first meet the Mikkian species in The Clone Wars at the Battle of Ringo Vinda. Two Jedi generals leading the charge during the battle were twin Mikkian sisters Tiplee and Tiplar. General Tiplar is the first Jedi killed by a Clone trooper, in a preemptive, order 66 malfunction in clonetrooper Tups inhibitor chip. The twins were responsible for coordinating attacks against Separatist forces led by Admiral Trench. Tiplee was killed later by Count Dooku on Vizsla Keep 09. Years later during the reign of the Empire there was another pink skinned female Mikkian, Sakas, who was part of a group of Rebel Pathfinders led by Han Solo. They eventually stormed an Imperial facility uncovering the Empires retaliatory attack called Operation Cinder. There are a couple more Mikkians mentioned throughout Canon lore, but they aren't a popular species despite being so unique. But what makes a Mikkian so special and unique? A Mikkian had unique head tendrils that served as sensory organs, being able to not only pick up delicate sounds but “humidity, temperature, magnetic direction and radiation.” Tendril readings were used by mystics in their culture to read their future, with every tendril playing a vital role in uncovering what is to come. Mikkians were known to be brutally honest in their opinions, often brushing off as rude to other species in the SWU. The belief in the force played an integral part in Mikkian culture, predominantly in their religious affiliations. The Mikkians design (above) was “based on an unused piece of concept art for a female Sith that Ian McCaig created for the film Star Wars Episode II : Attack of the Clones.” Source; Wikipedia; Mikkian

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What's the least believable thing in Star Wars?
Answer: I think it's the way Palpatine jumps from his old body in Return of the Jedi to a new clone body on the planet Exegol. For decades Palpatine worked with his master, Darth Plagueis, to find a way to cheat death; to become immortal and have Sith rule over the galaxy for 10,000 years. Plagueis tried to manipulate the midichlorians into achieving this goal, but with limited success. He could regenerate cells to help heal wounds, he could revive necrotic tissue and bring Darth Venamis back from the dead,..and he could create force pregnancies in his subjects. But he never worked out how to achieve immortality in this fashion. It was only after his apprentice Darth Sidious murdered him, took off where Plagueis ended..and then ultimately learned of a way to cheat death through ‘essence transfer’. This is apparently the way “Palpatine somehow survived”, and kept on keeping on in The Rise of Skywalker. But none of this makes sense to me. Palpatine had been trying to cheat death for most of his life. He saw the way his master struggled for years to become immortal by way of the force. They invested years and billions on this plan. He supplanted himself in the Galactic Senate for literal decades, plotting to overthrow the Republic and exterminate the Jedi. Starting a war just to usurp power over the galaxy as a dictator was just his way of establishing dominance as a Sith Lord. He may have finally conquered the galaxy and achieved his goals,..but he hadn't achieved all of them. His ultimate goal throughout his entire tenure as a Sith Lord was to become immortal, and by the time events in TROS rolled around we see that he had worked out the secret to death many years prior. Even before Vader threw him down that chasm in ROTJ Palpatine had worked out the secret to live on in another body. So instead of becoming old, and worn out by decades of using the darkside, why didn't Palpatine just transfer his essence into another clone body before Vaders treachery above Endors moon? Why did he have to establish another regime on Exegol,..Star Destroyers, stormtroopers and the lot, costing untold trillions, if he already had his Galactic Empire ruling the galaxy already? He certainly liked playing the long game, but come on! The man spent his entire life trying to take over the galaxy and live forever. He achieved the first part after decades of carefully plotting and conspiring with his evil machinations, and ultimately established his corrupt Empire and worked out how to transfer his consciousness into another body. This took him well into his old age to achieve, and after he does you're telling me that he just sits on the secret to conquering death without exacting what he had worked so very hard to achieve?! The way The Rise of Skywalker portrayed his return kind of glossed over this point. It was conveyed in a very haphazardly manner, with a lot of people wondering how Palpatine survived anyway. I still don't understand if he had perfected essence transfer then why not just do it already, and just focus on strengthening his Empire? He even destroyed the cloning facilities on Kamino, yet they had the ability to produce an eternal amount of bodies for him to possess. After Endor Palpatines plans just seemed so overtly grandiose and vague in conception. He punishes his old regime with Operation Cinder, despite them staunchly defending his ideals all along,..and then sets up the Final Order as a last insult for their efforts. If he just diverted all the funding from his future endeavours into his already established Empire he would have become more unstoppable. There would have been no need for the First Order, the Final Order and untold trillions of dollars worth of waste. He'd have a brand new body, and an Empire that would be too great for any threat to oppose. Instead he wastes everyones time,.. “somehow returns”, and then foolishly burns up like those Nazis in Raiders of the Lost Ark.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What do you think happened to the traitor Clonetrooper 'Slick' after the Galactic Empire took over?
Answer: Slick was a clonetrooper who genuinely thought he was doing the right thing. He believed that if the Separatists won the war early his millions of brothers in the Grand Army of the Republic wouldn't be left with years of servitude to the Republic. Slick wanted freedom more than anything, but the way he went about it jeopardised the entire clone army. He believed the Jedi were incompetent leaders, only sacrificing the clones, and so fed information to Ventress on the Separatist side. During the Battle of Christophsis he acted as a spy sending encrypted messages, and he led the clones and their commanders into an ambush..until ultimately Rex and Cody apprehended the rogue clone. Slicks behaviour taught the Jedi that the clones aren't entirely obedient, and may harbor resentment towards their Jedi commanders. His betrayal was quickly hushed up by the Jedi, because if other clones learnt of the motive behind his treachery similar sentiments could spread throughout the ranks of the clones. After the Republic eventually won the battle of Christophsis they covered up the whole incident. The only ones aware of his treacherous actions were the ones present when he was apprehended, and Republic High Command. After the battle was over Slick would have been imprisoned in one of the Republic Detention Blocks for treason against the Galactic Republic. After the Empire rose from the ashes of the Republic the fate of Slick has never been established in canon. But just like Dooku captured Kix and entombed him in stasis(for discovering Order 66), the Republic could have done likewise to Slick, and kept him stored in a detention facility in a stasis pod. His free will complicated the war for the Republic, and his actions could have jeopardised its safety. He was silenced one way or another, under the Republics assumption that he'd never be heard from again. Despite this his story spread throughout the clones and the Jedis ranks. Ahsoka referenced him to Barriss Offee and some other clonetroopers, and Commander Cody mentioned his betrayal to Jedi commanders Bayons and Akar-Deshu. Republic High Command couldn't completely sweep Slicks story under the rug, and his story was learned by a famous Ithorian artist Gammit Chond, and Gammits paintings of Slick, along with his story were archived at the Graf Archive on Orchis 2, in 35 ABY.
