Before the fall of the First Order the Graf Archive, and its Shadow Stacks, was a planetary wide facility containing vast information on everything in the Star Wars Universe,..or galaxy. It was previously used as an archive for the Empire, until it ultimately ended up back in the Graf families hands. Slicks treason at the Battle of Christophsis was noted in the section on Christophsis itself. So apparently Slicks story survived well after the fall of the Republic, beyond the reign of the Empire and into the rise of the First Order.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: In Star Wars, are medical droids the friendliest driods and life savers too?
Answer: Yes. Medical droids in the Star Wars Universe are probably the most friendliest droids you could ever encounter;..and thanks to their crucial programming and essential skills these droids were genuine life savers. During the Clone Wars the clonetroopers of the Grand Army of the Republic had to rely on a small army of medical droids patching and treating the wounded and recovering. For these clones the 2-1B series medical droids were miraculous life saving miracle robots. Many a trooper owed their life to these incredible droids. Later the Rebel Alliance would employ the services of these lifesaving droids at its locations across the galaxy. Lukes particular 2–1B droid was very attentive to his needs, after being attacked by a Wampa, and later again after having his arm severed by his father. The droid even wished him good luck. Vaders model was less fortunate, and after giving the Sith Lord lifesaving surgery it was imploded in Vaders very first fit of rage in his new cybernetic suit. What a thanks for saving the life of one of the galaxys most powerful men. Now, imagine waking up in a hospital and finding out that you just lost an arm in a terrible car wreck. Now imagine these droids giving you life saving surgery, and attaching a cybernetic prosthesis to where your limb was severed. You would hail them as miraculous, wondrous creations, and owe your very existence to their extraordinary talents. As for being the friendliest droids in the galaxy, well..you certainly can't deny that droids like AZI-3 have a winning, friendly personality. He was a Kaminoan surgical assistant droid, and programmed to have a jovial, friendly personality that translated into a warm bedside manner. After a traumatic, excruciating physical ordeal one would be most grateful to recieve their treatment, and thankful for their helpful and friendly conversation during recovery. AZI-3 wasn't just a friendly, lifesaving medical droid but he also had another hidden talent. In the event of an emergency, where no other transport is available, AZI-3 is fitted with repulsorlifts and programming that can allow him to double as a small one seated speeder. Friendly,..and convenient.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who is the best Star Wars doctor, and why?
Answer: We have all these incredible medical droids in the Star Wars Universe, and some are better than others but the models and varieties of these medical droids are infinite in number. We have 21-B series med droids, used by the Republic, the Empire and the Rebel Alliance alike. Both Vader and Luke were treated by one of these droids, also with an accompanying FX unit. Kaminoan medical droids such as AZI-3,.. FX series medical droids,.. the EW-3 Midwife droid,.. EV series, First Order and Imperial, and Old Republic medical droids,.. ..and even some IG units can be programmed to deliver vital medical treatment when required by organic beings. But these mechanical automatons just don't have the warm, delicate, sensitive touch that a human hand can administer during medical treatment. Dr Harter Kalonia was a brilliant doctor serving both the New Republic and later the Resistance. She also held the rank of Major. After Finn was wounded by Kylo Ren at Starkiller Base Dr Kalonia teated Finns wounds. She also attended to Chewbaccas injuries after the First Order assault at Mazs Castle on Tokodana. Her bedside manner was enough to placate Chewie after a nasty blaster burn, and her knowledge of the native Wookiee tongue, Shyriiwook, also helped calm the injured hero. If she can soothe an injured Wookiee without having her arms ripped off,..then she wins the title of being the best doctor in the Star Wars Universe.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Which character introduced in Star Wars: The Force Awakens is the best?
Answer: The best new character from The Force Awakens was a character that had no lines, barely any screen time, and hardly anyone knows his name. Yet he embodies the spirit of Star Wars, and is a very intriguing and fascinating character. His name was Sidon Ithano, aka The Crimson Corsair, aka The Red Raider, aka The Blood Buccaneer. With nicknames like those you'd think he was an incredible new, mysterious character, with a rich backstory and loads of potential,…and he was! Sidon Ithano was a pirate, smuggler and an all round kick ass character, with a cool costume and interesting background. He was a Delphidian pirate from the Outer Rim, who rose to prominence as the most successful pirate in the region after the collapse of the Empire. His name was regarded with reverence and fear, and to give his character an extra layer of mystery he wore a red Kaleesh War mask, that he stole of course. 50 years after the Clone Wars had ended he and his crew found the remains of an old Separatist vessel, the Obrexta III. Expecting to find the lost ‘Treasure of Count Dooku’, and a wealth of kyber crystals, they instead unearthed an old stasis pod in the wreckage, containing inside the cryogenically stored body of Kix the Clonetrooper from the Clone Wars. He had been put there by Dooku for uncovering the plot to kill the Jedi. Ithano was an interesting character, but only seen for a few brief moments in Maz Kanatas Castle on Tokodana in The Force Awakens. When Finn decides to leave Han, Rey and the group, Maz informed Finn that he could get work with Ithano and his crew,..and right before Finn embarks with Ithano and his first mate Quigold the First Order blows up several planets and assaults Mazs Castle. Besides a brief stint in an episode of the Star Wars animated series Resistance, season 2, Ithanos interesting story wasn't explained..yet warranted more attention. He had potential to become someone great in the sequel trilogy, but after TFA his character wasn't really explored or developed much further. This is such a shame as this guy could have his own series. Between the collapse of the Empire and the rise of the First Order he fought several battles, went on crazy adventures with his team, as mentioned, and had a crew each with their own unique story, like Quigold the amphibious Gabdorin. In his fisfit crew of pirates and adventurers there was also an Arcona named Reeg Brosna,..a Gamorrean named Squeaky,...the Ishi Tib Pendewqell,..and a red female Twi'lek called Reveth. Just imagine these guys in a series that's all about pirating, and blowing up the First Order. Imagine seeing a live action version of The Crimson Corsair and the Lost Treasure of Count Dooku.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Which 'Star Wars' creature best represents our bulldog or pitbull?
Answer: There are two creatures in the Star Wars Universe that best represent bulldogs and pitbulls from our universe. Massiffs are large Pitbull sized reptilian creatures that fill the role of Pitbulls in Star Wars. They are native to places such as Tatooine and Geonosis, and when domesticated can prove loyal as guard dogs, and attack dogs. The Tusken Raiders use them as guard dogs, sentries and to protect their children when adults aren't near. They have a fearsome demeanor, like a Pitbull terrier, and are capable of doing similar damage like its Earth bound equivalent. Despite this they can be friendly, very loyal and playful companions. On Geonosis they are guard dogs, being employed in sensitive facilities, important personnel and also to heard colliseum beasts in the Petranaki Arena. During the Clone Wars the Grand Army of the Republic used Massiffs as guard, attack and search dogs in a specialist K9 unit as part of the Coruscant Guard. His name was Grizzer, and his clone handler went by the name Hound. When it comes to a creature from Star Wars that is most reminiscent of our earthly Bull dogs you can't look past the Frog-Dog. One such Frog-Dog resided at Jabbas Palace on Tatooine named Buboicullaar;..or Bubo for short. He was stocky, small and with a mouth that is the SW equivalent of a bulldogs. Bubo was actually very intelligent, and had been a spy for many years. Originally he had been owned by a Jawa tribe, then found his way to Jabbas court. He foiled a plot by Ree Yees to blow up the Hutt, and remained loyal to Jabba until his demise. After the Hutt died Bubo specifically requested that the B'omarr monks remove his brain, and place it in the spiritual enlightenment jars afixed to the spider droids commonly associated with the order. Over his time at Jabbas he had developed a strong companionship with the monk Evilo Nailati, and ultimately decided to spend eternity pondering the mysteries of the galaxy..and the great unknown.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Is there anywhere in the Galaxy where droids are treated as equals (Star Wars)?
Answer: If droids are lucky enough they might reside near a Droid Bar, where they can feely mingle with other droids in a normally safe and private atmosphere. Most droids have not been emancipated from their owners or employment, and usually live in service to organic beings as, well…robotic slaves. But just like in ancient Roman times when a slave had finished his or her work for the day, and only if they had kind masters, they could visit a tavern or bar for some refreshments. Some droids also had the desire to explore human pursuits and past times, and hanging out in a bar happened to be one of them. Some droids in the SWU had kind masters also, and after their daily requirements had been achieved they were free to go to a Droid Bar, and instead of having an alcoholic drink they injested Nepenthe. This was a type of lubricator fluid that delivered ‘program patches’ to the droids central processor. It was a way for the droids to spend their free time with other droids, and share in something that organic beings take mostly for granted. Bars like this gave them an option, considering in large parts of the galaxy droids weren't allowed to enter bars due to lingering anti-Seperatist sentiments. We see one of these Droid Bars in season 3 of The Mandalorian, named ‘The Resistor’. In these bars they were treated as equals by their fellow droids, as they were free to interact with others, share information and generally relax in a kind of way. It was also a way for them to develop and learn new skills from other droids, and avoid negative sentiments from organic beings. Other droids who had been liberated, or emancipated from service, usually took on professions to gain more independence. Some droids which had combat programming and capabilities entered the bounty hunting fraternity, and after establishing themselves as a proficient hunter often earned the respect of their fellow Guild members. The Bounty Hunting Guild did not discriminate, and a successful bounty hunter droid such as IG-88 or 4-LOM could earn the respect of the guild and its members. 4-LOM was a protocol droid who actually overrode his programming, ultimately leaving him with an independent personality and traits. After his freedom was obtained he found work as a bounty hunter. This eventually landed him employment with Darth Vader himself.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did Palpatine ever fear Darth Maul?
Answer: Palpatine never feared Maul, not for one second,..but he did fear what his meddling could amount to if Maul was left unchecked. On two separate occasions Maul attempted to end Palpatines machinations, and on both occasions Maul made wrong decisions. But had he acted differently he could have been a very real threat to his former masters plans, and this was something that forced Sidious to play his cards early. Once Maul and Savage had killed Pre Vizla, becoming ruler of Mandalore, he became an immediate threat to his rise to power. Sidious trumped Maul on that occasion, but he needed him alive to lure out Mother Talzin. His plan worked, but Maul survived and escaped once more. Palpatine knew that his apprentice had only gained in rage, anger and power since he last apprenticed to him on that fateful day during the Battle of Naboo. Palpatine was very impressed that his former apprentice had survived being bisected, and impressed that Maul had taken over the mighty Mandalorian homeworld. But after killing his mother, and his brother..Sidious knew that Maul would stop at nothing to avenge their deaths. And it was on Mandalore again that Maul tried to messy up Palpatines plans again. When Ahsoka confronts Maul on Mandalore he was expecting Kenobi, but instead he reveals his motives to Skywalkers apprentice. He planned to slaughter Sidious’ new prodigy, and ruin his plans in revenge for all that the Sith Lord Master had taken from him. He was going to take Skywalker from him, but instead he got Ahsoka who ruined everything. Kenobi was meant to lure out Skywalker, but once again the Jedi stood in his way. If these opportunities for Maul hadn't have ended in failure then his former master would have his grand plans ruined, by the one individual who should have been standing where Skywalker was. It was about vengeance, it was about retribution..and for Maul it was about proving to himself who was truly worthy of the title. This is what Sidious worried about, and after Ahsoka spent too much time with Maul, before and after apprehending him, doubt would have crept into his mind. Could Maul strike an alliance with the former apprentice of Skywalker? Could their meddling interfere with his new apprentice, and further ruin his plans? Could his former apprentice have enough influence to rally both Lady Tano and half of the 501st on Mandalore,..combined with his expanding criminal empire and stand against the rise of his new empire? Sidious may not have feared a direct confrontation with Maul, but he feared what his meddling influence could amount to.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is your favorite dark side ritual or tradition in the Star Wars Canon and why?
Answer: There's a tradition that Darth Vader bestows on every new Inquisitor that falls under his command. To fill them full of rage, pain, suffering and anger he teaches them the lesson of loss; but in the most brutal of fashions. Loss is something that Vader is all to familiar with. It started with losing his mother to the Tusken Raiders, then losing his apprentice Ahsoka during the Clone Wars. Then he suffers even more unthinkable loss in the form of having his limbs severed by the man he once called master,..and the most tragic of all was losing the love of his life. Vader used the powerful emotions that mentally stemmed from these terrible events to make him one of the most powerful Sith Lords to ever live. When he began leading and training the Inquisitors he tried to instil some of this power in his assassins. But to achieve the power they too needed to suffer loss. As a rite of passage for all Inquisitors he cruelly takes something from them, so as they may experience what he did. Dooku took Skywalkers arm and it taught him the lesson of loss. Vader would do something similar, and in the case of his Inquisitors he would sever one of their limbs..so they'd always remember the lesson of loss too. The Sixth Brother learnt this the hard way when Vader severed his lower left arm. This was the same injury that Dooku had inflicted upon Anakin, and from this he never forget what the Count took from him. Vader did the same thing to his Inquisitors, to make them draw upon the same pain and trauma of loss that he also drew upon. Some Inquisitors lost a hand, an arm..and at least one of them was bisected like Maul. This little ritual of Vaders was my favourite darkside tradition that he staunchly upheld.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Where would Starkiller fit in the empire if the Emperor allowed Vader to keep him as an apprentice?
Answer: Galen Marek was the son of a Jedi, kidnapped by Vader after the Dark Lord of the Sith killed his father on Kashyyyk. Dubbed Starkiller by his master, he became Darth Vaders secret apprentice. Vader used Galen to extract information and kill remaining Jedi left over from the Great Purge. Starkiller proved his worth by killing Jedi Masters Kazdan Paratus and Shaak Ti(Legends only). But Vader kept him a secret from the Emperor, and ultimately he was killed in an epic final confrontation between Vader and Darth Sidious. But had the Emperor allowed Starkiller to live, and let Vader keep him as an apprentice, how would he fit into their Empire? Firstly he would definitely not be a fully indoctrinated Sith Lord apprentice,..but rather an acolyte, an assassin and someone for Vader to wield as a tool. Darth Maul began his service with the Sith Order by firstly becoming Palpatines own Sith assassin. Palpatines own master, Darth Plagueis, was completely aware of Maul serving as an assassin for his own apprentice. He just wasn't aware that Palpatine planned on usurping the crown and taking Maul as a replacement to fill his old role. Starkiller may serve Vader in a similar role, but ultimately it may not be Vader that Starkiller serves. Starkiller wouldn't become Vaders personal assassin, but instead become Palpatines own apprentice. Like Vaders suit was designed by Palpatine to control the former Jedi, the Emperor had a similar suit in mind for Starkiller. It was called Sith Stalker armour and completely encased the wearer, again like Vaders suit. It was painfully grafted to the body through excruciating surgery, and left the occupant completely trapped. Had Starkiller survived his duel with Vader Palpatine had planned on doing the same thing he did to Anakin. He was going to entomb him forever in the Sith Stalker armour, remove his free will and use him as a kind of lobotomised version of Vader. Vader would be replaced by an apprentice that no longer posed a threat to his reign and title of Sith Lord Master, and Palpatine would be up to his fourth apprentice. Starkiller was always too powerful to serve Vader and his master in the Imperial Inquisitorious or the likes, and Palpatine would never allow him to serve Vader alone. They would pose too far a threat to Palpatines Empire, but if Starkiller could defeat Vader then Palpatine would still have a phenomenally powerful apprentice to command. Starkiller had to die, otherwise he would be doomed regardless; serving Palpatine forever as a faceless, nameless, mindless minion under the title Lord Starkiller.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What was the reason for the Tusken Raiders' presence on Tatooine?
Answer: At some point in Tatooines ancient past the planet suffered a devastating cataclysm, ultimately turning the once lush world into a barren desert rock. The Tusken Raiders had long been the traditional custodians of the land. It is their homeworld, and as Fett put it in The Book of Boba Fett, about Tusken culture and heritage… “These people lay ancestral claim to the Dune Sea, and if you pass a toll is to be paid to them.” After all the water on Tatooine vanished it suddenly became the most expensive commodity on the rock. The Tuskens themselves grew possessive of water, over millenias of learning to ration and supply it. Ultimately they viewed all water on Tatooine their native birthright, and would kill to acquire and keep it sacred. This would result in nearly all the different Tusken tribes coming to violently mistrust outsiders and offworlders from poaching their precious commodity. Eight decades prior to 19BBY on Tatooine, one of the earliest human settlements was attacked and overrun by Tuskens because of this longstanding mistrust. Fort Tusken, as it was known, is also where the Sandpeoples moniker of Tusken Raider originated. Their presence on Tatooine began to stir fear in settlers and traders, and for nearly a century they fought against outsiders, and forever will. Only those who earn their respect may pass safely through their desert home. Tatooine is more than just their home,..its a sacred part of their ancient culture and the backbone of their society. Trespassers trying to hoard and take their precious water away from them invite doom at their own peril. Moisture Farms on Tatooine are deemed as a snub at their culture by the Tuskens, and the Lars Homestead was one of these such threats,..these insults. Anakin Skywalkers mother, Shmi, was abducted from right near the outskirts of the farm, prior to the Clone Wars, and the Tuskens claimed her life for encroaching on their sacred land. She took the mushrooms which grew on the moisture evaporators, and the Tuskens kidnapped her when she strayed too far from the Homestead. Yet on occasion the raiders will come to a truce with the settlers to face a common foe, such as when the settlers of Mos Pelgo banded together with a war party of Tuskens to defeat a Krayt Dragon which had been terrorising the local area.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: If Leia was forced to smoke Jabba's hookah, would she enjoy it? If not, why?
Answer: If she was forced to smoke Jabbas grandiose hookah pipe then I'm fairly certain she isn't going to fondly remember the experience any time in the near future. Jabba made a very lucrative profit from dealing and running Spice throughout the galaxy, especially through the use of smugglers, like Han Solo and Chewbacca among others. Jabba also liked to participate in the smoking of spice, and the SWU's version of tobacco, simply called t'bac. But like Lom Pyke of the Pyke Syndicate Jabba also liked to “get high on his own supply”, and in the safety of his palace he would smoke his hookah, and snack on his Klatooine Paddy frogs that were stored in the lower portion of his impressive looking smoking apparatus. Princess Leia was definitely not like Jabba the Hutt, and certainly would not enjoy it. Leia was raised by Alderaan nobility, and as a princess wouldn't be seen dead smoking from a filthy Hutt hookah. Sansanna spice was one of the more potent and addictive strains of the illegal narcotic, and Leias royal upbringing would leave her with mixed negative emotions after the whole ordeal. Such potent spice would dramatically affect her judgement, and produce behaviour very unbefitting of a princess; and she would be absolutely wigging out on sounds and lights after smoking Jabbas curious hallucinigentics. Imagine being imprisoned by a murderous Hutt gangster, made to wear some cheap, skimpy attire while hordes of prying eyes leer at you,…and then being forced by the crimelord to smoke spice from his saliva soaked bong! No,..no one would like to smoke from Jabbas disgusting hookah, especially after it looks like he's eating the Paddy Frogs from the dirty bong water. Yeeech!!

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What would have happened if Darth Vader had (somehow) found about Luke and Leia while they were infants?
Answer: Then Vader would have several big problems to deal with. Firstly by finding his long lost twins he is presented with the dilemma of how to conceal their identities from the Emperor. If Palpatine knew that the progeny of Vader had survived into childhood then he would want to claim Luke and Leia for himself. Seeing as how Vader failed on Mustafar, and became less than his full potential, Darth Sidious was somewhat disappointed in his apprentice. Either of the Skywalker twins could be instructed in the darkside and replace Vader, and this would be something that he would realise upon their discovery. The Emperor could never learn of their existence, for he would corrupt them..or even worse kill them. In Vaders worst dreams his master could even order him to slay his own children, but I believe that the Emperor would eventually do away with Vader and claim his children, or at least one of them, as a fully fledged Sith apprentice. If Vader managed to locate Leia on Alderaan it would be simple for him to seize her. Bail Organa and his forces would no doubt fight to the last to protect the princess, but their struggle would be in vain. Vader would march on the Alderaan Royal Palace and swiftly put an end to any resistance, but if he made a public spectacle out of it then surely the Emperors eyes and ears would alert him to Vaders actions. Then if Palpatine found out it would be game over for father and daughter. Vader would have to kidnap his own daughter in a very covert manner, and eliminate all witnesses to the affair..including his own men who took part in Leias extraction from the palace. Then he would have to keep her far from the eyes of the Empire, and hide her away until he could formulate a solution to this dilemma. No doubt the thought of killing his master would become a top option to solve this delicate predicament. If Vader managed to find Luke on Tatooine when he was a child then it could go any number of ways. Vader would have to stealthily extract Luke in the same fashion as his sister, so as not to arouse the Emperors suspicions. But there would be an added element of difficulty to this because of his former master, Kenobi, who vigilantly kept watch over his son. Vader would more than likely defeat Kenobi on Tatooine, as before Kenobi found his ‘inner Jedi’ during his standalone series he was beaten, tired and lacking in skill after such a stagnant and emotional period. Vader could defeat him as Kenobi was off balance, distraught and utterly consigned to defeat. But then again, if Kenobi came back in classic style Vader may lose, and Kenobi would have no other option but to flee with Luke..or finally end his former apprentices life on the spot. Every way that Vader would assess the situation it would result in a tremendous risk posed to his newfound twins. If he didn't play every move just right he would leave the door open to his masters wrath, and possibly condemn his children to a life in service to the darkside. But if he kept them a secret, and kept them safe, then together they could become a serious threat to Palpatine,..but would he risk their lives in a direct confrontation with Darth Sidious? There would be too many variables that Vader would surmise, that could jeopardise everything and then have his children taken away again,..but if the Emperor tried this then I think Vader would unleash his full potential on him. He would destroy the Emperor if he threatened to kill them at this point. Left: Grant Feely (Luke Skywalker), right Vivian Lyra Blair (Leia Organa), from ‘Obi-Wan Kenobi’ 2023

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is the significance of Ventress having a yellow lightsaber in Star Wars: The Clone Wars?
Answer: After rogue Jedi Barriss Offee stole both her crimson bladed lightsabers on Coruscant, during the Clone Wars, Ventress needed to improvise. She had entered the bounty hunting game only in the last couple of years after getting her foot in the door thanks to a young Boba Fett. After being betrayed by her former master Dooku and seeing her Nightsister coven wiped out..she came to realise now that it was her calling. She had pursued it as a more recent ‘career change’ and had always relied on her lightsabers since she was a Jedi padawan. Upon her Jedi masters death many years prior Ventress took his lightsaber as her own, and so adopted the twin saber fighting style well before her apprenticeship to Dooku. The Count only enhanced her ferocity and sharpened her skills. After the treacherous Offee stole her old sabers, that Dooku had given to her, she still felt the need to require one afterwards. She had also felt the encroaching darkness on the horizon and knew she needed protection; especially in the days of the growing Empire. A lightsaber had saved her life uncountable times, and would still prove effective in the bounty hunting business. So to begin anew and put her torments behind her she purchased a yellow bladed lightsaber off the black market. The criminal underworld was her workplace now so it wasn't hard for her to acquire one illegally.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did Boba Fett ever lose?
Answer: Sure he did. We see evidence of one of his first business failures during the Clone Wars. Initially he failed at an attempt on Mace Windus life, but this vendetta was deeply personal to the young man; it wasn't business in the traditional sense, and Fett was relatively unexperienced in the bounty hunting game at this point. He was even incarcerated with one of his mentors and teammates Bossk, on Coruscant for a period at the Republic Judiciary Central Detention Center, where he was paid off by Cad Bane to start a prison riot. Later during the war he reformed his team, only on this particular job he had a new member in the group; Asajj Ventress. She killed one of his crew, and Fett and his team ultimately coerced her to join them on their bounty hunt. The mission was simple;..upon arriving on the designated planets surface the crew would escort a sensitive ‘package’ to one of the planets wealthy despots,..return after delivering said asset and receive payment. Simple right? Turns out the package was a young girl who had been kidnapped by the despots men, and she was going to be forced to marry the uncaring sod. Ventress suddenly developed a conscious and ultimately turned on Fett. She returned the ‘bounty’ to her rightful people, after fooling the despot into believing she had delivered the young girl. Ventress took payment from the warlord, and then set foot on the path to becoming a skilled hunter herself. Despite ruining Fetts plans, she still honoured him..and only took her cut from the proceeds of the job. So Fett actually didn't end up losing any credits;..Ventress just dented his ego a little.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What was the saddest Star Wars death?
Answer: For myself it was the death of the entire Tusken tribe that saved Boba Fett..after his escape from the almighty Sarlaac. Firstly Fett miraculously survives his plunge into the maw of the enormous desert dweller, only to be ripped of all his armour by scheming, thieving Jawas. Then he is kidnapped by a tribe of Tusken Raiders and at first treated very poorly by his hosts. Ultimately he wins their trust by saving a young Tusken boy from a vicious Tatooine Sand Beast; and choking and beheading the monster. He is welcomed into their tribe, and despite the opportunity to escape he chooses to remain a member of their family. He develops close and strong bonds with members of the tribe, and sees them as more than just captors..more than just mindless savages, and views them as his family. After helping them take down a Pyke desert train transporting Sansanna Spice, that was attacking the tribe, he further earned the respect of the tribal elders. They too considered him a member of the family tribe and guided him on a spiritual journey, as part of Tusken culture. This relationship that Fett had with the Tuskens was truly special, and they helped him to become a better man. It's as if Fetts time with the Sandpeople had changed him. Changed him from a ruthless killer into someone who truly wanted to redeem himself as a good person. He even states that he was ready to leave hunting behind. The Sandpeople even had a small ceremony where they clothed Fett in his own unique Tusken outfit, and guided him to create his own Gaderffii Stick which is critical in their culture. It symbolised that Fett, who began as an outsider to them, was now truly one of their own. The way they accepted him as a great warrior, and as a brother, was quite touching, and added an element to the Tuskens that is rarely mentioned. But then something absolutely heartbreaking and utterly senseless happens. In retaliation for their loss out in the desert the Pykes strike back with a terrible vengeance. While Fett was in Mos Eisley the Pykes speeder gang, The Nikto Sand Riders, laid waste to the Tuskens encampment..and killed every member of the tribe; even the women and children. As Fett mourns, and ceremonially cremates his dead family..he openly weeps. He didn't cry when he seen his father decapitated by the Jedi, but the deaths of the Sandpeople, he regarded as family, profoundly affected him enough to openly mourn them and subsequently avenge their deaths. The way he guns the killers down in Slave I is so very satisfying. He later sadly laments to Fennec Shand how he tried to help his tribe, but inadvertently got them all killed. This is one of the more sadder moments in the entire franchise for me.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: In Star Wars, after the defeat of the separatist forces, did some battledroid army desert and join the rebellion forces and fought against the Galactic Empire?
Answer: In Rebels, season 3, episode ‘The Last Battle’ we see remnants of a battle droid army fight the forces of the Galactic Empire on the former Separatist world of Agamar. During their search for vital weapons, particularly proton bombs, members of Phoenix Squadron travel to the remote world, and arrive at the wreckage of a colossal Separatist Command vessel. Upon arrival they are captured by former Separatist General, Super Tactical droid Kalani, and his small army of B1 Battle droids and Droidekas. But Kalani and the droids never joined the Rebels, so to say; only to join the Rebels and face a common threat together being the Empire itself. Kalani took the initial droid shut down order from Mustafar to be a Republic trick, and never deactivated himself or his droids. Here he remained unaware of the fall of the Republic, and was also unaware of the approaching Empire that rose from ashes of the Clone Wars. But ultimately he determined that the Empire was the successor to the Republic..and joined the Rebel members to defend against the Empire. And so the Rebels, and the droids, combine their efforts to attack the Empire when they assault Agamar. The B1 battle droids rolled proton torpedoes and began firing at them when the AT-ATs and the AT-DPs made their approach. Kanan and Ezra deflected the droids blaster bolts towards the bombs as they made contact with the legs of the Imperial walkers. The Droidekas provided extra support for the group during their attack on the Empire. Ultimately their plan allowed enough time for Phoenix Squadron, and Kalani and his remaining droids, to escape the grasp of the still reeling Imperial forces.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Is it possible for a Storm Trooper to shoot all their ammo quickly?
Answer: Yes it is,..if you're talking about them shooting the standard Imperial issue E-11 Blaster rifle. This weapon was manufactured by three different companies; BlasTech Industries, Sorosub Corporation and Merr-Sonn Munitions Inc. All three made the blasters specifications common throughout the entire galaxy. Weighing in at a compact 2.7 kgs, and holding a capacity of 500 shots, the E-11 was effective up to 300 metres..and more efficient at 100 metres. It was so valuable in its role that it was kept in service for more than 150 years after its initial success. It would serve throughout the Galactic Civil War and well beyond. As I mentioned it had a capacity of 500 rounds, but its power cell only lasted for around 100 shots. Power cells could be replaced depending on the 3 settings, and were located on the left side of the weapon, above the trigger. “The E-11 possessed select fire capability, allowing the user to choose between semi automatic and pulse fire settings, as well as a rapid fire setting that exchanged accuracy for an expanding fire area” So if an Imperial Stormtrooper wanted to blast through their ammunition it would be quite easy for them to carry extra power cells, crank up the setting, and just fire away! But its also easy for them to be efficient, and conserve their ammunition by just adjusting the blasters settings. Source; E-11 Blaster rifle Wookiepedia.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is the significance of Palpatine's black robe in Star Wars? Why does he change into it when he becomes emperor and what does it symbolize?
Answer: Before Palpatine ascended to Emperor he had to remain hidden, anonymous, and conceal his true identity at all times. Part of his attire were his Sith robes, which hid his face from full view. When he was in disguise as his alter ego, Darth Sidious, he had to use the black robe to stop people seeing his face, but as Supreme Chancellor Palpatine he had to wear his diplomatic robes of the Senate. Once he declared himself Emperor of the galaxy he didn't need to hide his face anymore, or return to his mundane, civilian outfit. When he fought Mace Windu in his office he was wearing these robes, but after he killed him he changed into the dark Sith robes again. This symbolised the death of the Republic, and the birth of the Empire. Darth Sidious didn't need to hide anymore, and he could embrace the darkside; and wear traditional dark clothing which pertained to the Sith Order. Whereas he told the rest of the galaxy that an attack by the Jedi left him scarred and deformed, hence he wore his hooded robe to disguise the ‘fact’.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What technology from Star Wars would you use to build a modern day army?
Answer: There's one piece of Star Wars technology that would surpass the need to use an army, and it's very existence could probably pave the way for peace talks in every corner of the globe;..Palpatines Sith Eternal Star Destroyers, and their ‘reactor-fed axial superlasers’. These new and improved Star Destroyers, classified as Xyston-class destroyers, are “fitted with efficient automation systems to cut down on crew requirements”, meaning they only needed a fraction of the crew to operate, and its primary weapon was enough to destroy any ship or planet. Quite simply, it was the most powerful ship ever created in the Star Wars Universe, utilising micronised Death Star technology. The Xyston-class Final Order Star Destroyers superlaser would be enough to make any democracy hating villains bow down or perish. One test of its incredibly destructive laser is all it would take to ensure the path to world peace is not hindered by any megalomaniacs oppressing less powerful countries. If this Star Destroyer and its weapon existed it could be deployed to anywhere on the planet in a moments notice, and suppress any hostilities present in a heartbeat. There would be absolutely no need to outfit thousands of soldiers with absurdly expensive weapons and hardware,..and risk their lives unnecessarily. Just one of these ships could use orbital bombardment, without the use of the superlaser, to destroy a tyrant in his palace anywhere on the planet and eliminate his armies, navies and air force within moments of striking. If any foolish despot dared to oppose its authority the time for diplomacy would be swiftly stood aside, and they would be annihilated before they could start a conflict or war. This is the only bit of Star Wars tech that you'd need to keep the peace.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How did Anakin feel while he was slaughtering the Jedi younglings?
Answer: Only the Darth Vader comics give us a small glimpse into what was possibly going through the mind of Anakin Skywalker when he killed the Jedi younglings during Order 66. Both the movie and the novelisation of Revenge of the Sith don't describe how Vader felt when he had to kill the temple younglings. But in some of the extra canon material, like the comics for instance, we see that Vader was clearly traumatised by what he was doing. His face displays anguish, sadness and fear as he he remembers killing them. Their images appear to haunt him. He displays outward sadness when he kills the Separatist Leaders on Mustafar, and this wasn't that long after what he did to the younglings. More than likely Vader used these overwhelming emotions to fuel his powers in the darkside, and by reliving his atrocities he hated himself. By hating himself he became an even more powerful Sith Lord, and continued to use emotions and memories like this to make him stronger. This is something that remained a theme throughout his life. Sadly, the only member of the Jedi family that ever called him a master was the poor youngling who first spoke to him in the temple. He said this blindly believing that because Anakin was on the Jedi Council that he surely was a Jedi Master. He was giving him the respect that Anakin yearned from the Council, but was never shown. Sadly this youngling was the first to fall, and this would have been something that Vader would have remembered to the grave.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How would things have played out if Darth Plagueis trained Anakin Skywalker? Would Anakin have found a way to save Padme?
Answer: I don't think this ultimately would have worked in Darth Plagueis’ favour for a couple of reasons. In Lucenos novel Plagueis literally pisses off the force to the point where it retaliates by creating ‘the chosen one’, to ultimately avenge it because of Plagueis’ meddling. The Muun Sith Lord delved far too deep into the darkside, and became obsessed with midichlorian manipulation, to the point he performed hideous experiments in his quest. His goal was to become immortal, which he eventually succeeded in by way of essence transfer; which Palpatine actually used to escape to Exegol in Return of the Jedi. But his manipulation of the force, and his laboratories full of experiments, allowed him to uncover research into cheating death. During the course of these lab experiments he was able to bring back Darth Venamis from death repeatedly, and he could even influence the force to create ‘force pregnancies’ in his test subjects. He was just looking in the wrong places before essence transfer became evident to his apprentice. This outraged the force, as if it was a singular being itself. It sought to balance what Plagueis and ultimately his apprentice and legacy did, by attempting to become as powerful as itself. In retaliation it created Anakin as it knew he would grow up fulfilling what even the Jedi were aware of,..but low key the real reason why Anakin was chosen to bring balance to the force was because of what Plagueis started. The Jedi just reinforced Plagueis’ fear with their prophecy which was older than his experiments. Plagueis may have been arrogant and centred on his work, but if he hypothetically survived Palpatines attack and went on to kidnap and train Skywalker,..deep down he knew he would later regret it. The boy would mature and avenge the force for how Plagueis manipulated its children; being the midichlorians themselves. This wouldn't seem like a viable option, training the boy and all..but Plagueis would nonetheless see incredible potential in the slave boy from Tatooine. In the novel there is also a part that ties in with episode I. During the scene on Coruscant where Darth Maul and Darth Sidious speak on a Coruscant balcony.. ..Darth Plagueis was secretly spying on them both. He was curious as to how his apprentices assassin, Maul, interacted with Palpatine. He took this opportunity to view them both from afar, and apparently did likewise when Qui-Gon Jinn and young Anakin were conferring on Coruscant at another location. Before Qui-Gon took Anakin away to the Jedi Temple he wanted to look upon the boy that was dubbed ‘the chosen one’. But had Plagueis trained Anakin, and made him his confidante like he did to Sidious, then possibly through the force Skywalker or Plagueis could have saved Padme. But then again, if Plagueis took Skywalker as his apprentice would the relationship between the Queen of Naboo and the slave from Tatooine even taken place? By taking Anakin as his own could he twist the prophecy to his liking? Could he avert it entirely? I don't think so. More than likely Anakin would preemptively fulfill the prophecy by killing Plagueis, instead of killing Palpatine decades later. Then the force would have its balance restored, and billions of lives would be saved because there would be no casualties from the nonexistent Clone Wars, or the Empires reign. But Palpatines plans were initially Plagueis’ own design, so instead of Palpatine and Vader, it would just become Plagueis and Skywalker. Either way Plagueis would die at the hands of Skywalker..because you can't trick or fool the force.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: In Star Wars, what happened to Jar Jar Binks, and where is he?
Answer: After the Battle of Endor Jar Jar wasn't just booted out of the Gungan swamps again, but he was made completely homeless. But despite being shunned and ostracised by pretty much all of Naboo, Binks didn't let it crush his spirit. In the capital of Theed Jar Jar found work as a street performing clown. Here he entertained the local and other children with his funny antics, and resigned his fate to putting smiles on peoples faces for the rest of his days. It's as though he was shunned by an entire society, and he never really understood the gravity of his actions during events from The Phantom Menace. I know many of you will disagree with me here, but I think Binks’ fate was rather sad given the tremendous loyalty he showed. Even though Binks’ character recieved so much negativity I felt kinda bad for him. He proved his loyalty to the ones he cared about time and time again. He even saved Padmes life on Mon Cala, when the Karkarodon, Riff Tamson, punctured a hole in her dive helmet. Jar Jar spat a gungan slime that sealed Padmes helmet, which prevented her grim underwater death,..but this is never credited to him. He bravely impersonated Gungan High Council member Boss Leonie in front of General Grievous, and he bought enough time for his friends to prevent a Separatist attack on Naboo,..but this isn't remembered later. Even under extreme circumstances he tried his best, and did it in his own unique way. I don't think he should have been reviled to the ridiculous extent that he was. Ahmed Best, who portrayed Jar Jar Binks, once said that there was going to be a scene in which Palpatine actually gives thanks to Jar Jar for granting him the emergency powers in senate that lead to Darth Sidious’ hostile takeover of the galaxy. But this was obviously cut from the final movie. Just imagine that scene playing out in the Imperial Senate to the eyes of the galaxy!

Answer: Standard question. Okay, this is easy considering that two of them I'll never see again, and one of them I'm going to be married to forever. Let's start with which Star Wars character I would kiss. Now I'm only choosing this character to kiss if she is willing herself;..if not then I wouldn't dream of kissing her without her permission! Bo Katan Kryze always makes my heart race every time I see her kicking ass, or whenever she gives one of those inspiring speeches. I always wondered if she was a good kisser, so I'm definitely not passing on that opportunity. Now who would I kill? This is a hard one because there's so many insanely cruel, and piece of s#@t characters to choose from. Most of you would say Palpatine, well..because he murdered billions, exterminated the Jedi, and plunged the galaxy into years of brutal subjugation. Some of you would say Jar Jar Binks, but I actually liked the guy..so lay off him okay. No, my choice here is that a-hole acting like a drunk redneck at a bar in A New Hope. Dr Cornelius Evazan. Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is something that people miss while watching Star Wars?
Answer: There's something that happens at Maz Kanatas castle on Tokodana that symbolises the end of the old saga, and rings in the new sequels. But it happens in a way that I never realised until I watched it a couple of times. When Han Solo takes Rey and Finn to Tokodana, he tells them about his old friend Maz. Her castle on Tokodana was like the Cantina in A New Hope, or Jabbas court in Return of the Jedi,..except it was one giant party! Before entering her fine establishment you have to pass under dozens of flags that adorn the top of the entrance way. These flags are from the original trilogy, and the sequel trilogy..and encompass many different characters and groups from the entire saga up until Disney bought the rights to Star Wars. Of the flags present we have the Mandalorian Mythosaur symbol and Boba Fetts symbol, various pod racer flags from episode I, Hondo Ohnakas Gang symbol, Ziro the Hutts symbol, and even Vaders Fist 501st smbol. Each one represents something from almost every pre-Disney film, including The Clone Wars, The Phantom Menace, and Return of the Jedi. Each one also represents many different characters from Boba Fett, Ziro the Hutt, Anakin Skywalker, Hondo Ohnaka,..and Sebulba, Aldar Beedo, Ark Roose, and Teemto Pagalies; who were all Pod Racers on Tatooine. Everyone knows and loves these stories and characters, they were iconic, revolutionary and idolised by fans for decades. Then Disney takes the reigns, appoints Kathleen Kennedy boss of the show, and a new order of Star Wars begins. In The Force Awakens Kylo Ren and the First Order come to Tokodana, looking for BB-8, Solo, Rey and Finn. When Ren arrives in grandiose style his First Order smash Mazs castle to rubble, as the aforementioned flags get crushed and burned. This symbolises the old being swept away for the new, Darth Vader and the Empire to Kylo Ren and the First Order,..Lucasfilm to Disney,..and from George Lucas to Kathleen Kennedy. It symbolised the end of something that myself and every Star Wars fan held dear, and ushered in a new era of Star Wars that killed my favourite characters,..had glaring plot holes, recycled plots and characters, and met some terrible criticism for its crappy dialogue and unoriginal storylines. When Mazs Castle fell it took with it the last of the old respected lore, and completely set the agenda of one person which nearly killed the franchise. I can just imagine Kathleen cackling quietly to herself on premiere night of episode 7, as the First Order completely destroyed Mazs, then grinning like Palpatine when he overthrew the Jedi.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is the future of Admiral Ackbar's character in the Star Wars franchise?
Answer: Admiral Ackbar sadly doesn't have a future in the Star Wars franchise because he was killed in The Last Jedi. In 34 ABY Princess Leia convinced Ackbar to come out of retirement, to help the Resistance fight the ever growing threat from the First Order. When the Resistance was evacuating from D'Qar he was aboard the bridge of their flagship, the Raddus, when Kylo Ren and his wingmen opened up on the Resistance ship. Admiral Ackbar was killed in the ensuing explosion, along with every other Resistance officer on the bridge, ..except for the Princess herself. Admiral Ackbar was one of the greatest assets the Rebel Alliance, and then the Resistance, ever had, and he valiantly served them for more than 60 years. He was instrumental in coordinating attacks on the second Death Star, finally bringing the Empire down at Jakku,..and years later he was critical in destroying Starkiller Base. His tactical genius and military planning was what literally saved the lives of untold billions throughout his career, and when he died an enormous statue was erected in his honour. This statue was on Mon Cala, and even though his body was never retrieved from the dark vacuum of space..his incredible life and astonishing achievements were remembered, by way of this statue in the great undersea memorial known as The Mourning Shrines. After the Battle of Crait Princess Leia and Gial Ackbars son, Aftab, dive down to the vast memorial to pay their final respects to the admiral.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: In Star Wars, what would happen if Darth Nihilus encountered Darth Vader or Emperor Palpatine and tried to consume them to feed his hunger?
Answer: Darth Nihilus was an absolute beast, but not as powerful as some may think. Yes, he became a wound in the force, capable of draining the living force from an entire planet, he wielded extremely powerful red force lightning, and his very presence felt like death itself. But ‘The Lord of Hunger’ never met Darth Sidious or his prodigy, Darth Vader. Palpatine and Skywalkers fates and legacies were inexorably intertwined, and both shared a strong connection as master and apprentice, but alone..each of these powerhouses in the force should be enough to stop Darth Nihilus in his tracks. Darth Sidious himself was enough to extinguish Nihilus, but what would happen if Nihilus tried to feed off Sidious? Sidious was steeped in the knowledge of the darkside, and one of the most powerful Sith Lords to ever exist. His extensive experience, knowledge and power in the darkside would surpass his opponents, and in canon his force lightning is the most powerful of the Sith Lords. If Nihilus tried to feed off Sidious I'm assuming that Palpatine will take it as a deep, personal insult, a threat to his power,..and act accordingly. Darth Nihilus was controlled by the force, not the other way around,..and his spirit was just along for the ride. He was consumed by it after surviving the effects of the Mass Shadow Generator superweapon, and from there his tangible body was completely obliterated over time, leaving him with no other option but to call upon the force itself to hold his spirit together and contain it within his mask and robes. Sidious could use his devastating lightning to flash fry Nihilus if he caught him off guard, but there would be no coerceing, convincing or persuading Nihilus to bow. He was the embodiment of the darkside, but Sidious's control over it, and his power of foresight, give him the advantage here. Vaders go to move is his signature force choke, but seeing as how Nihilus has no physical body to speak of, Vaders reach may not have an affect on the Lord of Hunger. But this would only enrage and empower The Chosen One, pushing him to call upon the force to unleash his fury. Vader could not wield force lightning, but he could create a powerful force barrier, capable of repelling almost anything. He was devastating with force crush, and could use this ability to implode Nihilus’ mask, and mangle his form into burnt embers on the wind,..but Vader relishes in having the last word, the final triumphant sneer at his downed opponent. Palpatine taught him about other Sith Lords in order to learn from their achievements, and their mistakes..and most likely Vader gleamed all he could from his masters teachings. After all, he was long prophesied to bring balance to the force, and his life couldn't end until he had achieved this purpose. Nihilus would fall to Vader, just like all the Jedi he had slaughtered,..just like Count Dooku,..and just like his own master in good time.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What are the most important things that a clone trooper has?
Answer: Besides having the genes of the galaxys most impressive bounty hunter a clone trooper has something in their arsenal that has proven invaluable time and time again. I'm talking about a clone troopers sidearm;..the DC-17 hand blaster pistol, and the DC-17S. This heavy blaster pistol was one of the most reliable, durable and accurate blasters ever produced in the Star Wars Universe. It is based on the real world M1911 Colt pistol, which was made famous during the Vietnam War. Manufactured by Blastech Industries, the DC-17 was small, compact, lightweight and had a capacity of 50 shots. For its size it was a highly effective weapon with impressive stopping power, suited for close quarters combat, yet also highly efficient at ranged combat. It was designated as a backup weapon, but proved to be far more effective wielded as a pair;..in the right hands. Clone captains and commanders, especially ARC troopers and high ranking officers were usually issued these blasters, like Captains Rex and Fordo, Doom, Fox and many other clones in the Grand Army of the Republic. Rex was highly effective using twin blasters, and on many occasions they saved his and many other lives. Without them his kill count would have been significantly less, and his proficiency with them made him and others that used them heroes on the battlefield. One or two captains or commanders brandishing twin DC-17's could turn the tide in a heated battle, and many times the Jedi have been saved by clones using these blasters. Unlike its predecessor, the DC-15S, the DC-17, and the suppressed version being the DC-17S, were far more powerful blasters with a higher rate of fire, and lower recoil. This weapon was one of the most import pieces of kit that a clonetrooper could ever have.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why is the title "Darth" used in Star Wars instead of just "Vader" or "Lord Vader"?
Answer: Because the title ‘Darth’ was from the time of Darth Andeddu, an extremely powerful and very wise Sith Lord who reigned for hundreds of years, and eventually worshipped as a God King. Before Andeddu the title was simply ‘Sith Lord’, and a very powerful Sith Lord was called a ‘Dark Lord’. But after Darth Andeddu arrived on the scene those titles were rescinded in the Sith Order, and replaced with the more grandiose title of ‘Darth’. Andeddu was born thousands of years before the Empire was even a twinkling in Palpatines eye, and his spirit was eventually destroyed in 137 ABY. He accumulated vast, extensive archives on all the Sith lore he could possibly get his hands on. All this incredible knowledge was stored in a holocron of his own devising, and so the other Sith plotted against him believing he was coveting tremendous power. Eventually his Sith brothers betrayed him, and he fled to his homeworld of Prakith, to an impregnable fortress where no one could reach him. Here he ruled unchallenged and was believed by the locals to be a god. To them he was known as ‘The Immortal God King of Prakith’, and for centuries he sat as supreme ruler of the planet. From here it is believed he created the more fitting title of ‘Darth’ for himself, and every other Sith Lord after his reign. He also discovered a way to transfer his consciousness into another being after death, which was the secret power that Andeddu had kept to himself. Darth Bane found Andeddus coveted holocron many centuries later, and believed that the title of Darth held a position of power and authority. From Darth Andeddus reign, all the way up to Darth Bane, the title began to establish itself, and in time instil fear, terror and tremendous respect to all who heard it. From Star Wars: Book of Sith we also learn that Darth Bane believed that the title was only reserved for the worthy, and after he also established ‘The Rule of Two’ the title of ‘Darth’ held more reverence and meaning. From the time of Bane up until the end of Palpatine and Vaders reign the rule of two was loosely adhered to by most Sith Lords…but the title of ‘Darth’ would always remain constant.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who is the most powerful female Sith Lord in the Star Wars universe? Is she more powerful than Palpatine?
Answer: There were more female Sith Lords than we first think, with; Darth Shaa, Lumiya, Darth Cognus, Darth Zash, Vestara Khai, Darth Lachris, Tahira Veila, Darth Nyriss, Olaris Rhea, Darth Talon, Darth Atroxa, Darth Zannah, Visas Marr, Darth Maladi, Exal Kressh, and Darth Traya to name but a fraction of the more powerful, and even obscure and mysterious Sith Ladies. But of all the incredible female Sith Ladies in the Star Wars Universe which one is the most powerful, and could she defeat the mighty Darth Sidious? Her name was the last one on the above list; Darth Traya. This female Lady of the Sith is reported to have been the most powerful female Sith to have ever lived, and there is a lot of evidence regarding her abilities that suggests she could have defeated Palpatine. Originally a very powerful Jedi Master and galactic historian, Kreia, as she was known before succumbing to the darkside, was the master of Revan. After he turned to the darkside and committed crimes against the Order Kreia was banished from the Jedi for failing Darth Revan. This is when she steeped herself in the darkside, and became something else entirely. Besides Revan, she was master to such incredibly powerful apprentices as Darth Sion, Meetra Surik, and the Lord of Hunger himself, Darth Nihilus. Her immense power in the force made her one of the most frightening, most prodigious, and most skilled force users; being able to use a wide arsenal of powerful force abilities, including; Force Speed, Force Crush, Force Lightning, Force Scream, Force Cloak, Force Horror, Force Choke, Energy Resistance, and a powerful version of the mind trick. She was so knowledgeable and powerful in the force that she could manipulate it to control animals and creatures, and even a more obscure force ability called Force channel. She was one of the most powerful force healers, and could manipulate a counter ability of it called Dark Healing. She used this to simultaneously kill dozens of Sith assassins on Malachor V. Darth Traya was one of the more powerful force wielders who could manipulate the rare ability called Shatterpoint, where the practitioner can actually glimpse events in the future. Before she died Traya accurately predicted the death of Jango Fett at the hands of Mace Windu…more than 4000 years before it happened. This ability would allow her to predict Sidious’ moves in advance and plan accordingly. She could also telepathically communicate over many light years of distance, and was a master at Breath Control..which made her virtually immune to most poisons and lethal gases. In combat she could wield three lightsabers simultaneously, with each one independently fighting with a ferocious will all of its own. She could literally get inside your head, fill it full of doubt, confusion and terrible fear…and even modify your memories to make you believe that she never even existed. I could keep going on and on about her unfathomably incredible powers, but in short;..Yes,..yes she could kick Palpatines wrinkly old posterior from Coruscant to the Outer Rim.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did Darth Vader ever remove his mask for reasons other than needing to breathe?
Answer: Besides removing his helmet in his private meditation chamber, and meditating in his bacta tank on Mustafar,..Darth Vader didn't have any other reason to remove his helmet. It was virtually impossible for Vader to breathe without the aid of his mask and life support systems. His meditation chamber, known as the Qabbrat, allowed him to survive without the mask because once the chamber was hermetically sealed it worked by combining high pressure, and sterilised hyper oxygen. Together the combination allowed Vader to breathe freely without the annoying and cumbersome restraints of his mask and helmet. The original chamber was stolen by a Rebel cell on Murkhana, and Vader used its tracking node to run down the thieves before they jettisoned it out into space. He had exact replicas created for his Venator class Star Destroyer, the Executor, and at Fortress Vader on Mustafar. It was more that Vader had a problem with Jedi, and secret apprentices, trying to remove his helmet on him. Firstly his former master, Obi Wan Kenobi, removes a portion of Vaders mask during their heated reunion,..and then his former apprentice Ahsoka Tano does exactly the same thing on Malachor;..only on the opposite side of the mask that time! In Legends Vader has a secret apprentice, named Galen Marek (aka Starkiller), who Vader took from Kashyyyk after killing his Jedi father. Eventually Marek turns on Vader, and they have an epic confrontation in the enormous cloning facilities on Kamino. During the fight Starkiller hurled an energy field generator straight at Vaders head. This resulted in most of his mask and helmet being completely destroyed,..along with large portions of vaders suit..and left his prosthetics scarred and exposed.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who was the most unusual Sith Lord in the Star Wars Galaxy?
Answer: Darth Caldoth wasn't unusual in appearance, but what he did to his scheming apprentice was unusual, in that Caldoth had a diabolical counterattack prepared..which we'll get to in a moment. Darth Caldoth was a Duros Sith Lord, the same species as Cad Bane, and he was unusually powerful in the art of Sith Alchemy; and it's believed he used his unique darkside abilities to create Sith Warbeasts. Sith had created Warbeasts for centuries before the rise of Darth Caldoth, but it seems he was the first to write a complete, comprehensive compendium. He wrote a controversial book on Sith Warbeasts in 1032 BBY called ‘The Beastiary of Darth Caldoth’, which described creatures such as the Veergundark, the Tuk’ata, the Krastenane, and the Silooth. It was something akin to a Lovecraftian compendium of nightmarish Sith creatures, that it was rumoured Darth Caldoth could create using ancient Sith Alchemy. Eventually many years after Caldoths demise, his creepy encyclopaedia of creatures, and the alchemy behind their creation, fell into the hands of Jedi Master Count Dooku, Master Lene Costana, and Master Sifo Dyas;..after taking it from the Jedi archives. It was securely locked away in the bowels of the temple archives because of the tremendous risk it posed. Costana stole a fragment of the cursed book, and tried to unwittingly get Dooku and Dyas to translate it. After quarrelling occurred amongst Dooku and Costana it eventuated into a heated lightsaber duel, quashed by Yoda after realising the dark origin of the disturbance. Dooku even suspected Costana of being a Sith Lord, and eventually Yoda demanded the fragment returned immediately. Yoda was actually angered by Costanas hidden motives, because of something he knew about Caldoths book..that the Jedi didn't; something dangerous enough for the book to be kept under guard. It is revealed in ‘Star Wars: Book of Sith’ 2012 that the Jedi Council had strictly forbidden living alchemy, seeing it as “an affront to the living force.” Now, back to Darth Caldoth, and his apprentice Ry Nymbis. In traditional Sith custom Nymbis plotted to kill his master, and tried to use his own Sith Alchemy against him. Nymbis stole an alchemical ritual and the materials needed from Caldoths library, and planned to use it against him. Darth Caldoth became aware of this treachery and cleverly changed the words to Nymbis’ ritual in advance. Ultimately Nymbis was going to turn his master into stone using the ritual, but it backfired horribly,..and left Nymbis frozen in stone. The effects of the alchemy left Caldoths foolish apprentice trapped in an eternal nightmare which he could never awaken from. Darth Caldoth also tried experimenting with a Nightsister burial pod, and eventually trapped the spirit of a Nightsister called Zeldin in his mind. In Caldoths mind the witch was imprisoned in a cage, and after her eternal incarceration Caldoth would only remember her spirit on rare occasions. Source; ‘Book of Sith’ 2012,..and Wookiepedia; Darth Caldoth and Ry Nymbis

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What are some other aspects of Dathomir and its culture that have been explored in Star Wars Canon?
Answer: Dathomir is even more terrifying and mysterious than we first imagined. Throughout the galaxy whispers are heard whenever someone mentions the planet Dathomir. It is shrouded in superstition and the darkside, and teaming with brutal, voracious lifeforms that makes the local fauna on Dagobah look cute and cuddly. One of these nightmarish creatures is the Rancor, which is native to the planet,..giving Dathomir the nickname “Rancor Planet”. The witches here long ago tamed the creatures, and rode them as mounts in battle. Other more nightmarish creatures on Dathomir that wanted to feast on your decaying corpse were; the Bane Back Spider, which was enormous, and spat lethal venom at its quarry and spewed acid when killed.. ,..large, brutish bipedal predators known as Nydaks.. ,..and the mighty Chrirodactyl; which was essentially a gargantuan bat. One of the largest of the species was Gorgara, also known to the locals as “The Winged Daemon of the Canyon”. Another mysterious creature, which was crucial to the Nightsister Magicks was ‘The Sleeper’, which lived deep in the dark blue waters of the Nightsisters lair. It was essential to Nightsister magicks because it created “an ingredient vital in ‘The Water of Life’”. All these gruesome creatures existed under Dathomirs crimson glowing sun named Domir, which bathed the entire planet in a blood red glow. Dathomir was first exposed to the darkside by a technologically advanced species called the Zeffonians, who were lead by a twisted and psychotic sage named Kujet. He built a large ominous palace deep within the forests, and here he introduced Dathomir to the darkside. He massacred untold numbers of his enemies, and had them murdered and thrown into an extremely deep pit beneath his throne room. Ultimately the Zeffonians abandoned Dathomir, but irrevocably stained the planet with the taint of the darkside. It's been said that an exiled Jedi named Allyah was dumped on Dathomir in 600 BBY. At the time the Republic used Dathomir to transfer and leave its more “troubled” prisoners and criminals,..and Allyah was supposedly one such criminal. She was exiled to the mysterious planet, and taught the witches how to manipulate the force and all the intricacies involved with it,..and ultimately began the legacy of the Nightsisters of Dathomir. This is despite the fact that their was never any record at the Jedi Temple on Coruscant of a rogue Jedi named Allyah, and there were also conflicting reports from the Nightsisters themselves about the origins of their coven. Years later during the aftermath of Order 66 another Jedi came to the planet, named Taron Malicos. He fell to the strong, evil temptations of the planets emanating darkside, and eventually ended up becoming the leader of the Nightbrothers.. after murdering their leader, Brother Viscus. From within the abandoned Nightsister lair, Maul controlled his expansive crime syndicate Crimson Dawn, and it was from here the dark saber found its path back into the hands of the Mandalorians. Maul also summoned his new minion, Qi'ra, to Dathomir..explaining the Rule of Two,..and later Maul, accompanied by Ezra Bridger, would evoke the spirits of the Nightsisters to find the location of Mauls nemesis…Kenobi! There was also a hidden room within the Nightsister Fortress, that was home to the coven elder, Daka. This powerful witch could even use her magicks to summon the army of the undead. Ultimately it was determined that the Nightsisters.. “..had enough magick and technology to reproduce without the necessity of the Nightbrothers”. Source; ‘Star Wars:The Dark Side’ 2018 Tricia Barr, Wookiepedia- Dathomir, and Nightsisters.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Could Anakin defeat both Dooku and Grievous at once?
Answer: If Grievous had joined the duel on board the Invisible Hand, especially after Dooku had dealt with Kenobi, then I think that the tables would have been turned against ‘The Chosen One’ Anakin Skywalker. During the duel that eventuated between Dooku and Skywalker the Count held his own until he made one mistake, then lost his head for being so supremely overconfident. But had the Count faced Skywalker with General Grievous at his back then the odds start working against the champion of the Jedi. Grievous was instructed in saber combat by Dooku, and taught each lightsaber form as part of his training. He had also never fought the Jedi Skywalker before, but in conjunction with his commander fighting next to him the Kaleesh Warlord, and the Count from Serenno could end Anakin's career; especially if he became complacent. During the Clone Wars Skywalker beat Dooku fair and square, with Dooku not realising that he was feeding Anakin's negative emotions..which actually empowered him. It wasn't until he transformed into Vader that he could wholly embrace the darkside and his growing abilities. But when he faced Dooku alone he was conflicted and off balance within the force. Despite ending Dookus life there was much turmoil brewing within the young man. Had Dooku and Grievous taken him on simultaneously they may have been enough to throw him completely off balance, and distract him enough to land one crucial strike. But then again, if they provoked Anakin enough he had the ability to summon incredible power. The time Anakin controlled both the Son and the Daughter on Mortis is testimony to his immense skill in the force, and probably enough for him to best both the Count and the good general. But Dooku and Grievous were unpredictable whirlwinds of chaos and incredible anger. The cool demeanor of Dooku, combined with the psychotic fury of Grievous, would be more than enough to exterminate any normal lone Jedi,…but as we know, Anakin was more than just a normal Jedi.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How does Chewbacca’s Clone Wars appearance hint at his strange past?
Answer: When we first meet Chewbacca in season three of ‘The Clone Wars’ he has been taken prisoner by Garnac, a Trandoshan chief who lead a ruthless Hunting Guild. Chewie was taken to the Trandoshan planet Wasskah, specifically Island Four, where he and other captives were to be cruelly hunted as sport. What the writers of TCW were hinting at here is the long established hatred, a blood fued, amongst the two species. Trandoshans are vicious slavers, hunting and killing prey is a huge part of their brutal culture and customs. Wookiees were prized not only as slaves, but for the challenge they presented in the hunt. Wookiee pelts and furs were also coveted by the bloodthirsty Trandoshans, as seen at Garnacs hunting lodge, and in The Book of Boba Fett. Before his debut in TCW most of Chewbaccas early past still remains a mystery. In Canon its stated he was born on Kashyyyk, in the Wookiee city of Rwookrrorro, 180 years before the Clone Wars even started. This is during the High Republic Era. He was even married to his love, Mallatobuck, and also had a son called Lumpawarroo. But after this, in canon lore, not much is known until he meets Ahsoka, and the other young Jedi on Wasskah many years later. Prior to being captured by Garnac and his crew canon states that he was also a combat engineer, defending the Republic and Kashyyyk. His role as a military engineer may give us a hints or clues suggesting that his proficiency at starship repair and piloting may stem from his days serving with the Wookiees defending Kashyyyk;..long before we see him serving again with his brothers during Revenge of the Sith, and even many more years again after that against The First Order. Source; Chewbacca : Wookiepedia.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What annoys you about the Star Wars sequels?
Answer: One thing that Disney did to the sequel trilogy, that annoyed the crap out of me was the fact that they ditched a load of old alien species that we were all familiar with, and replaced them with their own new aliens and creatures. Maz Kanatas Castle on Tokadana for example is loaded with new alien species to the point where I didn't even recognise a single one! How can we have 6 episodes of the saga lined with alien species that are common in our minds, and then begin the sequel trilogy full of new species we've never seen before. Sure, a few new species here and there wouldn't be uncommon, but if you completely replace them then there's something deeply wrong with the folks who created the sequel trilogy. Take the scenes at the Casino on Canto Bight as another example. As you scan your eyes around the bustling crowd on the casino floor you can't help but notice that they're nearly all new editions to the saga. The only species I thought I could identify was the table attendant, with his tiny little croupiers outfit on, who I first thought was a Zilken like Colonel Meebur Gascon from The Clone Wars,..but as it turned out he was another new addition as well;..a Troglof to be specific. Almost every other character, besides an Ithorian I think I spotted, is of a species unfamiliar to the saga at the time, which to myself doesn't make a lot of sense. Why isn't there one familiar species, besides humans, that we can identify in these two immense scenes full of characters? Don't get me wrong, I enjoy the addition of some of the new alien species and characters, as they continue with the charm of Star Wars and new species being introduced,..but I feel that had Disney included more of the common and familiar species we know then it possibly could have added more value, charm and credibility to the film. Later productions like Solo, Rogue One, The Mandalorian, and Kenobi were more successful in this regard, with the inclusion of species like Twi'leks, Gamorreans, Rodians, Pau’ans, Trandoshans, Ithorians and even Jawas by the truck load. They even had familiar characters and cameos. But in the sequels I feel they went overboard on bringing new too many new species into the saga, without including some of our favourites to add more appeal. Look, my gripe is small compared with most other people's opinions on the sequels;..but I guess when I look at the bigger picture, like killing off my beloved Admiral Ackbar,..and some of the dialogue like “Palpatine somehow returned” didn't do the sequel trilogy justice neither.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did Darth Vader have any friends or did he hate everyone?
Answer: It's not like he was an easy guy to get along with. He pretty much hated everyone in general, but there were several individuals that the Sith Lord had a good working rapport with. You see, there were two sides to Vaders close circle of those who he had confidence in. There was ‘work hours Vader, and there was ‘free time Vader’, and each had their own level of trust and commitment. When Vader was at work there were very few officers and troopers that he had faith in. Grand Moff Tarkin and Vader had been close acquaintances during the Clone Wars, and this courtesy extended beyond the Republic and into the Empire. Tarkins methods and opinions were close to Vaders own, so they had a good working relationship; especially seeing as how Tarkin actually outranked him. Palpatine told Vader that he could deal with any Imperial officer how he felt fit, except for Tarkin; he needed him. Vader didn't have a problem with that. General Maximilian Veers was one of the only few officers that Vader had trust in to lead, as well as Admiral Piett, and Wolf Yularen who served him during the days of the Republic and the Empire. There were also several lower ranking officers that Vader had an inkling of respect for, like this guy from A New Hope.. Then there was ‘free time Vader’. Usually any free time Vader had he would spend it at his fortress on Mustafar, or in various other, non work related activities. His attendant and servant, Vanee, was once an Imperial officer himself, but succumbed to the evil and toxic gases emanating from Vaders castle. He served the Empire as an Imperial Inspector, sent to Mustafar to determine why several stormtroopers in the garrison stationed there had gone insane. After becoming insane from the lava fumes Vanee bowed the knee to Vader, and became his personal attendant. He was responsible for ensuring the safety and comfort of his master while Vader was at home, and Vader even trusted him enough to torture one of his captives for months, for breaking into the castle,..and once Vader even rescued him from marauding Mustafarians locals.
