He cared about him enough not to allow him to be killed by any interlopers, though eventually Vanee pissed off Vader once to the point that the Sith Lord locked him in the castles dungeons. Another one of Vaders close confidantes was Dr Chelli Lona Aphra;..a rogue archaeologist who was hired by Vader on many different occasions. Aphras father was once a scholar obsessed with Jedi lore, but a young Chelli paid more attention to the Sith literature that he had. Eventually her intelligence, skills and knowledge impressed the dark lord and he hired her to assist him on missions to locations like Geonosis, Naboo, the Anthan System, and worlds in the Outer Rim. Vader cared about her enough to protect her, using a force barrier, during a massive explosion and raining debris and rubble. Although Aphra eventually had a falling out with the Sith Lord, whom she idolised..and had to fake her death just to evade him. Vader had a bit of a problem with pushing people away.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What was the reason behind the Kaminoans creating clone troopers?
Answer: The Kaminoans were businessmen, specialising in making clones. This was what they did. The amphibious locals of Kamino had been pioneers in cloning and genetic engineering, ever since the end of an ice age that forced them to abandon their homes and live in enormous domed cities high above their flooded world. They were known to be extreme isolationists, and kept to themselves, but only to conduct business if it was profitable. They adapted their own genetic code in order to survive the great cataclysm of their world, and in doing so became experts in the field of cloning. They created clones and related technology for various clients across the galaxy, and those that knew of their business ventures, like Dexter Jettster, were aware that you had to be very financially secure to conduct said business with them. After taking the order from the Jedi, for a clone army for the Grand Army of the Republic, the Kaminoans considered the clonetroopers to be their most triumphant achievement. They had recieved the genetic material for the clone template from a bounty hunter named Jango Fett, who had been chosen because of his incredible proficiency in combat and despatching Jedi. After the first 200,000 clones had reached maturity Fett stayed on board with the Kaminoans, and assisted them with training the first generation of ARC troopers at Tipoca City. The Kaminoans played a crucial role in ensuring security for the planets of the Republic with their clone troopers, and recognised that their crowning achievement had been pivotal in opposing the onslaught of the Separatist Alliance. Kamino wasn't the only planet that had clone producing facilities, with a previous facility on Bora Vio being maintained until the major production facility on Kamino was established. The reason behind creating the clonetroopers for the Jedi was strictly business,..until the Empire had no further use for doing business between them; and terminated all existing and future contracts with the Kaminoans.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What was the worst Republic defeat in The Clone Wars?
Answer: The ‘Malevolence Campaign’. During the Clone Wars the Separatist Alliance created a superweapon capable of destroying entire fleets of Venator class Star Destroyers;..and this is exactly what Count Dooku and General Grievous did. Before the completion of The Malevolence the Republic Navy had never seen destruction and devastation on the scale that General Grievous’ new flagship could bring. The campaign itself would span for several months, and by the end of it the Republic Navy had suffered the loss of tens of thousands of clone lives. The Fourth Fleet was left almost completely destroyed, entailing the navy's worst cumulative loss of the war to date. The most disturbing thing about the Malevolence was that it's twin ion cannons left no survivors after an attack. For months the enormous Subjugator-Class Heavy Cruiser stalked the cold reaches of space, annihilating every single witness she encountered. Each time she obliterated a Venator class destroyer she would not only cripple the ship, leave it defenceless and without means of communication..but massacre its entire complement of over 7,500 clonetroopers aboard. Each Republic destroyer and each fleet completely disappeared without trace for months, instilling tremendous fear amongst the Republic Navy and all her personnel. Grievous was in control of the most deadly ship the Clone Wars had produced at this point in time, and it's continuing existence was a massive threat to the Republic. After the Battle of the Phu System the Jedi sent Council member Plo Koon to ascertain the Malevolences position; and after the ensuing Battle of Abregado it's existence and location were confirmed. But before Skywalker could destroy it Grievous’ superweapon had laid waste to a considerable portion of the Republics fleets. It's silent, almost invisible nature, the unbelievable destruction it could wreak..and the way it eliminated any survivors was its key to creating panic, widespread fear and incredible chaos. The Malevolence was the very testbed for the Subjugator-Class destroyer, and laid the foundation for this type of gargantuan vessel. It did not fail..and before it's untimely demise the Malevolence, with Grievous at the helm, taught the Republic the value of loss on a tremendous scale.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who is the most cruel Sith in Star Wars?
Answer: It is a close tie between Lord Momin and Darth Nihilus. These two each had their own “unique” way of being cruel, sometimes on the level of a depraved psychopath,..all the way up to a cruel, genocidal monster. By the time both of these insanely ruthless and bloodthirsty Sith Lords were defeated they had committed unspeakable acts of cruelty and viciousness, snuffed out the lives of millions of innocents,..and upon their deaths their evil spirits lingered on in their masks. The mark they each made on the galaxy was profoundly disturbing, and each Sith Lords name epitomised the word cruelty and destruction. Darth Nihilus was a wound in the force, so powerful that he developed a hunger for the living force energy found in every single being. He drained the life force from entire planets, cruelly killing every single soul on multiple planets. His level of destruction was absolutely phenomenal,..he drained the very life from everyone around him,. when he spoke it physically hurt to hear his voice,..and he was so consumed by the darkside that he had to call upon it to keep the fabric of his very spirit held together. He existed solely to feast on every living being in the galaxy, and it was the absolute lack of emotion, pity or remorse that made him just like Darth Momin. Darth Momin was evil and cruelty incarnate. From a young age Momin began creating bizarre, and horrific artworks..sculpted from death and decay. Momin was a pure psychopath, and tortured creatures to appease his cruel tendencies. Everyone who viewed his ‘masterpieces’ were disgusted, disturbed and reviled in horror at what they were actually witnessing! These acts lead him to become incarcerated for his crimes. From there he only got worse, after the female Sith Lord Darth Shaa began instructing him in the darkside. He ultimately killed his master and developed a weapon of mass destruction, capable of destroying an entire city;..and leaving them frozen like statues, with the expression of sheer pain etched in their faces for an eternity. Yeah, I know Nihilus claimed the lives of millions,..but Momin was the very definition of the word ‘cruelty’. Even Darth Vader came to him for advice!

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What was the reason for Yoda's hatred towards Palpatine? Was it solely because he was a Sith or were there other factors involved?
Answer: Yoda didn't have hatred towards Palpatine, it was the fact that a Sith Lord usurped the Republic from straight under the noses of the Jedi, and then turned the Grand Army of the Republic against the Jedi Order. Yoda would have recollected several instances where he could have stopped Palpatine, or at least hindered his plans during the Clone Wars,..but also Yoda would come to the very stark realisation that Darth Sidious was more intelligent and far more powerful than he was. It wasn't hatred, it wasn't jealousy..it was utter humiliation that Yoda felt. Yoda would also have a degree of remorse for the times he let Palpatine control his devious plans. He should have realised when Kenobi returned from Kamino, with news of an army created under the authorisation of a senior Jedi Master that something wasn't right. It was Yoda who personally went to Kamino, and basically took possession of Sifo Dyas’ order;..which was another time Sidious pulled the wool over his eyes. But the Sith Lord had left him with no opportunity. This decision of Yodas would haunt him forever. Yoda would have regretted allowing Kenobi to train Skywalker, despite warning the council in the dangers of training the boy. There were so many times he should have acted differently. All that time on Dagobah gave Yoda years to reflect, and think of his huge role in the failure of the Jedi Order. Hindsight can be a very terrible thing, and I assume that Yoda would have thought of all the different times that had he acted he could have averted the destruction of the Jedi Order;..and the enslavement of the galaxy at large to a maniacal dictator. Hatred isn't a part of him, as he teaches us what dangers lay behind this emotion, especially if a Jedi is to walk down the path of hatred. He knew that this is what happened to Skywalker, and he knew that Sidious would have taken extreme advantage of Anakins vulnerabilities. He would have felt foolish and ignorant of the fact that Sidious played everyone,..and especially for fooling..and defeating the Grand Master of the Jedi.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did Darth Plagueis torture Palpatine?
Answer: Yes,..he tortured Sidious nearly to the point of death, in the EU novel ‘Darth Plagueis’. During Sidious’ tutelage under Darth Plagueis the master takes the apprentice to the frozen, inhospitable world of Mygeeto. As they begin a lesson in overcoming physical restrictions Plagueis tells Palpatine how from the age of eight he could go outside in the most harshest of conditions. Over time he had adapted to survive almost anywhere, thanks to his wisdom of the darkside. He tells Palpatine that his blood is near frozen, and that he won't survive long on Mygeeto without overcoming what it takes to survive the worst conditions imaginable. He gets Palpatine to recount the tale of how he killed his parents, family and even all the guards aboard their family starcruiser; getting him to describe it in graphic, gory detail. He wanted Sidious to gain authority over his terrible memories and use it to empower him even further in the darkside. But during this time Palpatine tries to agree with his master, in a bid to escape the paralysing cold..and then Plagueis tells him this; after tearing open his thin environmental protection suit.. “I am your torturer, Sidious. Soon you will make every effort to appease me, and with each lie you tell, with each attempt you make to reverse our roles, you will make yourself as shiny as an Aurodium coin to the darkside. So appease me, Sidious. Tell me again how you killed them.” Plagueis then sits atop a tall cliff face, as he watches a frantic Sidious climbing beneath him,..attempting to reach his master at the top. Sidious is utterly frozen, bloodied, bruised and very near to the point of death. His master kept him here for an extended period,..several days in fact, and even deprived him of food and water. Plagueis then tells Sidious that they need to abandon the philosophy that Darth Bane set forward, and instead rely and trust in each other; and essentially to not adhere to the Rule of Two. “If you don't already want to murder me, you will before the time I'm through with you.” says Plagueis to a Sidious who is seething with pain and anger. He was trying to get his apprentice to use his hatred towards his master, and channel it into the darkside, thus allowing him to achieve what he first thought impossible. But during his many torturous days on the frozen hell of Mygeeto Darth Plagueis taunted, laughed..and even used the force to humiliate and anger his apprentice. There were many times when Plagueis allowed Sidious to try to scramble to the top, where he was perched, and many times Plagueis allowed Sidious to fall straight on his face, and tumbling back to the bottom of the jagged rocks beneath. By the time Plagueis was done with his apprentice Palpatine was covered in cuts and bruises, and went through one of the most torturous periods of his apprenticeship to Darth Plagueis the Wise. Source; ‘Darth Plagueis’ James Luceno, pages 182–188

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who would win, an FX medical droid or Droideka?
Answer: The Droideka mops the floor with the FX series medical droid. Droidekas are classified as Battle Droids, and the FX Med-Droid is classified as a…well, Medical Droid. This is a no brainer situation, as the Droideka has been programmed to kill opponents as skillful as a Jedi Knight. The FX droid is only programmed for medical and surgical purposes. It has no combat or military programming and therefore wouldn't stand more than a couple of seconds against the Droidekas. They weren't even the lead droid during surgeries and were delegated to the role of assistant. The FX-9 model assisted in Vaders life saving surgery, and the FX-9 model assisted his son Luke, recovering after a Wampa attack. Droidekas were armed with twin laser cannons, more than enough to disintegrate the medical droid. They could also reach speeds of up to 75 kph, which was also enough to send the Med-Droid catapulting off its stand. It's only weakness was a vulnerability from behind them, or slowly rolling grenades through its protective shield. I don't think the FX-model is going to be aware of its droid cousins Achilles heel in time to formulate an attack. The Droideka would finish off the FX model before the latter would even realise it was under attack. These fearsome battle droids were manufactured by the murderous Colicoids of Colla IV,..created in their own image by the Colicoid Creation Nest. They were a vicious, warlike, carnivorous species that were extremely hostile to outsiders. Eventually the Old Republic stopped sending representatives to their planet, and so this made them the perfect choice to manufacture a new breed of battle droid before the onset of the Clone Wars;..far from the prying eyes of the Republic.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did Sidious have a reason for not using Dooku to retrieve Maul after his defeat on Mandalore?
Answer: Because Maul was a loose end that he personally needed to tie up. When Darth Sidious left Maul for dead he instantly made designs on a new apprentice to completely replace his former Dathomirian disciple. Sidious personally mentioned this to Maul, telling him that since he was replaced he had become a rival. As a rival Maul was in direct opposition to Sidious now, and as such Sidious had to finally deal with Maul himself. Sending Dooku to mop up one of his failures would be beneath him, and Sidious wanted to personally see his former apprentice with his own eyes..after such a long time. This was something that Sidious handled with relative ease, as if he was toying with Maul and his brother. He knew he would be victorious upon returning to Coruscant, but Dooku was far too valuable as a pawn in the Clone Wars. He needed Dooku for the moment, to still remain as the face of the Separatist Alliance. If Maul and Savage actually managed to kill Dooku then it would slightly hinder the Sith Lords plans, whereas facing the Sons of Dathomir alone would leave Sidious to deal with his one time apprentice on his own terms. Maul was a living violation of ‘The Rule of Two’, and had to be eliminated because of it,..and because Maul was privy to some of Palpatines plans he was a liability. He also needed Maul alive to lure out Mother Talzin, and finally deal with the witch and her offspring. Dooku had an invitation to that occasion, but initially it was Sidious who had to capture Maul alive. He couldn't risk Dooku foolishly killing him, and that's essentially why he didn't need the Counts intervention on Mandalore.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who is the weakest Sith?
Answer: Maybe not a Sith, but did you catch that Inquisitor that Ahsoka Tano battled in ‘Tales of the Jedi’? This guy had it all going for him; the cool menacing helmet, flames burning poetically in the background, the dark mysterious voice with blazing red eyes, and the cool hooded cape constantly flowing in the wind, but when it came down to business this guy was all talk and no action. We first see this mysterious member of Vaders Inquisitorious in the animated series ‘Tales of the Jedi’, after he locates Ahsoka Tano in hiding..amongst a farming community on a far distant planet. Under the alias Ashla we find Ahsoka hiding out, shortly after attending the funeral for her dear friend Padme. After using the force to save a villager from being crushed, and bringing attention to herself, Ahsoka is ratted out to the Empire by an ambitious and cocky little traitor. After the Inquisitor locates the village where Ahsoka is staying, he murders the innocent townsfolk and sets their peaceful village ablaze. Then when he goes to execute the traitorous informant Ahsoka force grabs his weapon, swiftly takes it off him after he poses some more,..kicks him in the stomach, deactivates his saber..and decapitates him accordingly. This Inquisitor, albeit not a Sith in the traditional sense, was one of the weakest darkside wielders in the saga. The other Inquisitors show some degree of skill throughout Rebels and Kenobi, and even take on opponents like Kanan Jarrus, Ezra Bridger, Maul..and Ahsoka herself. They all put up far better efforts than this postulating, fake Sith,..who cowardly murders a whole village of men woman and children to stroke his ego. Then when it came down to matching blades Ahsoka doesn't even bother wasting time with the fool. She doesn't even use a lightsaber! She just dodges several crap attempts by the Inquisitor to slice her in two, then uses his own blade to swiftly end his life. Strangely though,..when Ahsoka severs his head and it lands on the ground, it turns to mist and evaporates. Canon has his death officially listed at an ‘astronomical object’…and despite his head being removed from his body..this inquisitor might make a comeback in the future, seeing as how his physical body evaporated into the wind. I was just expecting so much more from this guy, but totally let down.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How did the Jedi defend against non-magical attacks while serving as peacekeepers for the Old Republic? Did they have a specific protocol for protection, such as using shields?
Answer: A Jedi has no need for shields of any kind, as they can use the force to substitute for a physical shield. The true test for a Jedi in combat, against non force wielders or magical practitioners, is to utilise the force to block and repel such attacks as laser bursts, grenades, missiles and other lethal projectiles. To use a shield would completely undermine their abilities as a Jedi, and a true Jedi has no use for a shield. Jedi Knights are noble and honourable fighters, and training with a shield is not part of their training regime. Most seasoned Jedi are capable of blocking projectile and laser bolt attacks, to a certain degree,..and a shield would be cumbersome and possibly limit their fighting. Even a young Jedi such as Grogu, was capable of creating a force shield to block certain attacks such as flame throwers, explosions and maybe more. Vader has even demonstrated the ability to create a powerful force shield when facing the backlash of exploding debris and flames, and even as a barrier against torrents of lava and the ocean. Aayla Secura, Anakin and Yoda create one such force barrier when faced with clouds of poisonous gas on Coruscant,.. ..and Kanan Jarrus used one of these force shields to temporarily protect members of Phoenix Squadron from an impending, enormous refinery explosion. The ability to create a force barrier is something that a Jedi strives to achieve in their training, and the deployment of shields would completely defeat the purpose of practicing and training so very hard. The Old Republic was no different to any era the Jedi fought in, and the use of shields was something considered to be beneath the Order. Only in very exceptional and rare circumstances will a Jedi use a shield.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How did the Galactic Empire deal with the Umbarans when you consider how formidable they were against the Republic?
Answer: During the Clone Wars the Separatist aligned world of Umbara put up extremely fierce resistance, and proved to the 501st Legion that they weren't a people to be trifled with. Their starships and ground vehicles were revolutionary in design and efficiency, and even considered superior to Republic technology. They utilised a precious metal called Doonium to build their vessels and other technologies. Their reputation became formidable, and they claimed many clones lives in the Battle of Umbara,..which was one of the more bloody and brutal battles of the Clone Wars. But after the demise of the Republic, and the rise of the Empire, everything changed for the Umbarans. During the early days of the Galactic Empire Palpatine dealt with Umbara the same way he dealt with any worlds that opposed his reign;..and swiftly mopped up any pockets of foolish resistance on the planet. Umbara was prized within the Empire because of its vast subterranean mineral wealth, and was pillaged by the Emperor for it accordingly. Ultimately the Galactic Empire imposed a debt on the Umbarans so colossal that they had no choice but to submit, and bow to Palpatine or perish. During this time there was an initial rebellion,..that was quickly suppressed by Captain Thrawn. The Chiss Imperial Captain made an example of the leader of the insurrection, Nevil Cygni. The pirate leader, Nightswan, attempted to take over the mineral wealth of the planet, but Thrawn also shut that down in classic style, and ended any ideas of future insurrections on the shadowy world. During the Imperial reign on Umbara new pockets of Doonium were discovered, which led to the ultimate sell out of the planet. The Mining Guild moved in accordingly after the Imperial contracts were signed,..and then the last remaining wealth on Umbara was greedily exploited and absorbed into Palpatines coffers.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is your favorite Star Wars game that isn't KOTOR or Battlefront?
Answer: I enjoyed playing The Force Unleashed 1&2, as it introduced some of the best EU characters in Star Wars, and it's storyline was actually quite compelling. You play the game through the eyes of Darth Vaders secret apprentice Galen Marek. Vader gave Marek the codename Starkiller, and after pledging your allegiance to the Sith Lord you embark on a series of missions and adventures that takes you from Kashyyyk to Kamino. This is one of the most enjoyable SW experiences that I've ever had, and I have very fond memories of playing this game. It's successor, The Force Unleashed II, was an incredible SW game itself and together they made one of my most favourite memories in the saga. At the beginning you can play as Darth Vader, as he pushes his way through the forests and treetop canopies of the Wookiee warriors on Kashyyyk. This level was particularly memorable as I used Vaders lightsaber,..or the force, to grab unsuspecting Wookiees and fling them to their deaths over the bridges and platforms dotting the landscape. Vader issues Starkiller with an official Imperial pilot named Juno Eclipse, who enhances the main character and adds a degree of depth that I found fascinating. Throughout the games Starkiller falls in love with Juno, and that side story was refreshing and very emotional for a SW video game. Starkiller has some killer moves, such as using the force to send stormtroopers flying into the air, grabbing missiles midair and sending them straight back to the agressor, and even plucking an Imperial Star Destroyer out of low orbit while avoiding its lasers locked onto your position below. When you get full of rage Starkiller can use his full potential, and send waves of force lightning into the enemy. It still looks cool even all these years later! And the alternate endings have some of the coolest plot twists in any video game I've ever seen.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did Darth Maul fear Darth Vader?
Answer: Judging from his reaction to Vaders incoming approach, in Rebels, I'd say that Maul held a healthy degree of fear towards Darth Vader. Before Maul and Ezra Bridger met up on Malachor Darth Vader had already dispatched his Inquisitors to the ancient Sith Temple, built by Darth Tanis nearly 4000 years previously. Vader was more than aware of Maul thanks to Palpatine, and as for the Dathomirian he knew of Vaders tremendous powers. He knew that his former master had taken Skywalker as the apprentice that he should have become, and he knew that Vader had not only been trained by Sidious..but commanded the entire might of the Galactic Empire. Vader had been doing the bidding of Darth Sidious for over a decade and a half at this point, and would stop at nothing to not only eradicate the last remnants of the Jedi,…but annihilate any possible threat to his power. That included Maul, being Vaders predecessor, and a living violation of ‘The Rule of Two’. In Vaders eyes Maul should not exist…and Maul knew it. During the last hours of the Galactic Republic Maul knew that Darth Sidious would be taking on his new apprentice, and after the rise of the Galactic Empire Maul knew the extent of Vaders reach. He also knew that he could not survive in single combat against Vader, and that his rage was something to never provoke. He feared him for various reasons, but he feared him most because the former Sith Lord knew of the Jedi prophecy of ‘The Chosen One’. He knew what that entailed, and even in his last moments alive he had to know if Skywalker really was the prophesied bringer of balance to the force. He didn't want to stand in Vaders way, because Vader was the one man alive who could achieve what he dreamed of most;..killing Palpatine and destroying the Sith Order. Maul feared Vader because he knew if the prophecy was true there would absolutely be no stopping him; until Vader had finally stopped Sidious first. Kenobi relieved his doubts, and as Maul died he believed that the chosen one would avenge he and Kenobi both.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Can Vader sleep?
Answer: He is human after all, so yes, when the need arises Darth Vader can sleep. He doesn't lay down in a comfy bed, and sleep the traditional way, like we all do, but he does have the ability to sleep in his bacta tank at his fortress on Mustafar. Sith Lords don't really have the time to be doing a lot of sleeping anyway, but their physical bodies require time to rest and process information in their brains, gaining strength to keep them functioning properly. Darth Plagueis was rumoured to not have slept for the better part of a decade, but did require rest in his personal residence. Vader was no exception, and rarely would have slept;…but did have the benefit of the healing properties and personal solitude of his bacta tank. If Vader knew he needed some sleep, particularly after extensive periods awake and after gruelling physical missions, he could program the tank to lower his functions and put him into a sleep state. Then it was just a matter of the tank adjusting the sleep cycle to Vaders exact requirements. The Sith Lord more meditated than slept, and could use the meditation chambers he had aboard some of his his command vessels to relax..and at least sit down for a period. He could also breath without his helmet and mask on. Whereas the Bacta Tank could physically make you sleep, or even induce you into a comatose state in preparation for the Bacta to do its miraculous work. Sometimes Vader needed to do both, but the meditation chamber was more required, because Vader couldn't use the Bacta Tank at his personal residence to meditate constantly. Boba Fett, Obi-Wan Kenobi and Vader himself have all experienced the side effects of the tanks effect, by having dreams and flashbacks from their past, and often reliving traumatic memories. Boba Fett kept dreaming about his nerve wracking time inside the Sarlaac, and memories of his youth spent with his father. Kenobi relived his horrible past of watching his friend turn to the darkside, and subsequently kill children and become an angry limbless burn victim. And Vader dreamed of all the horrific things he did, and the life lessons he learnt. It seems that when the Bacta begins it healing process the tank puts the user into such a deep sleep state that they recall good and bad experiences, and memories from their life. With the healing comes the positive of having the body rejuvenated and repaired, but the negative of reliving experiences one might want to forget indefinitely.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who is the large blue Droid seen behind Anakin Skywalker in Episode 1 (Star Wars, droids, object identification, sci-fi)?
Answer: That colossal antique taking up valuable real-estate in Wattos Junk store was an R1 series Astromech,..kinda like R2-D2s grandfather! The R1 series was Industrial Automatons breakthrough into the launch of the first astromech series droids. Also known as the R1 Reactor droid this two meter tall, one legged giant had a single photoreceptor, twin manipulator arms, a holo projector;..and were the first units ever created to communicate with the language ‘droidspeak’. The particular unit in Wattos Junk store, standing behind Anakin Skywalker, was a shop keeping drone fitted out by the Jawas on Tatooine. It ran all of Wattos various transactions and business affairs, leaving the Toydarian free to conduct his gambling and other shady affairs. Jawas were quite proficient at reworking these R1 units into similar drones that Watto had in his store. One such tribe of Jawa junk dealers and scavengers tried to offload an R1-series Astromech to Owen Lars at his moisture farm. R1-G4 was practically an antique at this point in time,..and was ultimately overlooked for far more recent models, by galactic standards; R2-D2 and C-3P0. The R1 model from the “sale of the droids” scene even has its own action figure! Other R1 series models were used as security droids aboard starships, such as the ones seen in the episode ‘The Prisoner’ on ‘The Mandalorian’. The difference with these ones, such as the R1-B series, were that they had repulsorlifts instead of the standard clunky single foot. Not to say this made them more intelligent, as the Devaronian in the episode proved;..and he wasn't the sharpest knife in the drawer neither.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How did the clone troopers recognize Darth Sidious to execute Order 66?
Answer: Because his very image was ingrained into their subconsciouses, thanks to the organic chips that the Kaminoan scientists had implanted in the clones from when they were just a baby. The entire point of Order 66 was for Palpatine to gain control of the galaxy by killing the entire Jedi Order. He needed every last one of the clonetroopers, spread out all over the galaxy, to immediately obey his orders. He didn't even need them to obey all his orders,..just one. Because after that he would have assumed complete control of the galaxy, and their subservience would then come without question. It's a bit like mind control, something akin to the movie The Manchurian Candidate, where the use of mind control is used by the US Government on its own troops. Only it comes in the form of an implantable bio, inhibitor chip; most likely containing images of Palpatine in his hood, knowledge of his name being Lord Sidious, and a voice imprint containing Order 66's prime directive..that is somehow imbeded into the chip by the Kaminoan scientists. The chip is implanted from infancy and remains something more subliminal, until the ultimate command is actually given. Also contained on the chip were other orders, but only as countermeasures. Somewhere contained within the chip is the repetitive disciplinary chant..”Good soldiers follow orders.” This backup measure was most likely implemented to emphasise the importance of completing the main objective;..being the swift execution of Order 66.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What are some gross Star Wars facts?
Answer: I'll give you one gross Star Wars fact that will make you think twice. This one is from The Book of Boba Fett, and takes place out in the lonely deserts of Tatooine. As part of ones spiritual journey in local Tusken tribes a Horned Gecko is used to create hallucinations within the initiate. When Fett had earned the trust of one particular tribe on Tatooine it was his turn to recieve the blessings from the gecko,…and so it quickly burrowed its way abruptly up his nose and somehow inside him! Here it made him experience something like an acid trip, and see terrible visions from his past, and faded memories from his youth. Basically the Horned Gecko violently enters your nose..and makes you hallucinate on previous traumatic memories! And it kooked pretty intense! But none of it looked like a pleasant experience, no matter how you try and justify it. But that's not the disgusting part. The truly disgusting part is that this slimy little Gecko could have been up the nose and insides of untold other strangers…before it burrows its way up your nose and into your throat, or chest..or wherever it secretes itself until it's done making you trip balls! Fett didn't seem to realise this, but when you really think about it it's a pretty gross fact from Star Wars.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why did Emperor Palpatine not utilize both droids and clones to fight the Rebels?
Answer: Clones were phased out in favour of galactic conscription, and as for droids,..Palpatine had droids in his service to the Empire; but had one particular droid made the final cut it would have had the ability to assassinate even Mon Mothma, or Han Solo himself. The main reason why the Empire didn't use battle droids was because the Imperial Senate had banned the production and use of them, particularly after the effects that the Separatist Droid Armies left on the galaxy during the Clone Wars. But the manufacturers found a loop hole by billing them as “security droids”. They also did this by designating them as Probe Droids, Seeker Droids, Sentry Droids,..just never “Battle Droids”. Emperor Palpatines Galactic Empire had many other droids in its employ, such as the KX-series security droids, the RA-7 protocol droids,.. Imperial Probe droids,.. R4-K5 was Vaders personal astromech droid,.. the DT-series Sentry Droids,.. All versions of the Imperial Dark troopers,.. Buzz droids (because they were designated as Sabotage Droids), and even old Droidekas were reprogrammed for use by the Empire on occasion, utilised as a security droid. But the Empire could only use certain droids because of the bothersome ban imposed by the Imperial Senate. They were very limited by this, but had the Imperial Department of Military Research had its original idea implemented the fall of the Rebel Alliance would have been imminent. They were working on something that would have made even John Connor from the Terminator franchise blush. The Imperial Department of Military Research hired Simonelle and Massad Thrumble to create an infiltrator, or assassin droid, capable of crippling the upper echelons of the Rebellions military and political hierarchy. A Human Replica Droid. Previous versions had been experimented with, but nothing as grandiose and impressive as this had ever been undertaken. An impressive prototype was created, but instead the Thrumble brothers sold her to a vicious crimelord known as Prince Xixor of Black Sun. Her name was Guri, and she was absolutely everything that the Empire could have ever dreamed of. Instead she ended up in the hands of one of the galaxys most dangerous crime syndicates. Guri could pass for a human in every single way, except for her body temperature being around 10°C degrees cooler than a regular human female. She could run the entire affairs of a massive major corporation,..or snap the neck of a Rebel leader in a heartbeat. Her strength, relexes, agility, stamina, intelligence, and leadership were far more enhanced than even the strongest man, or the smartest woman in the galaxy;..and her beauty was more stunning and breathtaking than the most beautiful Queen in the galaxy. She could bend or break duranium handcuffs or bend titanium bars with ease. She was an expert and lethal marksman with a rifle, proficient with all manner and make of weapons, programmed in different martial arts and close quarters combats, and was one of the best pilots money could buy. She was like the ultimate female James Bond Terminator of Star Wars! Speaking of buying,…the Thrumble brothers sold her for 9 million credits to Prince Xixor. Maybe that was a good thing, because if the Empire ever got their hands on her they would have been able to create more,…and program them as Imperial spies and assassins to bring down the Rebel Alliance. But ironically she eventually became a mercenary for the New Republic.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why is Darth Maul considered a Sith Lord if Plagueis was alive during The Phantom Menace?
Answer: When Darth Sidious was an apprentice to Plagueis he took Maul from Mother Talzin, and trained him in secret to all but his master. Maul was trained at the Orsis Academy on Mustafar and other locations. He was deliberately chosen because of his potential in the darkside, but to serve as a mere acolyte…and not a fully fledged Sith Lord. Palpatine did have other designs on the youngster, but until the ‘Grand Plan’ was further in motion Maul would be but a servant to the Sith Lords. His role was to be an assassin, and tie up loose ends, gather intelligence and anything else Sidious so desired. Plagueis knew that his Sith Lord apprentice had an assassin to aid him with his nefarious tasks, but never did he really believe that Palpatine would turn on him, and take Maul as his own Sith apprentice. Plagueis should have known this, not just being a Sith, but especially after taking Sidious under his wing knowing that he was a psychopath;..even before he pledged himself to his teachings. Back to Mauls Sith training. The Dathomirian was subjected to some of the harshest darkside training regimes and reprimands that any one individual could undertake. Sidious taught Maul how to master the darkside, but what good was it without formal training. His instructor at the Orsis Academy was a 200 year old Falleen named Trezza, who had a good understanding with Palpatine. Below; Trezza, Mauls Falleen instructor at the Orsis Academy. Trezza said himself that he was never a fan of the Jedi, and he didn't ask a lot of questions..which Sidious liked. Here Maul learnt to fight with his hands, all the way up to sophisticated weaponry training. Coupled with his Sith training, and his time on Mustafar under the tutelage of Trezza, Maul was fashioned into Darth Sidious’ own personal weapon. He was never intended to serve as a Sith Lord,…until Palpatine carried on the rule of two, and killed Plagueis accordingly. After that Maul took on Sidious’ former position, and became a fully indoctrinated Sith Lord. Source; ‘Darth Plagueis’ James Luceno, Legends, and Trezza; Wookiepedia.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is the most dangerous animal/creature in the Star Wars Universe?
Answer: There's two creatures in the Star Wars Universe that are by far the most dangerous creatures you could find in the entire saga. One of these creatures is possibly the largest living thing in the galaxy,..and the other is small enough to fit inside your fist. They both possess the ability to destroy life on a genocidal scale, or even manipulate and control all life as we know it. The first creature is the gargantuan Summa Verminoth, of which several species exist. By far the largest version of this behemoth exists in the Akkadese Maelstrom, near Kessel. Known as ‘The Maw’ a giant black hole exists near the centre of the maelstrom, and the Summa Verminoth lives here in the unknown regions of the Si’Klaata cluster. The largest one has measured in at over 7 kilometres in length, possessing enormous tentacles big enough to engulf an entire Star Destroyer. This nightmarish space Kraken would be capable of levelling entire cities within minutes if it reached a planet like Coruscant. If left unchecked it could annihilate millions of lives, and leave untold billions worth of damage in just a day! It's mere presence alone would be enough to cause widespread pandemonium and chaos on a biblical scale, and it's carnage would leave its mark for generations. The smaller creature I've selected for most dangerous in the SWU existed on the planet of Geonosis. A Geonosian Brain Worm, classified as a parasite, is capable of entering a host and controlling it via a hive mind connected to a Queen. If enough brain worms infected the upper echelons of a military or heavy population they had the terrifying potential to invade entire planets. During the Clone Wars Republic forces discovered the existence of a “brain bug”, or Queen; known as Queen Karina of Geonosis. This horrifying monarch had the ability to control the dead, and use them at her whim. She laid the eggs which the Brain Worms hatched, and after that it took just a single worm to begin the the mind control invasion process. The only weapon against these terrifying parasitic invaders was low temperatures, which drew the worm from its host leaving it vulnerable. But the ability to wipe out entire civilisations makes these two creatures the most dangerous by far.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Which scrapped Star Wars movie scenes would have made the films better, and why?
Answer: There's a deleted scene from Revenge of the Sith that shows General Grievous kill the the great Jedi Master Shaak Ti. Another deleted scene shows Anakin Skywalker kill the Togruta Jedi, while she is meditating in her chambers during the attack on the Temple. In another version of her death it shows Anakins lightsaber kill her in a vision had by Master Yoda,..and in a fourth depiction of Skaak Ti's death she dies at the hands of Vaders secret apprentice, Starkiller, on the planet of Felucia. Shaak Ti's death was the centre of controversy for a very long time, and is still debated..although the first deleted scene, where Grievous kills her, appeared in Lucas’ first drafts for the Revenge of the Sith script. This was the earliest version of her death, although the official version is that Skywalker killed her on Coruscant, at the Jedi Temple. In Yodas vision, during the Clone Wars, Shaak Ti is murdered at the hands of Skywalkers lightsaber..and later when Vader is christened Master Ti goes into a deep meditation in her chambers. This is when Vader marches under Order 66 and slaughters her in accordance with Yodas original vision. But I don't know if I like Shaak Ti's death better at the hands of Vader or Grievous. The canon version makes sense, because when Vader first marches on the Temple he is overheard asking where Master Shaak Ti is located, and also it ties in with Yodas vision in TCW. Either way it's a blue lightsaber seen in Yodas vision so both versions slot in nicely. But then again, if it was the deleted scene where Grievous kills Ti in front of Skywalker and Kenobi it would also make sense. When Grievous abducted Palpatine on Coruscant Master Shaak Ti was in attendance with other Jedi, so it wouldn't be inappropriate for Grievous to capture and cruelly kill her;..and in front of his nemesis Kenobi too! It would also enhance General Grievous’ character somewhat by actually showing him kill more than just one Jedi canonically; which was Jedi Nahdar Vebb in the animated series. It would give Grievous another personal layer to his character, which was sorely lacking in the original theatrical release, and by adding this deleted scene it gives her death a shred more dignity;..Grievous had the decency to allow her to address Kenobi and Skywalker one last time,..whereas Vader snuck up on her like a coward while she had her eyes closed.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who would win in a fight between Darth Vader and Kylo Ren? How close would the fight be?
Answer: How close would the fight be? Surely you jest,..as the closeness of this fight would be as far as from one end of an Imperial Star Destroyer to the other! If we put aside the family feelings and just focus on each opponents strong sides Vader categorically beats his grandson on nearly every matchup. Speed and agility is about the only thing young Kylo has going for him here, because his infamous grandfather trumps everything else from strength, durability, resiliency, and sheer focus and depth in the darkside. Ren idolised his grandfather for obvious reasons;..because he was a god compared to himself. But remember the way he reacted to Rey Palpatine telling him that he was afraid;..afraid he could never be as powerful as Darth Vader? That's the difference between these two; Kylo Ren had too many conflicting emotions swirling around in his head, with fear being the most prominent. Vader did not. Vader embraced fear and basically fed off it. He was disciplined, extremely focused and despite being a little petulant, not a candle compared to Rens cock-blocked teenage outbursts. Vaders feats were legendary in comparison to Rens, despite the latter being able to bring down a mighty Zillo Beast in the comics. Vader did the same and more though, being capable of plucking massive vessels from orbit, surviving the molten hot lava of Mustafar, single handedly taking on entire platoons of the enemy, killing a Summa Verminoth, taking on Palpatine himself, and more importantly..killing Jedi. Vader was a Jedi killing nightmare and his skills in the force, both before and after falling to the darkside,..towered far above the meager talents of an angsty young boy. Disgraced former Jedi, Kazdan Paratus would have had a better chance at defeating Vader than Ren, and that cowardly little Aleena ran away from the Jedi Temple during Order 66! Vader was the chosen one, created by the force itself to bring balance back to it, and he was driven by pure rage, fury…and an anger the likes Kylo could only dream of possessing. He was a true Sith Lord, trained by the most powerful being in the entire galaxy. Ren was taught by a puppet of Palpatines own devising. I imagine if Kylo Ren could actually stand before his grandfather Vaders presence alone would be enough to instil more fear, and awe than Ren thought possible. This fight isn't even close enough to call a contest, with Vader uttering one last badass one liner.. before putting an end to Ben Solo. Never send a Knight to take out a God.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why do Imperial TIE fighters not have shields unlike Rebel X-Wings?
Answer: This all boils down to money,..and an evil Empire that showed very little regard to its minions of ‘expendable’ personnel. The TIE Fighter, and it's pilot, were basically viewed as cannon fodder to the Empire, and also very quick to be replaced. The ship itself was just a set of powerful laser canons strapped onto some giant wings, and was the standard Imperial starfighter. It's role was to swarm the enemy with sheer numbers, and this was achievable for Seinar Fleet Systems because of massive cost cuts. It didn't have any shields, a hyperdrive or even life support..and provided the pilot with the bare necessities for a combat engagement. It's twin Ls-1 laser cannons were more than enough to damage or completely destroy another starfighter, and so long as that was the case the pilots welfare was absolutely irrelevant to the Galactic Empire. Despite the lack of everything necessary a pilot needs to stay alive, like shields and life support, the TIE/LN had independent generators for the engines and weapons installed! Literally millions of these were produced for the Empire so cost cuts were absolutely necessary. This made the TIE Fighter easy to manufacture on a mass scale, they were easy to maintain, and were completely replaceable in a heartbeat. The main costs could then be diverted to producing the two main components of creating a TIE/LN Starfighter; Titanium for the hull and structure, and Quadanium steel for the solar panels. The Rebel Alliance on the other hand weren't as fortunate as the Empire with its infinite pockets. The X-Wings were not expendable, neither were their pilots.. and the Rebels had to rely on the same ship over and over;..usually until being swatted by a swarm of TIE's. After each engagement a severely damaged Rebel ship, such as the X-Wings, were patched up and repaired until that was no longer an option. They needed a hyperdrive, life support and shields to last longer than their enemy, and shields were essential in engaging the Imperial Navy. If they had none of the added extras that their TIE counterparts lacked they would be overwhelmed, and possibly destroyed on their first engagement against a squadron of TIE'S. An X-Wings hyperdrive was essential for suprise attacks and quick retreats, and helped the pilot win more combat engagements. Despite a TIE Fighter having no shields they were actually fitted stock with an ejection seat. So the Empire deemed that an ejection seat is more cost effective than installing shields on all its TIES. After all, without life support in the vacuum of space why would you use the ejection feature,..but if you were engaging an enemy within atmosphere and realised your number was imminently up…you could eject and maybe live to fight another day for the Empire.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Is Mas Amedda evil?
Answer: Hell yes. This guy was basically the only one individual that Sheev Palpatine trusted to carry out his orders, and clean up his messes. The sly Chagrian had been in Palpatines corner from the beginning, and was one of only a handful of beings in the galaxy that was privy to Sheev Palpatines alter ego; Darth Sidious. He was already in the Office of the Chancellor, before Palpatine was elected to the position after his predecessor, Finis Valorum,..and he was there after Palpatine “somehow” perished in Return of the Jedi. Amedda was appointed head of the Strategic Advisory Cell during Palpatines long extended term in office, during the Clone Wars, and supported Palpatine as a brilliant war time leader. This in turn gave Amedda tremendous power, and when the incognito Sith Lord was preoccupied with Sith business, Amedda basically ran all of Supreme Chancellor Palpatines daily affairs. He knew what Palpatine was up to, and basically supported his evil machinations up till the end. He was pompous and arrogant, Darth Sidious’ kinda guy,..and would arrange his little Sith outings for his master, like when he arranged a shuttle for Sidious when he went to deal with Maul and Savage on Mandalore. He continued to be Palpatines puppet as his Grand Vizier in the Imperial Senate, and Imperial Ruling Council, extending Ameddas greed and corruption on an even grander scale. Palpatines evil lackey did very well for himself under his masters cruel Empire. Amedda always had a smug contempt for the Jedi, and was in Palpatines office when Master Yoda confronted the Sith Lord. When Order 66 was executed he was proudly beside Palpatines side when he gave his first Galactic Empire formation speech. You couldn't wipe the smug, evil grin from his face at that point. After this Amedda officiated a very cruel and evil ceremony outside the burning Jedi Temple, where countless lightsabers of dead Jedi were publicly incinerated. The guy relished in sweeping away the last remnants of the now but extinct Jedi Order, and did it with an air of malice the entire time.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How much would it cost to buy every single LEGO Star Wars set? Only Lego Star Wars sets, no other kind of Lego sets.
Answer: I love Star Wars Lego as much as the next fan,..but are you kidding? Okay,..as of October 2023, according to ‘Bricklink’, the official Lego databank, there are 910 Star Wars Lego sets;…and a staggering 1,386 Star Wars Lego Mini-Figures! If you started collecting now you'd be looking at laying out over several hundred thousand dollars in this very crazy and commendable pursuit! Some of these sets are now turning almost 25 years old, dating back to the release of The Phantom Menace in 1999. The first few sets ever released were based on the original trilogy, and today are highly sought after in auctions and sales the world over. Some of the most expensive Star Wars Lego sets include; #75192 Millennium Falcon, #75313 AT-AT and #75252 Star Destroyer. These sets have 4,000 pieces up to over 7,500 pieces each, and can take many hours to days to finish their completion. Each complete set costs more than USD$1,000. Each Star Wars Lego set encompasses scenes and locations, situations and some even have light-up features and moving components. One of the more harder to complete, newer releases is the Lego Razor Crest, which was discontinued at the end of last year. That's going to be one of the biggest hurdles in trying to get all the 910 sets, facing discontinued sets and some becoming extremely rare to find. And by the time you find all the sets listed as of now, Lego Star Wars will probably be over 1000 different sets!! By then your collection could even be worth up to USD$400,000 and far beyond. These sets are always increasing in value and scarcity. Lego can become so addictive and competitive that ultimately you could end up with hundreds and thousands of pieces of Lego, slowly invading the rooms of your home, until you are forced to sleep in a caravan in your back yard. You could literally spend years building all the sets, that encompass nearly every movie and series in the vast saga,..but given all in the world nowadays..that doesn't sound like such a bad idea.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who is the best bounty hunter in Star Wars?
Answer: Cad Bane. Why? Because this bounty hunter was the ‘go to guy’ whenever a Sith Lord needed a job done. Bane hired his own mercenaries as well as other hunters during his quests, and was affiliated with the likes of not only the Sith, but; the Pyke Syndicate, the Hutt Clans, the Kaminoan Government and the Confederacy of Independent Systems. He mentored Jango Fett, whose skills and very likeness went on to become the clone template for the Grand Army of the Republic, and Bane also took on a young Boba Fett; who later took on the title after killing the infamous Duros hunter. But it was Bane who was recognised by three Sith Lords for his incredible talents, and subsequently took on some of the hardest jobs a bounty hunter could ever accept. He personally worked for the galaxys greatest crime families and syndicates, but being hired by not one,..not two,..but three Sith Lords has to make him the best bounty hunter in the SWU. After the death of his friend and fellow hunter, Jango Fett, Bane became the number one hired gun credits could buy. In the beginning of The Clone Wars Darth Sidious needed a very delicate job done, and turned to the man who held the top title. Bane stole a Jedi Holocron for Sidious, straight from the Jedi Temple, and proved his title to the Sith Lord Master. Sidious was so impressed he hired him to capture a Jedi, which he killed,..then forced ‘the chosen one’ Anakin Skywalker to open the holocron. Sidious then got Bane to pull off the trifecta and kidnap force sensitive children for his evil plans. He not only stole from right under the Jedi’s noses, and held Galactic Senators hostage..but he broke Ziro the Hutt out of Coruscants most high security prison block. He previously held a contract with Darth Maul, which he and Aurra Sing subsequently aborted,..and during the Clone Wars he worked directly for the Sith Lord Count Dooku. Dooku placed tremendous trust upon Bane to get the job done, and Bane impressed Dooku again by surviving “The Box”; a lethal obstacle course on Serenno concocted by Banes former cell mate, Morolo Eval. He then lead a team of hunters to kidnap Supreme Chancellor Palpatine and even went on to serve as a mercenary for the Confederacy of Independent Systems; commanding droids and battle ships. After the demise of the Republic he worked for the Kaminoans and the Pyke syndicate, and was reunited with his former apprentice Boba Fett. It was Fett who finally took down his former master, under the twin suns of Tatooine. Cad Bane had built his fearsome reputation against the Jedi by being able to take on force wielders; just like the Mandalorians. His arsenal consisted of weapons able to take on Jedi and win, much like Jango and Boba, but Bane improved his arsenal. He used rocket boots instead of jetpacks, more powerful flamethrowers, he had breathing tubes to defend against a force choke attack, and could still take out deadly gunlingers well past his prime into his 70's. He was a true hunter, unlike Boba who saw the light and redeemed himself. Bane was able to take out clonetroopers because he believed they all fought the same, just like Jango, and could even quickly take out Boba and Cobb Vanth in a gunfight. Bane takes the title.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who is the best actor in the Star Wars films for all times?
Answer: Natalie Portman. Her portrayal of Padme Amidala was absolutely perfect, and her commitment to the role was commendable indeed. Of the 200 girls that auditioned for the role of Queen Amidala, a 16 year old Portman was chosen from all the rest, and she debuted as the Queen of Naboo at the age of 18. The way she embraced Padme's character was remarkable, as she took on the role for all three movies in the prequel trilogy. Before accepting the role she would have been aware of the tremendous pressure on her to nail the part of Luke and Leias mother. Star Wars fans were holding their breaths in 1999 waiting for the very long anticipated release of episode I, The Phantom Menace,…and Natalie definitely did not disappoint. Her versatility and creativity was well conveyed, especially when episode II, Attack of the Clones, was released. In the timeline Padme has aged 10 years, and the way it was believable that Padme could boss Anakin around wasn't unbelievable at all, and her acting in those regards was well thought through and executed. Padme had to be courageous, brave, dedicated, selfless and full of hope..and Portman beautifully captured these qualities. Her performance in episode III was my favourite, as her acting went through a scope of powerful emotions. For myself, her acting throughout the saga was more credible than most other actors performances and usually outshone others on screen with her. She played the role of an outspoken, courageous and hopeful heroine to a tee, and yet still portrayed a vulnerable character without fault. Throughout her exceptional performances throughout the movies she constantly exudes style, class and perpetual elegance; always stealing the scene with her beauty and grace. Coincidentally, in a Q and A interview with GQ Magazine Portman admitted to stealing something from the set of episode I;…one of Hayden Chistensens (Anakin Skywalkers) padawan braids.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How was Vader able to choke out Admiral Ozzel through a monitor?
Answer: Because a Sith doesn't need to be in the same location as someone in order to force choke them. On several occasions throughout the clone wars we see that a force user doesn't need to be in the same vicinity as their target, or even on the same planet, to execute a force choke. So long as the user has an exact location of the target they can perform this move, especially if they are strong in the force. We witnessed this in The Clone Wars when we see Count Dooku getting force choked by his master Darth Sidious. Dooku was at his personal palace on Serenno, and presumably Sidious was back on Coruscant. These two planets are many light years apart, and would take many hours to travel to, even using light engines. The power of the darkside is very potent, with a very wide reach. When Vader was force choking Ozzel, Vader was aboard the same Star Destroyer as the incompetent Admiral. Once Vader ascertained Ozzels position distance became irrelevant, and Vader reached out through the force to reprimand his pompous officer. Vader also liked making very public examples of his foolish subordinates, and through the view screen he could inspire the next officer in line after Ozzel. This was just another one of Darth Vaders ways to instil terror, establish dominance and hopefully inspire leadership and determination. Force choking the former Admiral served its purpose, and let all aboard the same vessel know the price for failure.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did Emperor Palpatine collect anything?
Answer: Palpatine was an avid collector of art when he was much younger, but when he became a Sith Lord his collection mainly consisted of Sith and darkside artifacts. Proir to his ascendancy as Emperor of the entire galaxy Palpatine had an extensive collection of Sith artifacts in his luxurious Chancellors office. Of the items on bold display there were Bronzium statues of The Four Sages of Dwartii,.. a Sith Chalice,.. two enormous spirit urns,.. …and a giant stone relief on the red Sith themed walls. In one of the spirit urns he kept the ashes of his former master, Darth Plagueis. The stone relief was a huge, intricate piece depicting the Great Hyperspace Wars, and while he was Chancellor he kept this collection in full display for the Jedi, and for all to see! Whilst he was plotting his revenge against the Jedi Palpatine initially kept his collection in an old derelict building in Coruscants dank industrial sector-943, known as The Works. Here, at the Li Merge building, he kept items that couldn't be explained in front of the Jedi, such as the Great Crystal of Aantonaii, a huge Sith Holocron from Morriband, along with a large repository of other Sith Holocrons and weapons. This enormous tower was his secret lair during the Clone Wars. This collection was expanded upon at any chance that Palpatine could seize, and before he became Emperor he had his collection from The Works moved to the Grand Republic Medical facility. Palpatine took advantage of when the facility was shut down, due to CT-5555 (Fives) threatening the life of Palpatine himself; after the poor clonetrooper discovered the biochip containing Palpatines Order 66. Here he converted the lower levels into a “Sith retreat” and had the rest of his collection shipped over from The Works. After he became Emperor this all would have been moved to the new Imperial Palace; built straight on top of the old Jedi Temple. Here he kept many of the Jedi artifacts, as well as his own private Sith collection.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What if Count Dooku betrayed Darth Sidious?
Answer: Then he better bring some help with him, because if he faces Darth Sidious alone then he will probably be defeated. Darth Sidious faced both Maul and Savage on Mandalore. He killed Savage and actually captured his former apprentice Maul. During the epic duel Darth Sidious didn't even break a sweat, and was grinning sadistically the whole time. This was no contest for the dark lord of the Sith, and we must remember that Dooku was trained extensively by Palpatine. Sure, Dooku was one of the most skilled swordsman when he was a Jedi, and even more refined and ferocious when he became a Sith. But Sidious didn't even need his lightsabers, and almost every other opponent he faced was met with a barrage of devastating force lightning. Dooku was force choked by his own apprentice, Savage, and subsequently fled from said confrontation. If he couldn't defeat Savage then I don't like his chances with Sidious. With Dooku defeated all that Darth Sidious loses is time. Dooku was going to be replaced by Anakin Skywalker, this is a given because Sidious had his sights set on ‘The Chosen One’ even when Skywalker was a padawan. Dooku was always going to be supplanted by a younger, stronger apprentice, and later Sidious even tells this to Vader. Dooku was viewed as a proton torpedo, that served his purpose and was gone. Until Skywalker is turned to the darkside Palpatine would have to do without the Count, and more than likely replace him within the Separatist Alliance until the Clone Wars ceased. Grievous could fill this role, but within the Separatist Senate someone with a more diplomatic touch would be required to keep the Confederacy of Independent Systems in line. Either way as I said before, the only thing that Darth Sidious is going to lose is time, with the Clone Wars being stretched out just a little further. In time Skywalker would be his to control, regardless.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: If Darth Maul had not been defeated and killed both Jedi, would Count Dooku still have served Palpatine before the clone wars?
Answer: This would be a very interesting situation, and one that I've always wondered about. Darth Sidious took Maul as his apprentice while he was still under the tutelage of his master, Darth Plagueis. Sidious had seen extreme potential in the young Zabrak, but only used him as an assassin and intelligence gatherer. Meanwhile Sidious was making designs on Plagueis’ title,..as any self respecting Sith would do,..and finally killed his old master. Now Maul was his true Sith apprentice, and not some mere acolyte. Palpatine had trained Maul from a small child, and probably had a stronger bond with him than any of his other apprentices. Darth Sidious had not planned on Obi-Wan Kenobi and Qui-Gon Jinn interfering in his affairs, and when Kenobi supposedly killed his apprentice he viewed it as a genuine loss. He even admits this to his new apprentice, Darth Vader, many years later. Sidious was not only meticulous but also an opportunist. If he found a better candidate to be his apprentice, whilst he still had one under his training, Sidious wouldn't hesitate to replace them. We see during the Clone Wars, when Sidious visited Mandalore to confront Maul, that Sidious coldly admits that Maul had been replaced. So casual, so blasé…so cold. This is the nature of the Sith, and if Maul had actually killed both Jedi on Naboo then his master would be joyfully pleased. There would be absolutely no reason why Maul shouldn't still serve as his apprentice. By killing two of the most skilled Jedi Maul would continue to prove his loyalty to his master, and serve him indefinitely. Maul had been privy to some of his masters secrets, and we see this when Maul is reunited with his brother Savage and his mother on Dathomir. He is aware of the Clone Wars starting without him, meaning he was going to be a part of Sidious' bigger plans. Sidious wouldn't have told Maul this if he wasn't going to need him. Maul even laments on how his destiny was stolen from him, and how he was destined for so much more. This isn't to say that Count Dooku wouldn't have served him. More than likely he could use Dooku, especially as the political face of the Separatist movement, seeing as how Mauls diplomatic skills weren't as honed or delicate as Dooku's. Count Dooku was a far better choice for heading the Separatists than Maul. But if Maul killed the Jedi on Naboo then I believe that he would still be serving his master. If that was the case then there would be no Jedi to protect Skywalker, and he would either be killed by the Sith…or Palpatine would take him on as another apprentice. The rule of two was more of a guideline, rather than strict policy with the Sith. Palpatine was no exception, but if young Skywalker wasn't killed in the aftermath on Naboo then Mauls time with Sidious would be cut short upon Skywalkers maturity.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why did Queen Amidala look so Japanese?
Answer: Because the inspiration for many of Queen Amidalas outfits, costumes and face makeup were from Japanese, Chinese and Mongolian traditional culture and costumes. Japanese influences are very clear in Queen Amidalas kimono inspired outfits, and her iconic regal outfit, from The Phantom Menace, was based on a 1921 photograph of a royal gown and headpiece worn by a Mongolian Queen. It was rumoured that her character is strongly based on Genepil, who was the last Queen of Mongolia. Amidalas outfit, seen below (top), has so many similarities from the headpiece, braids and tassles..and even the accentuated shoulder padded cloak. Traditional noble outfits in Mongolian culture are of the same style, as seen beneath. Queen Amidalas face makeup, in particular her lipstick, is very reminiscent of Eastern cultures; and her headdresses have a few other cultural influences. Some of her headpieces incorporated traditional Chinese elements, such as the Chinese Traditional Bridal Headdress, seen below. There are other influences in her headpieces from elaborate Russian tiaras and traditional headresses (seen below), …to even an elaborate piece inspired by a Byzantium Empresses headdress. Even Queen Amidalas successor, Queen Apailana (below middle), bore the same distinctions in her regal outfits. Queen Amidalas style was regal, extremely elegant and it's influenced by traditional cultures from the world over. Her costumes were a mash-up of different earthly designs, even certain styles on the planet of Naboo were very Mediterranean in influence. When in royal costume her style was more Japanese aesthetically, mainly because a lot of her outfits had loose flowing sleeves known as tamoto, and a wide flowing belt known as an Obi; both features of the Japanese traditional Kimono. Her face makeup was heavily Japanese in influence, but also taken from English Victorian era and 17th century baroque makeup (seen below). So ultimately because of the influences in her make-up and costumes Amidala looked like she wasn't only wearing traditional Japanese outfits, but Mongolian, Chinese, Russian, Byzantium and even 17th-18th century baroque English and French. It was just the Japanese influences that weighed more heavily on the viewers mind.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is tactical Droid intel in Star Wars? What are some examples?
Answer: I'll give you one example where the droid intel was going to be used to help defeat the Empire. During the early days of Palpatines new order former Clone Commander Rex hired two sisters to track down and retrieve a T-Series Military Strategic Analysis and Tactics droid. The vital intelligence contained within the droids head could be of assistance to anyone wanting to fight the Empire. These droids were placed in senior command positions during the Clone Wars, aboard Command Vessels for the Separatist Alliance, and at Command Centers for droids based on a planets surface. The longer a Tactical droid remained in service the smarter it got. After sometimes years of commanding the droids brain was able to analyse the battles, and formulate better strategies that could effectively defeat the clonetroopers of the Grand Army of the Republic. When the Empire replaced the Republic many clones remained in service, and it was Captain Rex who hired the Martez sisters to locate one such tactical droid; which contained vital battle information and strategies contained within its central processor. Clone Force 99 was just so looking for the same tactical droid, and encountered the Martez sisters on their assignment. Ultimately Hunter, who lead the rogue clone contingent, let the sisters keep the tactical droids head and it's crucial intelligence;…because it was going to be used to combat the ever growing evil Galactic Empire.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why weren't the Jedi more suspicious of the cloners on Kamino since one of their own had been said to have ordered the army from them without authorization?
Answer: Both Kenobi and Yoda had visited Kamino, prior to the outbreak of the Clone Wars. First Kenobi witnessed the clones for himself when he visited the Kaminoans at Tipoca City. All this began when Kenobi took a Saber Dart, from a murdered bounty hunter, to his old friend Dexter Jettser at his diner on Coruscant. The dart had come from Jango Fetts arsenal, which had Kaminoan technology Fett used. Dexter immediately identified it as a Kaminoan Saber Dart..and sent Kenobi down the rabbit hole. At this point in time the Republic wasn't in dire need of an army to control, but when Obi-Wan returned to the Jedi Council revealing that it was a long lost member of their own that placed the order it became a bizarre mystery. How did this happen? But Master Sifo Dyas had been sent by Chancellor Valorum at the time, to amend a problem on behalf of the Republic. His disappearance had remained a mystery to the Jedi Council, but Dyas was a very respected member of the Jedi. By the time the Jedi had learnt of the Separatist Alliance creating millions of battle droids, that need for an army became something like a blessing to the Jedi, and the Republic as a whole. The councils suspicions only lay on who pretended to be Dyas, upon learning the Kaminoans side of the story. The clones were a fine army created by beings that specialise in the art of creating a purchasable fighting force. This opportunity couldn't be ignored, especially when the Republic faced the new threat of droid armies wreaking havoc and invading their worlds. Dooku's and the CIS's invasion forces were too much of a threat for the Jedi to ignore at this point, and after Master Yoda signed off with the Kaminoans and saved the day with his shiny new army on Geonosis…the Jedi felt compelled to trust the Kaminoans. These cloners never lied to the Jedi, and this was what Kenobi had ascertained in his very first visit to Kamino. Their manufactured, pre-ordered, saviours had arrived at the right moment, and proven their loyalty throughout the first Battle of Geonosis. After this the Jedi as a whole were not suspicious about the Kaminoans, and came to rely and trust the soldiers that had saved their lives; and defended the galaxy from tyranny and oppression. Little did the Jedi know that all of this had been carefully orchestrated by a Sith Lord many years in advance.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What are your thoughts on Count Dooku? Do you think he was a good Jedi before he turned to the dark side? Why or why not?
Answer: Before Count Dooku turned to the dark side he was exactly what a Jedi should strive to be like; and I believe it was his lingering doubt towards the Jedi that made his character complicated, conflicted and more relatable. When we see Dooku during his time as a Jedi he exudes less confidence than he did as a Sith Lord. It's as if everything Dooku did in his life gravitated him closer and closer to the darkside, as seeds of dissent began growing inside him. Up until he crossed the line by killing Master Yaddle Dooku was a supreme example of what it meant to be a Jedi. His saber skills were on par with every opponent, and his skills when facing Master Yoda were unsurpassed. No other Jedi could duel the Jedi Grand Master, and go toe to toe for such a period. He was capable, diplomatic and extremely focused on his goals, and had a certain degree of arrogance and determination that other Jedi did not. His quiet but outspoken personality was one of his greatest traits, and his advice was highly valued amongst his fellow Jedi, especially senior members like Masters Yoda and Windu. His arrogance actually impressed me, especially his cock-sure attitude towards approaching a situation. His sauve and charismatic demeanor gave him the quality of a leader, never a follower; despite the fact that after he fell to the darkside he became a servant to the dark. From watching a younger Dooku he gave me the impression that he felt restricted by the Jedi, especially when it came to using his powers. His noble heritage, his strong opinions, and his conflicting ideals all tumultuously overlapped and collided when he met Darth Sidious, and from there his descent into darkness was sealed. Once he crossed the line by killing Master Yaddle he knew he had only one choice. That was to serve his Sith Lord Master until the end, but he ultimately had typical Sith aspirations to overthrow Sidious; but with Ventress by his side. Sidious dashed those plans by making Dooku prove a test of loyalty to him, and eliminate Ventress. Dooku had conflicted feelings from the beginning of turning to the darkside, and even later tried to get Obi-Wan to join him. So ultimately he felt conflicted on both dark and light sides, and couldn't be content on either team. This is where I believe his arrogance actually got the better of him, and foolishly believing that his master thought that he was inexpendable. Sidious always viewed Dooku as a tool to be used and discarded, once the time was right to take Skywalker, “The Chosen One”, as his new apprentice. Had Dooku known this prior to submitting to Sidious I don't think he would have been so ‘disillusioned’ anymore.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is the most ridiculous, bizarre character/concept in Star Wars Legends (EU)?
Answer: There's a few ridiculous or bizarre character concepts but I have a few that really stand out. Let's begin with Jaxxon, who was a Lepi smuggler from Coachelle Prime. This guy is one of Han Solos friends and rivals in the smuggling game, but it's his bizarre appearance that throws me off. He's basically a giant green rabbit, and wait…it gets even more ridiculous because this big green bunny named his ship..the Rabbits Foot!! This guy even has his own action figure,..wtf! Now we have such a ridiculous character concept that it makes the Jedi Order seem desperate to for new recruits. His name is Sha'a Gi, and his stupid character design is based on Shaggy from the kids cartoon Scooby Doo. This is annoying, ridiculous and just absurd…and his very brief appearance in Tartakovskys '03 Clone Wars was thankfully cut short,..when General Grievous literally stomped him into the ground. Here we have a character that just didn't need to be in the Star Wars Universe. We all know Jar Jar Binks from Naboo, but has anyone heard of his father…George R. Binks? In Star Wars Tales #20, 2004 we see how George is the long suffering father to Jar Jar. One day he couldn't take it anymore and attempted suicide. Instead the bullet only grazes his skull, and he lives on to exist in torment because of his numbskull son. This is one of the most bizarre characters I've seen in a while.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What are some Star Wars images that mirror real life?
Answer: The inspiration for Darth Vaders iconic black helmet and mask were from a Samurai's headpiece. Each part of Vaders helmet matches up to the traditional pieces of a Samurai's garb. The imposing face mask of a Samurai was intended to intimidate or throw off an adversary, as can be said about Vaders ominous mask. The fight scenes, in particular Mauls ultimate demise at the hands of Kenobi, are how an actual swordfight would have occurred; swift, tactical and premeditated.
