Their duel out on Tatooine was a perfect example of how quick a real contest could be. Kendo is a Japanese martial art descended from Kenjutsu, that uses bamboo swords and padded body armour. The stances and attacks are very close to those that the Jedi and Sith use in combat. Count Dooku's fighting style is also reminiscent of the graceful moves associated with the sword fighting sport of Fencing. Ultimately we see a blend of Fencing, Kendo and Samurai influences that play heavily throughout the entire saga. The beautifu regal outfits and dresses of Queen Padme Amidala are straight from the Japanese Kimono and other ceremonial outfits, as well as Mongolian royalty outfits. The woman in the black and white photograph on the bottom right is actually a Mongolian Queen, who heavily inspired Padme's iconic outfit that she wore during the invasion of Naboo. The almighty Sarlaac that Jabba used as a method of insidious execution is based on the real life insect known as an Antlion. The Antlion digs a hole and lays in wait at the bottom, covered in sand. Then when an unsuspecting ant slips down into the trap the Antlion seizes and kills its prey with massive jaws. This is almost identical to the Sarlaac in how it captures prey. Although Antlions don't slowly digest you over a thousand years. The cockpit of the Millennium Falcon, the Ghost from Rebels, and other starships in the Star Wars Universe was heavily inspired by the cockpits of aircraft used in World War II. The B-29 Superfortress had a cockpit that was the direct inspiration for Lucas. Even the sounds of some ships in the SWU are taken from WWII aircraft; for example the sound of a ship travelling through hyperspace is actually “two tracks of the engine noise of a McDonnell Douglas DC-9, with one track slightly out of synchronisation with the other introducing a phasing effect.” And finally we have the Telstar, which was designed as a communications satellite, and was launched in 1962 aboard a Thor Delta rocket. This relatively small satellite was responsible for relaying the first telephone calls, television pictures and even provided the first live transatlantic television feed. Although the Telstar 1 & 2 are no longer operational they are still out there orbiting the Earth. When I look at this device I don't know whether it's more reminiscent of the Imperial IT-O Interrogation Droid…or a tiny little Death Star.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Would Darth Maul be able to kill someone with the horns on his head? Would he be able to impale someone with them?
Answer: Well, Savage his brother did this exact thing to the Jedi Adi Gallia during the Clone Wars. After responding to Hondo Ohnaka at his pirate base on Florrum Adi Gallia and Obi-Wan Kenobi encounter Maul and his brother Savage. Gallia and Savage engage in combat and after holding her own against the enormous Zabrak for a short while his incredible strength and fury gets the better of the small Tholothian. Savage uses the force to send Gallia flying into the hull of a wrecked space craft, then takes a run up and impales her directly in the chest. More than likely this killed her, as her body is motionless before Savage lands his cruel killing blow. This little move of his really harks on his namesake. Maul is capable of doing the exact same thing, although it's not really his style. When Maul was languishing on Lotho Minor, after being bisected by his nemesis Kenobi, we see that his horns if left unchecked can grow much longer than we first thought. If he used the ‘Savage technique’ on someone with those gnarly horns it would definitely messy up their day. Even his horns at their typical length could do enough damage to kill or maim an opponent, but just imagine him headbutting someone in the face! So,..I think its safe to say that Maul could kill someone with the horns on his head.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did General Grievous ever take vengeance on the Huk after becoming a general in the CIS?
Answer: Yeah,..he did. In Legends, the Huk thought they'd scored a major victory against Qymaen Jai Sheelal, after killing his lover on the shores of the Jenuua Sea. But Qymaen re-emerged as Grievous, and commanded eight Kaleesh generals and their forces known as the Kolkpravis. The Huk lost thousands to Grievous, and this is what began the eventual annexing of his planet by the Republic and the Jedi. Grievous even lead assaults on the Huk homeworld, and the Yam'rii (the Huk species name) foreseen the extinction of their race. They used this knowledge to petition the Jedi, and convince them that the Kaleesh were the initial aggressors. Before Grievous’ shuttle crash orchestrated by Dooku, he had assembled a team of lieutenants to organise one last offensive against the Huk cowards. They Huk had desecrated the Kaleesh world of Oben, which was a ceremonial planet used to bury the dead. The Huk had desecrated sacred burial grounds of Grievous’ ancestors,…and he was about to obliterate them; before Dooku and the Intergalactic Banking Clan had other ideas. His faithful lieutenant, Bentilais san Sk'ar, survived the crash and later went on to finish what Grievous had started. The Huk conceded defeat, and fled the colony world of Oben,..but Grievous wasn't finished there. After Grievous emerged as completely cybernetic warlord for the Confederacy of Independent Systems he still had vengeance against the Huk on his mind. In 22 BBY, at the outbreak of the Clone Wars, Grievous now commanded the vast fleets and armies of the CIS. During the Huk wars the insectoid invaders had subjugated many Kaleesh worlds. Tovarskl was one of these worlds, and now it fell into Grievous’ sights. One day he touched down on the former Kaleesh world with his hordes of Seperatist battle droids…and slaughtered every last Huk invader on the planet. Revenge and retribution were his to finally savour, after waging a war that had lasted most of his life. After this Grievous firmly set his sights on the Jedi, and the Republic,..because they were next on his hit-list. Grievous was ultimately defeated by Kenobi, but his former lieutenant Sk'ar went on to work for the Empire. Source; General Grievous Legends, & Bentilais san Sk’ar

Name: John Bambrook
Question: When rebels used ion cannons on Hoth, how far away were the imperial star destroyers? In other words what is the range of an ion cannon?
Answer: It's range is far more than 100 kilometres, which is the distance between the surface of a planet, and to the point where you reach space. It could fire as far as up to 2000 kilometres. During the Battle of Hoth the Ion cannons that the Rebel Alliance were using were the V-150 Planetary Ion cannon. It was powered by a dedicated reactor which was usually erected within hours of construction. It was also called a Low Orbit Ion cannon. Its primary use was protection, although pirates had used it before to disable starships before looting them. The V-150 was similar to what General Grievous’ Subjugator-Class Heavy Cruiser, The Malevolence, had fitted to the middle of both port and starboard sides of his enormous cruiser. During the evacuation of Hoth the Planetary Ion Cannon fired at the Empire, prior to their invasion. It made a direct hit on the Imperial Star Destroyer Tyrant, and resulted in the complete shutdown of the enormous destroyer. The burst of the Ion cannon travelled more than 100 kilometres to disable the Imperial ship, which sat in orbit just above the frozen planet. So in other words the range of a mega Ion cannon, which the ones on Hoth were classified as, is up to several hundred kilometres from the surface, into a planets lower orbit, and beyond. Depending on the power supply, and the size of the cannon, it could be even further than that! Lower Orbit for Earth is classified at up to 2000 kilometres in altitude, so a powerful Ion cannon could fire up to that distance.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Was Count Dooku a feared man?
Answer: Yes he was. Count Dooku came to prominence as one of the greatest Jedi and swordsman of his time. As a Jedi he was revered and respected by his fellow brothers and sisters, and had the trust of the Jedi Council. He was a role model for young padawans, and a source of guidance and inspiration for many other members of the Order. But when he fell to the lure of the darkside and became Darth Sidious’ apprentice all that changed in a heartbeat. Dooku became the face of the Confederacy of Independent Systems, and appointed General Grievous as his commander. From there they declared war on the Republic and split the galaxy in two. Fear was his weapon, and Grievous and his armies became his tools in instilling this tremendous fear upon Republic worlds. The inhabitants of Republic planets had a very real reason to be terrified of the former Jedi turned Separatist leader, especially after worlds began to fall to his droid armies. For the Jedi it was a mixture of fear and frustration, because Dooku was once one of them. He had created confusion and betrayal amongst his former peers, who had once respected the man for his incredible abilities. But upon learning that he had fallen to the darkside the Count instantly became an enemy of the Jedi Order, and instilled a degree of fear amongst younger padawans and Jedi. Their former brother had become a feared opponent to behold, and now he had been consumed by the darkside he became an even bigger threat to their Order. He had to be stopped, and his continued existence would only cost more lives in the Clone Wars. To end the war Dooku had to be killed or held accountable for what he had done to peaceful worlds, and the ongoing oppression that his regime perpetuated. For Separatist worlds Dooku was their hero, but still a man to be feared and respected. For everyone else he was a tyrant and a terrorist, and viewed by most as a murderous leader hell bent on their subjugation and oppression. Despite the fact that he was a puppet for Darth Sidious Dooku was even feared by dark acolytes such as Ventress, Mother Talzin and criminal syndicates allied to the Separatist cause. He was definitely a man to be feared, and never to be underestimated.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Which is the least important character in Star Wars who has an action figure?
Answer: Wol Cabasshite,..and that's just the name of his species. His actual name is Ghoel, but his action figure only lists him as Wol Cabasshite. He was just another one of those ‘blink and you'll miss him’ characters, and was quite possibly one of the least important characters in the entire Star Wars saga. But regardless, this bizarre character got his own action figure. In Return of the Jedi Ghoel is literally a tiny wall parasite that licks guests when they enter Jabba's Court. We see him lick C-3P0 when he walks past an archway. But not only did the Wol Cabasshite character get his own action figure, but so did two more in Jabbas Palace that were each equally unimportant to the entire story. One of the spider-like B'omarr Monks got their own figure, and so did Bubo the Frog-Dog guard dog of Jabba. Together Ghoel and these two other figures were included in a 3 pack titled ‘Jabbas Palace Court Denizens’. The disembodied B'omarr Monk at least has a cool backstory, and Bubo made sense as a guard dog…but Ghoel came from a species that was often mistaken as pests. He literally just hung around Jabbas..creepily licking passerbys, and generally looking like a wall fixture. The action figure even had its own little suction cup, just in case you wanted to recreate Ghoel sticking on the walls at Jabbas.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Were the Sith misunderstood and actually the good guys?
Answer: No, they certainly were not. The Sith existed solely to achieve ultimate power and intergalactic domination. Their very Order was self destructive in nature, and their methods, tactics and exploits were sadistically brutal and unspeakably vile. They embraced the darkside and perpetuated a set of values and ideals that were against everything wholesome and right. They cruelly murdered men woman and children in the name of an ancient evil cult, and tried with all their ceaseless might to eradicate the peacekeepers of the galaxy. Their motives were shrouded in secrecy and mystery, and their actions left murder and chaos wherever they visited. They were evil incarnate, and despised or used every other being in the entire galaxy. Darth Sidious played the long game, and groomed Anakin for years to become his Sith apprentice. He used a blend of subtle persuasion and suggestive psychology to eventually win over Skywalker, and relied on years of evil coercive, and sometimes subliminal tactics to convince Anakin that the Sith were the genuine good guys. He tried to make the Sith appear misunderstood, and as though they were trying to prevent evil and not destroy it. This is the nature of a Sith,..to make you believe that they were “misunderstood and actually the good guys”. Palpatines political posturing and diplomatic silver tongue were actually weapons in his arsenal against the Jedi and the Republic. After spending decades fine tuning his evil machinations the art of subtle persuasion came natural for Palpatine. The Sith excel in being academy award winning liars, and he was up there with the best of them. Sith are narcissistic, abusive and very controlling individuals who stoop to no level to achieve their endgame. They will murder, extort, and manipulate anyone and everyone necessary for achieving their insidious goals, and perform the unspeakable as callously as a seasoned serial killer. To ensure that they are successful in their nefarious plans they typically eliminated all witnesses to their dirty deeds, and blackmailed and controlled those deemed of any future value. They were neither misunderstood, nor were they they good guys;..not for one moment.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Can droids reproduce Star Wars?
Answer: No, but organic beings can use a ‘mechanical womb’ to give birth to droid offspring. Usually droids are manufactured on an assembly production line, and some more advanced droid models can repair and replace body parts, but they could not self replicate or reproduce in the traditional sense. During the Clone Wars the Geonosian Queen, Karina, could reanimate the dead and control her brood via a hive mind. When she perished, thanks to Republic intervention, the only egg to remain after the mass ‘sterilisation’ of Geonosis fell into the hands of a Geonosian named Klik Klak. After retreating deep into the bowels of the planets underworld Klik Klak kept the egg safe until it eventually hatched; giving birth to another Queen who also took on the name Karina. The new Geonosian Queens womb was unfortunately sterile, most likely due to the Empires chemical weapons being previously deployed on her homeworld. To ensure the survival of her race she opted to have a mobile droid factory surgically attached to her abdomen,..effectively becoming a bizarre mechanical surrogate womb. This womb produced creepy hybrid B1 droid workers, still remaining loyal to Karinas hive mind. Vader and his henchman Dr Aphra became aware of this droid factory and Vader himself severed it from Karinas body…ultimately to steal it for himself and the Empire.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What's the most bizarre, humanoid, non-plant species in Star Wars?
Answer: The Sollux were first seen in The Clone Wars, episode ‘Mercy Mission’, when R2-D2 and C-3P0 went on a subterranean adventure on the planet of Aleen. Orphne was a bizarre female Sollux who at first tried to eat our droid duo, but after realising they weren't organic she decided to help them along their way. This is terrifying just in itself, because imagine if it wasn't the droids she encountered, and instead it was Commander Wolffe and his men! Now that would have been a very different episode. Sollux were around average human height, but were more amphibious in appearance. Their skin was light green and white, and she had enormous purple eyes for seeing in the dark; most likely an evolutionary trait from living underground. They had bulbous fingers and a suction cupped, prehensile tongue that could extend to 10 feet. A Sollux was also capable of lightning fast speed and agility. But more extraordinary than anything else Orphne could vanish into rays of light! Her abilities originated from the Light side of the force, and according to Dave Filoni, in a Q&A interview, her powers are actually magical. He likened it to a light side version of the Nightsisters of Dathomir. He also said that she was a “frog lady”, much like Din Djarins passenger in season 2 of The Mandalorian. Also in the same episode were some pretty crazy-looking, over 3 metre tall, humanoid, botanical based species even more bizarre looking than the Sollux, called the Kindalo,…but you don't wanna hear about ‘plant based’ species..so…

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Could Darth Plagueis have fully healed Darth Vader after Mustafar?
Answer: Maybe not completely but yes, because if he was still alive by the time of the events in Revenge of the Sith then he would most definitely have been able to heal most of the newly anointed Sith Lord. And there was also something else that Plagueis and Skywalker had in common; something unusual for a Sith to admit. Love. But we'll get to that in a few moments. In canon, if you want to take Darth Sidious at his word, said Dark Plagueis was… “so powerful and so wise he could use the Force to influence the midichlorians to create life. He had such a knowledge of the darkside that he could even keep the ones he cared about from dying.” In the EU Plagueis had proven that his manipulation of the force was so great that he could actually revive damaged and necrotic tissue, which he had done to himself after attempts on his life were made. He captured and experimented on his former masters backup apprentice, Darth Venamis, and bought him back from the dead uncountable times. These experiments strengthened Plagueis’ knowledge in the darkside and midichlorian manipulation, and if left to his own devices he could have refined this technique to the point of near perfection. Sadly Sidious’ greed seen an end to that, but had Palpatines former master lived beyond the events of The Phantom Menace he would have been able to heal most of Anakins burns; but unfortunately not his missing limbs. This would only be achievable with something along the line of cloned limbs for example. Now back to where I mentioned love. Both Skywalker and Plagueis confessed their “love” for different things in their lives, which was unusual for a Sith to do. Plagueis mentioned the love he had for the incredible creatures in his intergalactic zoo on his personal moon,.. and Skywalkers love for Padme was clearly obvious. Now if Skywalker had not only learnt of The Tale of Darth Plagueis the Wise, but also met the Muun himself then Skywalker would definitely seek Plagueis’ groundbreaking knowledge in resurrecting the young Sith Lords deceased wife. Plagueis would honestly understand Skywalkers plight, and prove beyond all doubt how powerful the Sith are. First Darth Plagueis would heal and restore Skywalker, as he was a medical genius when it came to genetics, cloning and diseases,..on top of his force healing abilities. He could even use the force to create a pregnancy within a test subject. Then after that the only thing that Skywalker would seek would be to reunite with his lost love. Plagueis would finally show Skywalker what his treacherous apprentice could only aspire to. Darth Sidious may have been one of the most intelligent beings to ever exist in the galaxy, but what Plagueis could offer Skywalker would be far more valuable than Sidious’ little plan for intergalactic domination. Palpatine could only dream of what Plagueis achieved, despite conquering the galaxy himself.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How in Star Wars did Yoda survive twenty years on the planet Dagobah?
Answer: Because Yoda was the Jedi Grand Master. He was the pinnacle of what a Jedi could achieve to be, and was the most skilled and wisest Jedi that the Order had ever produced. He knew that after Darth Sidious had destroyed the Republic, and the Jedi Order, he would have to remain hidden on the swampy planet until the time was right to guide “the new hope”. Kenobi was keeping an ever vigil eye on Luke during his own stay on Tatooine, and Bail Organa and his wife were raising Leia on Alderaan. These two were the only hope of restoring the Jedi Order, and Kenobi and Yoda were crucial in Lukes ascendancy within the light side. Yoda had known from the Clone Wars that Dagobah was rich in the force, and first learnt to communicate with Qui-Gon Jinn there on the shrouded planet. It was a forgotten planet, with no technology, and teaming with hordes of dangerous predators. It was shrouded in the darkside of the force, and actually perfect for Yoda to hide out. Yoda could attune himself with the force, and avoid being eaten by enormous fanged swamp beasts, while staying under the Empires radar. His stew that consisted of herbs and reptiles sustained him over his two decades on Dagobah, and he also had the vital nutrients from his walking stick, or Gimer stick. Made from the Gimer tree, native to planets such as Dagobah and Kashyyyk, it's bark could be chewed to release nutritional qualities, that could sustain Yoda enough to not need food for extended periods. It also aided in his long meditations and time in seclusion. He gathered what food he could use, and compensated elsewhere in the swamos with local flaura and fauna. The Rootleaf stew that Luke tried was just one example of Yodas gourmet swamp cuisine. By meditating, communicating with others throughout the force, maintaining his hut and it's supplies, and avoiding the larger swamp denizens Yoda spent his time in relative peace and seclusion from the gaze of the Empire. He also had a lot of time to reflect on how he ended up on a miserable swamp planet for 20 odd years ..after the very near obliteration of the Jedi Order.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why would Emperor Palpatine need any Royal Guards?
Answer: Not that he actually needed them but upon becoming Emperor of the known galaxy Palpatine needed to present himself as royalty; the ruler that the galaxy desperately needed. In doing so some Royal Guards acting as his personal bodyguards would seem quite normal. But it was more the Sith Lord posing in front of his subjects and followers, and giving everyone the impression that he was just a frail old man. Darth Sidious didn't need a walking cane but he used one as part of his guise, pretending to be an unassuming elderly statesman, that had been disfigured by the traitorous Jedi. With the incredible powers that he possessed Palpatine had absolutely no need to have guards protecting him. But he did it to keep up the facade of royalty and supremacy. The guards also served to enforce the Emperors word, which was law, and the Royal Guards acted directly on behalf of Palpatine. They did actually serve as personal bodyguards to Darth Sidious, and were established by Palpatine back in the Clone Wars. Originally they were created as an order of protectors for the Office of the Chancellor, and were called the Red Guard,..and then after the formation of the Galactic Empire they were called Royal Guards.. befitting the Emperors regal title. Out of the millions of soldiers in the Empire these crimson guards were the very elite. Their skill and intestinal fortitude was second to none, with each ones loyalty to the Emperor being unquestionable. They would gladly give their lives in service of their Emperor, and even sacrifice another of their own circle for him. They were even used in the service of other high ranking officials such as Mas Amedda and Darth Vader. Castle Vader on Mustafar had Royal Guards to accompany Vader on missions, but more importantly to guard his ominous fortress. Others would say they were also moonlighting as spies for the Emperor himself.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Which Star Wars vehicle has the worst design?
Answer: The Twin Ion Engine line of vehicles had many flaws, from reduced line of sight, to impractical wing design that presented the vehicle as a bigger target in combat. But one of the worst designed vehicles in this Imperial line of war machines has to go to the TIE Crawler. This odd vehicle was mass produced by the Empire, which always lead to reliability and repair issues, but the actual problem with this bizarre contraption was that it left its pilot more exposed than the TIE/LN Fighter. This Imperial tank was designed to climb mountains of debris on the battlefield, but didn't actually use repulsorlift technology. It was very cramped inside the tank, and offered little protection with no shielding, but that was typical of Imperial scrooges when it came to design cuts. It came as a way for its designers, Seinar Fleet Systems, to expand after the decline of the Empire and the rise of the New Republic. They were trying to break into a new market, while using old technology. It was basically a TIE command module attached to two tank treads, and had no major defence to deter would be assailants,..boasting a weak complement of 2 medium blaster canons and 1 light turbo laser. It was some disastrous hybrid of two very different vehicles, and Seinar Fleet Systems cut costs tremendously in the manufacture of the “Century Tank”. Recycled parts were commonly used in its creation, as the use of the command pod cut down on training times and additional design upgrades. No shields, shitty armaments, second hand parts, and outdated technology made this Star Wars vehicle one of the worst designed, and most ridiculous looking vehicles also.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who was the wisest (i.e. most fully realized) Star Wars character one could look up to?
Answer: Tera Sinube. Sinube was an elderly Jedi Master who had once sat on the Jedi Council, but left his esteemed position before the Battle of Naboo. He was more than 400 years old, and due to his strong connection with the force he became a Jedi investigator; which allowed him to solve crimes and mysteries quicker than a seasoned detective. His knowledge of the Coruscant crime world and the different criminal factions proved invaluable when working on an assignment, and his eagerness to help any Jedi in need was well known. During the Clone Wars Sinube was approached by a young Ahsoka Tano, after a thief had stolen her lightsaber. Sinube taught the young Padawan the virtues of patience, and the value of her lightsaber. During his time with Tano we see that Sinube was still no slouch with a lightsaber, and that his kindness and knowledge made him someone to appreciate and look up to. His lightsaber was one of the coolest in the Order, being a lightsaber cane with the palest blue blade, and his slow and steady philosophy towards life was most admirable. Besides Grand Master Yoda Tera Sinube was one of the oldest and wisest Jedi Masters, and the fact that he was once on the Jedi High Council but resigned his position says a lot about his character. Despite giving the impression that he was old and slow he was a lightsaber instructor at the Temple, and on one occasion where he was training younglings he witnessed the duel between Anakin Skywalker and the traitor Barriss Offee. Not only did he take a genuine interest in his students but gave them life lessons that would help them beyond the Jedi Temple. His friendly and approachable nature made him someone to aspire to be like, and the depth of his knowledge pertaining to the Jedi, the force and all that he had seen in four centuries would have been phenomenal! He also graciously volunteered M5-BZ, his personal astromech droid, on a mission to retrieve a Separatist encryption module; from which the droid never returned. His fate was undeserved, as he ended up a preserved corpse deep inside the bowels of Fortress Inquisitorious. During Kenobi we see his dead body on display next to those of younglings. This could suggest that Sinube died whilst trying to save younglings in the attack on the Jedi Temple during Order 66. Regardless, Tera Sinube was one of the wisest and most respected Jedi, and definitely someone in the Star Wars Universe for someone to look up to. He was heartfelt, honest, sincere..and didn't deserve to go out the way he did. The only consolation is knowing that Sinube possibly died a hero; trying to save the lives of the younglings he treasured so much.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why was General Grievous in charge?
Answer: Because he knew what he was doing as a military leader. After his cybernetic transformation from Kaleesh Warlord to Intergalactic Warlord Grievous had become much more than he was previously. While insectoid invaders waged a brutal war on Grievous and his people the Kaleesh General had become a demigod on his planet. Proir to ‘The Huk Wars’ Grievous used a Czerka Outland rifle to become a crackshot, and when he grew older he climbed the ranks of the Kaleesh military until he legitimately earned the rank of General. During the wars between his own people and the Huk Grievous personally coordinated and led extensive campaigns against the invaders. Ultimately he pushed them from his homeworld and it was his tactical ingenuity that was essential to that. After he became an enforcer for the Intergalactic Banking Clan he was then chosen by Count Dooku himself to become Supreme Martial Commander of the Droid Separatist Armies. Grievous was given this role as he had been a military man first and foremost, and proven himself as a brilliant strategist and commander. War was a part of him, and he was good at winning battles..plus he had a personal vendetta against the Jedi which would motivate and drive him further in defeating their forces. It was the Intergalactic Banking Clan that gave Grievous the initial offer to work for them as an enforcer, and from there his impressive skills ultimately drew the attention of the Count; who had already planned to position the warlord as supreme general of the Separatist Armies. Grievous was a perfect choice to lead the droid armies and fleets as he was subservient to Dooku and his master, and his military genius was invaluable towards their cause. Grievous didn't sleep, he didn't need instructing and he didn't need to be told the cost of failure. Dooku knew that Grievous wanted to annihilate the Jedi for what they did to Kalee, and each victory he achieved during the Clone Wars would bring him closer to this. With Grievous in charge the Separatist Alliance was guaranteed victories against the Republic, and Grievous’ reputation as a Jedi slayer only added to the fear factor when new Jedi Generals and clonetroopers entered the battle.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: In Star Wars, what would happen if the Night Sisters like Mother Talzin left Dathomir and lived somewhere like Hutt Space where they could control people and do whatever they wanted?
Answer: The planet of Dathomir is what actually gives the Witches their powers, as it is steeped and shrouded in the darkside. The inner sanctum of the witches temple replenished their powers and helped them connect to the darkside of the force; and we see Nightsisters like Talzin and Ventress return there on occasion to do so. It had a Nightsister altar and shrine where many sacred ceremonies were also held in this ancient subterranean temple. They relied on Dathomir to invigorate them, although they could use their powers offworld. Talzin demonstrated this by imbueing members of her own coven with an invisibility spell that still worked offworld,..and she could even propel her dark magicks across the cosmos which she did when using Dathomirian voodoo to assault Dooku nearly killing him. But if the witches packed up and permanently relocated to Nal Hutta, or anywhere else in Hutt Space, their strong bond with Dathomir and its powers would wane in time. For thousands of years the witches dominated the males of their homeworld and its moons, and practiced their hybrid force abilities in relative seclusion. Their aspirations weren't over ambitious, like controlling the galaxy and making it bow to their will or anything like that, despite Mother Talzin perpetuating the notion. After General Grievous all but wiped out the Nightsister Coven, in the massacre of the Battle of Dathomir, the remaining witches top priority was survival. They didn't want to draw any needless attention to themselves, especially after Palpatine started purging the galaxy with the creation of his new Intergalactic Empire. Mother Talzin used her powers offworld, like she did after the massacre on Dathomir when she attempted to harvest force energy from the Dagoyan Elders. If Talzin so wanted to strengthen her position within the galaxy, and start controlling people elsewhere in the galaxy, then she would have enjoyed living somewhere else and doing so, but her connection to the force was strongest on Dathomir. If the massacre on her homeworld never occurred then Talzin would probably never have left the dark sanctuary of her home, but she was forced to flee from Grievous and his armies. Only later to return as a false idol willing to sacrifice innocents to empower her with the living force. Talzin was more bent on revenge, like her son, which lead her to obsess over Sidious’ death. After that she would have wanted to return to Dathomir…but Grievous all but put an end to that.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Can force users fly?
Answer: No, but they sure can make it look like they do. In the 2003 Clone Wars Dooku appears to fly down from a very high balcony onto the ground to face Ventress,..but what he was doing was actually levitating, using the force to lightly guide his body to the ground. This might have looked effortless for the Count, but actually required a great deal of practice, concentration and sheer discipline. A force user can levitate objects from one spot to another, and this can also apply to their own body. A skilled enough force wielder could give the impression that they were actually flying, whereas they were just levitating themselves. Some sentient species such as the S’kytri and Toydarians have wings and can fly naturally, and in Legends there were S'kytri on both the dark and light sides of the force. But they could only fly thanks to their wings. Force users can jump and leap great distances, and slow their momentum using their skill in the force,..and even propel another Jedi or Sith an even greater distance. Ezra Bridger and Kanan Jarrus had developed a similar technique, and Maul had used it on Ezra inside the Sith Superweapon on Malachor to access a Sith holocron. When General Leias ship is attacked, and she is blown out into the vacuum of space, she uses the force to pull herself back aboard; also giving the illusion that she was flying. Other force wielders such as the Inquisitors used their own unique lightsabers to fly in and out of situations, and most force users could fall great distances and slow their descent down to survive. But they certainly couldn't fly like Superman.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Is the TIE bomber considered a variant of the TIE Fighter or are they separate ships altogether? What is the difference besides TIE bombers having the ability to drop explosives and different wing designs?
Answer: The TIE/sa Bomber is a variant of the TIE Fighter. Designed by the same manufacturer, Seinar Fleet Systems, the TIE Bomber boasts the same Twin Ion Engines as the standard TIE/LN Fighter. It is slightly longer at 7.8 metres, over the TIE fighters 7.2 metres. A standard TIE Fighter is 8.8 metres tall, and the Bomber is 5.1 metres. It is slower at 850kph, under the TIE Fighters 1200kph, and has no shields or hyperdrive like its counterpart, but does have onboard life support. It did have inclined wings, much the same as the TIE Advanced, which gave it better manoeuvrability whilst carrying heavy ordnance into situations. It's main distinguishing feature, that set it apart from a regular TIE was its iconic twin operational pods, which had one for the pilot, and the other for bombing ordnance; complete with a bomb chute connected to the on board targeting systems. In addition to its various bombs, concussion missiles and proton torpedoes the craft was also equipped with homing missiles and twin laser cannons. They could be fitted for various roles in their anti-emplacement anti-trap air support positions. These bombers were usually deployed to carpet bomb the enemy and weaken its infrastructure, and they could even be fitted to carry up to six stormtroopers for rapid deployment. Source; Wookiepedia- TIE/sa Bomber and TIE/LN Fighter.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is the most terrifying thing about Darth Vader?
Answer: He is a virtually unstoppable, long foretold prophesied “chosen one”, that can effortlessly use his mind to implode your head..and no one could stop any of this carnage and madness until he had returned balance to the force. His utter lack of humanity was absolutely terrifying, and he didn't care if he had to slaughter women and children to achieve ultimate power. He was driven by fear, yet ruled by it…and his methods were harsh, cruel and sadistic in nature. His mere presence instilled pure dread in all but a few, and he didn't even have to be on the same planet as you to kill you. I think that last one was pretty terrifying, because imagine for a moment that Vader was your boss, and you'd been using his favourite mug in the work place, or parking in his reserved spot,..or even just nodded at him in a fashion that he felt unbefitting for a Sith Lord. What then? The answer is nothing that matters; because there is nothing that you could possibly do if Vader was dead set on killing you. He could use the force to make you trip down a huge flight of stairs, or open an airlock unexpectedly blowing you into space, or wait until you began eating a meal and make it look like you choked on a piece of food. Or he could just get real shitty at you and crush your larynx from his kitchen, or the other side of the planet..or the other side of our whole star system for that fact.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why didn't Sidious turn younglings into inquisitors?
Answer: He did, but first he sadistically made them fight each other to the death,..before the winner reluctantly joined the Inquisitorious under the oversight of Sidious himself. This was the cruel Sith Lord postulating over his victory over the Jedi, and rounding up the survivors of Order 66 and the Great Purge. Palpatine would have the survivors starved and beaten, then bought before him. Then he would make them fight to the death, with the victor being promised freedom. It's not that Sidious ever intended for the young Jedi to become Inquisitors, but if they survived his punishment and killed their fellow Jedi they stood a good chance of becoming one of his agents. He did this to a group of young survivors and ‘persuaded’ a Verpine Jedi named Beyghor Sadhett to turn on his Jedi brothers and sisters. This didn't mean that he was instantly to become an Inquisitor at all,..because he was later killed by Vader. Sadhett died because when he first met Vader he immediately assumed that the two of them were equals or allies on the same team. Vader took immense displease at the Verpines unsolicited insolence. Less than one percent of the entire Jedi Order survived the purge, making that just less than 100 Jedi left on the run. Of the remaining Jedi far more survivors would have been adults than younglings, and it was easier for Palpatine to use seasoned adult fighters than children in his army of Jedi Assassins. The younglings in the Temple were a test for Vader orchestrated by Sidious..to test his conscience and morals, and ensure his descent into the darkside was cemented. Sadly these younglings were just fodder for Vaders initiation, and nothing more. Reva Sevander was a youngling that actually survived the Purge by playing dead, but then it's hazy on how she actually came to join the Inquisitorious afterwards. Eeth Koths infant son was immediately taken by Vader and his Inquisitors after crossing the Jedi off their hit list. But the majority of the younglings from the Temple were slaughtered, and those that survived either quickly went into hiding like Grogu, or were swiftly hunted down. Sidious wanted to be done with the Jedi Order for good and didn't want to take forever achieving it. A youngling survivor could be a serious threat further down the road, like Sevander proved to be, so the Emperor had the unfortunates immediately dealt with. Younglings could integrate easier into a large society, and have a family smuggle them.. whereas older Jedi had more risks of being detected. Sidious was meticulous with his ages old plan, and the younglings had their purpose to serve after he began sweeping away the Jedi.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What are your favourite story/episode arcs in Star Wars: The Clone Wars?
Answer: The ‘D-Squad’ Arc is my favourite as it reminds me of the Star Wars version of the mission to capture the Nazi Enigma device during World War II. It begins with the episode Secret Weapons, where the Republic learn of a new Seperatist device that encrypted all of their top tier communications. An encryption module is developed by the Separatists that the Republic assemble D-Squad to retrieve from behind enemy lines. Leading the squadron of droid heroes is the diminutive Zilken, and Geonosian War veteran,..Colonel Meebur Gascon. His aspiration to be promoted to the rank of Brigadier General is what makes his role so reminiscent of a grisled old major from a comedic war movie straight outta the 1960's or something. His character was very memorable and a great highlight of the series. Firstly the squad of astromechs, including R2-D2 and a modified Pit Droid, named WAC-47, formulate a plan and steal the crucial encryption module from straight under the Separatists noses. On their way back to the Jedi Temple they encounter an unexpected frozen comet field, and crash land on the barren world of Abafar. This place was more barren and dry than Tatooine, and distorted the senses severely. Gascons descent into madness in the wastelands of Abafar, known as ‘The Void’, is quite hilarious,..and the introduction of Clone Commando Gregor working at a cafe while experiencing amnesia is a nice touch. We were only briefly introduced to the Clone Commandos in the episode Witches of the Mist, with Delta squad returning the bodies of murdered Jedi back to the Temple. But in this arc we meet Gregor, and explore the elite clonetrooper role in a bit more detail. I really liked this inclusion as Gregor became the hero of the story when he apparently sacrifices himself to get D-Squad off the planet and back to safety. His heroic assault on the Separatist Outpost was an epic display of courage against overwhelming odds,..and when it appeared like he perished in the Rhydonium explosion it genuinely made me respect his character. Later when Gregor returns in Rebels it appears as if the explosion damaged him psychologically, despite his attempts to remain the same old Gregor. This was bittersweet for me, seeing as his heroism was one of the most badass displays from a clone in the whole damn series. He was one of my favourite characters from the entire show, but what I enjoyed most about this arc was that it deviated from the main characters, and bred fresh life into memorable new ones. It explored the respect that organics develop for droids, and one of the best little touches in the series was the inclusion of the original Ponda Baba ‘Walrus Man’ action figure, bought to life as a seedy background character lurking on Abafar. He's seen hanging around the diner where Gregor was forced to work by the the surly Sullustan proprietor, Borkas. Walrus man is even later spoted in the seventh season of TCW on Coruscant! The Ithorian next to him is also based on the original 1970's Vintage ‘Hammerhead’ figure.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who will win, Godzilla (Monsterverse) or Darth Vader?
Answer: Darth Vader has already tackled something bigger than Godzilla. On Exegol The Emperor tested his apprentice by leading Vader to fight a sub-species of the Summa Verminoth; the galaxys largest apex predator. We first see this humongous beast lurking near ‘The Maw’, a huge black hole, in Solo. It took the most destructive force that could ever exist to kill the Summa Verminoth, as its very skin was ripped off and it's body consumed by the maelstrom of power. I don't know about you, but I think that a black hole would do the same thing to the King of the Monsters. But Vader used his powers to defeat one of these enormous creatures, despite having to construct makeshift limbs, after Sidious decided to put Vaders resources, skills and all his powers to the test. Godzilla cannot defend himself from the force that Vader would unleash on him, except if he could use his atomic breath on the Sith Lord, or go into Ultimate mode. But Vaders suit was capable of withstanding extreme punishment, pressure and heat; enough so that Vader could resist the magma hot lava on Mustafar. Godzilla could attempt stomping the bothersome black beetle, and if he could jump on Vader it would be a hard attack to defend against, but Vaders prowess in the darkside was phenomenal. He could move enormous objects at will, and if crushed by Godzilla he may be able to use his abilities to lift or topple the King over. Or Vader could just use the force to crush Godzillas skull and brain, or snap his neck. Godzillas sheer size works tremendously in his favour, but it was Master Yoda who said that “size matters not”. Going into this contest we are presented with a David versus Goliath situation, but first impressions are not always accurate. Vader is highly unpredictable, and I wouldn't be surprised if he did something similar to the Summa Verminoth and jumped on Godzilla; rendering his atomic breath useless at this point. If Vader could do this then I assume Godzilla would end up just like the dead creature on Exegol. Now we know what Palpatines minions ate all that time on the hidden planet until Kylo Ren showed up. Summa Steaks!!

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who was more evil Count Dooku or Darth Maul? And why?
Answer: Count Dooku was born into the lap of luxury on his home planet of Serenno, then entered the discipline of the Jedi Order under the tutelage of Master Yoda, among others. His birthright gave him an air of superiority and entitlement, and heavily shaped his personality. He knew right from wrong, but ultimately when he turned fully to the darkside he murdered Master Yaddle knowing the consequences. This act cemented his path into evil, yet Yaddle had told him that it wasn't too late to stop. Dooku had a choice all along..but Maul was never as fortunate. Maul was taken from a very young age, after having been born into a brutal society. Once his new master had procured him from his mother, Talzin of the Nightsisters, Maul never had a choice in the matter of how his life unfolded. Sidious molded and shaped the young Dathomirian into a murderous weapon. Mauls concept of right and wrong had been warped by Sidious, giving him the illusion that the Jedi were corrupt and evil, and that the Sith were righteous. He was made evil, whereas Dooku had to be seduced to the darkside. Both committed unspeakable acts of cruelty, but Maul was the one to grapple with himself far more emotionally because of the pain the Sith had heaved upon him. He wanted to destroy the Sith, and put an end to Sidious’ machinations but Dooku wanted to be top dog, as he tried to convince Kenobi to join him. Mauls evil was from a very sick mind, that was completely instigated by Sidious from the beginning. His suffering was compounded by issues such as abandonment and obsession, ..whereas Dooku had the political acumen to lead the Separatists and a very sharp, attentive mind. He chose to join the darkside, and fell to its lure..but Maul was oppressed by it and couldn't escape its torment. Maul was ultimately rendered mentally unstable by what Sidious cruelly did to him, whereas Dooku relished in being a Sith Lord. Both had been duped by Sidious, but Dooku's cold hearted betrayal of the Jedi stemmed from a calculated and self gratifying evil. That's more scary to me because Mauls evil was almost inherent, due to his Dathomirian culture, and how he knew no better from a very young age. Dooku was more evil in my opinion because he chose to ignore the light, full well knowing that what he was doing was evil..and so very wrong.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: If Count Dooku fought Darth Maul, Savage Opress and Ventress all at the same time could he win?
Answer: Count Dooku was one of the finest swordsman the Jedi Order ever produced, and his mastery of the force was astonishing, but not even this enigmatic Sith Lord could best the likes of Maul, Savage and Ventress simultaneously. Remember that time when Savage force choked both Dooku and Ventress; at the same time? Remember that time when Maul took on a ship full of clonetroopers and ripped a hyperdrive engine from it's mounts? He wasn't even in possession of a lightsaber at this point! Remember that time when Ventress simultaneously engaged both Luminara Unduli and Ahsoka? These are examples of what this vicious trio can do when they're fighting solo against multiple odds. Now try to imagine if they united and took on Count Dooku at once. Count Dooku is no fool, nor a stranger to taking on multiple opponents at once. He has fought multiple opponents on many occasions, and even fought Skywalker and Kenobi together. He is a fearsome adversary with lightning reflexes and adept at all lightsaber forms. It's been said that the Count could at one point have defeated his master Darth Sidious in saber combat, and despite being older than his master had skills that frequently outmatched his much younger and stronger opponents. But against the Sons of Dathomir and the Dathomirian Witch herself I fear the odds against the Serenno nobleman are very high. Dooku may take out one or two of these opponent's, but I don't like his odds on defeating the third. Dooku eventually lost to Skywalker, and Kenobi, after having dueled them previously. Facing these three opponents would be a hard task for the Count to tackle, and to win he'd have to muster his all. Maul hated him as the Count filled his shoes after Kenobi bisected him on Naboo. Savage hated him for betraying and using him, and Ventress despised him for abandoning her despite being his loyal apprentice to the end. The pure rage and fury that these three would produce, coupled with their unbelievable skills in the darkside, would give Count Dooku the fight of his life and keep him on his defence constantly. Dooku would carefully assess his odds, and maybe even flee to fight another day, but if these Dathomirians got him off balance for just a moment they would instantly seize the opportunity to slay the Count. My bets are on Maul pulling it off.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What if Obi-Wan and Anakin’s roles were switched and Obi- Wan fell to the Dark Side instead?
Answer: Then I fear that Skywalker would not be a strong enough force to overcome Kenobi as a Sith Lord. Obi-Wan Kenobi was one of the most talented and gifted Jedi the Order ever produced. He was a phenom when it came to his mastery of the force, and was one of the most impressive lightsaber duelists of his time. He was far more disciplined than his former padawan, and never fell to the temptations of the darkside; even when the closest person he ever had as a lover was murdered before his eyes. If Skywalker and Kenobis roles were reversed then it would make for a very different ending on Mustafar. Kenobi defeated the likes of General Grievous, Darth Maul and then went on to trounce Vader in the Kenobi series. This is no small feat, and required the highly focused mental discipline that Anakin did not possess. When this Jedi Master put his mind to something he was nearly impossible to convince otherwise, and if he fell to the darkside he would be virtually impossible to defeat. If it came down to a duel between a lightside Anakin, and a darkside Kenobi then I fear that Obi-Wan would gain the high ground regardless. This would result in the same conclusion as we originally seen on the fiery planet, instead it would be Kenobi as the Sith Lord walking away triumphant. Anakin would put up a valiant effort, but I fear Kenobis determination and skill within the darkside would be too much for ‘the chosen one’ to contend with. This would please Darth Sidious very much having a fully intact apprentice by his side to carry out his orders, and when the time inevitably came for Kenobi to retire Sidious in classic Sith fashion the Emperor would have a real contender to challenge his rule. Sith Kenobi versus Darth Sidious would be a showdown for the ages.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: In Star Wars, which Imperial officers should have stayed loyal to the Empire instead of defecting?
Answer: Imperial agent Alexsandr Kallus of the Imperial Security Bureau is a good example. He had it all at one point. A distinguished military career within the upper echelons of the Empire. He had the respect of such Imperial heavyweights as Thrawn, Tarkin and Vader himself, and had the brains and foresight to climb even further up the ladder. But after an on board ship mishap involving members of Phoenix Squadron the seeds of dissent were first sowed in the ISB agents mind. After breaking his leg upon crash landing on one of Geonosis’ moons, Bahryn, Kallus had to virtually rely on one of his greatest enemies, Garazeb Orrelios, the towering Lassat from the Rebel cell. After successfully negotiating their way out of a subterranean cave full of hungry Bonzamis the Lasat and the Imperial Agent had somewhat bonded over their harrowing and thought provoking experience. His time with Zeb eventually led him to become Fulcrum, a Rebel sympathiser and eventual defector. But had Kallus never betrayed the Empire I would assume that he would have kept climbing the Imperial ladder until he couldn't do so anymore. He was cunning, meticulous and someone that took the fight directly to the Rebel Alliance, and proved time and time again that he had the intestinal fortitude to get the job done;..no matter how dirty he got his hands. Kallus had the perfect Imperial ideology to sustain a very promising career within the Empire, but after seeing and experiencing things from the “enemies” point of view he became totally disillusioned at his former masters and their evil regime.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What happened to General Grievous' wife and/or kids in Canon or legends? How was he portrayed as a father (if at all)?
Answer: In Legends General Grievous has a very large family consisting of ten wives and thirty sons and daughters. This is first mentioned in the 2005 James Luceno novel Labyrinth of Evil. When Grievous was known as Qymaen Jai Sheelal there is also the mention of his great grandmother who fought in a great war between their Kaleesh species, and the Bitthaevians at the Invasion of Guetica. She also served alongside a group of Jedi who firstly aligned themselves with Grievous’ people. During the war she used a Czerka Outland Rifle to help liberate her people, and in time this family heirloom was passed down to Grievous’ grandfather who taught the 9 year old Qymaen to become a demigod amongst his people with the weapon. When Qymaen matured and took the name Grievous after losing the love of his life to vicious insectoid invaders known as the Huk, or Yam'rii, he fought a brutal campaign against them and routinely returned home wounded from the battle. In such times Grievous “relied on the support of his wives and children to restore him to life”. It would seem that before the Huk, and the Jedi ripped his heart out Grievous was very family oriented, much like an ancient Viking who would return from voyages and battles to the loving arms of his wife and family. After Grievous was betrayed in a deliberately orchestrated shuttle crash he was given an ultimatum by San Hill of the Intergalactic Banking Clan;..become a cyborg, due to the extent in which his organic body was destroyed, and also become the leader of the droid armies of the Confederacy of Independent Systems. The war that Grievous waged against the Huk drew the attention of the Republic and the Jedi, and after siding with Grievous’ enemies the Jedi imposed harsh sanctions on the planet of Kalee. This cruelly lead many of his wives and children to starve to death and suffer indignitys too depraved to mention,…along with hundreds and thousands of Kaleesh that Grievous swore to avenge. After his shuttle crash San Hill bought in Grievous’ remaining wives and children, and with this the former Kaleesh Warlord took a mask that resembled his fathers death mask,…and began his immense hatred towards the peacekeepers who had willingly doomed his people. After Grievous accepted the offer to lead the droid armies of the CIS his family is never heard from again. Source; General Grievous Wookiepedia, Legends and Canon.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why are blatantly evil characters such as Darth Vader and the Storm Troopers so popular and deemed "cool" in popular culture? It’s bizarre that they're glorified on shirts, mugs, and all sorts of memorabilia.
Answer: But why is it bizarre to you? Blatantly evil characters are plastered on shirts, mugs, and all sorts of memorabilia…all the time! And when it comes to Disney and Lucasfilm they do it constantly..everyday!! Villains such as Cruella De Ville from 101 Dalmatians, Ursula from The Little Mermaid, Queen Grimhilde from Snow White, and Maleficent who is based on Disneys Sleeping Beauty,..are all proudly displayed on every item conceivable by their owners at Disney. And they're just the ladies! Blatantly evil male characters such as Scar from The Lion King, Jaffar from Aladdin and Captain Hook from Peter Pan are just a sample of the evil characters chosen to adorn consumer merchandise. But that's the key word here; Consumers. The demographic audience for all these delightful animated treasures are children, as is the target audience for Star Wars. We all know that kids love to emulate their heroes from their favourite movies,..as well as their favourite “bad guys”. So it's actually not a big suprise to see Darth Vader and his Stormtroopers stuck all over promotional and collectable items. Children, as well as adult viewers, find these particular characters “cool” because…who wouldn't find Vader and his gang just a little bit cool? Kids will be kids, Disney will be Disney,…and baddies plastered on mugs, t-shirts and everything else will continue happening until the end of time. It's all part of the plan to allow huge companies to make you part with your cash. You may find the hijinks of Vader and his Stormtroopers to be vile and outrageous, as most do…but for children he's a big, bad villain who makes them feel cool when they dress in a t-shirt with his face on it. They want to feel a part of the whole Star Wars rush that comes from eating Darth Vader chocolates and swinging a toy lightsaber about the kitchen. They want to drink Stormtrooper flavoured orange juice with a Darth Maul straw,…and just do what kids have done since seeing their beloved characters come to life from their favourite stories. As do the big kids!!

Name: John Bambrook
Question: If General Grievous could use the Force, would it have been a game changer in The Clone Wars?
Answer: If General Grievous could use the force then Obi-Wan Kenobi would most likely have died in the first year of the Clone Wars. It wouldn't just be a game changer, but could possibly be the game changer. In Legends Count Dooku gives his general a blood transfusion from the late Jedi Master Sifo Dyas. Now let's say that this transfusion worked and enabled Grievous to use the force. What now? Depending on circumstances if Grievous kept this little secret to himself then he could possibly add even more lightsabers to his growing collection. Imagine all those times when Grievous scuttled away from a duel,..and now imagine those times if Grievous could use the force! Jedi like Mace Windu, Kit Fisto and Kenobi himself could all have fallen to his blades, and countless more soldiers, vehicles and ships would have followed. Grievous was already proficient in lightsaber combat, and already a highly skilled opponent for any Jedi. If the cybernetic Kaleesh Warlord could wield the force then all it would do is make him more lethally efficient, and fuel his new murderous appetite. Grievous accepted his ‘modifications’ in a bid to destroy the Jedi, but now he can wield the force he is instantly better than a large chunk of the Order. It's rare for a Jedi to be proficient in all 7 forms of lightsaber combat, but Dooku instructed Grievous in all of them. That makes him better than a large chunk of the remainder of the Order now. Up until the breakout of the Clone Wars the Jedi had spent a millenia as peacekeepers, instead of war generals. Grievous had spent his whole life in combat as it made him the tactical genius that he was. The Jedi had to acclimate to their roles on the battlefield, whereas Grievous relished at the opportunity to lead the charge. If you consider all the aforementioned factors, and now reset them to account for the fact that the general is now evenly matched for most Jedi,..then I'd call that a game changer. Now Grievous is going to wait until he is up close and personal with the first Jedi he encounters, and unbeknownst to the Jedi Grievous can now force choke him, force crush his lungs, and force throw he or she straight into a solid duranium wall. The odds have turned against the Jedi severely, and because of the force Grievous can not only kill the Jedi with his lightsabers…but practically force pull his opponents towards him and into his swirling sabers of oblivion. His lightsaber collection at this point would even make Professor Huyang blush.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who would win in a fight, General Grievous or Azog the Defiler?
Answer: Azog the Defiler, of Moria, beheaded a dwarf King and carved his name in the unfortunate ones head. Instead of returning the severed appendage his Orcs threw a pouch of coins in its place. Then after a lengthy campaign of battles and retribution the filthy ‘goblin’ was in turn beheaded at the Battle of Azanulbizar; by another dwarf who impaled his severed head on a stake, and stuffed the same pouch of coins back in his mouth like a suckling pig. That was the paperback version. In the movies he was no different, except for being more brutish, cunning and murderous, but at the end of the day was of weak organic flesh compared to the cybernetic warlord. And in case you didn't get it…Azog was slain by a dwarf; in both versions. General Grievous, of Kalee, was one of the most gifted military minds of his time, drove hordes of murderous invaders from his homeland, sacrificed his own organic body for a cybernetic one, became the leader of the largest droid army the galaxy had ever seen,..and prided himself on killing the Jedi. He killed Jedi, he killed intergalactic leaders, and he waged a three year war that bought the Republic to its knees. He assaulted the galactic capital of Coruscant and kidnapped the most powerful man in the entire galaxy. He struck fear in nearly all who stood in his presence, and killed untold thousands of highly trained Clone troopers in a bloodbath stretching from the Core worlds to the Outer Rim. General Grievous claimed more lives against Republic forces than probably any other entity during the Clone Wars, and was ultimately bested by one of the Jedi Orders most powerful masters. He wielded four lightsabers in combat, in a fearsome display that would drive most to flee;..and became the face of the military might of the Separatist Alliance and it's near infinite supply of killer droids. After all that I'll put it this way;..if Azog the Defiler could last more than 30 seconds against the most feared Jedi killing machine in the entire galaxy then I would be shocked. Azogs odds upon entering this pathetic, one sided warm up are slim to nil, and against Grievous’ whirlwind of death he doesn't stand a snowflakes chance on Mustafar. Yes, Azog was much larger than most Jedi but his blows would mean for nothing, and his struggle would be futile in this situation The good Generals four spinning lightsabers would make very quick work of the disgusting Orc, and if Grievous jumped 30 metres in the air and came slamming down on the little urchins head it would be goodnight. Azog was used to dealing with Orcs and Goblins,..and General Grievous was trained in the Jedi arts by Count Dooku himself and proficient at killing Jedi. Honestly, we all know who walks away from this one.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: In Star Wars, which characters could have become the emperor?
Answer: There are only about a handful of beings in the Star Wars Universe that were capable of becoming the Emperor, but it was Darth Sidious who after the death of his master became destined to wear the crown. Most casual Star Wars fans believe that Darth Sidious, aka the Emperor, came up with the diabolically genius plan to overthrow the Jedi, and take over the galaxy with his mighty Empire. Little do they know that it all began with the master of Sidious’ master setting the grand plan into motion. Darth Tenebrous was the Sith Lord who took Darth Plagueis as his apprentice. Tenebrous had already begun the groundwork for devising what would become Palpatines plan for intergalactic domination. But his neck was snapped by his apprentice Plagueis. Upon assuming the Sith Lord master title for himself the Muun Sith Lord continued work on his masters plan, and when he took Palpatine as his apprentice he tinkered with Tenebrous’ plan, like in departments such as the clone template and even supplanting his apprentice in the Republic senate. But Plagueis foolishly let his guard down on the eve of Palpatines ascendancy to Chancellor of the Senate he was fried to death by his apprentice. After Plagueis the next candidate that could have been the Emperor was Dooku. The charismatic Count was the leader of the Separatist Alliance on behalf of the Confederacy of Independent Systems. His political prowess was second to none, and he was more of a political leader than Palpatine. He had the voice, the charisma and the foresight to be Emperor, and if given the right apprentice he could have had a damn good run at the title. He certainly would have given Sidious a run for his money in the lightsaber duelling department. Methinks that Sidious demanded that Dooku kill his apprentice, Asajj Ventress, because if the two joined forces against him he'd have a real power struggle on his hands. Now Maul and Vader just didn't have the politcal acumen to keep an Empire alive, but Grand Admiral Thrawn,…now there's a guy who could've had the job, but the Chiss was a military man first and foremost. He had wit, charisma and was a brilliant strategist and military leader, as well as had the political voice that could sway many to his opinion. But after being entangled by a bunch of Purgill Thrawns plans were all but thwarted.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What if a country’s military developed a death star?
Answer: Then we better hope that it's not the bad guys who do it first, because we all seen how the Death Star in Rogue One was capable of destroying a city without destroying a whole planet. Orson Krennic, who was instrumental in the Death Stars creation, and before Tarkin ordered that the destruction of the Holy City was a sufficient enough test,..wanted to destroy all of Jedha itself. This was the Death Stars crowning moment, and the first time that the Star Wars Universe had seen its unfathomable power unleashed. Jedhas Holy City served as a test run for the Death Stars superlaser, which was blamed on a mining accident, but when the Emperor absolved the Imperial Senate Tarkin obliterated Alderaan with the fully armed battle station. Now imagine a county like North Korea or Iran developed their own Death Star, and which country they would test the superweapon on; and it would be even worse if it was a terrorist organisation like Al Qaeda or Hamas. The free world as we know it would quickly become a thing of the past, as one unfortunate city in one unfortunate country would become the first casualty of a new world order. All the countries of the world would have to bow down towards this new global dictator. The looming threat of what this new Death Star could do would be too much for any country to resist, and seeing as how no country has X-wings, and a Luke Skywalker, we're all going to have to get along with our new overlords,…depending on where you live of course. But if it's a freedom loving nation that develops this new superweapon then we could expect to see peace on Earth follow swiftly. The Death Star might not solve any of the problems we all face in society, but it sure as hell will solve the problem with warring nations, and aggressors that have out welcomed their stay on this planet. Imagine if the current war in Ukraine began, and say a country like Iceland or Denmark (being two of the most peaceful countries) came out and announced that they had created a Death Star, straight outta Star Wars!!! I can imagine that the aggressor would cease all hostilities, lay down their arms and retreat from all occupied territories. And if not then the Death Star would become the final ultimatum in all negotiations pertaining to the war, sorry…”military exercise”, and then repatriation of prisoners and compensation would be paid following the cessation of hostilities. Which country's leader on this planet would be utterly foolish enough to ignore the incredibly destructive firepower of the Death Star? And the advent of the Death Stars main power source, a hypermatter reactor, and the hyperdrive itself would raise more questions…such as could this near unlimited power source solve world hunger and allow us to travel to new worlds? Now this may be so but the advent and final production of a Death Star would create future predicaments. The incredible cost that it would take to run, man and operate the Death Star would be astronomical, and likely unfeasible for it's creator. A Death Star would cost 18 quadrillion dollars to create, plus trillions more in added costs. World War II cost 4 trillion dollars, adjusted for inflation to todays dollar. Now to build a Death Star would cost 4,500 times the amount it cost to wage WWII as a total. And it would take more money than exists on Earth just to run it for one day, being 7.81 Octillion dollars. That's 30 trillion times all the money on Earth!! It's more likely that Darth Vader and the Death Star would show up in Earths outer atmosphere, and start making outrageous demands,..before any country could dream of creating their own mega superweapon to rival the awe inspiring Death Star.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Was there a way to heal Anakin Skywalker without putting him into the Darth Vader suit?
Answer: Yes,…but not from a Jedi…because they all nearly perished during Order 66. The Sith, and even races like the Kaminoans and Techno Union have technology that could have either healed Darth Vader completely, or been able to outfit him with a suit that wouldn't have been painful to wear. Sith Lords such as Darth Plagueis, Darth Sion, and Darth Krayt exhibited darkside force healing abilities amongst themselves. The Nightsisters of Dathomir have also exhibited this extraordinary ability. Palpatine was aware of this, had learnt from Mother Talzin herself and even aspired to achieve what his master had accomplished when it came to mastering life over death. Below; Darth Plagueis’ experimenting on Darth Venamis, who Plagueis bought back from death on many occasions. Part of of his plan with Vader was to engineer his suit in a way that made it painfully unbearable to wear at times. This was deliberately conceived by Palpatine to fuel Vaders strength in the force, and empower him in the darkside. This worked but could have been avoidable if Darth Sidious hadn't planned it this way. Sidious expected a fully healthy and non dismembered Darth Vader after Mustafar, so the suit was designed to enhance his rage, and turn him into the Sith Lords personal servant. Sidious only made a passing comment about saving Padme's life before Anakin was entombed in the suit; and after she died the problem was done with as far as Sidious was concerned. Below; Darth Sidious explaining his masters powers to his new apprentice, “the chosen one”. The Cloning technology from the Kaminoans still existed, as the Empire retained its secrets after Tipoca City was obliterated in The Bad Batch. These cloning techniques could have been used to either repair Vaders burnt skin tissue, or grow cloned limbs for him to have surgically transplanted. Force users couldn't be successfully cloned but body parts could. Lukes mechanical hand was another example of the incredible technology in the SWU that could have been utilised to prevent Vader from living in a walking hyperbaric chamber, but the medical technology did exist to heal him. He may have never been the same physically again, but he could have had a body that didn't restrict his movements and limit his health functions severely. Above; Lukes mechanical hand, replaced after his first duel with Darth Vader. If all that failed then races like the Geonosians and the Skakoans of the Techno Union owned and managed some of the largest droid manufacturers in the galaxy. They could have easily created a much more functional, and virtually painless cybernetic suit for the Sith Lord to wear, or have cybernetic prosthetics surgically attached to his severed limbs. Above; General Grievous before his transformation. Then there was an option that I've thought no-one has utilised before. All that remains of General Grievous organic body is his eyes, brain and a few internal organs. The rest of him is a cybernetic suit, but that's not to say what kind of suit you can place someones organs in. Above; the extent of how much of General Grievous’ organic body actually remains. Grievous wanted the raw killing power of his new metal body, but had he opted differently afterwards he could have chosen a more organically appealing suit. Guri is a human replica droid created in 7 BBY by the Thrumble brothers, who also collaborated with the Empire. She was developed as a spy to serve the Empire, but later became an assassin for a crimelord who paid nine million credits for her. Below; General Grievous training in his new cybernetic body after his successful transplant. Had Vaders body been damaged to the point of no return a similar transplant to what Grievous undertook may have been a more suitable approach. He could have been transplanted Grievous style, but into a human replica droid instead of the body that pained him so. Below; Guri, Prince Xixors personal human replica droid assassin. I do believe that had the effort been made Vader could have avoided wearing that particular suit of his, and returned to health far more than what Sidious deliberately prevented. Palpatine basically used Vaders suit as a prison to control his duped apprentice.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who is Xizor, and why is he such a popular character in the Star Wars universe?
Answer: When Shadows of the Empire came out way back in 1996 it bought with it everything a Star Wars movie could expect; from the novel, the comics, the video game, toys and action figures, clothing and accessories and entire universe of memorabilia. The only thing was it didn't actually have a motion picture to accommodate the hype,…but for Star Wars fans it was still a dream come true. It was the story set between the events of The Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi, and as well as all our familiar characters from ESB it introduced a plethora of new ones. Prince Xixor was introduced as one of the main antagonists in the new story, besides Vader and the Emperor himself. Xixor was a Falleen and the current head of the Black Sun criminal syndicate. Upon first impressions we see that he is powerful, charming and loyal to the Empire. We see his predecessors in The Clone Wars, when Maul and Savage absorb the criminal empire into their own Shadow Syndicate. Savage beheads the main leadership at the time convincing the new head of operations to his brothers cause. Although SOTE is an old EU story we are first introduced to Xixor in canon via the more recent SW comics. Xixor was a popular character because he introduced a new type of crime lord outside of the Hutts, and one significantly more powerful. Black Sun worked very close with the Emperor, much to the anger of Vader. Ultimately Xixor tried to kill Vaders son Luke, and paid the ultimate price for his treachery, but the Falleen was popular for being more than just another bad guy. His species uses pheromones to sexually attract females, and Xixor tried using this trick on Leia, who found it hard to resist yet denied his advances. Xixor was one of the few to try and usurp Vaders position as right hand man to the Emperor, and tried to make Vader look weak and useless in the eyes of Palpatine. It was the first time we were introduced to Black Sun itself, and Xixors personal bodyguard was a human replica droid named Guri, who became another popular EU character. His story was fascinating, his species and crime syndicate was intriguing, and his introduction into the SWU bought a fresh new character with tons of potential. As a villain he impressed, with his might, influence and power,..and was another one of the unforgettable characters from Shadows of the Empire. Like many characters from the EU fans of the Steve Perry novel have been waiting to see this enigmatic figure appear in a new series, and given the success of recent projects like The Mandalorian I somehow think we'll see this character appear sooner or later.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is something that most people don't know about The Force?
Answer: The ability called ‘Force Sever’. We know that Jedi such as Luke Skywalker and Ahsoka Tano purposefully distanced themselves from the force, in times of self imposed exile. Jedi like Kanan Jarrus diminished his connection to the force after Order 66, in a bid to outrun the Empire. This ability for a Jedi is a personal choice, and in most cases the individual force user who severs their connection to the force can reverse the effects and embrace the force once again. But imagine if there was a way that a force user could use the ability as an imposition on another Jedi or Sith. What if someone soo deeply invested in the force could actually strip you of your connection to the force, and completely sever its spiritual bond. There was one account of this actually happening. Darth Nihilus, the Lord of Hunger, did exactly that, and to his former master at that. When Nihilus was first touched by the darkside he was tutored in its ways by a Sith Lord called Darth Traya. She taught him how to control his hunger for the living force, but in time Nihilus and the other member of their Sith Triumvirate, Darth Sion, would turn against their master in classic Sith tradition and cast her from the Sith Order. After all, this guy could also devour the lifeforce from an entire planet so this seemed like a parlour trick compared to that.
