But it was Nihilus himself who used a dark variant of this ability, actually allowing him to sever another force wielders connection. His knowledge of the darkside was immense and his mastery of Sith Alchemy was extraordinary. Nihilus used this ability to turn around and strip his former master of the force, then expell her from the Sith Triumvirate. Now just imagine if a Sith Lord like Sidious or Vader learned this ability.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What if Kylo Ren's mask was a permanent part of his face?
Answer: Then he wouldn't seem so pouty, annoying, moody and petulant. If we couldn't see the expression on Kylo Rens face then it would probably be a good thing, and I actually think it would have made for a much better way to evolve his character. If Kylo Ren had come to the light as he did in The Rise of Skywalker, and then maybe taken his mask off,..or if it became damaged whilst fighting and then revealing his face it would have been a better way to make his character a lot more appealing. Another idea would have been to just show his eyes through vents in his mask, or made the mask completely different all together. Below; an early concept for Kylo Rens helmet and outfit. None of the Knights of Ren took their masks off, thus adding to their mysterious identities and none of them spoke, that I can remember. For myself they appeared as menacing assassins, or silent aggressors with a hidden, ulterior agenda. If Ren kept up the same thing then we may have seen him as a more ruthless, mysterious individual…rather than an emotional temper tantrum of moody angst. The new look broken Ren mask that was reminiscent of Kintsugi, the Japanese art of porcelain repair, was a nice touch after Ren smashed it, but his mask needed a bigger story to accompany it. Although Albrekh, the Sith Alchemist and metalsmith, did an exceptionally good job on the finish. But yet again his fascinating character was wasted, and relegated to the realms of a silent bit part. Rens helmet remaining on would limit his character emotionally, and restrain some of those petulant outbursts but provide him with a boost of power and make him more relatable to his grandfather; who is probably the most popular character in the franchise. The sequel trilogy pretty well got the ‘copy and paste’ treatment of the Death Star with Starkiller bases destruction, so why not just give the same treatment to Ren with the Vader-esque helmet vibes.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What happens to all the dead bodies on a star wars ship after a battle has taken place?
Answer: That depends on what side the bodies were on before they perished. Usually after a battle in space the victor will either capture or kill any stragglers or survivors, and either abandon or scuttle the remains of the downed ships. As for the bodies aboard the ship,..and the ones floating around in space, well…if they're aligned with the Republic for instance the bodies will be collected, recorded and processed, then usually go on to be cremated or buried at a later date. Below; a deceased trooper after a space battle. If the deceased were Jedi then their bodies will be ceremonially cremated back at the Jedi Temple, but if they're clones then they will more than likely be put on ice and disposed of at a later date. If the deceased were Separatist soldiers or officers then they'll probably be left to freeze in the cold vacuum of space. Above; B1 Rocket Droids who routinely scoured the battlefields for survivors to kill. There are specialist droids that will scour the debris fields for any survivors, or corpses and inter the bodies for later disposal. The Separatist Alliance would send “mop up crews” after a space battle, and search for any lifepods that may have been ejected. Upon locating any survivors the B1 Rocket droids will use a massive device to pry the lifepod open,..and jettison the bodies into the void of space. Junkers and scrap dealers will also scan the now quiet battle fields of space junk fodder and look for anything of value; from weapons, parts, droids and on occasion…lifeless corpses. Above; Separatist droids ‘opening’ a Republic lifepod. Certain races in the SWU are cannibalistic, and if given the chance will eat organic beings; dead or alive. Races such as the Marits, the Rakatan, Collicoids, Zanibars and Trandoshans all consume human flesh, so after an enormous battle has concluded it wouldn't be strange to find aliens stealing corpses for later consumption. Above; Trandoshan Scavenger Gha Nachkt presenting R2-D2 to General Grievous. Gha Nachkt was a Trandoshan salvage captain who would search the debris and ships after a space battle, looking for scrap, parts, and droids. I bet if he found dead clonetroopers in the debris fields he'd more than likely take the corpses, skin them in Trandoshan tradition and then turn the bodies into space jerkey.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why didn’t Yoda and Kenobi do anything except wait in hiding for 20 years after ROTS?
Answer: After the Clones carried out Order 66 Yoda and Kenobi each accepted different roles as well as Bail Organa and his wife, and Owen and Beru Lars. They were six individuals who held the spark of hope alive quite literally. If there was was no one else privy who understood the gravity of seeing the Skywalker twins to maturity then all hope would just fade away. The Lars and Organa families became adopted parents to Luke and Leia, and raised them to become intelligent, thoughtful, and resourceful young people. Together these two children carried the legacy of the Jedi, and it's future. Kenobi became the protector of young Luke, and in time would lead him to his destiny. Yoda would become his master and teach him the ways of the force, and through Luke ensure the survival of the Jedi Order. For nearly two decades both Jedi masters had to lay low, as not to draw the attention of Vader and his Emperor. Kenobi drew the short end of the stick on that one, having to contend with Inquisitors and Vader himself. Yoda spent his exile pretty well avoiding the whole scene, and kicked back on Dagobah. But it was his role to come that was the most crucial. Kenobi had to ensure Lukes survival long enough until he could rationally get the teenager to realise his destiny. It just so happened that the events of Rogue One eventuated in his sister obtaining the link to fight the Empire. This would force Luke to step up and confront his father, which was the culmination of his training. But as I said previously Kenobi and his master had to keep a low profile until the time was right. This wasn't a plan, rather than Yoda and Kenobi relying on the force to guide them…and the Skywalker twins. The entire Jedi Order had been all but exterminated, and Kenobi and Yoda were about the only two surviors of the purge that could reignite the Jedi again. Their own survival was critical in ensuring this, and one of the only logical steps in both defeating Vader and the Emperor..and bringing forth the return of the Jedi.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did Darth Vader make promoting officers while executing their predecessors a habit?
Answer: When you or I have something that breaks down usually we might try and fix it or have it repaired. Not the Empire. If something broke down or fell into disarray the Galactic Empire would more often than not have the entire object, weapon, vehicle or whatever replaced immediately. The same can be said for Darth Vader, as he wasted no time at all on incompetent, weak or foolish officers. He also used his position of power, and the radius of fear that the darkside created to instil motivation, fear and unquestionable loyalty. Vader took this stance immediately and established dominance the first time he was presented by the Emperor to the upper echelons of the Imperial military. Out with the old and inferior, and in with whoever is next in line. This grim spectacle served as motivation to the rest of Vaders men, and was done in a bid to boost performance. Their deaths would serve as a reminder of who employed them to all onlookers,..and the high standards that Vader demanded. Admiral Ozzel, Captain Needa, and other unfortunate Imperials lost their station, and were replaced by the Sith Lord. This courtesy didn't just apply to the Imperial officers, but also untold numbers of Stormtroopers and support staff. Vader used tremendous fear and an ominous, unsettling mood to convey his intentions. Like his master, and every Sith before him, he used fear, anger, and hatred to empower himself in the darkside, and create an aura of “If I stuff up while the boss is over my shoulder…I'm a dead man.” Those Imperial officers that were replaced had outworn their rank and position. They had demonstrated ineptitude in their tenure as an Imperial officer, and were given ‘early retirement’ for their services to the Empire. We may see this a couple of times in the movies, but in the Darth Vader comics the dark lord disposes of officers and troopers as if he's trying to beat a personal best; or set some kind of twisted record for how many he can execute in a day. It's not as if the Empire couldn't replace them, and the line of officers eager to prove their worth to Vader was a very long one. Once again, Vader knew that there were many other officers keen to impress him, and that by making examples out of incompetency he would set a very high standard for all his officers. Sometimes Vader executed officers for betraying him.. Fear would be their greatest motivator to ensure that they don't get looked over, especially when the next promotion was imminent. Vaders influence would produce ruthless, efficient and ‘take no s#@%’ officers that were loyal to the Empire…but more importantly loyal to Vader himself.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Do you find violence in the Star Wars series funny?
Answer: Just take a look at this scene from, Return of the Jedi and tell me that it isn't funny. Even if you don't then you have to realise the target audience for this franchise; kids. If kids see the scene above, and it provokes joy, humour or laughs then the good people who create it have achieved their job. Ewoks are just one example of where violence within the SWU is viewed by the demographic audience as something they want to see. And if it comes across as ‘funny’ for them, then so be it. Ever since I was a kid I found the violence in star wars funny on occasions, and on other occasions I never liked its outcome. For example, in that scene from ROTJ, where an Ewok mourns over the loss of a fallen comrade, I found it hard to digest and it made me realise that the Empire was the true villain. Then whenever another Ewok took out a stormtrooper I found the violence appropriate, and funny again. Star Wars is a story of good versus evil, light versus dark…and sometimes violent moments in the saga are not appropriate to laugh at; such as the slaying of the younglings, or the death of Shmi Skywalker and the subsequent massacre of the Tusken Raiders. These moments are meant to convey great sadness, anger or upset emotions, but when an Ewok kills a stormtrooper we mostly find it funny because the little guy is just defending his home, albeit in a comical fashion. A lot of the violence is also staged to be funny, because as I said the target audience is young people and children. When we watch the Jedi mow down battledroids, and see their comical reactions, it's intended to be funny. This is why little boys, and girls, swing toy lightsabers around in joy, because they want to emulate the heroes and villains in the movie or series. Not all violence is intended to be funny in the franchise, as I mentioned previously…but without it most of the scenes would be stale and unappealing. It's called Star Wars, not Star peaceful negotiations. This is what the saga is all about; lightsaber duels, intergalactic space battles, monsters and cool planets. If the violence wasn't funny occasionally then the creators wouldn't be doing their jobs right.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What happened to Colonel Meebur Gascon after the Clone Wars and after the clones were decommissioned?
Answer: Colonel Meebur Gascon was a “map reader” who aided Republic forces during The Clone Wars. His miniscule size meant that he could access areas that regular clones and commanders could never dream of. He commanded a unit of droids during TCW, called D-Squad, and lead a successful mission at the time, much to the delight of his overseers at Republic Strategic Command. WAC-47, who was part of D-Squad, said that the squad had been assigned to Gascons platoon until the end of the war. Ultimately Gascon achieved his dream of attaining the rank of Brigadier General,..but what became of the tiny Zilken commander? His fate in canon lore is never revealed, but there was a legends comic strip, from Star Wars Insider #180, that portrayed a rather bleak and boring future for the tiny alien. In the comic strip Gascon ultimately ended up working in the customer service department of an astromech repair company. He just couldn't get work after The Clone Wars, and was forced to accept this new role in civilian life. The comic depicted Gascon fielding a customers calls using his telemarketer headset, and telling the customer “where to find the droids toggle switch”! Another interesting fact about the headstrong Zilken was that his concept sketch ideas came from scrapped ideas that would later evolve into Jar Jar Binks. Years later the production team who worked on The Clone Wars would revive these sketches, and rework them into the character of Meebur Gascon. It certainly would have been different having Gascon fill Binks’ role during the prequels and the animated series. Below; an early concept for Jar Jar Binks, that became the inspiration for Brigadier General Meebur Gascon. Source; Wookiepedia- Meebur Gascon Canon & Legends

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why was Luke surprised that Obi-Wan had fought in the Clone Wars in Star Wars New Hope?
Answer: Even the citizens of far off Tatooine had been affected by the impact of the Clone Wars, and nearly two decades after it's conclusion it's aftermath was still felt in many corners of the galaxy. Luke would have heard secondhand stories about the Clone Wars from his buddies like Biggs Darklighter, and older folks like his aunt and uncles generation. It was just like when World War II concluded, and for decades people spoke about it as if it was still fresh in their minds. For three years the galaxy was plunged into chaos and uncertainty, and billions lost their lives. It was one of the galaxies most devastating and ongoing conflicts that would stand in the memories of those who felt its impact. Luke certainly knew about it, but obviously had never met anyone who had directly served in the war. So when Kenobi mentioned that he had fought in the Clone Wars Luke was clearly suprised. Luke had only ever known Kenobi as “Old Ben”, the loner hermit who was one of his familys more obscure neighbours. In the teenagers mind Kenobi was just a strange old man dwelling on the fringes of society, and the young man had never assumed that once upon a time Ben may have been a soldier, a pilot,…or even a Jedi Knight. When Kenobi just casually mentioned that he had served in the conflict Lukes suprise reaction was totally justified. But little was he to know that very soon he would be propelled into the spotlight; and learn some even bigger suprises.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Before Hayden Christensen was chosen as Anakin in Episode 2, what other actors auditioned for the role of Anakin?
Answer: Charlie Hannam recently told Variety magazine that he blew his chance to play Anakin Skywalker, and that he was actually among the top three actors chosen for the upcoming role of a lifetime. He described his audition as being very awkward, and he was one of the few contenders in the part to meet George Lucas himself. His work in Pacific Rim, King Arthur and the long running series Sons of Anarchy was stellar acting, and he would have made for a brilliant Anakin. Just imagine this guy marching on the Jedi Temple in Revenge of the Sith. Other actors considered for the role, according to movieweb.com were Christian Bale from the Batman franchise and American Psycho,.. Paul Walker from The Fast and Furious saga,..James Van Der Beek from Dawsons Creek,.. and other actors that would go onto stardom in different projects such as Colin Hanks, Ryan Phillippe, Devon Sawa, Topher Grace and Chris Klein. Christian Bale and Charlie Hunnam would be my two favourite choices,..and just imagine some of the Sons of Anarchy bikie fuelled ultra-violence going down during Order 66.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is the scariest movie in the Star Wars universe?
Answer: Solo. Why? There are things in this movie that are absolutely terrifying to see, and to think about their deeper, darker, scarier implications. What am I talking about? I'll explain a couple of things from the movie, and then you can tell me that I'm wrong or not. Solo begins with a teenager stealing a car, after getting bashed and assaulted for stealing fuel,..and then he has to return to a filthy subterranean tenement building full of child captives and slaves, operated by an enormous aquatic worm. This cruel slaver was capturing and enticing children into a life of crime, and child abandonment, abuse and exploitation. Then when Han escapes Qi'ra is forced into an even more sinister crime syndicate, and went from child slavery to full time slavery. The Battle of Mimban itself was dark, ominous, filthy and terrifying. The Empire came to overthrow the locals, who had previously been their allies against Separatist forces during the Clone Wars. It was a muddy bloodbath for the Imperials, who were ill equipped for the guerilla tactics of the Mimbanese Resistance forces. And to make it worse the corrupt Imperial Mudtroopers were starving Chewbacca in a mud soaked pit, and letting him feed on the bodies of dead victims. They even placed bets on how long it would take for “The Beast” to kill his “fight to the death” opponent. Mimban was one of the more scarier campaigns that the Imperials waged, on a planet that wanted to slaughter them all. Kessel is just a giant spice refinery ran by the vicious criminal syndicate the Pykes, employing slaves that are “clipped and tagged”! It's basically a big drug lab using slaves to mine for intergalactic dope, run by murderous thugs. And to and from Kessel, if you stray from the designated flight paths, you could end up in a gigantic black hole that tears everything pulled into it apart. To make it worse there's a gargantuan space Kraken called the Summa Verminoth, that stalks the creepy regions of the Maw devouring unsuspecting starships,..that eventually has its skin slowly ripped off as it is torn apart by the violent black hole. The worst crime syndicate of all in Solo is Crimson Dawn, and Enfys Nest recalls the terrifying tale of how the gang cut the tongues out of all the men, women and children of a town that they were extorting for a precious commodity. Dryden Vos, who overseen the operations of Crimson Dawn, had slaves aboard his Yacht called ‘The Decraniated’. They were victims of insurgency attacks, that had been taken from the battlefields and turned into mindless slaves; missing the top half of their heads in bizarre cybernetic surgeries carried out by the sadistic Dr Evazan. Solo also has droid cage fighting, where unwitting droids are butchered by their opponents whilst drunken onlookers place cruel bets. We see more corrupt and brutal tactics employed by the Imperial forces, explore the grim realities of drugs, slavery and oppression, and explore some of the more darker, grittier sides to Star Wars that aren't detailed more in previous films. The movie itself has a darker vibe than the others in the saga, and some of the deeper implications at work here are truly scary. Slaves with only half a head, gigantic space squid, and drug lab workers forcibly having their testicles removed. Now you tell me that isn't scary.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What smallest and biggest change in Star Wars would have changed the entire stories outcome?
Answer: If R5-D4, from the beginning of A New Hope, never fried his motivator then the entire original trilogy simply wouldn't have happened. R2-D2 wouldn't have taken his place, delivered Princess Leias message and the plans of the Death Star to Kenobi. Luke stays on at his Uncles moisture farm for more than “just one more season”, Princess Leia is tried for treason against the Empire, which is just another way of saying “Tarkin has her executed, and then blows up Alderaan and Yavin IV”. This destroys most of the Rebel Alliance, leaving the Empire to crush the last resistance to their absolute rule over the galaxy. This is just one small change that would have completely affected the outcome of the OT, but what are some more examples. Imagine if Phoenix Squadron never took Ezra in,..or if Luke never managed to free his lightsaber from the ice on Hoth. Imagine what would have happened if Palpatine somehow didn't return, or if Rey never bypassed the compressor; or if Ben Solo returned to the light, and never killed his father Han Solo. Or even think of the outcome if Qui-Gon and Obi-Wan were never forced to land on Tatooine,..or if Palpatine was never elected into the office of Supreme Chancellor. What would have happened if Din Djarin never had a conscience on Nevarro, after delivery Grogu to the client, or if Luke never made his “one in a million” shot on the Death Star. What would have happened if Wookiees were used on Endor, or if Qui-Gon killed Darth Maul…or if Mother Talzin actually killed Dooku using Nightsister magicks? Imagine the outcome if Anakin got the high ground on Mustafar,..or if General Grievous got the low ground on Utapauu.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How effective would the Clone Army have been without Jedi generals?
Answer: By Mace Windu and Anakin Skywalkers own admissions, the Jedi were peacekeepers, not soldiers. They certainly weren't seasoned military generals with enough tactical, and battlefield experience to justify their positions as ‘Lords of War’. Mace Windu also personally stated that “there aren't enough Jedi to protect the Republic”, and in hindsight he was absolutely right. But after the first Battle of Geonosis the Jedi realised that the Clone Wars had left them with no other option; join the fray or perish under Separatist oppression. This pushed them over the line between peacekeepers and soldiers, and left the forces of the Grand Army of the Republic disadvantaged from the outset. Had the Galactic Republic opted to allow the Clone Commanders to personally coordinate the battle strategies of each conflict, then I believe the Republic military casualties after the conclusion of the Clone Wars would have been significantly less. Overall battlefield efficiency numbers would have favoured the clone armies..had they been left to their own will. Don't get me wrong, the Jedi helped turn the tide of battles time and time again, so would have been more suited in a support role during the conflict. The Clone Commanders, had they been given the role of military generals would have been more conscious of the projected casualties of each battle…and therefore more lives would have been spared. When we watch Tartakovskys '03 Clone Wars we see exactly how effective Clone Commanders were on the battlefield without Jedi Generals to take orders from. Clone Trooper Commanders, such as Rex, Cody, Bacara, Bly, Neyo, Blackout, Havoc, Wolffe and Gree had all proven their military expertise early during the war, because that's what they were trained for. Original ARC Troopers were personally instructed by Jango Fett himself, and given a lifetime of military expertise and planning provided by their Kaminoan overseers and other highly skilled bounty hunters. They were bred to not only win wars, but do it in the most effective and efficient manner conceived. The Jedi had no need to personally coordinate battles, especially when they paid for the services of the Clone troopers. The Jedi, albeit light years ahead in skill, were too familiar and accustomed to the role of peacekeepers. The onset of the war thrust them out of their comfort zone and into unfamiliar territory. Sure, they'd solved intergalactic conflicts many times in the centuries previous, but the Clone Wars spread their numbers too thin across the galaxy. This was part of Darth Sidious’ bigger plan, because he knew that when the time came to execute Order 66 the Jedi would be vulnerable, weak..and in no position to mount an offensive.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Do you know what the biggest and smallest ships are in the Star Wars franchise?
Answer: The difference between the largest Star Wars ship, and the smallest, are enormous in contrast,..and make each other look ridiculous in comparison. In Canon lore one of the biggest ships ever to grace the screen was Supreme Leader Snokes the Supremacy, and in Legends was the mighty Eclipse Class Dreadnought baring the same name. The Supremacy, a Mega Class Star Dreadnought with over two million crew, measured in at a gargantuan 60,542 metres in width, and over 13,000 metres in height. The Eclipse, also classified as a Space Station, measured in smaller, but at a respective 17,500 metres..making these two behemoths two of the largest vessels to ever jump into hyperspace. Now even though some battle stations are equipped with hyperdrives, they aren't really starships in the traditional sense; but examples such as both Death Stars, from A New Hope, and Return of the Jedi respectively, make the aforementioned vessels look miniscule in comparison. Then we jump into the realms of planetary sized monsters, with the introduction of Starkiller Base in The Force Awakens. Standing up at an immense 660 kilometres in diameter, this colossal planet turned superweapon was one of the most impressive feats of intergalactic engineering ever pulled off by Palpatines lackeys. Above; Starkiller Base from ‘The Force Awakens’ Now nudging back to the small scale vessels in the Star Wars Universe, the Jedi Starfighters of the late Republic era were classified as among some of the smallest ships in the galaxy. The ETA 2 Actis-class light interceptor was the Jedi Orders fighter of choice, and Grand Master Yoda had a smaller, modified version of the swift little ship. Above; Yodas modified ETA 2 Actis-class Starfighter Even Kaminoan flight pods were classed as starships, because they had a functional hyperdrive installed on board, and were but a mere claustrophobic bubble that encased the occupant. We see these tiny ships multiple times throughout The Clone Wars, and even Asajj Ventress and General Grievous escape the Battle of Kamino in one. Above; a Kamino Flight pod. But something that we've never seen a mention in SW canon lore are ships belonging to some of the smallest races in the galaxy. Yoda was small, but races such as the Zilkens, the Anzellans, and the Patatites made the Jedi Master look like Shaquille O'Neil in comparison. Colonel Meebur Gascon was a Zilken who served as a “map reader” during The Clone Wars, and was so tiny in size that he could actually fit inside an astromech droid. The Patatites, who hailed from Patatite Pattuna, were very adept at repairing spacecraft, as we see in TCW. They repaired R2-D2 and C-3P0's Y-Wing before setting them on their way. This suggests that these tiny beings were familiar with starship travel. Above; The Patatites, in ‘The Clone Wars’ season four, episode ‘Nomad Droids’ Then we have the teeny weeny Anzellans, who are about the size of a kids action figure. We first meet one, Babu Frik, in the sequel trilogy, and an Anzellan Droid Repair shop can be seen in the third season of The Mandalorian. Din Djarin even had a hard time squeezing into their incy wincy repair shop. Above; An Anzellan droid repair technician. These three races were very small compared to Master Yodas, and I can't help but wonder what tiny little ancestral spacecraft these diminutive aliens possessed. Those vessels would certainly have been the smallest in the whole galaxy,..even compared to Yodas or the Kaminoans.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What would happen if the separatist leaders had B2 battle droids or commando droids with them/defending them at Mustafar while Darth Vader was killing them would it even matter?
Answer: Not in the slightest. In fact it would only fuel Vaders rage empowering him further in the darkside,..and just give him more practice during his new apprenticeship. Sidious deliberating sent all the Separatist Council to the relative safety of Mustafar, so he had all his eggs in the one basket when the time came to dropping them from a cliff. It was a massacre, as opposed to a last stand, so the introduction of B2 Battle Droids and Commando Droids would matter very little to the enraged Sith Lord. He had just callously slaughtered his brothers and sisters at the Jedi Temple, and had been instrumental in Darth Sidious' bloodbath from the moment Sidious first laid eyes on him. He turned his back on all that he ever held dear, fuelled his newfound anger and rage, and unleashed it upon the galaxy for all to see. Droids were completely irrelevant to him, and in a short time he would learn that the Sith use lethal training droids to practice and hone their deadly skills. The B2s wouldn't stand a snowflakes chance in hell against Vader, and despite the Commando Droids being far more lethal than their burly counterparts..they don't really stand a chance against Vader. Remember the scene where Vader was reborn at the end of ROTS, and he destroyed the entire room; droids and all? This would be just a crash course for Vader to please his new master, and just a mere test in the larger scope of ‘Imperial’ affairs. Even if the Separatist leaders bought an entire battalion of droids at their back Vader would only relish at their pitiful destruction.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What alternate scenarios would you want to see in a Star Wars What if series?
Answer: Here's a few. Instead of Jango Fett being chosen as the clone template it is Cad Bane, or Durge, or even Aurra Sing. In the Star Wars: What If series we could feature an episode where it explores the possibilities of having different bounty hunters take Jango Fetts stead as the Kaminoans main clone template. Imagine Kenobi and Skywalker being all chummy with Cad Bane clonetroopers, and fighting alongside them in battle. Imagine Durge was the template, and his clones could utilise his Gen'Dai physiology and take out swathes of battledroids in a single swing. Imagine having legions of female clonetroopers all cloned from the lethal Aurra Sing. She'd certainly be a sight to see, as thousands of her destroy B1s on the field. She may have been female, but her skills were legendary, and she was the one who gave Boba his headstart in the game. Here's another one. We've all heard of the Joe Schreiber novel Deathtroopers, well..imagine a version of that only instead of being set on an abandoned Imperial prison frigate..its set on Hoth in the aftermath of the Imperial assault on Echo base. Now here's the twist; instead of the villains being zombie stormtroopers they're actually zombie Wampas and Tauntauns! Imagine hordes of undead Wampas stalking and hunting Imperial Snowtroopers. It would be something like John Carpenters The Thing,..only undead monsters on Hoth, instead of a psychotic alien changeling in the Antarctic. Another alternate scenario for a Star Wars: What If series would be an episode that follows The Bendu from birth, and details his unbelievable life up until he meets Kanan Jarrus,..or something similar that portrays the childhood of ‘The Ones’ brother and sister, and how as children their powers were astronomical. The same series could reveal the origins of the nightmarish Abeloth;..and another possible alternative scenario is a Jedi exploration team sent to survey and explore Dagobah; 100's of years before Yoda ever set foot there. It would be creepy to have a long forgotten Sith spirit, dwelling deep within the cave from The Empire Strikes Back, who controls the menagerie of deadly creatures on the eerie swamp planet;…and systematically hunt down the Jedi one by one using vicious beasts. All of these aforementioned ideas would certainly make for interesting episodes on a SW What If series, but if you actually think about it…the possibilities here are mind blowing.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: In the genocide of the Jedi in Revenge of the Sith, what happened to the Jedi whose parents didn’t let them take them?
Answer: These children would have been noted down somewhere in the Jedi archives, but after Darth Sidious issued Order 66 it was only Jedi that were targeted during The Great Purge. It wouldn't have been until after the ascendancy of the new Galactic Empire that Palpatine and his Inquisitorious would actively seek and hunt these youngsters. If Palpatine could obtain another holocron with the names of force sensitive children, like he did during The Clone Wars, then these force sensitive children would only have one option left; give themselves to the will of the Emperor or die. No exceptions. Obi-Wan is assisted by Kawlan Roken during the Kenobi series, and he recounts the story of how his wife was force sensitive;..and how the Inquisitors hunted her down. He portrays a very bleak future for any force sensitives after the rise of the Empire. Eeth Koth was killed by Inquisitors and his child was personally taken by Vader, and Luminara Unduli was rumoured to have been killed by the Grand Inquisitor himself. More fell to their blades, but there would have been children who would have escaped the aftermath of the purge. One particular Jedi youngling, the Wookiee Gungi, survived Order 66, despite later ending up in the hands of slavers. Then there were also the force sensitive children who didn't make the grade to padawan. These children were supervised by a Jedi body called The Council of Reassignment, and it's uncertain of these particular kids fate. It's almost certain that children who remained with their parents would have been overseen by this same council, and you can bet Sidious would have tried to get his hands on this particular list,…if he already didn't.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Do you think Darth Maul suffered more than Darth Vader?
Answer: Maul was practically born into the Sith, and separated from his mother while he was a very small boy. His suffering began from that day forward; Darth Vader had more than two decades before Darth Sidious did the same to him, as he did to Maul. But in my opinion Mauls torment and suffering just outweighed Vaders, despite what many of you may think. But I believe that it was this suffering that both Sith Lords used to catapult themselves into the Sith Lord Hall of Fame. Both were two of the most aggressive fighters the Sith had produced, and as a result of their compounded emotions their suffering transformed them into pure forces of nature. Taken as a small child Mauls suffering was something that he began to endure at a far younger age than Skywalker did. Born into the Nighbrothers he is tested from birth in skills such as agility, strength, cunning, and speed. His daily life would have been tormenting enough before Sidious took him away to begin his Sith training on Mustafar. But after that his life became a nightmare of pain, torture and suffering. His cruel master Sidious would have him beaten, use force lightning on him, deliberately push him to anger, and punish him for the slightest mishap during his tenure as a young Sith apprentice. Gruelling training regimes against lethal training droids, starvation, exposure to extreme temperatures, brutal obstacle courses and more demeaning methods were used to break Mauls spirit. Whereas in Skywalkers case Sidious basically just dangled an illusion in front of him, and turned him to the darkside using more diabolical psychological methods. Vaders suffering began when he started to have visions of his mother dieing, but Mauls began when he was mentally and physically tortured upon entering the Sith as a mere boy. Maul was stolen from his family, broken, moulded and fashioned into a servant of evil. Then he was abandoned on a whim and left for dead on a filthy junk and garbage planet. Here Mauls suffering truly propelled him into the depths of madness, and despite his mother literally removing his 10 years of languishing in the dark..he never truly recovers from his extended ordeal on Lotho Minor; coupled with his obsession for Kenobi. He becomes utterly consumed by revenge and personally admits that it was the thought of it that kept him alive. This is a theme that will grip Maul until the very end. Maul never redeems his spirit and dies still in the grip of a terrible rage. Vader has an epiphany upon seeing Sidious frying his son to the brink of death, and returns to the light. Mauls suffering highlights how much pure vengeance, abandonment and a different kind of rage, than Vaders, twisted him as a man. Mauls suffering took him to darker places psychologically, to the point of no return. It was the good still in Vader that Padme spoke of that eventually came to the surface again, and helped him redeem himself in the end. Any good that Maul had probably died years before Skywalker even became a Jedi Knight.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is a Stormtrooper's armor effective against? I just watched a teddy bear with a walking stick take down a fully armored Stormtrooper. I've also noticed that they can't take more than a single laser blast without dying.
Answer: Stormtrooper armour was officially stated as being effective against “protecting the wearer against glancing and low power blaster bolts”. Low power blaster bolts. The weapons usually used by factions of the Rebel Alliance, and other individuals with ill opinions of the Empire, were high power blasters that could easily penetrate the armour. Rebels such as Han Solo, Sabine Wren, Baze Malbus all used weapons that certainly exceeded the definition of low power blaster bolts, so this can easily explain why the Stormtroopers 18 piece armour set often looked inferior during combat. It was manufactured by the Imperial Department of Military Research and typically made from white plastoid. The armour usually gets a bad rep in most Star Wars media, with people saying it's far too inferior for the most powerful fighting forces in the entire galaxy, but it was actually some of the best armour in the Empire. Beneath the armour was a vacuum sealed body glove that adjusted to the wearers body temperature. The suit of armour could support the wearer for short periods in the vacuum of space, and protect against harsh environments of differing terrains and temperatures. But how did the ‘Teddy Bears’ penetrate this armour with such ease? These Teddy bears exploited the weaknesses and limits of the Stormtroopers armour with tactical efficiency, because they were already used to facing far tougher foes than some glammed up appetisers in white shells. The Ewoks on Endors Moon were like guerrilla fighters utilising traps, and hit and run tactics, then blending into their home environment. The armour worn by the Imperials had its tolerances and protective limits, and the Ewoks instantly realised that strikes to gaps between the armour were extremely effective at bringing down these intergalactic interlopers. Also, the armour was only effective against glancing shots and blows, not direct hits from heavy weapons. With enough blunt force a sharp edge could pierce the plastoid exterior of the armour, leaving the Stormtroopers inside vulnerable to the Ewoks clubs, axes, rocks, spears and arrows. The traps that the Ewoks used against the AT-STs and Stormtroopers weren't originally intended for the minions of the Empire; instead they were strategically placed to take down a far worse threat. A threat that the Empire would have assumed would make quick work of these unassuming forest dwellers. The mighty Gorax of Endors moon stood at nearly 9 metres tall, and could hurl boulders like a football. It was the apex predator of the moon, and the biggest threat the Ewoks had dealt with for untold generations. It was a nocturnal hunter, leading vicious raids in the middle of the night to capture, kill and eat the Ewoks. To combat this towering giants the adaptive Ewoks not only built their homes in high treetop canopies, but built concealed ground defences to stop or delay the terrifying Gorax from attacking their homes. When the Empire rocked up without an invitation they just didn't know who they were actually dealing with; and completely underestimated an already well equipped and lethally prepared combatant. This proved to be one of the Empires most embarrassing engagements. Source; Wookiepedia-Stormtrooper armour, and Wookiepedia-Gorax.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What if General Grevious’s ship exploded, killing Grevious, Palpatine, Anakin, Dooku, and Obi-Wan all at once?
Answer: The Invisible Hand, General Grievous’ flagship at the time he abducts Supreme Chancellor Palpatine…explodes in the upper atmosphere over the galactic capital of Coruscant, in the year 19 BBY. Aboard at the time are the Separatist Commander General Grievous, Count Dooku, Jedi Knight Anakin Skywalker, Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi, and the Supreme Chancellor himself. The Clone Wars effectively come to an intergalactic cease fire momentarily, as the Confederacy of Independent Systems loses its top leadership, and the Galactic Republic is devastated by the loss of the Supreme Chancellor, and two of the Jedi Orders greatest generals. The destruction of The Invisible Hand bought forth tremendous upheaval on both sides of the conflict,..and left the door open for possible peace at last in the galaxy. This scenario is very difficult to predict how it will ultimately pan out, but the death of the five aforementioned individuals will leave a power vacuum that will leave the galaxy holding its breath. The Galactic Republic will need to re-elect a new Supreme Chancellor; possibly a candidate like Bail Organa winning the seat. But Mas Amedda, who served in the Chancellors office, may have other ideas. In said event Palpatine may have already issued the Chagrian with contingency orders in the event of his death. Or he might just act like he did when the Rebel Alliance overthrew the Empire, and surrender the seat of office to a legal successor. But then again, there may be other figures who step up to challenge rule of the galaxy. Maul may seize this opportunity, and as we know from The Clone Wars he was privy to at least some of Palpatines plan. We're also certain that he was aware of Order 66, and through the comics we have ascertained that not only the Supreme Chancellor could activate the order to the clones. In Marvels Dark Vader #17 we see two Jedi use Order 66 against a team of Imperial Inquisitors, so Maul using the same idea may use it to his,..and Mother Talzins advantage. That's just one of many different scenarios that could possibly occur. But with the loss of Darth Sidious/Supreme Chancellor Palpatine comes the ability for the Republic to rule without the looming spectre of a Sith Lord hanging above its head like a guillotine. Palpatines emergency powers are stripped upon his fiery death, freeing up the Senate to return to honest democracy. The Jedi Council will have to elect two new members following the loss of Kenobi and Skywalker, and the Separatist Alliance will have a power struggle for supreme leadership. The Droid General Kalani, or another Separatist general, may assume control of the fleets and armies of the CIS…but now without Palpatine the Intergalactic Banking Clan, who provided Darth Sidious with all his financial backing, would immediately back out. The CIS and Galactic Republic may make reparations towards each other and ensue for galactic peace,..seeing as how the Empire will never be. This leaves the fate of the Skywalker twins in their mothers hands, for now Padmes lifeforce isn't drained from her when giving birth. Her will to live is strong, and so is that of her new son and daughter; Leia and Luke. Yoda trains them upon learning of their connections to the force, and so the saga continues…

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did Cad Bane and General Grievous ever meet?
Answer: Although they came very close to meeting during The Clone Wars, these two Separatist sympathisers never actually met in the flesh. Both Cad Bane and General Grievous worked heavily with the Confederacy of Independent Systems during the war. Grievous controlled the might of the CIS fleets and armies, and Bane worked extensively with Count Dooku on specific jobs. It's actually surprising that these two psychopaths didn't cross paths, seeing as how each of them interacted heavily with other Separatist agents such as Dooku, Ventress and Sidious himself. Grievous controlled vast fleets of Separatist warships and destroyers, and on one occasion Sidious tasked Cad Bane with capturing a Jedi and extracting knowledge from him. To do this Sidious gave Bane control of a small fleet of Munificent Class Star Frigates, and C9979 Landing Craft that Bane commanded personally. Bane coordinated an aerial bombardment and ground assault of the planet Devaron as a distraction to capture Jedi Master Bolla Ropal. Bane tortured and killed the unfortunate Jedi, and Grievous also fought and killed Jedi Knight Nahdar Vebb on the third moon of Vassek, so each of them controlled Separatist fleets, worked for Count Dooku and Darth Sidious, and killed Jedi for the thrill. But maybe Darth Sidious prevented them from ever meeting, seeing as how if the good general and the bounty hunter ever got chatting about their employer Sidious might have something to actually be concerned about. Bane even got a hold of a lightsaber once and attacked..Kenobi, so himself and Grievous really have something to chat about.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why does Jabba the Hutt live in what looks like a medieval palace if he has tons of money? Wouldn't he live in a more advanced looking place in a Galaxy such as Star Wars? Shouldn't Jabba update his real estate?
Answer: Jabba the Hutt lives in an ancient B’omarr Monk monastery, that the ancient order built prior to 700 BBY. The reason why Jabba lives here is simple; he is beyond the reach of the Galactic Republic on Tatooine, and it is ideally located to carry out his criminal operations unheeded by the eyes of the galaxy. Tatooine provided Jabba with enough distance from Coruscant and the core worlds, and his conniving family on their homeworld of Nal Hutta. As we see in The Phantom Menace slavery existed on Tatooine, which Jabba exploited wholly. But the former sandrock and durasteel monastery, which he transformed into a palace, had a previous occupant that first began upgrading the Hutts future residence. Above; Alkhara the bandit After over 150 years of solitude out in the vastness of Tatooine the B'omarr monks were going to be laid seige by a pirate named Alkhara. Instead the monks willingly opened their doors to the outcast and his small army, and so Alkhara and his men stayed there for the next 34 years. In that time he upgraded the monastery extensively, beefing up security measures, extending the labyrinth of corridors and living quarters, defensive battlements, and even built torture chambers and dungeons. His largest addition was a nine story communications tower which he named after himself. Then Jabba came along and seized the monastery from Alkhara in 516 BBY. Jabba the Hutt then beefed up security even more, and transformed it into his personal palace and base of operations. He covered the outside of the palace in ditanium, which is highly resistant to blaster fire and bombing strikes, and most typically used in military structures. Finally a thick durasteel door was installed at the entrance to the palace, and a vast hangar and maintenance bay was installed to house his fleet of vehicles. Deep in the bowels of the palace was also a holy room installed by the monks, where they would cast the bodies of their ‘enlightened’ colleagues into a “seemingly bottomless pit”. During The Clone Wars it took Maul and his Shadow Syndicate, complete with Deathwatch Mandalorians, to breach Jabbas defences. Jabba lived here relatively uninterrupted for centuries before Luke Skywalker showed up, and he obviously had everything that he needed there. He had no reason to live in a ‘more advanced looking place’ because the Hutt didn't care about marble floors, inground spas, and diamond chandeliers. He was a crimelord, a gangster, and more importantly..a Hutt. His number one priority was keeping his criminal empire growing, and not the quality of silk sheets in his opulent boudoir. Jabbas palace provided enough protection for him from the outside, for it was the seedy denizens inside of his court that presented a bigger threat to the ganster. Coincidentally his uncle, Ziro the Hutt, owned another B'omarr monastery on the planet Teth, where he once kidnapped Jabba's son Rotta and held him there during the early days of the Clone Wars. So it seems the Hutts are quite fond of B'omarr monasteries and their secrets.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Can Darth Nihilus turn to the light side?
Answer: Darth Nihilus became a Sith Lord after surviving the global devastation of a superweapon during the era of the Old Republic. The Mass Shadow Generator superweapon was unleashed on Malachor V, and created such a destructive spatial phenomenon that the shadow it cast destroyed everything on the planet; except for Nihilus. As a direct result of this he became a ‘wound’ in the force, and inadvertently craved the Force Energy created by living beings. Ultimately this craving would possess Nihilus, and without even realising he would drain the life from everything living. A Sith Lord, Darth Traya, taught Nihilus how to feed on the force but eventually he and another Dark apprentice overthrew their former master, severed her connection to the force..and exiled her. He became so immensely consumed by his hunger that he had to actually call upon the darkside to contain his spirit within his mask and robes. Darth Nihilus embodied the very essence of the darkside, and became consumed by its fury. He and Darth Sion conceived a plan to purge the Jedi, and bought the entire Order to its knees. Nihilus fed on entire planets, draining the life from every living soul,..and each time he fed his thirst for living souls increased. Whenever Nihilus did this it stopped his traumatic memories for a brief period, but then acted as a narcotic and made The Lord of Hunger crave relentlessly. The Sith Order to him was just a means to an end, and he didn't care one bit about their lineage, history or status. He lived only to feed on the force, and embraced the darkside wholly. He was a threat to all life in the galaxy, and was so steeped in the darkside that he became the living embodiment of it. If Nihilus ever even thought of turning to the light, the immense dark within him would most likely quash that motion in a heartbeat. The Darkside controlled him, and not the other way around. It was virtually impossible for Nihilus to turn to the light, as the dark absolutely guided all his actions. One of the only ways that he could turn to the light would have been to somehow use his powerful ability, Force Severe,…on himself; but that would be a death sentence for him, because it was the darkside that kept his very spirit held together.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did Obi-Wan's burns sustained during his mission to rescue young Leia cause permanent damage similar to what Vader suffered on Mustafar?
Answer: The burn injuries that Kenobi suffered at the hands of his former padawan were absolutely nothing, and only superficial compared to the horrific injuries that Skywalker recieved on Mustafar. On the planet Mapuso, when Vader finally caught up with Kenobi, the Sith Lord seized a moment that he would relish. An Imperial garrison was set up here to oversee the mining operations for the valuable mineral Vintrium. This mineral was a highly valuable ore, but also highly flammable. When Vader realised this he uses his lightsaber to ignite the spilt Vintrium on the ground, between himself and Kenobi. This set the strewn minerals ablaze, and that's when Vader uses the force to pull Kenobi into the flames. Although Kenobi screams in pain, and is clearly injured from his harrowing ordeal, he is rescued by Tala Durith and within a short time is placed in a Bacta Tank to heal his burns. Kenobi only burned for a short period of time, but Vader suffered such horrific burns that the healing qualities of the Bacta could only superficially assist. After he completed healing Kenobi didn't bare any visible scars from his attack, yet Vader regularly required bacta baths due to the extensive nature of his injuries. Bacta cannot grow back limbs, nor completely heal extremely damaged skin tissue.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Would Dr Doom make a great Star Wars villain?
Answer: Dr Doom from the MCU would make a great Star Wars villain, but there's already a character directly based on the Infamous iron man. Clone Commander Doom was a battle scarred veteran of the Clone Wars, introduced during the sixth season of TCW, and was assigned to Jedi Generals Tiplar and Tiplee. His most notable appearance was during the Battle of Ringo Vinda, against Separatist leader Admiral Trench. Doom led his men, dubbed the ‘Doom Unit’, against overwhelming Separatist forces, and utilised weaponry different to other units. They were armed with Z-6 Rotary Blast Cannons, Electromagnetic pulse grenades, and personally designed M3 Bulwark Blast Shields that were all used to tremendous effect. But it was his striking green and metallic themed armour that is directly reminiscent of the villain Dr Doom. But on the other hand the good doctor himself would have made an excellent supervillain within the SWU. His knowledge of arcane magic and science, coupled with his diabolical invention engineering skills, would make him a fascinating opponent against the Jedi and the Sith alike. He could align himself with the Separatist Alliance and create weapons of mass, intergalactic destruction,..or actually oppose the Sith and replace their images with giant statues of himself! He has unlimited potential as a supervillain within the SWU, and his ego could easily outmatch that of Darth Sidious. A confrontation between Doomie and Palps would be a very interesting conflict indeed. And if Dr Doom somehow managed to defeat The Emperor the galaxy would look like one gargantuan shrine dedicated to the worship of Latverias most notorious export.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: A lot of people wonder how Reva survived after being stabbed by Vader, I kinda wonder myself. But this one question that a friend and I have been wondering and it is how did Reva get off of Jabiim and went to Tattooine after being left by the Empire?
Answer: Reva Sevander, The Third Sister of the Inquisitorious, had only one agenda on her mind, and that was the murder of Darth Vader at her hands. Even though the Grand Inquisitor dubbed her as ‘the least’ of all of them Reva proved that she was superior to each and every one of them. But how did she survive being run through with Vaders lightsaber, and how did she get to Tatooine before Kenobi? I can't answer the latter but I can tell you how she survived and persevered. When Reva attempted to kill the Grand Inquisitor she was actually trying to get closer to Vader in order to kill him. But the Grand Inquisitor, just like Darth Maul, used their tremendous knowledge of the darkside, coupled with pure rage and sheer will to survive being almost killed with a lightsaber. Maul survived being bisected, and Vader himself survived multiple amputations and burning up near a river of molten lava. The Grand Inquisitor survived in a similar fashion, using anger and his will to rise above imminent death. Reva was superior to her darkside colleagues, in that she eventually returned to the light side out of fear of becoming the one thing that she despised most. But when she survived her former employees blade she was still consumed by the darkside. The rage, fury and blind anger she possessed helped her overcome death, and filled her with new purpose. After finding a holoprojector that revealed Luke was Vaders son Reva found new purpose to live, and intended to kill Luke, out of revenge for Vader killing the only family she ever had; her Jedi brothers and sisters. How she was able to get to Tatooine before Kenobi is never explained, but it was anger and the darkside that gave her the ability to survive Vaders attack. The planet Jabiim itself was an Imperial mining outpost stripping the planet of its precious ore. Imperial vehicles were stationed everywhere on the planet because of this, and it's possible that Reva was able to use her Imperial identity to gain access to a ship. This would explain how she was able to get to Tatooine, to confront the Lars family and Kenobi.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why do a lot of wikis like "Pure Evil" Wiki lie and say General Grievous is a "villain" when he's a hero?
Answer: ‘Pure Evil’ Wikipedia is a community site that anyone can contribute to, a lot like many other Star Wars informative and fan based sites, but General Grievous is stated as a villain because he is one; even though this was not always the case. For the sake of Revenge of the Sith, and The Clone Wars General Grievous’ character is one of the main antagonists, and is portrayed as an evil, cybernetic nightmare who controlled the vast droid armies of the Separatist Alliance. Darth Sidious pitted the Separatist Alliance against the Galactic Republic as part of his diabolical plan for intergalactic domination, and as the Jedi are depicted as the heroes and defenders of the Republic,..the Separatist Alliance were depicted as the villains in the conflict. Despite most of the Separatists being normal, peaceful citizens of the galaxy, just like Republic citizens, The Clone Wars divided the galaxy in two. It just so happened that Grievous was on the side of the perceived ‘bad guys’, and you have to admit that his role during the Clone Wars was one of a maniacal, bloodthirsty, Jedi killing whirlwind of ultra violence,..but as I mentioned before this wasn't always the case. Before Grievous joined the Intergalactic Banking Clan, and then underwent his transformation and agreed to work for the Separatists he was a proud Kaleesh General, defending his home planet from vicious, insectoid invaders called the ‘Huk’. Before he reinvented himself as Grievous he was called Qymaen Jai Sheelal, and after his home suffered devastating attacks from the Huk he and his brave soldiers fought several large battles that drove them from Kallee. The Huk lied and petitioned the Jedi and the Republic for help, despite themselves being the instigators and aggressors towards the Kaleesh people. Before Grievous and his leadership could respond the heartless Jedi annexed his planet, dooming thousands of his kindred to cruelly starve to death. Then to make matters worse the Huk ambushed and murdered his partner and lover, Ronderu; discarding her corpse into the sea. Now some say that General Grievous responded far to harshly against the Huk, wiping them out by the hundreds of thousands in retaliation for invading and slaughtering his innocent people,…but if you were in his position how would you respond? Would you just go quietly into the night…or would you avenge those who you loved and cherished? After ‘improving’ himself through ridding himself of his weak, organic body in exchange for a nearly indestructible version, he tried to make himself a Jedi killing machine out of anger, remorse, and for them callously betraying his people; despite calling themselves defenders of the galaxy. Yes, Grievous committed atrocious acts during the Clone Wars, but he was pushed to the brink of insanity by brutal, murderous scum who killed all of his family and loved ones. His brain chemistry was also altered, by Dooku and the Intergalactic Banking Clan, to make him more violent and aggressive than he previously was. The Jedi made Grievous who he was out of their arrogance, but it was the Sith who utilised him as a weapon. This story is completely neglected in ROTS and TCW, and most fans are uncertain as to what Grievous’ life was like before Dooku and Sidious utterly ruined it. So after all is said and done the only depiction of Grievous, that everyone was presented with in Revenge of the Sith, and The Clone Wars, was that of a murderous ‘villain’…if you want to judge a book by its cover that is.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: If you can make a base in Star Wars, where would you build it? What equipment would you have? What starfighters would you use?
Answer: The perfect base already exists, so I wouldn't have to build it,…and it was personally designed to keep people out, and also to prevent people from ever leaving alive. This base was once owned by one of the most fearsome entities in the entire galaxy, and served as his hidden fortress; complete with booby traps and a massive ‘guard dog’ named Gor. Built into the rockface of a deep, expansive gorge and surrounded in fog this impressive castle could serve me as a base, a fortress..and a very impressive home to boast about. On the third moon of the planet Vassek lays a massive, concealed fortress, completely shrouded in fog and nearly undetectable to the naked eye. This enormous, ominous looking castle was once home to the infamous Separatist leader General Grievous. It would make for a perfect, hidden base…and is already stocked with equipment that would suffice. Grievous had a complement of IG-100 Magnaguards, which if equipped with T-7 Ion Disruptors would make for excellent sentries. Of course I'd have to beef up the already bolstered security measures, which already included a molten incinerator trap hidden beneath the floor, and other various concealed traps. It also had a central control room to keep everything in check. As for my starfighter, well..Grievous had a custom Bellbulab-22 Heavy Starfighter, manufactured by Feethan Ottraw Scaleable Assemblies, dubbed Soulless One. This impressive vessel boasted Triple Rapid fire laser cannons and was coated in Impervium. If modified correctly, its armaments were improved and it's Class 2 Hyperdrive was upgraded, it would serve as a perfect Starfighter, to complement my perfect base. Plus Grievous had some classy garden statues going on at his place which added that “homely” appeal, so a few indoor plants, some mood lighting, and maybe a fountain would spruce the old place up.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Does Jabba the Hutt realize that Darth Vader is Anakin Skywalker, the little boy who won the pod race?
Answer: Jabba the Hutt probably wouldn't have remembered who won a pod race more than 30 years prior to when he met Luke Skywalker, and he most definitely would have kept this secret from Jabba at all costs. There's nothing to suggest that the Hutt knew Anakin Skywalker was the second most powerful being in the galaxy, despite the fact that Vader once rescued his son Rotta during the Clone Wars. Rotta was kidnapped by Dooku in a bid to destabilise relationships between the Republic and the Hutts, but Anakin and Ahsoka were tasked with returning the 55 year old infant back to his crimelord father. During the reign of the Empire Jabba became aware that Luke was Vaders son, meanwhile he was completely unaware that Vader was once the great Jedi Knight Anakin Skywalker. It's uncertain if Jabba remembered little Anakin Skywalker, when years later he became a Jedi and saved his son, but then again if Jabba knew Darth Vaders identity I don't think he'd be foolish enough to let the Sith Lord know. You might assume that Jabba may have used this juicy information as leverage against Vader, but the Hutt didn't control Tatooine by being headstrong and stupid. When Jabba eventually learned that Luke was Vaders son the Hutt was genuinely suprised that anyone of decent reputation was ever born on Tatooine, suggesting that he had no clue about Vader,…and his strong, very familiar ties to the desert planet. But I'm guessing that if Jabba knew how he was going to die he would have killed Skywalker immediately after rescuing Rotta.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Is there anyone in the Star Wars universe more evil than Palpatine?
Answer: Maybe not compared to the grand scale of Palpatines evil machinations, but there are some pretty twisted individuals in the Star Wars Universe that warrant mentioning due to their infamous and despicable deeds. Let's take a look at one particular evil little sod, who operated at the beginning of the formation of the Galactic Empire; Dr Cornelius Evazan. Beginning his career as a talented plastic surgeon he took a dark turn and began getting “creative” with his patients surgery,..and soon left a slew of deformed and disfigured victims in his wake. Ultimately he ended up on the wrong end of a bounty hunters wrath and got his own face disfigured as some kind of cosmic Karma. You'd think someone of Evazans low standing character would stop after that, and for getting convicted for his crimes, but instead he teamed up with a brutish Aqualish named Ponda Baba and the two racked up death penalties on various systems they ‘operated’ in. Evazan, in a bid to evade intergalactic authorities, became a personal physician to Crimson Dawn crime boss Dryden Vos,..and sunk to even lower depths after creating personal slaves for Vos dubbed ‘The Decraniated’. Evazan and Baba would snatch bodies from battle fields, or just kidnap unsuspecting victims, and remove the top portion of their heads from the eyes up. He would then implant a cybernetic interface to control them, and upon completing the surgery they lost all free will and became soulless, organic droids,..free for Vos to command at will. Dryden Vos himself was also another heavy contender for being more evil than Palpatine, and just another atrocious individual in the same vein as the Sith Lord Master. For his lead role in the aforementioned crimes Evazan became known as the ‘Mutilator of Milvayne’. Before the destruction of the holy city of Jedha Evazan and Baba were looting the battlefield for ‘participants’ from recent insurgency attacks, to bolster the number of Decraniated that he could sell to Vos..and other buyers. One such victim was the unfortunate Caysin Bog,..who became Evazans prototype for the first of the Decraniated. In A New Hope Evazan and Baba may appear as just idiotic, drunken patrons of Chalmuns Cantina..getting all rowdy on Jawa juice and annoying the patrons, but the dark reality was that this pair (especially Evazan) committed atrocious, unspeakable acts on dead heroes and other innocent victims. Palpatine left most of the dirty work for Vader and his generals, but Evazan actually craved, delighted and relished in personally getting his hands bloody; And he did it all out of sadistic greed..just to line his pockets. He was one of the SWUs worst miscreants, and deserved each death sentence he was convicted of.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did Sidious ask Grievous to collect the lightsabers (for kyber crystals) or was it simply just for his collection?
Answer: General Grievous was a collector of fine things, but his lightsaber collection was his pride and joy. Darth Sidious didn't give a damn about the murdered Jedis weapons, and it probably delighted Palpatine knowing how his general acquired those weapons. Darth Sidious had a plan in motion that had been in effect for decades, and had no need to deprive the good general of his spoils of war. In the series Rebels we see that Palpatine was after enormous kyber crystals to help power the Death Star. Rogue Rebel operative Saw Guerrera sabotaged and destroyed one aboard a disguised Imperial vessel. That particular crystal was bigger than a Volkswagon..so Palpatine had no time for small fry, like the crystals in Grievous’ collection. Locations like Ilum and Jedha had enormous supplies of kyber crystal that he would plunder and deplete in the construction of the Death Stars superlaser. Grievous collected lightsabers because he hated the Jedi, and did so long before the start of the Clone Wars. Before his transformation the Jedi sanctioned his planet of Kaleesh because they believed the lies of the enemy to Grievous’ people..the Yam'rii. Before the Kaleesh could appeal against this decision their planet was effectively cut off from the rest of the galaxy, and Grievous had to witness his people starve to death in the thousands. After Grievous became a cybernetic warlord for the Confederacy of Independent Systems, his master, Count Dooku, gifted him his first lightsaber. It once belonged to Jedi Master Sifo Dyas. In Legends Count Dooku also gave Grievous a blood transfusion from Dyas, which was done in a bid to boost the midichlorians into his system, thus aiding him in his lightsaber training. From there his collection increased significantly.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why are some alien races in Star Wars always portrayed as evil like the Hutts and Trandoshans?
Answer: What might seem evil to us humans may be culturally acceptable to some of the alien races in Star Wars, but some races in Star Wars are just born with inherent evil tendencies. The Hutts and Trandoshans view something like slavery and bloodsport as inherent qualities amongst their cultures, and have been performing such practices for untold generations. To us humans slavery, murder for hire, sex trafficking, drug smuggling, racketeering, and extortion are abhorrent behaviours unfit for our society, but for these two particular species it comes part and parcel with their ancient cultures. Both species built impressive empires based on slavery and death, much like the Zygerrians who viewed it also as a necessary part of life. Karkarodons are basically giant great white sharks, that have very angry dispositions, and a tendency to rip beings apart with their bare teeth,.. …Amanis hunt humans for sport, and make trophies of their skulls,…and Grindalids beat and force children into underground pick-pocketing syndicates. But this isn't to say that every single member of their specific species has intrinsically evil tendencies. The Zygerrians were well known for being brutal slave mongers, but on the other hand we have a record of at least one being a Jedi. Tusken Raiders are widely known to attack and murder humans who trespass against them, but as we see in The Mandalorian the humans of Mos Pelgo, and the Tuskens worked together to defeat a common foe. But without ‘evil’ looking aliens in Star Wars it would make for a very boring universe. Devaronians look like Satan himself, complete with horns and a natural immunity to fire…but in Rebels we have Cikatro Vizago who was a Devaronian crime boss turned good guy by the end of the series. Shistavanens look like the SWU version of a werewolf, and we can see one in the cantina scenes of A New Hope. But Lak Sivrak became a hero of the Rebellion, and died in the Imperial assault on Endor. Ciddarin “Cid” Scaleback was a female Trandoshan publican in The Bad Batch, and she ultimately respects and helps the good guys, and even had a soft spot for Omega. One rule to live by in the Star Wars Universe is never to judge a book by its cover.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Are there cars in Star Wars?
Answer: Yes, cars do exist in the Star Wars Universe..but they're not really popular, and given the fact that technology has far surpassed the advent of the automobile in the SWU we rarely see or hear mention of them;..but they do exist. They were called, funnily enough..Groundcars, and not to be confused with Cloud cars. Groundcars were any type of wheeled vehicle that didn't use repulsorlift technology. This was cheaper, ancient technology, and far more prone to failure..and mainly used just to ferry civilians around. A more familiar mention of groundcars in the Star Wars Universe is from the audiobook From a Certain Point of View: The Empire Strikes Back ‘Amara Kels Rules for TIE Pilot Survival’. This Imperial pilot describes the roar of a TIE Fighters engine as “a cross between an angry beast and a ground car skidding on wet asphalt”. This is one of the best Earth related references, besides when in ESB Leia exclaims…”Would it help if I got out and pushed?” Source: Wookiepedia;Groundcars, and ‘Amara Kels rules for TIE Pilot survival (probably), From a certain point of view :Empire Strikes Back edition.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why didn’t Darth Vader ever visit his mother’s grave? Would have been easy pickings, in regards to Luke lol
Answer: I think the fact that Darth Vader never visited his mothers grave contributed more to Lukes safety than we first thought. Until Skywalker fell in love with Padme the only woman he ever loved was his mother, Shmi. When Tusken Raiders kidnapped, tortured and killed her Anakin snapped, and it was a major turning point in his life. He was grief struck, and consumed by anger…and murdered the whole tribe of Tuskens who committed the deed. From that day on the Lars Homestead held much pain and sadness for Skywalker, and when he became Vader he completely abandoned his former life. This meant all connections to his past were buried, including his mothers grave on Tatooine. Shmi's resting place held too much of Vaders past there, and so would have been a place that he would consciously avoid if possible. Right after the destruction of the Death Star Vader learns of the pilot who destroyed it…and visits his former home; The place where his mother was buried. When Vader visited here his past came flooding back in his memories, and affected him profoundly. After meeting Boba Fett on Tatooine, to task him with finding the man who blew up the Death Star, Vader took a little detour to take care of some business..and slaughtered another tribe of Tuskens.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: You come across the humanoids of the Star Wars universe, and they are on average the size of the old action figures (3 inches tall). How do you fare against a fully armed Darth Vader (and you can grab whatever is handy in your household)?
Answer: Wow, for some strange reason this question first reminded of the 1995 movie Indian in the Cupboard. Anyways,..if I encountered an action figure sized, itty bitty Darth Vader in my kitchen then firstly I would be super impressed, and wonder who drugged me,…but after realising that there was a real life, Hasbro sized Sith Lord glaring at me from my countertop..I'd have to act smart..and quick to survive this confusing conundrum. But I don't much like my chances, despite Vader being the size of a couple of Lego dudes. If the question says that I can defend myself with anything in my household then maybe I could fare half decently, especially if I retained some kind of element of suprise. If not then I'm utterly and totally screwed. Yoda was right about size not mattering, because even this little cake topper sized Vader is going to whoop my ass pretty bad. Just think about it; in multiple instances Vader has performed feats like yanking football field sized starships out of the sky, and force crush them until they explode. He didn't care who you were, or how big you were,..and he could even crush your throat via a video call. I might be like the size of a Zillo beast or a Gorax to Darth Kenner, but he's still going to bust me up..and most likely kill me. Even if he didn't use the force he could still drop my ass just by slicing my achilles or tibial nerve, or even slice off all my toes with just one swing. Even at that size Vader could force choke my larynx, or force crush my heart…so the only way I see to outwit the little f@&#er is to maybe entice him into the microwave somehow, just like in Gremlins. I could try and throw him in the juice blender, or bury him in a pot of sand in my backyard, or even swat him like a bug at a picnic, or stomp on him quickly like a spider,..but I own a taser so I'm hoping that will be enough to stop him. It's pretty well just doing the same thing Palps did to him at the end of Return of the Jedi, so here's hoping that my anti-burglar device is enough to stop a less than pint sized Darth Vader. Although, after that..it would be cool to add him to my action figure collection after I miraculously defeated the little guy.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Which Star Wars characters would you have loved to see in battle?
Answer: There's one guy I would have loved to see in battle. Darth Nihilus. Nihilus was a Sith Lord, but unlike any other you have heard of before. After becoming a wound in the force Nihilus became the stuff of nightmares, and made the fear that the great Darth Vader exuded look weak. This guy actually fed on the living force, the lifeforce held within all beings, and could single out worlds strong within the force…then consume the entire planet. His hunger for the living force became so immensely powerful that the darkside consumed his physical body. He existed as a being of absolute intent, with only his twisted spirit living on inside his robes and mask. This guy was fear, rage and fury incarnate,…and he lived only to feed on those who wielded the force, or even just possesed a small trace. Nihilus viewed death as the very meaning of life, and after each “devouring” his powers and his cravings only became stronger. Ultimately he lived only to feed. In battle those who witnessed Nihilus’ devastating abilities claimed that he was so powerful that his ability, Sever Force, could literally strip a Jedi or Sith of their ability to use the force. He did this to his former master, Darth Traya, and it rendered her completely useless against him. His hunger became so insatiable that his presence would instinctively feed on those living beings around him. When he spoke it sounded like demonic roars and primeval screams, and physically hurt…and he could keep an extensively damaged ship held together by sheer will alone. He totally embraced the darkside, and knew what tremendous fear he produced in the hearts and minds of all those he encountered. But to see him in battle would have been a sight to behold. He was described as a highly aggressive combatant, and used a furious, one handed technique to overwhelm his fear struck opponents. Although we have never seen a canon live action version of Nihilus I wait with bursting anticipation to see this absolute beast appear in an upcoming series.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Where did Darth Maul go when Obi-Wan cut off his legs?
Answer: He went to the worst place imaginable, especially for one who had just been bisected by a cocky young Jedi. After Maul was severed in two, his upper half was separated from his lower torso,..as he fell into the used coolant of the reactor shaft deep below. There he watched with terrible fury, as the recently severed lower portion of his body was incinerated right in front of him. Fighting for dear life in a containment capsule, he was pretty well labelled as hazardous medical waste..and loaded aboard a refuse disposal vessel. As Naboo was of a clean, pristine, natural environment all hazardous materials, like medical and radioactive waste for example were shipped to the planet Lotho Minor; an entire planet designated as an intergalactic dumping ground.
