Maul used pure rage, anger and fury to keep himself alive after his ‘incident’ with Kenobi,..and even later admits to Kenobi, towards the end of season 4, that it was the very thought of revenge that kept him alive long enough to construct a lower body. Upon being dumped on Lotho Minors filth ridden surface Maul had to scrounge and kill vermin just to survive, and then retreated beneath the planets destroyed surface into a nightmarish catacomb of subterranean horrors. Here he constructed a droid spider like torso and legs, held together by sheer hatred. For nearly a decade Maul survived deep below the acid rain soaked planet like this, with the assistance of a devious Anacondan named Morley,..who bought Maul victims via a trapdoor positioned far above the Dathomirians lair. Later when Mauls long lost brother Savage is united with him…it is through this trapdoor that they first meet. Maul initially saved Morley from one of the roaming Firebreathers on Lotho Minors surface, and in return for saving his life the Anacondan dragged him below the planet. When the now insane Maul had finished feasting on his murdered prey,..Morley was free to get the leftovers. Images from the comic series ‘The Clone Wars:The Sith Hunters’ 2012

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Do Battle Droids have emotions?
Answer: You just have to see a couple of episodes of The Clone Wars to see that some battle droids of the Separatist Alliance have slight personalities, that set them apart from almost all the other mindless minions in the droid armies. Not so much with the B2 Battle Droids, but the later versions of the B1 expressed some suprising emotions. If you look at the above scene, particularly the two B1 battle droids standing in between Kenobi and Grievous, just off in the distance. The droid on the right motions to his companion to watch their general take out his lightsabers. On this occasion the droid was trying to convey a “Wait for it” kinda feeling as he anticipated the excitement. Here we have the Battle Droids in the Geonosian arena, as they surround the Jedi. This B2 expresses frustration at one of his lesser counterparts getting in his way. It's almost as if that B1 genuinely angered him, giving the abrupt, violent way he hurled him aside. The B1 was shot a moment before the punishment from the B2, possibly meaning their programming here accounted for damaged and useless companions. Trash them and press forward. The above two droids here express shock and disbelief upon surviving a blast, and even check themselves to see if they were damaged. They even look genuinely astonished that they didn't lose a limb or something, despite being unable to express emotion on their faces. Above, this B1 gives a brief explanation as to why some droids were more independent. When we watch The Phantom Menace we see that when Anakin destroys the Separatist Control vessel he also destroyed the central computer, thus shutting down the droids who were remotely attached to it. Later models of the B1 were designed to operate more independently, without requiring the assistance of a central computer to program their orders. This allowed them to be more animated in their responses and actions, giving them a more emotional quality. The Clone Wars is the franchises best example to witness their emotional displays. Here a droid meets Wrecker from the Bad Batch, and right before the enormous clone pummels the poor droid into the floor the B1 expresses fear, particularly at the prospect of having his face messed up. The droid below even tries to warn his boss about an impending attack from non other than…Kenobi. He conveyed suprise and emergency with his tone, and sounded worried about Grievous possibly being attacked by the insolent Jedi. Below is where some droids are cornered by Skywalker, and upon realising that their fates are sealed resign themselves to the Jedi’s swing. The one on the right slouches his shoulders in defeat, as if he had seen Skywalkers fury firsthand. The other one still wanted to put up a fight, meaning there were conflicting emotions amongst themselves. It's rather sad how something programmed,..hard and cold, can express so much emotion just from some small body language. Finally, here's some more Battle Droid images, because I know that some of you out there are big fans of those B1’s! Roger Roger.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: [Star Wars] Let's say Vader is successful in bringing Padme back to life. What the hell was his plan after that?
Answer: Have you seen the 1989 Steven King movie classic Pet Sematary? After tragically losing his son the main character, Doctor Louis Creed, learns of an ancient place where he can bring his child back from the dead. His wife dies tragically also,..and he then uses the same method to bring her back from beyond the grave. On both occasions the results were abominable, and both parties returned from the afterlife as murderous, undead versions of their former selves. The point here is that Louis didn't have a plan,…even after he was personally warned of the horrible consequences involved. Louis was just like Anakin; he didn't care how he could bring Padme back from the dead…he just wanted to hold her, and have her again. No matter the cost. Doctor Creed, like Skywalker, knew of the risks involved with trying to bring back his lost love…but he simply didn't care. He didn't have a plan, he didn't have a way to ease her back into the land of the living,..he just wanted her back by his side. His own mother died in his arms, due to the most cruelest of ways..and then he is tricked into believing that he inadvertently killed his own wife. Don't you think he'd do absolutely anything, and everything to bring her back? He didn't know, or care, what state Padme would be in if he was successful in conquering death,..he only wanted his love back. No matter what she brought back with her.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why could clone troopers shoot Jedi but battle droids could not?
Answer: Quality,..not quantity. That's why. The clonetroopers of the Grand Army of the Republic were all cloned from the number one bounty hunter of his day, Jango Fett. Fetts impressive DNA, coupled with his lifetime of extensive training and experience, resulted in the clones becoming far more accurate than most fighting forces within the SWU. Count Dooku carefully selected the clone template candidate based on his abilities to kill Jedi. When Jango was still perfecting his skills he single handedly took out 6 Jedi during the Battle of Galidraan, which Dooku witnessed first hand. That fateful day the Count bore witness to the man who would ultimately become the face of the Republics impressive new army. The Kaminoans also used Jango to assist hands on in the training of new clones, giving them a far more lethal edge in combat..as opposed to the droids of the CIS. Every Alpha class ARC Trooper also went through extensive one on one training with Jango himself. So when the time finally arrived to execute Order 66 the clones were very well equipped to decimate the Jedi Order. Unlike the Stormtroopers of the Galactic Empire all of the clonetroopers had superior fighting blood coursing through their veins. However the droid armies of the Separatist Alliance were limited by their programming, which wasn't up to the high calibre of the clones physical training,..and so the droids blaster combat, and manoeuvrability skills, were simply no match for the clones lethal accuracy. The droids greatest advantage lay in their vast numbers, which were usually used to overwhelm the Republic forces en masse. This method was first displayed when Dooku's droids surrounded, then massacred most of the Jedi in the Geonosian arena. By swarming their enemy with outnumbered odds the Separatist Alliance were able to achieve victories, but had the odds been even for every single engagement the Republic had with the CIS then the clones would mop up the droids. Order 66 worked a lot like a Separatist droid attack during the Clone Wars. The soldiers of the 501st overwhelmed the Jedi Temple, but also retained the element of suprise..up until the first shots of the great Jedi Purge echoed throughout the hallways and rooms of the great temple. Their home ultimately became their tomb, at the hands of their former comrades in arms.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who did you find to be the most annoying character or creatures in the Star Wars Canon and why?
Answer: Jawas. Always with the Jawas. It doesn't matter if you find them on Tatooine, Nevarro or Arvala-7..as they're always swindling, or straight up ripping off folks. Yes, they have their talents, particularly when it comes to “acquiring” that rare or extremely hard to find piece of hardware..but at what cost? They'll probably steal from your neighbour, sell you the part, and create mixed feelings about the whole transaction. We first see their rip off tactics in A New Hope, where Owen Lars gets sold a droid with a bad motivator,..and the method for acquiring these droids is just straight up theft. They fried R2-D2s circuits out in the wastes of Tatooine, kidnapped him, and promptly sold him to the next sucker in line, (being Owen Lars). Din Djarin had his unfortunate encounter with these thieves when he was pulling a job off on Arvalo-7, and after leaving his Razor Crest parked he returned to find it stripped almost completely bare!! Then to get his parts back the Jawas had the nerve to make Din go and get dirty, and almost get killed, retrieving an enormous Mud Horns filthy egg. Obi-Wan Kenobi would also have to deal with shifty little Jawas, whereupon relocating to Tatooine one particular Jawa, Teeka, would steal Kenobi's items, then sell them back to him. It was just something that Kenobi had to accept if he wanted to keep getting items he desperately needed, because the damn Jawas completely cornered the market on most technical items on Tatooine. On top of all of this they apparently smelt really bad up close..and sometimes get extremely sarcastic during barters. Gamorreans and Gungans might be clumsy, lazy and inept simpletons, but they won't steal your parts and sell them to your neighbours.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What if Darth Maul and Mother Talzin somehow managed to kill Sidious, Grevious and Dooku during the encounter where Talzin met her end? What would happen and how would this effect the Star Wars Universe?
Answer: For starters, Talzin and Maul would have smirks on their face that would last for months…and it would leave Maul and his mother free to make plans on taking over where Darth Sidious left off. Mother Talzin had her son snatched from her when he was but a child, and she harboured deep resentment towards Palpatine and the Sith, just as her long lost son did. Sidious completely destroyed the connection between mother and son, and shaped her child into a cruel tool to be used at the dark lords whim. Each of them had real reason to celebrate at the death of Sidious,..and his lapdogs. Dooku had used Talzins abilities to only further himself, and his wicked masters desires,..and General Grievous led the massacre on Dathomir that drove the Nightsisters to the brink of annihilation. Their deaths would ring in a new era for the galaxy, and make the Republic tremble at the feet of the Sons of Dathomir, and the Witches of the Mist. Their actions would affect the SWU irrevocably, and put into motion a chain of events that would result in an eventual confrontation between the Republic and the Jedi,..and Maul, Talzin, Crimson Dawn and the Nightsisters. Or,..if Maul was more privy to Sidious's plans than we were led to believe then he and his mother could possibly utilise Order 66 to their advantage. Mauls control over the Shadow Collective and Crimson Dawn would allow him to unite the most powerful criminal syndicates in the entire galaxy, and with groups like the Black Sun under his control Maul could actually muster enough firepower to threaten the Grand Army of the Republic. In Legends material like Shadows of the Empire, it was Black Sun, under the lead of Prince Xixor, who supplied the Emperor with some of his battleships. Mother Talzin would be the greatest threat to the Republic, and after realising that Sidious had left behind a master blueprint on how to conquer the galaxy she would somehow use her magick to fulfill this grand plan. With Maul and his minions at her side she stood a half decent shot at retrieving something from the ashes of her former life. A life that Darth Sidious had stole from herself and her son…so very long ago. Talzin was much like Sidious, and as witnessed in TCW season 6, where she wished to be more powerful than the Sith and the Jedi. She was draining the life force from beings, in order to become rejuvenated and more powerful ..much like Palpatine in episode IX. She ordered Maul to form the Shadow Collective, and knew how to kill a Sith Lord,..which she nearly did during the Battle of Dathomir. Now with Dooku, Grievous and Darth Sidious out of the way, Mother Talzin and Maul pose a very real threat to the safety of the Republic.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is the largest Droid in Star Wars?
Answer: In the Junk Fields of the planet Lotho Minor resides a type of droid so enormous,..and very ancient, that nobody even remembers who built them. Standing at a colossal 34.35 metres tall are the Fire-Breathers,..an ancient class of refuse incinerator droid. Lotho Minor was designated as a garbage planet; somewhere the rest of the universe dumped its trash. These gargantuan incinerator droids prowled the mountains of garbage and refuse, slowly burning down the planets infinite supply of rubbish. These massive, nightmarish looking droids shared their dank, reeking planet with Junkers,..beings who were more machine than organic,…showers of acid rain, and at one point was the home to Maul for over a decade. These droids obviously served to burn up Lotho Minors waste, but became so overwhelmed by the staggering amounts of trash that upon first glance they appear to look like a huge pile of scrap metal themselves. Now they feast upon the decaying scrap of the dead planet, and wait for the salvage ships to come dump precious new garbage to them down below on the surface.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: If Savage Opress was still alive, would Darth Maul eventually betray him due to the ways of the Sith?
Answer: “..betray him due to the ways of the Sith” At this point in the game Maul despised,..no he detested, the Sith and all that it had taken from him. In Rebels Maul confesses to Jabba(Ezra Bridger) how the Sith took everything from him. They ripped him from his mothers care and fed him into a machine that twisted his very being. He was promised by Sidious that he would be by his side when he conquered the Jedi, the Republic, and the entire galaxy. But instead his master abandoned him for a rich old man, left him to languish and rot on a garbage laden planet for over a decade,…and completely erased his destined future. Maul became so mentally unstable, due to the Siths intervention in his life,..so much so that he forgot his name. If Savage somehow survived his encounter with his brothers former master then I honestly doubt that Maul would betray his brother. Maul would be driven to exact revenge on the Sith, and utilise all that Dooku had awakened in Savage. Remember, Savage Opress was imbued with Nightsister magicks,…and was capable of force choking both Ventress and Dooku simultaneously. Immediately after that event Savage effortlessly threw Kenobi and Skywalker around like they were drunk Jawas. So Maul would realise that Savage would be instrumental in their second, and hopefully last, encounter with Darth Sidious. After all, they were brothers..and when Sidious actually kills Savage in The Clone Wars Maul expresses shock and disbelief at seeing his little brother die in his arms. If anything, their failed encounter with Sidious on Mandalore would only make them strive even harder to overthrow the most powerful being in the galaxy. Once and for all. And thus make way for the ‘True Lords of the Sith’ to finally take their place and rule in Palpatines stead,.. leaving Maul free to locate Kenobi and exact his revenge.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What if Vader somehow managed to find Luke on Tatooine a couple of years after revenge of the sith (say he sensed him through the force or something)?
Answer: If Vader ever found his son Luke, then it would mean his confrontation with Kenobi would be pushed forward, and after defeating his former master Vader would almost certainly keep Luke a very well guarded secret from the Emperor. If Vader managed to locate Luke it would also mean imminent death for Lukes aunt and uncle, Owen and Beru Lars. This would be the perfect opportunity for Vader to tie up any loose ends, by procuring his lost son, eliminating the Lars for their betrayal,..finally dealing with Kenobi….and to ultimately teach his son the ways of the darkside so that together they can overthrow Palpatine; together as father and son. After ascertaining Lukes exact location the operation would more than likely go down something like this… Darth Vader assembles an elite death squad consisting of 4 Inquisitors, several squads of Death troopers and Purge troopers, and a backup battalion of Stormtroopers sitting in orbit. He then devises an extraction method to obtain Luke, which the Inquisitors and Purge troopers will execute upon his orders. This will eliminate Owen and Beru in the process,..leaving Vader and his Deathtroopers free to crush Kenobi at their will. After the defeat of Kenobi, Vader uses the force to eliminate all witnesses to the affair, including all the Inquisitors and Imperial personnel involved, then ultimately devises a lie to present to his master. The death of Kenobi, and the consequent “battle” on Tatooine would serve as the perfect cover to whisk Luke away to a well hidden location…and to indoctrinate his son into the Sith. The Emperor would be most pleased that Vader finally killed his former Jedi Master, and could now completely focus on eradicating the last remaining Jedi…Master Yoda. Unbeknownst to Palpatine though Vader would have already begun Lukes training in secret, ala Starkiller in The Force Unleashed. Only unlike Starkiller Luke would not be viewed as expendable. Vader would harness Lukes tremendous power,…and in time the two Sith Lords would usurp the Emperors throne. Unless Master Yoda somehow intervened Princess Leia would either grow up unawares of her connection to the rulers of the galaxy, or be eliminated upon her discovery..according to the Rule of Two. Unless Luke had future aspirations to acquire his fathers throne…

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Since Force Crush was banned by the Jedi council, and it's okay to use it against droids and not living beings, why was it okay for Windu to Force Crush Grievous's lungs in the 2002 animated Clone Wars?
Answer: Mace Windu walked a very thin line in between the dark, and light sides of the force,..and had to have his lightsaber form approved by the Jedi Council before continuing on his path within the Order. Vaapad, or Form VII in lightsaber combat, was usually only practiced by the Sith. Both Darth Sidious, and his apprentice Darth Vader, were among the few to wield this incredibly powerful form of sabre combat. But Windus exceptional connection to the force meant that although he was a Jedi, he employed a lightsaber form almost exclusively mastered by only dark side practitioners,..leaving himself with a beneficial advantage when opposing the darkside. Besides himself, only Master Yoda, and Jedi Battlemaster Cin Drallig, were among the only few Jedi to master all seven forms of lightsaber combat. With this also came the tremendous responsibility of keeping Windus darkside demons in check. So when Windu crushed General Grievous’ lungs in the now non canon, 2003 Clone Wars, he was about the only Jedi who could use force crush on an opponent, with far lesser risk of succumbing to the temptation of the darkside. He had perfected form VII to the point where he had total control of it, and actually used the ‘ferocity form’ to his advantage. Vaapad and Juyo created form VII, making it the most unpredictable and aggressive form of lightsaber combat conceived, and after Windus tweaking of the form aligned with the Jedi code he became a Jedi who was pretty much allowed to use the force to crush his enemies,..unlike Anakin Skywalker who Windu didn't trust from the very beginning. He also crushed Grievous’ lungs in a bid to prevent the Separatist leader from escaping at the height of the Clone Wars. It was a tactical, opportunistic moment that Windu seized. If he was successful in crushing General Grievous then not even Masters Yoda, Kenobi…or the entire Jedi Council would have batted an eyelid,..and in fact many Jedi would have praised him for using the force to defeat one of the Jedi’s most deadliest opponents.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How did Imperials on Coruscant and other core worlds react to the destruction of the Death Star?
Answer: Just ask the Imperial pilot that Cara Dune shot in the face. The destruction of the Death Star, and it's predecessor years later, reverberated for many years throughout the Star Wars Universe…and had a very profound affect on those Imperials serving under Palpatines yoke during the reign of his Empire. Darth Vader was the sole survivor of the destruction of the first Death Star, and his survival meant only to boost dwindling morale for the remaining Imperials throughout the galaxy. For the Emperors mightiest superweapon to be destroyed by a teenager from Tatooine was the Empires single largest loss since it's formation nearly two decades prior. The Death Stars destruction was such a significant intergalactic event within the SWU that dates are measured from before, and after, the Battle of Yavin…where Galen Ersos subterfuge led to the destruction of the galaxy's most powerful weapon. The Death Star was a symbol of ultimate power for the Empire, and it's supporters, and with its destruction was felt a terrible vacuum of power;..but only for a short time, before the unleashing of the Death Stars first reincarnation above Endors moon. The Death Star was a means of controlling the entire galaxy, but some high ranking Imperial officers thought that Palpatine hedging all his bets into one superweapon was ill advised. And so Lukes shot hit no-one harder than Palpatine himself. In one blast by a lone X-Wing pilot Palps’ grand plan was blown to pieces in the blink of an eye. He looked weak in the minds of the citizens under his control, and his supporters had very real cause for concern. Until the fully functional Death Star II was ready to rock Palpatine and his Imperials reacted very, very negatively to their failure over Yavin. Vader personally felt Palpatines wrath and fury over his failure to protect their greatest asset. This was a monumental set back for every Imperial, and it was safe to say that they were infuriated, at the least. Their moment of triumph became their greatest failure in a heartbeat. Resentment for years was felt within the Imperial community, and after the destruction of the second Death Star it only spurned some Imperials to harbor even more resentment towards the Rebel Alliance and their terrorist co-conspirators. This is witnessed during season 2, episode 8, of The Mandalorian, where operatives of the New Republic attack Imperial remnants led by Moff Gideon. During an Imperial shuttle hijack, led by Marshal Cara Dune, we hear first hand from an Imperial pilot on his thoughts about the destruction of the Death Star. He bitterly resented the actions of the Rebel Alliance that fateful day years earlier, and it strengthened his hatred towards all enemies of the Empire. He even shot his copilot in the back for not being loyal to the Empire. He condemned the loss of millions of lives aboard both battle stations, and viewed the destruction of Alderaan as a ‘small price to pay’ to rid the galaxy of terrorism. He was actually aboard the Death Star when it obliterated its first planet. Like every diehard Imperial this pilot viewed the destruction of both Death Stars as an act of galactic terrorism, condemning the millions of lives lost at the hands of Rebel criminals. Unfortunately this didn't stop Marshal Dune from shooting him in the face, for taunting her about the obliteration of her homeworld,..Alderaan.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who are the most underrated Star Wars characters?
Answer: I'll give you an example of a criminally underrated character in the Star Wars Universe,..so underrated that the actor who portrayed him, in Episode VII, wasn't even credited for playing one of the downright coolest characters to come out of The Force Awakens. He is only on screen very briefly, like all the notoriously underrated characters in the SWU, but left such an impression on me that I thought this buccaneer of the backworlds warranted a more fitting role within Disneys ‘fresh new repertoire’. But alas, this character with unlimited potential and prospects was relegated to a miniscule, non speaking role in Episode VII, and only thrown a wasted opportunity in the Star Wars animated series Resistance. This character had all the badass looks, the mysterious backstory, and his exploits were legendary, upon emerging on the scene shortly after the fall of the Galactic Empire. He began life as a humble Delphidian thief, who quickly rose to become a name within the criminal underworld not to be trifled with. He wore so many titles throughout the Outer Rim territories that he became more feared of a pirate than even the notorious Hondo Ohnaka. He was also fiercely loyal to his crew, and would give his life to save them. Known by the names, the Crimson Corsair, the Red Raider, the Scourer of Adratharpe, the Silent Scourge of the Lost Clusters, and the Blood Buccaneer… this enigmatic individual gained a reputation as the very best pirate in the Outer Rim regions. So without further suspense I give to you…Sidon Ithano. Sidon was leader to a crew of pirates aboard his ship, after first serving under a treacherous Weequay pirate named Scorza. Upon establishing himself as a new name to be feared within the pirate community the Crimson Corsair set about making his mark in the Outer Rim. He wore striking red robes, and a Kaleesh war mask,…he rarely spoke, used hand signals to command his crew,..and pulled off some Solo moves when he was the first pirate to sail through the Lost Clusters in the Outer Rim, making the Kessel Run look like childs play. He even turned a sandstorm tornado into shattered ice, by firing a kinetic disruptor torpedo at it,…shortly before discovering the lost treasure of Count Dooku, on a planet that made storm season on Mustafar sound appealing. That treasure surprisingly turned out to be a clonetrooper from 50 years prior, named Kix,..a clone medic who had prior knowledge about Darth Sidious’ plan to destroy the Jedi Order, but had been cruelly silenced by Dooku, and placed in stasis for years, kinda like Ripley at the beginning of Aliens. Kix was retrieved from a former Separatist vessel called the Obrexta III, which held in its memory core the location of every Separatist stronghold that operated during the Clone Wars. This information led Ithano to unplundered riches, and furthered his already epic reputation. Sidon Ithano is just one example of an insanely underrated character within the SWU, and possessed such wasted potential that hasn't been explored in depth. His exploits alone would make for an incredible new series, and deviate from the tired Skywalker saga. Also, his first mate aboard their pirate ship is a peg legged Gabdorin named Quiggold, whose species look surprisingly like the Vogons, from The Hitchhikers Guide to the Galaxy, making himself already another deeply underrated character from Star Wars. Finn really shoulda stuck with this crew… Reference; Wookiepedia:Sidon Ithano, and ‘The Crimson Corsair and the Lost Treasure of Count Dooku’, Landry Q. Walker, 2015.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Has a Jedi ever murdered someone? Droids and Grievous don't count.
Answer: Yes, the padawan of Luminara Unduli, Barriss Offee, meticulously orchestrated the bombing of the Jedi Temple hangar. In this unprecedented and unprovoked attack on her family and her home Offee ultimately murdered several Jedi, clonetroopers, Republic military personnel and several civilians that worked at the Jedi Temple. Offee became extremely disillusioned with the Jedi Order and firmly believed that they had lost their way. Befriending a Coruscant local, Letta Turmond, she had found someone who shared her own skewed view on the Jedi. Convincing Turmond to feed her husband nano droids, which acted as a bomb hidden inside him, her husband became an unwilling suicide bomber. The moment Lettas husband, Jackar Bowmani, entered his employment section within the temple, the nano droid bomb inside him violently detonated. Offee believed that by creating chaos, murder and mayhem that she would brew distrust towards the Jedi. It was later discovered that Offee was in possession of dozens of crates of these nanodroids, suggesting that she was planning further carnage. She even framed her dear friend Ahsoka Tano for committing the atrocity, and was quite happy to sit back and let her take the wrap. This was also the catalyst that led Tano herself to become disillusioned with her beloved Jedi Order. Barriss Offee became so twisted that she even attended the funerals of the dead Jedi which she murdered, including her friend Tutso Mara; a fellow Mirilian Jedi who taught her to hold her lightsaber properly. Later Offee force chokes her accomplice Turmond to death, and once again let's the Jedi believe that Tano was the culprit. Now that's cold.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why does it seem like Star Wars clone troopers with black hair are the unluckiest ones?
Answer: What the heck are you talking about? Every single clone manufactured by their Kaminoan creators had black hair! Jango Fett, as we all know, was the template for every single clone trooper in the Grand Army of the Republic, and he had black hair from birth. The Kaminoans sure as hell didn't care about the clones hair colour, and neither did the Jedi. Clones such as Captain Rex, Commander Gree and Crys, had different coloured hair, which they would have dyed and styled themselves. This was done to create an individual look to accompany their individual personalities. Gree rocked the double red stripe, and Rex had a short cropped, blonde hair style. As I said, this was an individual choice for clones to colour their hair,..but at the end of the day each and every single clone trooper was born with black hair. Commander Gree may have been wearing a different hairstyle than most of his brethren,..but he still lost his head when carrying out Order 66.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Can a Jedi be successfully poisoned?
Answer: The Jedi are mortal beings, who are as susceptible to poisons as you or I. Undoubtedly their connection to the force would give them an advantage, that non force users would definitely lack. Being able to slow down their circulatory system, a Jedi’s heartbeat and blood flow might give them those few precious moments to seek an antidote. But nonetheless, the Jedi can be successfully poisoned. When a Separatist bio weapons scientist reactivated the deadly Blue Shadow virus, Jedi Ahsoka Tano fell victim to its debilitating effects. If not for Skywalker and Kenobi finding the ingredients to manufacture a cure, the young padawan would have died due to the virus poisoning her body. Weequay pirate lord, Honda Ohnaka, attempted to poison Jedi Knight Anakin Skywalker, and Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi, at his base of operations on Florrum. The Jedi pulled the old ‘switcheroo’ on Hondo and ended up poisoning his own men to death. Kenobi had also been exposed to poisons, back when himself and his former master tried to use diplomacy on the Neimoidians and the Trade Federation. Demonstrating their Jedi abilities, Qui-Gon and Kenobi held their breath, avoiding falling victim to the Dioxis poison gas that the Neimoidians flooded into room. Later, in Legends material, Kenobi experienced the affects of poisoning again, when Separatist forces attempted to use a biochemical attack on Naboo. Just by looking at Kenobi you could tell it was taking a tremendous toll on him.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Are Jedi allowed to wear masks like Siths?
Answer: Of course they are! Several highly noted Jedi wore masks, and the very guards that protected the Jedi Temple wore masks, being Jedi themselves. The Jedi Temple Guard had been an ancient and sacred part of the Jedi Temple for thousands of years. Once a Jedi was summoned for guard duty, they surrendered their former identity,..even their faces,..hence the cool masks. The Grand Inquisitor, who was once one of these revered guards, wore exactly the same mask during his time at the Temple. Jedi Knight, Master Revan, wore a mask before and after his time switching allegiances, and Jedi Kanan Jarrus wore a mask after being blinded by Maul on Malachor. Jedi Master Plo Koon wore an Antiox mask, as well did Jedi Knight Bo Keevil, who were both from the Kel Dor species native to the planet Dorin. This served as a life support device to their species, and surely there were other Jedi from different species in similar situations. Even in more modern incarnations of Star Wars Jedi wear masks. Poli Dalpation was another Jedi master, first seen in a Jedi: Fallen Order comic, and in Disneys Star Wars: Visions we see a masked female Jedi. So yeah,..I'm pretty sure Jedi can wear masks if they really want to. Below; Top, Jedi Master Poli Dalpation, and bottom, the masked Jedi in Star Wars Visions, episode 4.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Whatever happened to the Wampa that Luke de-armed (Star Wars)?
Answer: ‘One Arm’, as she was dubbed by Skywalker, has two very interesting fates after her encounter with the young Jedi, after the Battle of Hoth. In Legends lore the female Wampa survived her ordeal, and later went on to lead a pack of other Wampas, against the intruders to their icy home. They were so good that they could break into Echo Base undetected, and attack the numerous inhabitants, who called it home since 3 ABY. In 12 ABY, Skywalker actually returns to the planet Hoth, and is recognised by the Wampa, despite nearly a decade passing since their initial encounter. The Wampa tries to exact revenge on Luke, but is ultimately slain by the Jedi. Originally when Mark Hamill filmed the scene where he chops off the Wampas arm, he believed that Luke would only scare away the creature. When the amputation was included in the final cut of the film it was stated that Hamill was horrified about it. Not that he'd care about crushing a Rancors head in the next movie, but ultimately the story would have it that the Wampa succumbs to its injury and dies;..until the 2020 Star Wars short story, Hunger, published in From a certain point of view:The Empire Strikes Back. Alleviating Hamills concerns, the story this time went that the Wampa did actually survive, and “recovered enough strength to leave its cave once again”. I guess the Wampa did knock out Luke, and kill his Tauntaun mount with one hand, so suffering the loss of just one arm wouldn't necessarily spell the creatures doom. Umm, just curious but..can I see the Wampa puppeteers arm in the bottom left of shot, when the beast is mauling the face of the poor Tauntaun?? Source; Wookiepedia, One Arm (Canon & Legends)

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How did ATST pilots enter their vehicle? I understand there were probably gantries at the base but how about in the field? What if they had to get off the vehicle to do stuff? How did they get back in?
Answer: I believe that The Mandalorian has given us a great insight as to how AT-ST pilots get in and out of their vehicle. When Din Djarin was looking for a quiet little backwater world, so he and little Grogu could lay low for a while, their journey took them to the planet of Sorgan in the Outer Rim territories. But it wasn't as quiet as Din suspected. A group of pirates and marauders had commandeered an old Imperial AT-ST. The pirates were utilising the ‘Chicken Walker’ to strike fear and terror into the local populace, and conduct raids on local villages. When Din and Cara Dune located the AT-ST in the middle of a thick forest, we see the vehicle sitting at a much lower height,..then raise itself to it's normal height. This suggests, that like a chicken, the AT-ST could sit, as well as stand. Out in the field a pilot would probably have had a remote to activate this feature. This would explain how the pilots could easily climb up, and enter the vehicle, although no canon explanation has been given. Coincidentally,..the Klatooinian raiders AT-ST constantly had its red emergency lights on. This was due to overwhelming maintenance issues neglected by the pirates, but gave the vehicle the appearance of having evil, red glowing eyes!!

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did Yoda come across a Sith Lord prior to The Phantom Menace?
Answer: The first Sith Lord Yoda actually encountered was his former pupil, Count Dooku, but this happened during Attack of the Clones. By the end of The Phantom Menace Yoda and the Jedi Council had concluded that it was indeed a Sith Lord that Obi-Wan had despatched on Naboo, and Yoda was firm in believing that his master, or his apprentice, still remained hidden. During his long lifetime Yoda was canonically alive at the same time as five confirmed Sith Lords. Legends includes Darth Tenebrous and his master. Darth Tenebrous and his Twi'lek Sith Lord Master, Darth Plagueis, Darth Sidious, Darth Maul, Darth Tyranus, and Darth Vader all lived and breathed during the time Yoda was a Jedi. It was Darth Tenebrous and his master that created a rift in the force, so powerful that the darkside made itself known to every Jedi when the two performed the ritual. Although the Jedi of the time could sense the darkside, none could tell who originated the powerful rift. Plagueis was living on Sojourn before events in The Phantom Menace, and Yoda never actually met his public persona, Hego Damask. Count Dooku, Qui-Gon Jinn, Sifo Dyas and Jocasta Nu actually did though, during a diplomatic meeting with the Intergalactic Banking Clan magister. Plagueis used this meeting to undermine the Jedi, and plant the seeds of doubt in Dooku's conflicted mind. Although Plagueis had Sidious as his apprentice, Dooku was already being subtly persuaded by a Sith Lord to join the darkside..long before Darth Sidious made designs on the Serenno nobleman.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is a Force saber in Star Wars?
Answer: A Force saber was a Rakatan invention which predates the Jedis lightsaber by thousands of years. It was created many millenia before 36,000 BBY, was constructed using a metal hilt and powered by an Ebon crystal. These vicious melee weapons were actually powered by the darkside of the force, which the Rakatan Force Hounds channelled into the Ebon crystals, giving the blades their tremendous power. The ancient Rakatan grew these crystals in their laboratories, and used the force sensitive individuals called Force Hounds to craft the eerie glowing weapons using a form of arcane force Alchemy. You could say that the Rakatan Empire was literally light years ahead of the Jedi when it came to developing each cultures most prominent weapon of choice. When they were created they could resemble a regular lightsaber, or force pike like the one Darth Plagueis wielded. The most interesting thing about the Force saber was the fact, that in Legends lore, it was considered to be the number one catalyst that created the divide between the dark and light sides of the force. Legend has it that because the Force saber drew its power from the darkside, it greatly affected whoever wielded the weapon. When the Rakata began waging war against the Je'daii many from the Order wished to carry the weapons themselves, given the great power they provided in resisting Rakatan attacks. Many Jedi were against this proposal,..hence leading to the beginning of the great divide. Source; Wookiepedia, and Force saber first seen in 2012 comic series ‘Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm’.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Is Boba Fett the best marksman in Star Wars, assuming that the Jedi and Sith both stay away from blasters?
Answer: When we compare Boba Fetts skills with a blaster or rifle, to those of other illustrious hunters in the Bounty Hunters Guild..and not forgetting other various hotshot gunslingers around the galaxy, Fett stacks up in the top ten or higher. He's good,..very good, but there are other hunters who are very excellent marksmen also. Now by definition, a marksman is “a person skilled in shooting”. Most hunters who are accepted into the Guild are fairly decent shots by profession, but there are some who are phenomenonal shots with a blaster. Fetts father, Jango, was a blur with his twin Westar-34s, and obviously handed this skill onto Boba. But another Hunter who was also as proficient as Jango and his son was Aurra Sing. When facing off against Jedi she was absolutely deadly with her twin blasters, and a highly proficient sniper implicated in dozens of crack shot kills. Another twin blaster toting deadshot is Cad Bane. With his twin LL-30s he put his competitors to shame, but wasn't as proficient with a rifle. This is why he usually hired Aurra Sing to act as his partner in crime, usually accompanying him on dangerous, or tricky bounties. Jango also utilised the services of the Clawdite, shape-shifer, Zam Wesell, as his spotter sniper, ..and Boba did likewise with bounty hunter Fenec Shand. Aurra Sing, Zam Wesell and Fenec Shand were all highly accurate marksmen, and probably better shots with a sniper rifle than Fett. History shows us that Jango and Boba both teamed up with a superior sniper, suggesting that the Fetts prefer to use their twin blasters or Carbine rifle, over a sniper rifle or heavy rifle. Bobas EE-3 Carbine Rifle was also favoured by other famous hunters like Sugi, and Q9-0, but the weapon itself had lower accuracy than larger rifles. Boba Fett was one hell of an amazing shot, and his status of being number one hunter in the Guild was undisputed, but as for when it came to being a better marksmen than all of the other hunters,..I think there were a couple of shots out there capable of besting Fett in a display of marksmanship.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who are the red soldiers in Star Wars?
Answer: You mean these guys right? Well they're the Emperors Royal Guard, responsible for.., oh wait sorry.., you mean these guys? These are just the same dudes, only at different points throughout galactic history. As the finest trained troops in Palpatines,..Oh, I'm sorry..do you mean these red guys from Rebels animated. The Royal Guard were another group of highly trained assassins and guards, hand picked personally by Palpatine to.. Umm, sorry..you must definitely mean these red guys.. Snokes Praetorian Guards, consisting of eight deadly members, were very much like Palpatines own Royal Guard, and were.., oh wow,..umm, okay maybe you're referring to the dudes below.. When Palpatine reincarnated, and reinvented the Empire into the Sith Eternal, or Final Order, he carried on the tradition of decking out his throne room by… Okay. If you aren't talking about the “red soldiers”, below, which were the bloody Sith troopers in The Rise of Skywalker, then I don't really know which bloody “red soldiers” you're going on about..

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Which bounty hunter(s) in the Star Wars universe have gotten less time in the spotlight than they probably deserve?
Answer: The 6 foot, 6 inch tall Kyuzo bounty hunter called Embo. Even though he features prominently in the Clone Wars this extremely deadly hunter should have gotten more time in the spotlight. During the Clone Wars Embo became so renowned and regarded as one of the best hunters in the galaxy, with Count Dooku himself saying that Embos kill count was only second to one other hunters. Joining forces with Anakin Skywalker and Ahsoka Tano in the Clone Wars, Embo uses his impressive skill set to help Felucian farmers defend their expensive Nyscillum crops from Hondo Ohnakas marauding pirates. But later Darth Sidious himself hires Embo to attack Senator Amidala, Rush Clovis and Anakin Skywalker. When the credits were there,..he did not care, as Embo completely abandoned the former alliance with Skywalker and ruthlessly hunted the Jedi and Padme. He was so effective that Skywalker had no choice but to flee the situation. Embo must have been pretty good to make Skywalker run off with his tail between his legs. During Mauls swift Shadow Collective assault on Jabba's Palace, the Hutt Cartel hired Embo to protect them and stave off the vicious attack. Embo was good enough to survive a pummelling from Savage Opress..and live to tell about it. He effortlessly survived Moralo Evals ‘The Box’ on Serenno, as Dooku assembled a band of ruthless hunters for a job, and later survived taking on the Count himself, after joining Boba Fetts gang, Krayts Claw. Not only did Embo work for two different Sith Lords, and the Hutt Cartel, but survived a direct encounter with three Sith Lords, including Dooku, Maul and Savage. Who else in the Bounty Hunters Guild could make such an impressive boast? This dude was absolutely badass and showed less remorse than Cad Bane, except for when it came to his pet Anuba Marrok! Embo most definitely deserved more time in the spotlight.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why was it difficult for even the Jedi to destroy Droidekas?
Answer: By the end of the Clone Wars the Jedi had killing Droidekas down to a fine art, albeit at the start of the war these Colicoid manufactured machines caused mayhem for the Republic. Take the Battle of Ringo Vinda, on a planetary wide space station that took place towards the conclusion of the Clone Wars. Jedi Masters Tiplee and Tiplar were utilising a Jedis force skills, combined with the skills of their ‘Doom Troopers’, which worked to great effect in ‘decommissioning’ assaulting Droidekas. This technique could work on up to three of these droids, provided adequate cover fire was provided from the sides and rear,..or was more effective if you could get the Droidekas in a bottleneck or corridor. You see, the Droidekas defensive shields were always the main problem in dealing with these three legged obstructions. The Jedi developed the following technique to completely bypass their defences. The Clone troopers would set up a barrier with combat shields, position themselves behind the defensive barrier and draw the Droidekas fire. Once the Droidekas began firing at the clones shield wall, the Jedi levitated the droids using the force. The clonetroopers rolled a series of EMP grenades straight under the Droidekas, then the Jedi dropped the droids right on top of grenades. Boom! Droidekas destroyed. But this was only an improvement on a technique developed earlier. Initially the clones would gently roll a grenade under the Droidekas to bypass their shields, but excessive speed generated by the roll would cause the grenade to bounce straight off the shield surface. Unless you had adequate practice this move could fail at a dire moment of a battle. This new technique we see successfully executed by Jedi Masters Tiplee and Tiplar completely took the difficulty out of destroying a Droideka…even for a Jedi.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What would Anakin do if he crash landed on Earth when slavery was still in practice?
Answer: Let's say Anakin Skywalker flew through a dimensional rift, and ended up crashing near the Great Pyramids of Giza,..nearly two and a half thousand years ago. What would he make of this situation you ask? Firstly R2-D2 would eject from the Jedi Starfighter and do a diagnostic sweep of the immediate area. Determining very little threat from this primitive species he would proceed to make repairs to his masters ticket off this backwater world. Meanwhile,..Anakin investigates the gold clad locals, rocking up on some sort of primitive chariot. Viewing his desert surroundings, very reminiscent to him of Tatooine..and his time as a boy.., he immediately determines that he is witnessing an army of slaves being put to work. Memories of the Zygerrian Empires cruel slavery legacy, from his own galaxy, would come flooding back;..and the memories of himself and his mother as slaves to the Hutts. The pyramid structures that are reminiscent of Zygerrian culture, the guards whipping and subjugating the slaves, and the cruel, opulent overseers barking orders and holding innocents against their will. Snap. R2-D2 gives the signal that it was a minor crash, and the little repairs needed to be done are already finished. Anakin briefly acknowledges his faithful astromech, as he sums up the situation in his head. As the first group of the Pharaoh's guards roll up, and begin to whip the astonished slaves milling around Skywalker, the Jedi force grabs the cruel guards and sends them hurtling off somewhere beyond the dunes. R2 fires up the Aethersprite and prepares to take off. Anakin stands on the bow of the ship, as he notices more chariots, more guards and what looked like their pompous rulers in a carriage, slowly coming down the pillared road. “Take me up Artoo!” As he beckons his droid to lift the ship up, and stop as he reaches the height of the great edifice, he uses the loudspeakers on the Jedi starfighter to announce his departure. “Citizens of this land..” He shouts, as he raises his hands in the air and gestures them in a choking manner.. “You are now free!“ Then, as the Pharaoh and all his bodyguards arrive beneath his floating starship,..Anakin Skywalker closes his fists and simultaneously crushes each and every last one of their larynxes. Baring witness to all of this the frightened slaves huddle in silent astonishment. Those few guards who are spared his wrath flee like rats, screaming into the desert wastes,…as a joyous roar of liberation erupts from the thousands of slaves surrounding the giant pyramid. “Take us home Artoo.” Says Skywalker, as he drops into his pilots seat.. and gives a little smirk of smug satisfaction. . . . Meanwhile back on Earth..in 1940s Nazi occupied Egypt, a bold archaeologist makes a startling discovery...

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is the most underrated moment in Star Wars?
Answer: When old Luke Skywalker gives one last wink to C-3P0. Now I know many of you might be thinking.. “Please don't bring up the sequels.” ..but I have to give credit where credit is due. This moment between Skywalker, and his old companion Threepio, is underrated in so many ways. But it is my favourite moment from the sequels, and is actually a fitting conclusion to the Skywalker legacy. Everyone thinks that it's Luke Skywalker himself, whose personally come to face down the First Order, all by himself, and singlehandedly save the Resistance. Ultimately Poe, Leia and the surviving remnants of the Resistance realise that Skywalker is just buying them some time with a hard light projection of himself. Cheapens the feeling, but there's more to this moment than meets the eye. Luke appears at their darkest hour, and makes his presence known to all. Then he has a moment with his sister, and actually hands her another hard light projected illusion. It was Hans lucky dice, and Luke projected this so that Leia and the Resistance would buy his ruse. It worked, except for someone in the room who noticed that something wasn't quite right. Threepios photoreceptors obviously picked up that his old master wasn't actually standing before the assembled Resistance members. This is the moment when Luke, not only takes one more special moment to say goodbye to his friend also.., but Luke is giving him the wink to just say.. “Play along with me here pal. Just one last time my old friend.” Threepio, although aware that master Luke is deceiving his companions and his sister, keeps it to himself and plays along with the rest of the group. This is a beautiful moment between these old friends, and demonstrated a droids respect, if not love for his friends. Threepio knew that by saying something he would diminish the hope that Luke was gifting to them all. He played along to keep this hope alive, and still remained silent even after the distraction had played to full effect. What Luke does after his silent goodbye to his friend also demonstrates the full power of a Jedi Master in all its glory. Luke was thousands of light years away on the remote planet of Ach-To when he summoned the full power of the force to pull off the unthinkable. An entire Legions worth of First Order minions, with their TIE Fighters, Gorilla Walkers and miniature Death Star beam, face down this lone individual on the battlefield and proceed to end his rush to oblivion. Or so they thought. Luke even gives one of the greatest flexes of his life, as he shrugs off the First Orders full might. Lukes clever ruse worked up until his nephew personally came down to challenge him, and subsequently worked it out for himself. By this time Luke had not only given the Resistance enough time to flee, but had fooled Kylo Ren and the entire First Order. He had fooled everyone,..except for his old friend, who knew better. That's why this moment is so very underrated.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Since the Darth Plagueis novel is no longer canon, is it weird for a Star Wars movie to mention a named character like that, offhand, and then to never expand on him/her in any canonical book, comic, or TV show? Are there other characters like that?
Answer: James Lucenos novel, Darth Plagueis, was never treated canonically, but the character of Darth Plagueis himself has been made Canon. Another interesting character, that has been bought to canon lore from the Darth Plagueis novel was Plagueis’ master himself, Darth Tenebrous. Even though the Legends novel is exactly that..Legends..the two Sith forebears to Palpatines legacy have finally been made canon,..and rightfully so at that. Below; Darth Tenebrous. As we all know Darth Plagueis was mentioned by his apprentice, Darth Sidious, in Revenge of the Sith. But what of his Bith master who helped design the initial stages of the plan that Palpatine would eventually take over? In the Visual Dictionary companion to The Rise of Skywalker, we learn that Darth Tenebrous, as well as a host of previously Legends relegated Sith Lords, have been added to Canon. Tenebrous’ name donned the 26th Legion of the Sith Eternal Empire. Other notable Sith Lords bought into Canon lore include, the legendary Darth Revan.. Darth Andeddu who created the title of ‘Darth’, ..and Darth Phobos, the Theelin female Sith Lord born on the Sith homeworld of Korriban. Once these in magnanimous monsters only existed in the Expanded Universe,..but now we can look forward to possibly seeing them making canonical cameos in future Star Wars productions.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What happened to the Jedi who fell in love (without counting Anakin)?
Answer: They either let their emotions get the better of them, and left the Jedi Order for the love of their life,..or, they remained steadfast to their faith, and carried the burden of having loved and lost until their time was up. Some Jedi have followed their hearts, and obviously over time the Jedi Order would have seen more than one devotee turn away from the Orders faith. Of course, if a Jedi’s love interest was made known to the Jedi Council, then their integrity, and future as a Jedi would most likely come into question. The relationship between Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi, and Duchess Satine Kryze is a perfect example of the point I'm trying to make here. Satine and Kenobi first met when the young padawan, and his master Qui-Gon, were tasked with guarding the future heir of Mandalore. Even Qui-Gon, in the Expanded Universe, wasn't immune to the effects of love, having once fallen in love with a fellow Jedi, librarian Tahl. Below; Tahl, Qui-Gon Jinns former love interest. During the course of these events in Kenobis young life the two became more than just acquaintances or even friends, and developed very strong emotions towards one another. Satine even affectionately referred to Kenobi as Ben. They fell in love. But each respectively chose to return to their normal lives, knowing that they would possibly regret it one day. They knew it would ruin each others set future. Kryze eventually became Duchess to her people, and Kenobi became a powerful member of the Jedi Order. Their paths crossed again in the future, which probably made it harder for both of them to supress old feelings. But even though Kenobi kept the faith, the love he shared for Satine was something that touched him very deeply inside. He still had feelings for his beloved princess, and the same could be said for the Duchess. Satine was seen grieving for Kenobi at his supposed funeral, when the Jedi faked his death to go on an important undercover assignment. Later during the Clone Wars,..Satine confessed her love to Kenobi as she died in his arms. Maul had murdered the one true love of his life before his very eyes. The look of absolute sorrow on Kenobis face said more than a thousand words ever could. My point is, that if you are a Jedi who falls in love, you can either abandon your faith and have a real life, with someone you genuinely love,..or you can spend the rest of your life wondering what might have been. That moment, where Satine tells Kenobi that she always loved him, was the moment that Obi-Wan regretted not taking a different path so long ago. He regretted not taking the plunge, that ultimately would have spared her life. Regret was the lesson Kenobi learned on this sad day.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What did Palpatine do with Darth Plagueis' body?
Answer: After Palpatine killed Darth Plagueis with a vicious barrage of force lightning, he needed an excuse to blame his masters death on. Darth Plagueis, aka Hego Damask, wore a respirator to assist him to breath. He sustained the injury years earlier in an attack by Maladians. After frying his drunk masters ass Palpatine concocted a story that his friend Hegos respirator suffered a ‘technical malfunction’, and electrocuted the poor fellow. Hook, line and sinker the Coruscant authorities bought this BS story, and so The Chairman of Damask Holdings official cause of death was ‘electrocution by faulty respirator’. As for Plagueis’ body? Well, like the Jedi the Sith sever all attachments with their former families, and Plagueis had done that in true Sith style. The Muun poisoned his own father, and murdered a great deal more of his relatives. This was to secure his inheritance and control of the Intergalactic Banking Clan, which was his peoples, and indeed the galaxy's main supply of wealth. After usurping his way to the top Plagueis had eliminated his entire family, just like his apprentice Sidious would do years later. Now Sidious had control of the largest banking entity in the known galaxy, and a means to fund ‘his new Empire’ in the making. So with no family to come and claim the Muuns body Sidious did what any Sith Lord in his position would do;…he cremated his former masters corpse,..put the ashes in an enormous urn,..and used it as aesthetic decor in his personal office. Below; Plagueis’ final resting place (urn on the right).

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How did the Galactic Empire use propaganda? How effective was it?
Answer: It was effective enough to keep a steady stream of Imperial recruits feeding the Empire for nearly two decades. The Galactic Empire used propaganda to maintain an illusion of false security and stability upon its subjects, and it worked with tremendous effect upon the gullible citizens of Palpatines Empire. Certain branches of the Galactic Empire were established to produce or enforce such propaganda, like the ‘Imperial Propaganda Bureau’, COMPNOR (Commission for the Preservation of the Republic), the ‘Office of Imperial Promotion, Galactic Truth and Fact Correction’, and of course the ‘Imperial Security Bureau’. Below; Anyone else think that the female Imperial officer in this COMPNOR poster looks a lot like a young Princess Leia? The Empire used every sort of promotional medium in their quest to keep the hearts and minds of its countless subjects Imperially aligned. Posters, holo films and documentaries, advertisements, and massive public paintings all took precedence when trying to either enlist prospective recruits, or trying to persuade the citizens of the Empire that factions like the Rebel Alliance were anti Imperial, and depicted them as being terrorists or in league with barbaric criminal syndicates. Imperial Propaganda was instrumental in driving up enlistment numbers, particularly after the destruction of the first Death Star. The Imperial propagandists spun the Rebellions quest into being akin to mass murder, and intergalactic terrorism. The Imperial propaganda poster was designed specifically by the Empire, to justify involving its citizens in its hostile seizure of the galaxy. Palpatine also used propaganda to convince the galaxy that he was a kind, benevolent leader that genuinely cared about his citizens. These were all cleverly concocted lies designed to completely fool the galaxy. The Office of Imperial Promotion created posters such as the one depicting the Rebel Alliance being in league with the Hutt Cartel, and another poster where New Republic troops are burning down an Imperial Academy,..complete with screaming children behind the windows! The Empire, like every dirty, corrupt, rotten little dictatorship, knew that if they perpetuated enough of these lies, that after enough time, the general public would just believe it. Propaganda like this was extremely effective in its campaign, as even though it was all just window dressed bullshit, over time it eroded the minds of brainwashed Imperial citizens.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What do clones wear under their armor?
Answer: Essentially it is just a form fitting body glove that is just a better version of what some of Jabba's dancers wore. In The Clone Wars, during the Battle of Umbarra, we see the clonetroopers without their armor on. When Fives and Jesse were charged with treason by their rogue commander, Jedi General Pong Krell, they were sentenced via a summary court marshall and ordered to be executed by their general. Stripped of their white armour we see what a clonetrooper wears underneath all those armour plates. A Clonetroopers Kaminoan issued body glove provided extra protection from extreme elements, and could even sustain them in the vacuum of space for short periods, provided that they were obviously wearing their helmet. A body glove was an essential piece of equipment for a clonetrooper, but different versions existed throughout the SWU, and were worn by individuals from all walks of life. Some body gloves actually had self cleaning properties, and made from ultralighweight material provided the wearer with more freedom of movement. One of Jabba's modest dancers, Rystall Sant, wore a form fitting Szona body glove, that didn't restrict her dance moves!

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What are the most dangerous creatures in the Star Wars Galaxy?
Answer: There is something that exists in the deep cold of space, that is something both extremely dangerous and utterly horrifying. In the EU, there is a creature that is beyond imagination, and capable of the unthinkable. It lives exclusively in the cold vacuum of space, and preys on unsuspecting deep space travellers trying to make their way in the universe. To the Jedi,..they believed this thing was a pure manifestation of the darkside itself. I speak of the creature known in the Expanded Universe as a Starweird. Appearing as tall, thin, desiccated and rotting, a Starweird had floating, long white hair and three razor sharp talons on each hand. These nightmarish abominations would appear out of nowhere whilst a technician did some repairs to a spacecraft for example,..and they could even materialise aboard a starship while it was still in hyperspace! What made these creatures truly dangerous was their ability to use the force. A Starweird was capable of using Force Grip, Force Lightning and could even drain the life from their prey. Once they had singled you out as their next victim a Starweird was relentless, and began its unholy attack by releasing a powerful telepathic scream. Much like Darth Sidious's force scream a Starweirds telepathic scream would render its victims paralysed with pure fear. Then it would lash out with the force, or just tear you to pieces with its huge claws. It didn't even matter if you were a powerful Jedi, because Starweirds had a particular hatred towards force wielders. This is what led the Jedi to believe that a Starweird was manifested by the darkside. These creatures could resist a conventional lightsaber attack, and could even pass through solid matter. Out of all the dangerous creatures in the galaxy a Starweird was one of the most terrifying and unpredictable,..and even feared by the Jedi Order.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What do you think could turn Obi Wan to the dark side?
Answer: This is the man who literally lost everything dear to him in his life. His childhood master, his apprentice, his beloved Jedi Order,..and the closest thing to the one true love of his life,..were cruelly snatched from him, and taken forever. Kenobi remained completely steadfast, and upheld his Jedi training. This is probably what kept him sane, and kept him alive. Kenobis inner strength, and sheer, unbreakable will, were what made him one of the greatest Jedi Masters to grace the Order. If there was something in all of the Star Wars Universe, that had the power to break Kenobis will and let him completely fall to the darkside, then even himself had not encountered it. His master Qui-Gon was his idol, and taught him everything he knew. His padawan Anakin was like a brother to him. His fellow Jedi were, for all intents and purposes,..the closest thing to a family that Obi-Wan had. Jedi are taught to abandon all emotional attachment, but after his apprentice became the one thing that he swore to destroy,..after his master was slain before his eyes,..and after the mass murder of his entire Jedi family, Kenobi remained the consummate professional. Instead of breaking his spirit it hardened his resolve. Prior to this tragedy of epic proportions, Kenobi had suffered the loss of his very close companion, Satine Kryze, former Duchess of Mandalore. Kenobi had known the Duchess since his master and himself were tasked with guarding her life, long before the Clone Wars kicked off. Each developed strong feelings for one another, but returned to their respective lives. Satine was the closest Kenobi came to having a normal life. At one point he would have left the Jedi Order just to be with her. Even when Maul murdered her before his eyes Kenobi did not even think of turning to the darkside. To live through such horrendous tragedy, and still resist the lure to the darkside, spoke volumes about this mans character.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Which Star Wars character had the saddest backstory?
Answer: Abeloth. Before this once mortal woman became an enormously powerful and twisted darkside entity, known by some as the Beloved Queen of the Stars,..and to others as the Bringer of Chaos, she once had a family;..that she genuinely cherished more than anything else in the entire galaxy. At some point in her life as a mere human female, Abeloth came into the servitude of the Celestial Gods, known as The Ones. Abeloth first served the gods, but then over time she became valued and loved by her masters. She became known as Mother, and joined the other gods in their family. The Father was constantly at ends with his two children, the Son and the Daughter. The Son aligned to the darkside, and the Daughter aligned to the light,..the Father struggled to keep peace and balance with his children, but Abeloth became the mother that they all desperately needed. She soothed their arguing, and quelled their fighting, and as a mother her children loved her. As a single unit they were almost the most perfect idea of a family to have ever existed in the Star Wars Universe. Abeloth was truly the happiest woman in all of the galaxy. Abeloths curse began when she realised that old age was catching up with her. She was mortal after all, and so over the decades watched in the mirror as she suffered the ravages of time..whilst her beloved family remained ageless. In a desperate bid to hold onto the family that she loved so dearly, Abeloth did the unthinkable. The God's Kingdom was hers at leisure, but two places were strictly forbidden. The Well of Power, and the Pool of Knowledge, were what gave the God's their immortality, and in her haste to become like her family she drank from the well,..and bathed in the pool. She knew this was forbidden, but literally took the plunge regardless. As a mortal woman her mind and body was immediately corrupted by the insatiable power that she had completely saturated herself in. Abeloth became the closest thing that resembled a powerful demon; a pure sadistic monster, that unless imprisoned, would create utter chaos amongst the stars, and murder billions of lifeforms. Until her familys death in 21 BBY, Abeloth was destined to play a wicked game between her loved ones, where Abeloth would desperately escape from the prisons designed by her Father, over and over while her family reimprisoned her, each and every time. Her family had become her hunters and jailers, and exercised no restraint in locking her away like a vicious, wild animal. She had become mad with anger and despair for what had happened to her. Abeloth only wanted to save her life with the family she loved, and in her desperate quest to do so she became hated by the Ones. She was abandoned on the planet by her family, and then ultimately imprisoned for trying to love her cherished ones, and keep holding onto that love. Her worst fear of being left all alone in the galaxy had finally come true. She then became a hideously corrupt, and nightmarish being, that needed to be locked away from the galaxy for everyones sake. What happened to Abeloth was truly sad, because ultimately she just wanted to love like the way a mother should,..but fate would rip it all away from her forever, and transform her into something that the entire galaxy wished death upon.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Was Darth Plagueis more powerful than Sidious?
Answer: Darth Plagueis was indeed more powerful than his apprentice, but as decades progressed throughout the course of their relationship, Darth Plagueis had grown complacent with Sidious. From the time when Plagueis killed his master, Darth Tenebrous, he inherited the ‘Grand Plan’, that would ultimately see Sith rule return to the galaxy. Part of his quest for intergalactic domination included learning how to transcend the physical body after death. He had an unbelievable knowledge of the force, that still would have superceded Palpatines long after the Muun was dead. Darth Plagueis was the one responsible for dubbing Palpatine Darth Sidious. Plagueis was the one responsible for Sidious’ training in the darkside, and Plagueis was the one who first found Palpatine; languishing without purpose to his powers. Palpatine had Plagueis to thank for teaching him almost everything he knew, before becoming Emperor. The Muun Sith Lord introduced Palpatine to the darkside, and honed his skills as a powerful Sith Lord. But Plagueis, like every ‘wise’ master, did not teach Palpatine every skill and trick in the book. Plagueis knew Palpatine was a cold blooded sociopath, hellbent on possessing power. After all it was Plagueis who covered up the truth as to how Palpatine murdered his entire family. The knowledge that Plagueis possessed far surpassed Sidious’ knowledge of the darkside. As for raw strength and speed, Plagueis was in phenomenonal form. Darth Plagueis was able to move at speeds almost unseen to a human eye. His personal assistant droid, 11-4D, only knew it was Plagueis rushing past at speed, thanks to replaying footage and slowing down his photoreceptors. Plagueis was incredibly fast, not just physically, but with a lightsaber also. He could take on multiple opponents with ease, and was a deadly proficient warrior in the darkside of the force. He was cruel in his deliverance of death, often maiming, or just fatally wounding his enemies, as he sadistically studied the life drain from them. Plagueis was meticulous, articulate, and methodical in everything he undertook, and was a nightmare for Sidious to even dream of killing. That's probably why Sidious got Plagueis drunk before he killed him, because he wouldn't dare confront his master while he was awake. Then told everyone that he killed him in his sleep just to sound slightly better.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who is the darkest Sith Lord?
Answer: We have two contenders here for this esteemed title,..but that all depends on your definition of ‘darkest’ Sith Lord. Our first entrant is non other than the Lord of Hunger himself, Darth Nihilus. This guy survived the activation of a planet killing superweapon, known as the Mass Shadow Generator, and became an actual wound in the force. From that day onwards he began to become so powerful within the darkside of the force, that he literally craved the living force within every living object surrounding him. Even his own crew, that operated his flagship The Ravager, suffered from Nihilus feeding from their living force. He was so dark that his physical body was completely consumed by the darkside, and he had to summon the force just to retain a corporeal form. The force actually consumed his human body! When he spoke it was so dark and distorted that he was basically unintelligible. He literally sucked the life out of every living being on the planet of Katarr, and became so immensely powerful that he severed his masters connection to the darkside, and absorbed her energy into his own. Darth Nihilus had become death,..destroyer of planets, and one of the darkest Sith Lords to ever live. His mask became the very symbol of death itself. Now if you wanna take the dark angle of which Sith Lord was the most darkest, depraved and downright devilish, then that title has to go to Darth Momin. Before he became a Sith Lord, this sick, twisted little *@#& used to create pieces of art, and his medium was dead animals. His mother got him a cat when he was a child, and Momin killed it and incorporated it into one of his ‘masterpieces’. When he got older he progressed, just like every true psychopath, onto actual murders, and still created macabre art out his victims. Just like Nihilus, upon his death Momins evil spirit was trapped in his mask; so that future generations of dark and twisted Sith seekers could speak to him from beyond the grave. Yeah,..these two Sith Lords were actually pretty dark!

Name: John Bambrook
Question: While serving as Viceroy for Mandalore during the reign of the Galactic Empire, why was Gar Saxon referred to as the 'Emperor's Hand?'
Answer: An ‘Emperors Hand’ was a title given to any number of secret operatives, faithful to the Galactic Empire, but more importantly, to Palpatine himself. These representatives of Palpatines ongoing manipulations are despatched as, troubleshooters, or problem solvers. The Emperor has no time to personally attend all pressing matters concerning the Empires ongoing security, so individuals like Gar Saxon are sent in the Emperors place. Saxon had already proven himself to his Emperor. It was himself, and another Mandalorian Super Commando, that broke into Palpatines personal prison block, the Citadel, and broke out Maul. This was done deliberately by Sidious in an attempt to lure Mother Talzin out of hiding. Saxon also played a pivotal role in leading Mauls forces on Ord Mantell, and later again during the Seige of Mandalore. It was here he personally killed Almec, Mandalores Prime Minister. This was enough to garner the attention of Darth Sidious. Once the Empire had risen from the ashes of the Republic, Palpatine made Saxon not only the Governor, but the Imperial Viceroy of all Mandalore. His most notable role, in being an Emperors Hand, was personally leading Palpatines ruthless Imperial Super Commandos. Needless to say, Saxons betrayal of his people lead to his demise in 2 BBY, against Sabine Wren and Clan Wren of Mandalore.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What has Disney done right with the Mandalorian that they haven't done in the movies?
Answer: I'll assume you're referring to the sequel trilogy when you say “movies”. What The Mandalorian, or more importantly Disney, have done right is pretty much everything compared to what they served up with those other ‘movies’. The sequel trilogy was set 30+ years after Return of the Jedi, and this detracts from everyone's memory of that good old fashioned ‘Star Wars feeling’. It introduced a plethora of new aliens, planets and characters that weren't well received by audiences, whereas in The Mandalorian, the story is set less than half a decade after the destruction of the second Death Star in ROTJ. The galaxy in Favreaus show was dirty, grimy, old and worn. It felt like a really bigass, real SW movie, which was in stark contrast with the shiny, sterile environment of the sequels. The comedy factor in The Mandalorian shat all over the wooden, hollow performances in the new ‘movies’. As for the lead role characters in both The Mandalorian and the sequel trilogy, the latter missed the mark by introducing overkill, no training, whiny Mary Sues for lead roles,..and killed off Han Solo, Leia, Luke friggin Skywalker,..and a couple of other beloved characters such as Admiral Ackbar. This disappointed me more than words can express..but in The Mandalorian the characters in the galaxy are familiar and fresh in our minds. Ahsoka, Bo Katan, Boba Fett, Luke Skywalker and more, transport us straight back into the story because they are familiar with us. Rey, Kylo and the gang just missed the mark, and as new characters copped a lot of criticism and backlash. They lacked character development, but in The Mandalorian the characters were either established, or had incredible character development. Din Djarin went straight up John Wick at some points, whereas Rey just… Lots of people are tired of the whole ‘Skywalker angle’, but The Mandalorian incorporated the Skywalker legacy with a whole new story, lead protagonist, but familiar locations and characters. The Empire was familiar, whereas The First Order was received in translation as a sloppy copy of its predecessor. Its things like this that detract from the main story being told in the sequel trilogy, whereas in The Mandalorian we can kick back, and enjoy relatable characters, in a familiar setting. The plot comparisons in each were vastly different also. Din Djarins quest to return Grogu to the Jedi, and all that it entailed, made for a much enjoyable viewing experience than that shipwreck of a plot from the entire sequel trilogy.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: If Obi-Wan did kill Anakin, would Palpatine have cared? Would the empire’s reign have been any different?
