Answer: If Vader had actually died at the hands of Kenobi on Mustafar, then yes…it would definitely have affected the Empire; especially the public image of it and more. Palpatine had invested a lot of time, and money, into coaxing Vader over to the darkside over many years. Then when Kenobi had dismembered his powerful new apprentice, Palpatine was shattered. If Kenobi, had say, decapitated Vader, then Palpatine would have been bitterly, bitterly disappointed. When Maul was supposedly killed on Naboo, Palpatine could barely hide his outrage at the funeral for Qui-Gon Jinn. Just imagine if Vader had died, and now Palpatine has lost two apprentices! Imagine how severely he's gonna flip his shit. Vader was to serve two crucial roles in Palpatines new Empire. Firstly, Vader was Palpatines Sith apprentice, and the most powerful one at that. Sidious did care about unlocking the secrets of immortality; but in no way did it have anything whatsoever to do with the yearnings of his apprentice. He wanted the immortal glory all to his greedy self, and if Vader could help him, however small the chance of succeeding, Palpatine would use Vader as a tool to achieve personal success. Secondly, Vader was to be the public face of the Empire, and a living symbol of its might and fear. Palpatine needed Vader to inspire the Legions of Stormtroopers under his command, and keep the top tier officers of the Empire on a tight leash. Vader could make an example of one officer, and by morning of the next day untold scores of Stormtroopers and Officers would be ‘motivated’ to perform at 110%;…or incur the murderous wrath of Vader. Vader was crucial in this regard, and was Palpatines enforcer. Without Vaders blunt influence the leadership of the Empires military might was susceptible to ‘free thinking’, inconsequential corruption, and failure to be correctly motivated. Vader was Palpatines lapdog, his enforcer, and a tool to ensure his grip on the galaxy tightened even further. It would be increasingly harder for Palpatine to maintain control of the Empire, without Vader to wield on a whim.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why does Bo-Katan hate Boba Fett?
Answer: Well, to be fair..when Bo Katan first met Boba Fett they both got off on the wrong foot. Bo Katan had very real reason to hate Boba Fett,..and it all began when she heard Fetts voice. As Kryze said in the second season of The Mandalorian, she had heard Bobas voice, quite literally, thousands of times. “You are a clone. I've heard your voice thousands of times.” Bo Katan Kryze to Boba Fett. She thought that Boba Fett was a Clone. For starters, no clone has any business wearing a suit of Mandalorian armour, according to Mandalorian custom, and the Mandalorians at this stage in the game were completely subjugated by the Empire. In the previous episode to where Kryze made her comments, former Imperial sharpshooter Migs Mayfeld regards on how Mandalore, as well as Alderaan, was destroyed by the Empire, and then in current events Fett mentions how the Empire turned Mandalore into glass. Could you imagine how infuriating this ignorant, thoughtless comment, made by a mere clone and an impostor of her people, made Kryze feel?! The once proud Mandalorian people were savagely murdered and subjugated by the Empire, scattered to the corners of the galaxy, sent into exile and hiding, and had their cultural identity completely stripped from them. Kryze wanted the Darksaber so she could rally and liberate Mandalore from the Empire. She wanted the Empire, and anyone remaining from its leadership, to suffer as her people had suffered. The Clones of the Republic were the forbears to the Empire, and therefore played a part in the maliciously planned downfall of Mandalore and her people. Bo Katan had once fought alongside the Clones of the Republic,..and then bore witness to their callous treachery during the events of Order 66. If they betrayed the Jedi with such murderous abandon then they would betray Mandalore and her people,..again, and again. They,..as in treacherous clones, definitely were not to be trusted in her eyes. And now Kryze was hell bent on finding the holy relic, and symbol of leadership of her people, the Darksaber, and she had killed an untold number of Imperial officers and troopers in her quest. Another clone certainly wouldn't bother her one bit, in righteously slaughtering her way back to liberating Mandalore. Fett eventually won Kryze over after ‘explaining’ his heritage to her and fellow Mandalorian Koska Reeves, but before this revelation was clarified in front of Bo Katan,..yeah, she hated him.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: In Star Wars, how do ship-based cloaking devices work?
Answer: Cloaking devices in the Star Wars Universe are extremely rare, and operated by utilising the even rarer stygium crystals. These crystals were mined on the volcanic and unstable planet of Aeten II. In Legends lore the planet was destroyed in 3 ABY, not long after the Battle of Hoth, but by then it had already stated that the stygium mines had nearly ran dry. But in Canon the planet fell under the control of the Empire, and more than likely a similar scenario occurred. Either way, the crystals that powered the cloaking devices became rarer and rarer, rendering stealth technology such as this very hard to acquire or maintain. When Darth Maul served under Darth Sidious he was given the Scimitar, which is stated was canonically built by Sienar Design Systems, and later customized in an unknown laboratory. The cloaking system operates on the premise of using the power from more than 30 stygium crystals, ran through a ‘Cloak Field Generator’, and then the field that was created from this process was used to envelope the star courier in an invisible field. It was regulated through an overload cache, located in the middle of each of its wings, and the process made possible by the stygium crystals blocked every pursuing crafts scanners. However, it could still be tracked via its magnetic signature. The Scimitar itself was also canonically stated to be able to track another vessels signature through hyperspace. After Maul supposedly perished on Naboo the Scimitar fell back into possession of Darth Sidious. It was used by himself and General Grievous to arrive on Dathomir unseen, as Sidious hunted and killed the witch Mother Talzin. Above; Xanadu Blood, Cad Banes Porax-38, Rogue Class Starfighter. During the Clone Wars Darth Sidious gifted a cloaked ship, a Rogue Class Porax-38 Starfighter named Xanadu Blood, to the bounty hunter Cad Bane as payment for his outstanding services. Above; the Republic stealth ship, the IPV-2C. During the Clone Wars the Republic developed a cloaked vessel, the IPV-2C Stealth Corvette, that they used to elude and defeat the forces of Separatist Commander, Admiral Trench; and later Grand Moff Wilhuff Tarkin used a cloaked vessel named The Carrion Spike, that was designed from the original Stealth Corvette. Below; Grand Moff Tarkins personal stealth ship, the Carrion Spike. In the reference book, Incredible Cross Sections: Episode I, it states.. “An invisibility field is a terrifying weapon, since it can detect most security systems and make acts of theft, sabotage and assassination all but unstoppable.”

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Could there have been a different level of force ghosts in the Star Wars universe?
Answer: There is a particular being in the Star Wars Universe that makes me believe that there are different levels of force ghosts;..and I'm not talking about helpful lightside force spirits neither. We know that Qui-Gon Jinn resurrected the forgotten art of transcending death, and becoming one with the force. At first he was a disembodied spirit, then later appeared as a typical force ghost, suggesting ‘different levels’ within the spirit realm. Above; the force ghosts of Yoda, Obi-Wan Kenobi and the ‘real’ Anakin Skywalker. In turn he taught Kenobi, then Yoda perfected the Jedi technique, and at some point Anakin Skywalker used the same knowledge to redeem his force spirit from the darkside. But then again,..the Sith had their own versions of ‘force ghosts’, but unlike Jedi force ghosts they were usually bound to a particular location or planet. Usually. Above; the trapped spirit of Dark Bane, bound to an enormous monument dedicated to the Sith Lord. Many years before Yoda became a force spirit himself, he underwent training to become closer to enlightenment. One of his trials was to face a tremendous fear. His quest took him to the Sith world of Korriban. There he met the spirit of Darth Bane, who was bound to a Sith Temple on the ominous planet. Likewise is what became of the Grand Inquisitor, after his death at the hands of Kanan Jarrus. Only his degree of becoming some kind of force spirit was on a whole other level. Below; the force spirit of the Grand Inquisitor confronts Luke Skywalker in the physical realm. Vader, so angrily disappointed that the Grand Inquisitor lost to a Jedi, used Sith Alchemy to bind his tormented spirit to an abandoned Jedi Temple; forcing him to act as a guard dog of sorts. He described this experience as a fate worse than death, and appeared to be eternally writhing in hellish, ‘Ghostrider’ flames. Bane was toasty, but this guy was straight up living a nonstop nightmare. Above; Vader traps the Grand Inquisitors spirit, in a hellish ‘Groundhog Day’ type of existence. Then I believe that the level of force ghosts, particularly when talking about darkside practitioners, plunges even further into madness, and tormented decay. There is a creature in the SWU called a Starweird. These horrific abominations show up randomly in deep space to the crews of freighters and starships,..and begin terrorising the ever loving shit out of them. Below; a Starweird appears behind a young Jedi padawan. These beings can pass through solid matter, as well as retain a physical form that was capable of killing a Jedi. See, Starweirds are drawn to force users, with Jedi being most susceptible. Starweirds absolutely can't stand being in the presence of a Jedi, and lash out with their sharp talons, and ‘psychic force screams’, that render you paralysed and wetting your pants in fear. The Jedi believed that they were manifestations created by the darkside of the force itself. Below; not even the highly attuned senses of a Jedi can predict a Starweird attack. These..creatures can utilise force powers including force choke and force lightning! Their face can also take on the appearance of a victims loved one or companion. This is where I came up with a theory… Starweirds are the tortured spirits of Sith, and darkside acolytes, that have descended into madness and decay, far deeper than Bane and the Grand Inquisitor ever fell. Look at the force ghost of Bane, compared to the GI,..and then look at the friggin Starweirds! Its just like the levels of decay and retentive sanity in the afterlife, in the 1988 movie Beetlejuice. The longer you are in the spirit realm the further madness and decay that your mind and body suffer; until you end up becoming so far deformed, demented, and depraved, that you descend to another level within the darkside spirit realm. These Starweirds would certainly explain the last supernatural metamorphosis as a darkside force ghost.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What are some mind-blowing facts most people don't know about Star Wars: The Clone Wars?
Answer: In The Clone Wars story arc, during the fifth season, when Ahsoka is framed by Barriss Offee for the bombing of the Jedi Temple, we see an enormous monument dedicated to the fallen Clones who died in the first Battle of Geonosis. It is carved out of a huge piece of unpolished stone from Geonosis itself, and was named ‘The First Battle Memorial’. Now the sheer size of this memorial wall brings in to scope the tragically immense scale of life lost..just by the Republics Clone forces, and also not taking into account all the other billions of lives lost during TCW. It is comparable to the Vietnam War Memorial, in Washington DC. This monument is 246 feet, 9 inches long, and 10 feet, 3 inches high at its tallest point in the centre. There are more than 58,000 names, of United States service men, and 8 service women, who gave their lives for their country. The monument seen in TCW is nearly 40 feet tall, and ,in black Aurebesh writing, contained the designation of the unspecified thousands of clones who gave their lives in the opening battle that kicked off the Clone Wars. The first Battle of Geonosis was a particularly brutal affair on the clones, during their first practical engagement under the Grand Army of the Republic. This was just one battle, during the course of a three year long, intergalactic war,..and this one battle cost more lives than the USA lost in an entire war. Does this not tell you the unfathomable scope of unnecessary, human life lost during the Clone Wars? And then you start thinking about all the wars,..in the entirety of the Star Wars franchise. To make it all the more sad and tragic is the fact that the clones were viewed as slaves and property of their overseers, were not paid accordingly or even thanked for their service in many cases. Does this sound familar to you?

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How might the Star Wars stories have changed if Qui-Gon Jinn was Anakin Skywalker's father?
Answer: Unless Qui-Gon Jinn cleverly arranged it, so that no one knew he'd had an affair with a slave woman from Tatooine nearly a decade ago,..then the Jedi would drum his ass out of the Order, and not buy for one second that Anakin was the prophesied ‘Chosen One’. But if he completely hid the fact that he was indeed Anakin's father, then not a lot would change until the Clone Wars. If Shmi Skywalker, and Qui-Gon Jinn were the parents of Anakin, then technically he'd be Anakin..Jinn! So it would erase the entire Skywalker saga, and replace it with the Jinn Legacy! That's just for starters. This being the case, then the actual ‘Chosen One’ would be created by the force, as another wholly separate being from Anakin. This new prophesied reincarnation, of the one that would bring balance to the force, would probably end up killing Anakin Jinn..if you wanna go by the prophecy anyway, and the entire Star Wars Saga would be irrevocably changed forever. Possible scenarios may include Palpatine still taking Anakin as an apprentice, but he ends up being killed by the real ‘Chosen One’,..or Luke and Leia growing up together as Sith apprentices, only to face the one true reincarnation of the prophecy. One thing is for certain though. Yoda and Kenobi are going to have words with Qui-Gon Jinn once they become one with the force.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How was Poggle able to scream after being beheaded by Vader? Is it due to the Geonosian anatomy?
Answer: It was only in the illustrated screenplay of Revenge of the Sith that Poggle was beheaded. In the final cut of the film Vader actually slices the Arch Duke of Geonosis in half,…Darth Maul styles. Poggle even tries to defend himself with his ‘Staff of Command’, which was rumoured to be the bones of his predecessor, but stated as being the tusk of an ancient creature. But anyway..the shock would have been more when Poggle realised who Darth Sidious’ new apprentice actually was. Rember, during the Clone Wars Poggle was actually captured at one point by the Republic, and ‘interrogated’ by Anakin Skywalker. Poggle would not have forgot the face of the Jedi who actually force choked him half to death, so when ‘Darth Vader’ came waltzing into the Separatist command center on Mustafar..could you imagine the immediate thoughts that went through Poggles mind? So when Vader finally caught up with Poggle, both adversaries realised it was all over for the Arch Duke. Being cut in half gave Poggle adequate opportunity to scream all the way, on his rush to oblivion; But something about Geonosian physiology might also explain how Poggle could scream,..after losing his head. Geonosians speak to one another using their ‘hive mind’ consciousness, mentally projected by their Queen, Karina the Great. Now granted that during the Clone Wars the Republic engaged Karina, and her undead horde, and defeated her when the Progate Temple collapsed on her. But Karina wasn't the only Queen, so maybe when a Geonosian gets beheaded..its not just them screaming..but the Queen giving one last shout of anger through the decapitated head.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How good is Dex's food (Star Wars)?
Answer: It must have been good enough, at least to pay the astronomical rent the Besalisk would have been forking out every month. Did you see where Dex's Diner is located?! Its on the freakiin surface of Coruscant, and is a one story dwelling!! And it's not like it was terribly busy or anything. I'm not concerned about the food here;..I'm just wondering how many of his ‘Sic-Six Layer Cakes’, and cups of ‘Jawa Juice’ Dex actually has to churn out each day,..just to pay the rent on this place! But seriously, Dex's Diner must have been good enough if Kenobi went there to dine. Just look at the dudes face, smiling ear to ear, just to be standing in Dex's place! This man had impeccable taste just being,..well..Obi-Wan freakiin Kenobi, so Dex must have turned out some pretty good food. But then again, it's not like the Jedi dined like Roman Emperors every night. Being a humble, monastic order, which shunned personal possessions, and encouraged you to supress emotions, didn't exactly mean it was a fine dining experience in the Temple at chow time. Modest food for modest Jedi. Each Jedi was served enough nutritional requirements pertaining to each Jedi’s specific alien physiology, and not much else. These standards may have even laxed after the Jedi were drawn into the Clone Wars. This is probably why Kenobi liked to get outta the Jedi Temple every now and then, and sample some good old fashioned fast food, in a good old fashioned diner. Obviously Dex and Kenobi were old friends, and it was rumoured that Kenobi had free Sic-Six Layer Cake slices on the house! So why wouldn't he like going down to Dex's, rather than being fed the same old, monotonous meals back at headquarters? Dex's Diner looked alright from the outside,..but don't let looks deceive you.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What if the carbon freezing process killed Han Solo in The Empire Strikes Back?
Answer: Then Boba Fett has to field one really awkward phone call with Jabba the Hutt; and he wouldn't be getting anything near the agreed price that the Hutt was going to pay neither. Solo was a highly wanted man, and a valuable commodity, and both Vader and Fett had concocted a plan that seen the dodgy smuggler finally captured on Bespins Cloud City. After this it was up to Fett to deliver the carbonite encased Corellian to his employer. But during the Carbonite freezing process, if Solo had not survived, then Fett would be looking at a much meager payday, and one pretty pissed off boss. Undoubtedly some yelling, and unsavory words, would be exchanged between Fett and Jabba, because after all.. “He's no good to me dead.” …were the words used by Fett to Vader. Vader then assures his bounty hunter associate that the Empire will compensate him in the event that Solo doesn't survive, so either way for Fett it's a big payday from Jabba,..or a split payment between the Hutt and the Sith Lord. The worst Fett has to put up with is being a bit light in the pocket, and Jabba spitting and foaming all over him for allowing Vader to kill Solo. But at the end of the day, if Jabba still has a problem, then Fett could just tell him to take it up with Vader personally. Oh,..oh yeah,..and then there's gonna be that whole big issue of Vader having to,..because of Solos unexpected demise, now deal with angry children, and a furious Wookiee and all that commotion, so…

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why isn't artillery and aircraft used more frequently in Star Wars?
Answer: Just watch The Clone Wars animated series and it will change your mind. Yes, many of the battles we see in the SWU take place in outer space, but down on the surface of planets we see plenty of artillery, and starships acting in the support capacity as bombers and fighter escorts. During the Battle of Geonosis, and later at the Battle of Christophsis, we witness two massive pieces of artillery being used by Republic forces. Firstly we have the AV-7 Anti-vehicle Artillery canon. This weapon was deployed at both aforementioned engagements by the Grand Army of the Republic, and was a giant, one man artillery canon. It could move into position via using it's four legs, or be moved using repulsorsleds. The second piece of artillery used by the Republic was the enormous SPHA-T, or Self-Propelled Heavy Artillery Turbolaser. This was the largest ground based weapon to be employed on the battlefields by the Republic, and its turbolasers were strong enough to penetrate the shields and armor of colossal starships. This marvel of technology could move into place via its twelve legs, and was operated by a crew of 30 Clonetroopers. However in the event of pulling back forces on the battlefield it was quite slow, often falling into enemy hands or being destroyed. Now as for air support, in the form of bombers and fighters, many small spacecraft, such as Y-Wings and A-Wings, filled these roles perfectly. During the Battle of Umbarra the 501st Legion was tasked with taking a main city, and its airfield. In taking the capital the Clones acted as air support by performing bombing manoeuvres on the Separatist aligned Umbarrans. The Clone pilot Oddball once again helped his brothers on the ground,..by raining hell on the enemy.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why are there some people who got angry when they made female stormtroopers a thing in Star Wars Canon? As far as I'm concerned, I couldn't care less if some stormtroopers were women as it barely affects the story.
Answer: WTF?!? Who are these people, and why are they being dicks? I always thought female Stormtroopers were canon..but anyway, who cares? Oh,..all the bigoted, chauvinistic, sexist neanderthals that call themselves Star Wars fans, who were somehow offended by ‘female Stormtroopers’, got their feathers ruffled? Please! To not make female Stormtroopers canon would be an even greater injustice. These girls were absolutely badass. The first female stormtrooper to be named was Jes Gistang(EU), from Corellia. In 137ABY Gistang served as a trooper in Darth Krayts Galactic Empire. Being homeless and taken in by an Imperial Mission Gistang was soon inducted into the Stormtrooper Corp, and found a home operating a BB-23 Heavy Blaster Canon. The first canon female trooper was this unnamed young lady, (below left) who served in the 501st around 130ABY. She was the very first canon female Stormtrooper. Going back to the Sequel Trilogy, two of the only redeeming characters in that travesty were Captain Phasma and Jannah, formerly known by her First Order operating number TZ-1719. Phasma was the Commander of the First Orders Stormtrooper Corps,.. and made fighting men look effortless. Her commanding presence and towering height made her one badass female Stormtrooper, but this great opportunity was wasted like so many other characters in the sequel trilogy. Jannah was a First Order Stormtrooper who desserted her Legion, along with the rest of her fellow First Order fighters. She led a clan of warriors on an ocean moon, then joined the Resistance and helped take down the Sith Eternal Fleet on Exegol. Jannah did help change the story significantly,..and coincidentally she was also one of the most gorgeous Stormtroopers I've ever seen! Then there was the only known female Deathtrooper, designated DT-F16. She was a Deathtrooper for the Empire, tasked with guarding a massive Kyber crystal that was going to be used in the construction of the Death Star. She went out with one almighty bang, as the crystal was damaged deliberately by a Rebel saboteur causing a devastating explosion. All these women are absolutely fantastic canon inclusions into the Star Wars Universe, and I say the more the better. I'd love to see a female equivalent of Thrawn! She'd be badass. Now why would stupid men..umm.., I mean Star Wars fans..get ‘angry’ at the canon inclusion of these lovely ladies?

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Which Star Wars animal would make the best house pet?
Answer: The Star Wars Universe has a zoological parade of creatures that could fit the role of house pet perfectly. We have Puffer Pigs, Porgs, Corellian Hounds, Convurs, Lothcats, Voorpaks and Vulptex’s..to name but over half a dozen. Each of these creatures has their own attributes that appeal to a wide audience. Some may like a pet to snuggle up on their lap, or you may want a guard dog like pet to protect your home and loved ones. There's something here for every prospective pet owner. Puffer Pigs are like the Earthly equivalent of a Pot Bellied Pig, and are quite a valuable creature. They have the ability to sniff out precious substances, like Tibanna gas, so fetch a hefty price tag in the SWU. Just don't scare them with any sudden sounds! Now Porgs;..I know what you're thinking..but they're just the same as owning a loud mouthed, Guinea Pig, and could make good company for the young and elderly. Maybe it's a bit pricey importing them from Ach-To. Corellian Hounds are just like owning a Mastiff, or Rottweiler, and will competently perform at guarding your loved ones while they sleep at night. Don't leave them alone with the Porgs though. Or if you'd more prefer a Pekingese or a Pug, then you can't go past a Voorpak. Torra Dozer, from the SW animated series Resistance, owns a loveable male Voorpak named Buggles. Buggles would actually make for a perfect house pet. Maybe you'd like a Vulptex, which closely resembles a Fox or Coyote, only they have a crystalline coat of spiny hairs. Yeah, maybe this one shedding on the couch isn't such a good idea,..so let's look at the more feline pet companion. Loth Cats are a great alternative to a common house cat, because they act as a guard pet, as well as a warm, snuggly lap companion. Did anyone check that Loth Cat out in The Mandalorian, when Din Djarin first met Cara Dune in the tavern on Sorgan? That thing wanted to shred Grogu to pieces. When it comes to my personal choice I would have to choose the same companion animal as Ahsoka Tano. After the celestial changing events on Mortis, a small green Convur, named Morai, befriended lady Tano. It was rumoured to be the reincarnation of the Mortis God, the sister. Morai was native to Mortis but Convurs are normally naturally found in the jungles of Wasskah. In the real world I own a foul mouthed, female Eclectus parrot from the jungles of New Guinea, named Rosie. Rosie can be quite loud, and aggressive when she is moulting, or going through hormonal changes,..so a Convur like Morai would be a refreshing change of house pet. My smart mouthed bird wouldn't last 5 minutes in the SWU, before some police droid took her into custody for using excessive profanity in a public place. Below; Rosie my parrot.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What was the purpose of carbonite in Star Wars?
Answer: Carbonite was created from carbon gas, and made as solid as steel through a rapid freezing process. Early throughout history in the SWU Carbonite was known by spacefarers for its incredible stasis qualities, and its use was employed aboard early navigational vessels and deep space freighters. Before the invention of the hyperdrive engine space travellers were encased in carbonite as a type of stasis in between long interstellar journeys. After intergalactic travel became possible without the use of Carbonite its use was primarily employed in the industrial sector, with Carbonite being used to transport unstable and volatile materials such as Coaxium and Tibanna gas. Thousands of years before the Battle of Yavin the Sith used Carbonite to encase entire armies,..ready for battle at the push of a button. The Carbonite chamber on Bespins Cloud City was used to safely store Tibanna gas, which was used in hyperdrive fuel, coolant and weapons systems. It was designed as an industrial model, which is why Han Solo experienced the lingering and debilitating effects of Carbonite, or hibernation, sickness. Much earlier models did not leave Carbonite encased passengers with such severe conditions upon ‘thawing’, as they weren't designed for industrial applications. Needless to say hibernation sickness was not missed at all upon the advent of the hyperdrive, and bio entropic field generators. Jabba the Hutt put a bounty on Han Solos head, and when Boba Fett delivered the prize, the Corellian Captain was encased in Carbonite. Jabba intended to use Solo as a grim piece of art to hang on his palace wall, but Jabba was inspired by another alien culture who did exactly this. The ancient Krath species used Carbonite on living beings, in their conquest of the Carbonite mines in the Empress Teta System. They were displaying their enemies, as wall trophies trapped forever in Carbonite, long before Jabba got the idea to do it to Han Solo. Below; a Krath warrior.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What makes CGI Tarkin from Rogue One land in the Uncanny Valley?
Answer: Why is no one asking the same question about Princess Leia from Rogue One ?!? Look, I might be the first one here to admit it but I actually think that Tarkin in Rogue One looks incredible, given that Peter Cushing died in 1994. The animation supervisor on R1, Hal Hickel, explained the process of getting Tarkin back to the screen, and it was quite fascinating. The actor who played Tarkin in R1 was Guy Henry. Henry acted the part of Tarkin whilst filming, and had CGI locator dots placed on his face. This was so they could superimpose a CGI Tarkin image over the top of Henry's face, and the two were merged into the final character. The problem here is when the animation studio does the “motion likeness” pass, where animators blend the CGI Tarkin head, to the actors body. The actor doesn't smile exactly like Tarkin, or use the same muscles in his face, so the animators carefully adjust the actors CGI face to blend in with the CGI Tarkin face. I believe that the translation between the memory of the original actor, and the new CGI version of him, is lost during this process in creating a fully believable version of Tarkin. Let's face it, we all knew it wasn't going to be Peter Cushing when we originally watched Rogue One, and this knowledge probably detracts from the visual image we are being tricked with. This leads our minds to put CGI Tarkin in the ‘Uncanny Valley’ category,..and after that point we can't ever believe we're watching the actual Peter Cushing. But that's not the point I'm trying to make here. The animators who created CGI Tarkin for Rogue One were presented with the challenge of making the actors face, line up perfectly with a CGI Tarkin model. This is where they either nail the deep fakery,..or lose it in translation on a whole with the audience. But in this case I have to tip my hat to Hal Hickel, and the team at Industrial Light and Magic. The CGI Tarkin in Rogue One was a lot more believable than that ‘uncanny’ as hell Princess Leia. Something sure as shit got lost in translation there!

Name: John Bambrook
Question: In "The Empire Strikes Back" the Millennium Falcon flies into the mouth of a creature on an Asteroid. How could such a creature survive in space?
Answer: The creature in question is called an Exogorth, and the one that the crew of the Millennium Falcon encountered in the Hoth asteroid belt was named Sy-O. Exogorths are enormous, silicon based, space faring creatures that live in the hollowed out recesses of asteroids and small moons. Reaching a mature age at 10 years the Exogorth divides itself into two beings, which can each continue growing up to an extraordinary length of around 900 metres. These creatures are classified as sentient beings, and can live for billions of years in the vacuum of space. Surviving by embedding tail tendrils into the asteroid, and feeding off the mineral deposits held within, Exogorths have been known to feast off space debris, and even swallow passing starships. The question of how it survives in space may lie in its physiology. Being a silicon based lifeform it's been theorised that such beings do not require oxygen to survive; but the Exogorth could also derive life sustaining elements from the mineral deposits it ingests. Purrgils were similar space faring creatures that also survived in the vacuum of space unharmed. They ingested an element, in the form of gas deposits, called Clouzon-36,which could propel them through hyperspace. This blueish green gas was also used as a hyperdrive fuel for starships, but the Purrgil gained tremendous sustenance from this mineral gas. The Exogorths may have survived in space thanks to a similar physiological means as the Purrgils,..or it may have been due to something else entirely different altogether. Sy-O was around a billion years old, and was considered a fledgling amongst his kind. Apparently Exogorths take pride in sustaining large ecosystems within their gargantuan bodies. Sy-O was ridiculed by other older Exogorths for only being able to sustain Mynocks in his ecosystem. Older Exogorths have ecosystems which could sustain many lifeforms, which could explain as to how Exogorths might survive in space. Sy-O wanted to swallow and keep the inhabitants of the Millennium Falcon, as to make his ecosystem more diverse to others of his species. Reference; Wookiepedia, Exogorths (canon section)

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What if Darth Vader found out about his children after he killed one of them?
Answer: Let's say for instance that Darth Vader actually killed Leia during her interrogation aboard the Death Star. After Kenobi becomes one with the force he pays Vader a visit,..and let's him know about the tragic news. What then? At first Vader is going to assume that Kenobi is playing tricks from beyond the grave, but after the story of Luke and Leia surviving becomes fully known to the Sith Lord, what would Vader do? This would cement Palpatines full betrayal in the eyes of Vader. He would realise that his master had decieved him, and so treacherously at that, and would probably respond by killing the Emperor in his sleep. Vader would certainly have not forgotten the tale of Darth Plagueis the Wise, which his master told him so long ago; and then had lied to him later, by informing him that it was himself who killed his own wife. Vader was no fool by any measure, and after the tragic death of his daughter,..by his very own hands..Vader would play his cards very close to his chest until the time to strike was right. But then again, Vader might waltz right on up to Palpatine and attempt to obliterate the old man on sight. By Kenobi revealing the truth to him Vader would then focus his efforts on turning Luke to the darkside, much the same way he did in the original trilogy. Only with the Emperor out of the picture Vader would be free to find his son, without Palpatine stalling him. The only question is how Luke responds, after his father tells him that he killed his sister. This question opens up a lot of other questions in answering it. Vader will definitely want revenge, and probably achieve it. The raw hatred and fury that Vader will draw upon to defeat his master will make him more powerful than Sidious; as Sidious once told Master Yoda. But the issue of Leias death is still going to reverberate long after the supposed demise of Palpatine.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How would you make a Star Wars horror movie?
Answer: There was an idea floating around a while back, that I thought had the perfect makings for a Star Wars horror movie. Let's face it, us more mature fans would love to see an R-rated, guts and gore, blood soaked, Star Wars horror fest,..and this idea was inspired by one of the most terrifying horror movies that came out of the 1980’s. Anyone remember John Carpenters 1982 horror flick, The Thing? Then its prequel was made even more @&#%ed up and horrifying again in 2011!! The highly intelligent, shape-shifting, Lovecraftian alien creature from these nightmarish movies is the basis for the John Carpenter/Star Wars horror crossover movie. When I was a kid in the 80’s my mom left me at home sometimes at night while she went to work. What she didn't know was that I would sit there with the old VHS player watching horror movies from the ‘grownup’ tapes. One of these movies was the 1982 nightmare, The Thing. This movie scared the ever-loving crap outta me well into my twenties, as I watched this remote Antarctic research team fight amongst themselves, and the shape-shifting alien that had infiltrated their base. The atmosphere of pure terror and horror this movie produced was absolutely unbelievable in my young mind, and I'll never forget the moments that I nearly shat myself as a 7 year old kid, watching Kurt Russell deliver some justice to this ungodly being. Now just imagine, that instead of the icy wastes of Antarctica,.. that it was the frozen world of Hoth this nightmarish alien and its ship crash landed on. Then imagine the shapeshifter killed and imitated a settler, or Rebel Soldier, a Tauntaun, or even a massive Wampa. Imagine the chaos and utter panic in a location like Echo Base, with this thing, *no pun intended*, running around causing mayhem, mistrust, panic and bone chilling fear. For some strange reason to me horror movies seem more terrifying when they're not just set at night time, but in the middle of the icy snow as well. This isn't even my own idea for a Star Wars horror movie,..but I would pay for first class seats to see this one. The last scene in the movie would be the Thing escaping in a busted up snowspeeder,..as it sees an Imperial Star Destroyer break through the upper atmosphere of Hoth, on its way to disembark it's troops below.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How powerful was the Star Wars Droid 11-4D?
Answer: For those of you who don't know the amazing story of 11-4D, this ‘protocol droid’ was once the servant to Darth Plagueis, and then he was inherited by Plagueis’ apprentice,..Darth Sidious. This peculiar droid was once privy to some of the most secretive information in the galaxy,..including how to unlock the secrets of immortality, and some of Palpatines juiciest secrets. In terms of physical power he was just as strong as any other droid in his class, except a few minor ‘modifications’ added by his masters over the years,..but in terms of the knowledge or data that he retained, I doubt that any other droid in the galaxy would have memories of such wicked and unbelievable knowledge and events. In Legends he was officially designated as a First Degree Medical Droid owned by Darth Plagueis, but later in canon he was classed as a protocol droid belonging to Darth Sidious. He was much like any other humanoid based droid, in that he had two arms and two legs, but he also had multiple appendages concealed in his midsection. These were designed for medical and interactive technological purposes, and two were retrofitted utility arms with a laser included. This droid had amazing optics and photoreceptors, and was a state of the art medical droid capable of performing technical surgical procedures by himself. Originally he was a medic droid from Obroa-Skai, and then fell into the possession of a Togruta freighter captain. This is where his journey under the two most powerful beings in the galaxy began,..after Darth Plagueis stowed away aboard the freighter Woebegone, then slaughtered the entire crew and took possession of 11-4D. After landing the job of Plagueis’ personal lab assistant 11-4D bore witness to all of the most unsettling and unbelievable experiments done by his Sith master. He learned applications pertaining to midichlorian manipulation, and the secrets of life and death. He was quite an efficient detective droid also, as he helped his master track down force sensitive beings. The droid also was present when Plagueis’ enemies used a nuclear bomb on his fortress on Sojourn. This droid gathered and analysed data that was worth hundreds of billions of credits in the wrong hands, and was privy to all of Darth Plagueis’ dark experiments. After Sidious killed Plagueis, 11-4D fell under his new masters control. 11-4D acted as a protocol droid to his new master. Under Chancellor Palpatine the droid acted as his personal holo video keeper. Just imagine what was in that library of unspeakable secrets! After Palpatine declared himself Emperor, and swept the remains of the Republic away, 11-4D became instrumental in creating another one of Palpatines secrets. Deep inside the Imperial Palace, which was built over the remains of the Jedi Temple, the droid excavated beneath the palace and temple, and located an old Sith Shrine that the Jedi built over the top of. This is why the Jedi originally built their beloved temple on that specific site;..so they could bury and banish the memory of Sith that were once located on Coruscant. 11-4D helped Palpatine locate and tap into the darkside temple, hidden deep under the bowels of the Imperial Palace. It was also highly likely that this droid was present at the medical facility on Coruscant when Vader had his life saving surgery. This droid held some of the most amazing secrets in its memory recordings, as it had served the most powerful and evil men in the entire galaxy. If knowledge is power, then outside of R2-D2, 11-4D was the most powerful droid in the galaxy.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: At what point on his way to Alderaan did Obi-Wan know that this was a one-way trip?
Answer: Kenobi knew that when he packed up the boys on Tatooine, and made way for the doomed planet of Alderaan, that he probably wasn't coming back. Nearly 20 years prior to taking up residency on the desert planet he was tasked by the most powerful, and senior member of the Jedi in the Order, to watch over and protect the son of Darth Vader. He had done this task, and protected Luke for the better part of two decades. But he also knew that at some point he would have to face Vader, and he doubted whether he could best his former pupil in open combat. The years had not been kind to his body, but Kenobi had already prepared himself for his confrontation with Vader. During his time on Tatooine Kenobi mastered the art of becoming a force spirit. He had achieved this by learning the technique from his former master Qui-Gon Jinn, who had become the first to learn this forgotten Jedi technique, then taught it to Master Yoda also during his seclusion on Dagobah. Kenobi was just waiting for the right time to choose his own passing, and transcend into the great unknown; but for himself he now knew what lay beyond his own death. He was too old to defeat Vader singlehandedly, and he had to ensure the preservation of the Jedi Order. The only way of doing this was to die in the physical form..and become one with the force. When Kenobi secured passage for himself and Luke to Alderaan he felt the billions of lives snuffed out on Alderaan, as a result of the Empire activating their new superweapon. He knew that the Emperor, and his servant Vader must be stopped from their hold on intergalactic power, and he knew exactly when to choose the moment of his own passing into the spirit world. That's right,..Kenobi never actually got cut down by Vader, which a lot of viewers of ‘A New Hope’ never paid attention to. He choose that moment when Vader took his death swing to transend beyond the physical form. Vader witnessed it..Luke witnessed it, and Leia witnessed it. Kenobi wanted Luke, and Vader, to know that he had become more powerful in death, than he was in the land of the living. Kenobi knew that before he even set foot on the battle station,..that this stop was the end of his one way trip.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Do you think Obi-Wan wanted Uncle Owen and Aunt Beru to die so nothing would hold Luke back from leaving Tatooine?
Answer: At some point Luke Skywalker was going to leave his aunt and uncles house on Tatooine. It was just a matter of ‘when’,..and not ‘if’. Luke had been raised on Tatooine for his entire life, and Owen and Beru had done all that they could possible to ensure that Luke was raised right. He was well spoken, a keen pilot, a sharp shot and educated to a galactic standard. They couldn't have done any better, with what they had, and were genuinely proud of Luke. Kenobi’s task was to watch over the ‘new hope’ that will rise someday, and he had fulfilled this purpose as Luke had become a man..unharmed and ready to make his own way in the galaxy. Kenobi knew that when he eventually revealed some of Lukes past to him that the young man's curiosity would eventually get the better of him. Owen had warned Kenobi for years to stay away from Luke, and had rejected the Jedi’s offer of help. Owen knew as well, that as soon as Luke got a whif of lightsabers and a mention about his blood father that he would want to leave the family's moisture farm. Kenobi certainly wished the Lars couple no harm whatsoever, and knew that they couldn't stop Luke because he had become a man. It was just a matter of time in Kenobis eyes, but as it turned out time had already caught up with Luke. The force was calling out to both Luke and his sister Leia, and drawing them inexorably together. Kenobi knew he had one final role to play in all of this, and that was to train Luke, and eventually confront Vader. He had been waiting for this moment for nearly two decades under the twin suns of Tatooine, and had already learned from his former master, Qui-Gon Jinn, how to transcend death and become a force spirit. In doing so he would be able to continue Lukes training, and hopefully one day restore the Jedi Order through the work of Luke Skywalker. This was his entire purpose of staying on Tatooine, and watching over the son of his former pupil. Owen and Beru had played their role as parents, but Kenobi knew that once Luke started training under his tutelage he would forget about emotional attachments; according to the Jedi way; and that once he was on the path to becoming a Jedi Own and Beru would matter no more to their nephew. A Jedi has no time for the emotional attachments, and setbacks, that loving their parents would create in a Jedi’s mind. But Kenobi certainly didn't wish death upon them by any measure. This is not the way of the Jedi.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: In Star Wars, how are the Hutts so powerful when they are all huge immobile blobs?
Answer: Look at the fictional, infamous Mafia crime boss Don Vito Corleone from The Godfather movies. He started his massive criminal empire when he was a young, fit and power driven young man. He knew he had the talent for it, and he was motivated by revenge after a Mafia Don killed his own father. By the end of his illustrious life of crime he was a bit of an ‘immobile blob’, as a result of delegating the running of his empire mainly to his head minions,..and living a lazy, lavish and luxurious lifestyle. Stress was undoubtedly another factor contributing to his eventual demise. Jabba the Hutt, and the rest of the Hutt Cartel, are much like Vito and the Mafia from The Godfather. The Hutt Cartel were a centuries old, extremely powerful and vastly influencial crime family, that profiteered from the drug trade, slavery, extortion, gambling and all the other trappings of an intergalactic crime syndicate; just like Vito and the Mafia. In The Clone Wars animated they even have a Hutt based on Marlon Brandos Don Vito Corleone,..aptly called Marlo the Hutt; complete with a cheesy little moustache like Vito! How cool is this little homage by Lucas paid to Don Vito Corleone!! Below; Marlo the Hutt, as seen in ‘The Clone Wars’. The Hutts had amassed their tremendous power, and more importantly influence, over centuries of being big time crimelords, so now they could kick back on their fat, lazy asses and let their criminal employees do all the heavy lifting..if you know what I mean? Above; the surprisingly buff Bokku the Hutt. The Hutts were much like big fat mafia bosses, who no longer needed to do the physical work of running an enormous criminal syndicate; and by no means were Hutts ‘immobile blobs’ at all. One was even a member of the Jedi Order at one point, so “immobile”..I don't think so. Others like Grakuss, and Bokku the Hutt, were actually quite buff, violent, agile, and powerful for a Hutt. Below; the extremely agile and aggressive Grakuss the Hutt, demonstrating that he is far from being an ‘immobile blob’. A Hutt, when his back was pushed to the wall, was quite capable of leaping into quick bursts of action..if it means saving their skin! The Hutts were known to use their massive size to their advantage, and can crush, whack and even eat their human sized opponents! Hutts just didn't need to spring into action like this anymore, because their ancestors had done all the hard work for them,..centuries prior to before they inherited their massive, criminal empires.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Do you think Darth Vader is the best pilot in the Galaxy?
Answer: Without a doubt! As Anakin Skywalker he was widely known amongst the Jedi to be the greatest starship pilot in the Order, but then after his transformation into Darth Vader I believe he was an even more deadlier and proficient pilot than before. In Rebels animated, during the ‘Seige of Lothal’, Vader singlehandedly takes on the Rebel cell Phoenix Squadron,..and hands their asses back to them in a little velvet lined box. Vader exhibits amazing prowess as a pilot, as he manoeuvres his TIE Advanced X1 with devastatingly lethal effect. Using the force, coupled with his natural piloting abilities, Vader cuts through the Rebels with ease, decimating them as if he was accompanied by a full squadron of TIE Fighters;..but it was just Vader doing it all alone. His attack destroyed many small fighters and even crippled a Corellian Corvette, forcing the entire Rebel crew to abandon ship. Hera Syndulla, the greatest pilot in the Rebel Alliance, bore witness to Vaders greatness this day. When he was only 9 Vader took the prestigious title of winning the Boonta Eve Pod race on Tatooine; and was the only human to ever do so. He then used his uncanny piloting abilities to completely destroy a Separatist Command ship during the Battle of Naboo. This turned the tide of the battle into the Republics favour. After that he used Jedi starfighters to become the greatest pilot that the Jedi Order ever produced. After the rise of the Empire nothing changed. Vader was a naturally gifted pilot that used the darkside of the force to make the absolute impossible seem possible. His unpredictable, death defying, spinning manoeuvres, and his unparalleled skill in any starship he jumped in, made him by far the greatest..and deadliest pilot in the entire Star Wars Universe.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Would Dooku do worse against Sidious than Maul did?
Answer: No,..in fact Count Dooku would put up a far better contest than Maul ever provided Darth Sidious. Palpatine used the good ‘ol force choke to keep his second apprentice Dooku on his toes, but take this little sly trick out of the equation..and give them some time to fight it out like a couple of men..then Dooku would fare much better than Maul did on Mandalore. Sidious used force push, force grab, a flurry of lightsaber moves..and force lightning to ultimately subdue Maul during their epic duel. Granted that Sidious didn't intend on killing Maul on this occasion, and Maul did put up a compelling effort, but Dooku was a more refined lightsaber combatant that was once revered to be one of the most skilled duelists in the entire Jedi Order. When he eventually succumbed to the darkside he furthered his skill set under Sidious’ tutelage. Dooku was capable of levitating someone, force choking them, and using force lightning on them…all at once! Dooku had trained under the best, and had eventually become the best. Then through the darkside he became an even more deadly opponent. During the events in the canon comic series, Son of Dathomir, Dooku and Sidious briefly spar, after the Count is possessed by the witch Mother Talzin, and Sidious remarks on Dooku's lightsaber skills. One force ability that Dooku possessed, which Maul did not, was force lightning. This would allow Dooku to avoid the fate of Maul, being electrocuted, and the Count would simply counterattack Sidious’ lightning resulting in them resorting to lightsaber combat. This happened when Yoda faced Dooku on Geonosis, only Yoda absorbed Dookus lightning resulting in a stalemate. Dooku put up a pretty good fight against Yoda, as did Yoda when he fought Sidious in the Senate building. But Palpatine won on this occasion because he elected to take the high ground and start whipping senatorial pods at Yoda. Against Dooku, on solid footing,..Darth Sidious would be presented with a genuine challenge from Darth Tyranus..and a far better contest than Maul provided his former master.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: In Star Wars, do the droids have feelings?
Answer: This is hard to answer, but I'm saying yes to this one. This raises a very ethical question in the Star Wars Universe, but there are many indicators to demonstrate that droids do indeed have feelings. The long standing relationship between C-3P0 and R2-D2 shows us that droids cared for one another, and organic beings as well. From the moment they met one another their relationship showed us a caring and compassionate side to them, as well as a difference of opinions, and a humorous quality to their relationship. Sometimes it was as if the two were an old married couple griping over the days events! The artificial intelligence in the Star Wars Universe far surpasses any that can be conceived yet here on Earth. Droids programming enabled a caring side to be displayed, as with droids such as protocol, medical and servant variants. But as time prolongs the AI in droids must develop a kind of artificial consciousness; the more they learn, the more expressive emotionally they can become, depending on how limiting their programming allows for. The factors that determine whether they express feelings depends on the cost of each droid in question. Take the comparison between a B1 Battle Droid and a Human Replica Droid. Human Replica Droids were rare, and extremely expensive. This allowed their creators to expand on the capabilities of their programming, and resulted in a powerful form of artificial intelligence capable of expressing emotion. Guri was a HRD that was developed by Imperial scientists, the Thrumble brothers. She cost 9 million credits to create, and was capable of expressing feelings; although anger was the main one. Her programming allowed her to build upon her emotional functions. Now compare Guri to the mass produced B1 Battle Droids of the Separatist Alliance. Initially they relied upon a central command ship to relay orders and extra programming, but after the Battle of Naboo Separatist command eliminated the need of a Central Command ship by giving them independent programming. The overload of information they processed developed in quirks in their programming. But one would argue that this independant programming resulted in the droids being able to express their feelings.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Is the Star Wars character Commander Doom's design based on Marvel’s Doctor Doom?
Answer: Actually..yes, it is! I always wondered this myself over the years, solely based on the name and the green cape synonymous with Marvels supervillain, Dr Doom. Then I did a bit of research and found out that the design for Clone Commander Doom was absolutely based on the MCU Supervillain. For decades now Dr Doom has sported his trademark green cape and outfit, with gold accents, covering his suit of armour. When it came to designing a cool new Clone Commander for Lucas’ The Clone Wars, Dr Dooms outfit design fitted the bill nicely! And so a new Clone Commander was created, and given the nickname ‘Doom’, to pay homage to great and infamous Dr Doom. Clone Commander Doom was introduced in season 6 of TCW, and was present during the Battle of Ringo Vinda, where a preemptive execution of Order 66 lead to the death of his Jedi General Tiplar. Commander Doom, and his men (the doom troopers) are seen battling the Separatist forces of Admiral Trench, and grieving over their fallen commander, as the culprit is questioned by Anakin Skywalker.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why did clone troopers paint their armor?
Answer: Because unlike their Stormtrooper successors in the Empire, the Clone troopers of the Grand Army of the Republic were encouraged to be individuals by their Jedi handlers. Despite being grown in a sterile lab, and being raised in a bland, sterile environment, the Clones were surprisingly artistic in their expressions on their helmets and armour. The Kaminoans created them as just another business venture to make profit on, and as such they had clean, shiny, sterile outfits when presented to the Jedi upon the orders completion. Above; just some of the many clonetrooper helmets, with their individual markings displayed. After the handover to the Jedi, the Clones on a whole were encouraged to be individuals, and not just serial numbers. The Jedi had been tasked with being generals in the Clone wars, and the Clones were the armies under their command. Unlike the Kaminoans, the Jedi allowed them to express their individuality on their armour, helmets, weapons and vehicles. More often than not the colours and designs on the Clones armour represented what battalion or legion each clone was attached to, and they were pretty creative in their designs. Take the 501st Legion for example. They characterised themselves with a navy blue colour, and each respective trooper in the unit gave individual markings and designs on their helmets and armour. Captain Rex has accentuated Jaig eyes painted on his helmet, Echo has the bloodstained handprint of a Rishi Eel on his chest plate, and when former Jedi General, Ahsoka Tano, rejoined the Legion during the Seige of Mandalore the entire legion painted their helmets in respect to their former commander.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did Darth Sidious respect General Grievous and his abilities?
Answer: Darth Sidious didn't genuinely respect anyone. He told his apprentice, Darth Vader, that he viewed Count Dooku as being just a “proton torpedo”, who served his purpose and was done. Now if he summed up Dooku in such a casual manner..like he was just a spent ammunition clip, then when it came to ‘respecting’ General Grievous he would have viewed him as being far lesser than the Count ever was. Palpatine was just a sociopathic, genocidal, and conniving monster. He never respected anyone..not even himself. I mean, after becoming a god like, intergalactic dictator, with an unlimited bank balance, you'd think that he would have gone to see a plastic surgeon, or a dentist,..or just someone!! He didn't respect his own appearance, only the power that he craved. The man that was Sheev Palpatine was a nightmarish ghoul that had become someone far worse after his descent to the darkside. After that the only respect that he truly gave to anything was his ‘grand plan’ for galactic dominance. After he'd seized the galaxy for himself nothing else mattered to him,..except for himself maintaining the monopoly on power he'd amassed over years of plotting and murdering. During the Clone Wars General Grievous was just another tool, or pawn, or any other individual that Palpatine manipulated as a means to an end. He certainly didn't respect him as a friend, acquaintance, or even as an associate. He may have given a slight nod to the generals leadership and tactical skills, but apart from that General Grievous was just another expendable goon. He had to get rid of the cybernetic warlord after the conclusion to the Clone Wars anyway, so Grievous was basically living on borrowed time..at Palpatines expense.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Darth Sidious once said the Jedi and Sith are similar in almost every way. How?
Answer: Both lightside and darkside,..the Jedi and the Sith, utilise the force to achieve greatness. Now its that greatness that is interpreted differently by both orders, that distinguishes the Jedi from the Sith. Besides this..Darth Sidious was absolutely right. He just interpreted it from a certain point of view,..as did the Jedi. The argument that Skywalker and Kenobi have on Mustafar perfectly explains the conflict going on in Anakins mind, after Sidious’ meddling with his thoughts. He had just converted from being a Jedi to a Sith, and the first order of business pertaining to ‘his new empire’ was reinstating galactic peace. The Jedi were much the same in that they too had been striving to maintain a stranglehold on intergalactic peace; and they were prepared to kill for it..just like the Sith. Both orders based their religious philosophies around the force. Both orders were strict and diligent in their training. Although the Sith, in the last thousand years leading up to Darth Sidious, used Darth Banes ‘rule of two’, both the Jedi and the Sith use a master and apprentice learning system. Both wear hooded robes and both carry lightsabers, and when in combat both sides draw upon the force, and the skills they have learned pertaining to the force, to defeat their enemies. The Jedi and the Sith were similar in almost every single way, except the line each was willing to cross to achieve victory.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Would Palpatine ever risk his cover to save himself with Force powers during a life or death situation?
Answer: A life..or death..situation. Palpatine is definitely going to blow his cover if the alternative is death, but in saying so he will probably kill any and all witnesses present to see him use his hidden force powers. He's not going to blow his cover in a heavily populated setting, because that would just be counter productive to all that he's worked for,..but if there are only enough witnesses for Darth Sidious to deal with personally, then.. In the EU novel, Darth Plagueis, Sidious’ Muun master taught his apprentice everything he knew, including the use of ‘the cloak of the profane’. This was a technique that Sidious used for decades to disguise his presence within the force. He fooled the Jedi, even as they stood only a foot from him, and it served him extremely well. It would have to be something pretty life threatening for Palpatine to abandon this disguise, but if it meant the demise of the Sith Order because a gang of Weequay thugs were pointing blasters at him, Palpatine would probably execute them in a heartbeat, and cover his tracks on the fly. Below; Darth Plagueis breaks his cover, first against attacking Maladians, and also on the freighter ‘Woebegone’, where he slaughters the entire crew. Palpatine was no fool by any measure, and he had used subterfuge to cover his murderous deeds in the past. When he murdered Darth Plagueis, after getting him highly inebriated, he blamed the cause of ‘Hego Damasks’ death on a faulty respirator. Palpatine fried his master to death, in a penthouse apartment, so he had to make the Muuns death look like an accident. Plagueis wore a respirator after being attacked by treacherous Maladians, and Palpatine used this to his advantage, saying that his friend Hegos mask malfunctioned..and electrocuted his poor friend to death. Palpatine would kill his would be attackers by frying them to death also..and probably blame their deaths on a faulty something or other!

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why does the seventh sister have such a unique voice, even slightly electronic?
Answer: Every Jedi who was inducted into the Imperial Inquisitorious was personally taught the lesson of loss..at the hand of Darth Vader himself. Now that may have included losing a limb, or being bisected! Vader was utterly merciless as he taught the inductees to fully respect the value of loss,.. and use the tremendous anger and pain that it generated to make them even more powerful darkside adepts. Each Inquisitors outfit was all black leather and fancy padding, so it was hard to tell if the Seventh Sister had lost a limb;..but she was one really intriguing customer. She did have an electronically enhanced voice when she has her mask on..but still an echo of it persists after it is removed. My suspicion was that during her day, that Vader instructed the lesson of loss to her, she may have gotten a bit too lippy with her new darklord overseer...and Vader possibly crushed her larynx or something equally appropriate. She could have suffered a neck or throat injury, requiring the permanent use of an electronic vocabulator, or she might even have been mute from birth..and taught to speak through the use of a voice enhancer. We just don't know the definitive reason behind why her voice is slightly electronically manipulated. Or..it might be because of the fact that the ageless Sarah Michelle Gellar, the actress who voiced the Seventh Sister, is married in real life to Freddie Prinze Jr, who voiced Kanan Jarrus in Rebels animated. Now when they confront one another in the series it might sound a bit like a lovers quarrel, or an old married couple arguing about something,..just totally detracting from the story being told; y'know..just give her voice that cold, mechanical tone to let you know who actually wears the pants around here.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Can viruses hinder Darth Vader and General Grievous?
Answer: Of course,..each of these cybernetic warlords were once organic beings, that had to resort to living in expensive survival suits. Both Vader and Grievous retained most of their vital organs after eachs respective transformations, but the skin was all but destroyed or completely missing in both cases. The outer layer of skin is one of the most important factors when it comes to the immune system. Without the skin their is no natural acidic barrier, meant to act as a buffer against bacterial infections and viruses. Both the good general and the darklord were highly susceptible to viral infections because of this factor. Darth Vader concealed his health issues via constantly hiding in his intimidating suit, but General Grievous’ lung issues were evident upon first appearances with the ex Kaleesh Warlord. When Grievous made the final steps into becoming a cybernetic Jedi slayer he completely discarded his epidermis and skeletal system. His vital organs, including his lungs were also transplanted, but didn't fully take once the procedure was complete. This resulted in a viral infection that led to Grievous’ infamous cough. Vader however made good use of his private bacta tank on Mustafar. The healing properties of the medicinal liquid supplied adequate relief for Vaders medical requirements, and his survival suit did the rest. Underneath Vaders cape, on his back, was the outlet to an advanced environmental filtration system. Outside his bacta baths this sophisticated piece of technology would keep Vader safe from the scum of the galaxy. Now about sand getting in…

Name: John Bambrook
Question: As a Star Wars fan, what's the most absurd piece of lore you know, canon or Legends?
Answer: I'll give you one that's straight up creepy..and absurd, and it's Canon, or is it Legends now.. Well, when A New Hope was released, and it went to VHS, we see the infamous Cantina scene, bristling with fascinating and mysterious aliens. One of these aliens was eventually cut from the original footage, and replaced with a more “less disturbing” character when the special editions were released in the 1990's. It was Lucas’ way of introducing extended scenes and new footage that he couldn't achieve in the 70's and early 80’s. But I believe the character that was replaced was done so justifiably. It was truly an awful character, and there was something unsettling about that little demented worm, that reminded me of a shrivelled up, baby Sarlacc. Let me introduce you to Dice Ibegone. She was a Lamproid, that was a Rebel Alliance member..and the lover of Lak Sivrak..the Werewolf looking dude. Anyways it was rumoured that Dice was ‘force sensitive’,..and wait for it,..was also rumoured that she had the “ability to shift through time”. Now the Wolfman was an intergalactic outlaw..naturally..and the eyeless, multiple appendaged, freak worm instantly fell in love with him. She tried to convince him to join the Rebellion, but it was too late. During the Battle of Hoth, Dice is mortally wounded by debris in the clash between the Empire and the Rebels..and dies in her Wolfman, outlaw lovers hairy arms. I could not make this #&@% up..but..after she died, the Wolfman did fight for the Rebellion until he was gunned down by TIE Fighters during the Battle of Endor. Now this is up there in ‘absurd lore’ knowledge’, but after Sivrak died, he and Dice Ibegone lived on as force spirits forever on the foresty moon! WTF! Now if that ain't absurd then I don't know what else to call it… Reference; Wookiepedia (Legends and Canon), Dice Ibegone.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: In Star Wars, how did the guys firing the Death Star laser even get that job?
Answer: Death Star Gunners, as they were called, were once Imperial Gunners. The highest ranked, and most experienced Imperial Gunners, were selected to become operators of the Death Star superlaser. One of these Imperials was Tenn Graneet,..the actual guy who blew up Alderaan. Graneet was selected among all of the Death Star Gunners to be the guy that flipped the switch of the superweapon. Although he was the main weapon operator Graneet overseen a whole contingent of Death Star Gunners, who trained as a group. Their role was to maintain the delicate energy levels of the weapon, and as a team they could fire the laser with ‘synchronised precision’. But at the end of the day the job of destroying worlds was ultimately in the hands of Graneet. Being the NCO IC of the gunnery crew was one of the most important jobs on board the Death Star, but becoming the galaxies greatest mass murderer began to weigh heavily on Graneets mind. After the destruction of Despayre, the first planet to be annihilated by the Death Star, and then Alderaan, he began to seriously question the Empire. On the day of the destruction of the first Death Star Graneet had begun to become so wracked with guilt, that when the order to fire the weapon was given by Tarkin,..he froze! In his panic he could only utter the words “Standby,..standby…”, which would become his famous last words. His hesitation to fire on Yavin IV gave Luke Skywalker those few precious seconds he needed to destroy the Death Star.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What are some of the dumbest decisions made by Star Wars characters?
Answer: There's a long list of offenders in this category of ‘dumbest decisions made by Star Wars characters’, so hold on while I run through just a few colossal mistakes made by the characters of the Star Wars Universe. Firstly, when Kenobi and Qui-Gon Jinn were dispatched to Naboo in episode I they opened a treasure trove of dumb decisions, with long lasting repercussions. Finding Jar Jar Binks in the swamp, and utilising his knowledge, was necessary, but by doing so the Jedi introduced an individual to the senate, who would ultimately give Palpatine executive powers..leading to the end. Also, and the big one here..was Qui Gon bringing Anakin back to Coruscant. Qui Gon bought Anakin into the fold, spelling the eventual doom of the Jedi. This was by far his dumbest decision. When Yoda found out that the Sith were behind the creation of the clone armies, in season 6 of The Clone Wars, he basically shrugged it off like it was nothing. He said that the Republic needed them..they had them now..who cares that the Sith created these guys! No bad could come of this right? Oh Yoda,.. I thought of all the Jedi YOU would have known better! That was a really dumbass decision on behalf of the Jedi Grand Master. The clones he blindly instilled faith into became the implement of the Orders annihilation. Obi-Wan Kenobi, the great negotiator, is not guilty of making some pretty dumbass decisions either. He failed to nurture and guide Anakin through his fears, and stood by and just watched him fall to the darkside. He was aware of Anakin and Padme, yet said nothing to his ‘brother’ to assure or help him. If he loved him like a brother dearly then why didn't he try to save Anakin long before their last meeting on Mustafar? Then, after realising that Anakin had become a dangerous Sith Lord..he fails to kill the murderer of untold Jedi, on the orders of Yoda. This mistake would cost billions of lives, yet Kenobi thought that by disappearing into a ‘ghost realm’ he could talk away or justify his actions. Colossally dumbass mistakes were made by this..Jedi. For a bunch of enlightened, intergalactic peacekeepers, the Jedi were prone to creating some of the greatest mistakes in galactic history. Mistakes that would plunge the entire galaxy into war, genocide, chaos and untold suffering for generations.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: In Star Wars, is it possible to have a dumb Jedi or is intelligence hand in hand with the force?
Answer: I don't think it's possible to have a naturally dumbass Jedi..but I do believe that on certain occasions Jedi can be dumbasses. Prior to the Clone Wars the Jedi weren't heavily involved in military concflicts on such a grand scale, and once the Clone Wars kicked off they had to adjust their game practically overnight. Some Jedi just lacked the foresight or even courage to participate in a large, military scale conflict. Above; Jedi Sha'a Gi..confirmed dumbass. Take the Battle of Hypori, in Legends. Grievous unveils himself for the first time..inspiring true fear into a young Jedi named Sha'a Gi. Ki-Adi Mundi tries to calm the young Jedi..but in a fit of dumbass'ery Sha'a Gi runs blindly into oblivion..being power stomped by Grievous. Was he a dumbass? Yes..but he was more a scholar than a fighter, and just canon fodder regarding plot. Above; Jedi Knight Nahdar Vebb..confirmed dumbass. Take Jedi Knight Nahdar Vebb. He knew exactly what Grievous was capable of, and that the cyborg had a reputation for being a Jedi slayer; yet still he blindly faces the general all alone, and suffers the fate for being a dumbass. He should have known better but proved he was lacking mental fortitude on this last outing. He wasn't a dumbass, but acted irrationally and with complete disregard for consequence. Above; Jedi Master Coleman Trebor..confirmed dumbass. Coleman Trebor, Jedi Master, couldn't even block two blaster shots from Jango Fett at Geonosis. Hmm..a Jedi master who can't successfully block two lousy blaster shots! Another Jedi named Zym, who was actually in charge of the Order during the Great Galactic War, succumbed to an act of sheer, total dumbass'ery…by actually signing a peace treaty..WITH THE SITH!! C’mon!?! This guy is proof that intelligence and the Jedi do not always go ‘hand in hand’. Below; Jedi Grand Master Zym..confirmed dumbass.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: If Vader, Starkiller, and The Grand Inquisitor teamed up against Sidious would they win?
Answer: At one point in Legends lore Vader actually considered using Starkiller, his secret apprentice, to help him overthrow the Emperor. But Palpatine untimely intervened and ruined that little pipe dream; albeit Vader faked his apprentices death, and still employed him in secret. Vader was a prodigy within the force, and in many respects so was Galen Marek. Vader found him as a small boy, after slaying his Jedi father during the Imperial occupation of Kashyyyk,..and sensed the boys ferocious potential. Trained in secret by Vader, Starkiller became tremendously powerful within the force. So powerful that in Legends he whooped Vaders butt, and was capable of doing smaller scale force lightning similar to what Palpatine did on Exegol. Starkiller could crush a speeding Tie fighter in mid flight, or create a temporarily invincible ‘force bubble’ around himself that could vaporize a whole squad of stormtroopers! The guy was overkill on so many levels, and with Vader staunchly backing him up they stood a good chance at defeating Palpatine. Now, you throw in The Grand Inquisitor and I think you have a winning team. The Grand Inquisitor was once a senior Jedi Temple Guard, which meant he was selected from the very best, and most skilled Jedi. The Order took the position of Temple Guard as a very sacred and respected position. The former Utapau local was a highly skilled and formidable opponent, but in this clash of the titans he would serve more in the capacity of like a ‘spotter’ in a weightlifting setting; he's there to help, but the beefcake is doing all the heavy lifting. Vader and Starkiller may have already have this one in the bag by themselves, but the inclusion of the Grand Inquisitor on their side would only give Vader and Marek an advantage against Darth Sidious. At the very least they could hurl the Inquisitor into Sidious’ face..then simultaneously attack the old man! Vaders force potential alone said he could do the job solo, but with Marek tag teaming, and the Inquisitor being an annoying distraction..this treacherous trio may actually do what the entire Jedi Order failed to.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What would happen if a battle Droid decided to surrender to clones? Would they take them back for interrogation or would they just shoot them on the spot?
Answer: In the Canon animated series, The Clone Wars, Mace Windu offers terms of surrender to a large group of battle droids. The result..non compliance..but my point is that in Canon the second most senior member of the Jedi Order offers the Clones to surrender. Even though the droids are non organic beings, the Jedi still try to maintain an aire of being ‘peacekeepers’ by offering a peaceful surrender. On this occasion the droids resisted and were destroyed, but on other occasions it is the battle droids that want to surrender. The clones offer no such offer of surrender when on the battlefield. The clonetroopers of the Grand Army of the Republic were aquisitioned, breed and conditioned to specifically follow orders and fight on behalf of the Republic and the Jedi. Their on field orders did not conflict with any battle droids cry for surrender, so they were blasted like any other ‘Clanker’ in the droid armies. This is what they were made to do, without surrender as an option for the enemy in nearly every situation. The Republic were facing overwhelming battle droid odds, so every dead ‘Tinny’ was a small tip back in favor to the clones. The battle droids also rarely surrendered, but those that did were B1 make battle droids. They surrendered due to their dodgy enhanced learning programming. The droids at the Battle of Naboo were defeated because of their total reliance on a Central Control Computer, but after this battle they were given independent operating and programming capable of learning somewhat. Their feeble attempts at surrender, after assessing their survival odds, were only met with the swift retribution of the Clones own programming.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What changed between Kenobi's 1st and 2nd confrontation with Maul and Savage in terms of his ability? In the first one he claims that Ventress and he are outmatched, in the second he wins confidently on his own.
