Answer: When Kenobi first fought both Maul and Savage, in the aftermath of the Massacre on Raydonia, he was caught off guard a little. The last time he had seen Maul was when he bisected him on Naboo,..and had actually thought he was dead; until Maul himself contacted the Jedi Council.. and executed civilian hostages on Raydonia in a bid to lure Kenobi on his own terms. Kenobi arrives, playing straight into the Dathomiri brothers trap, and after witnessing an entire village ablaze..and its citizens murdered..Kenobi is initially stunned a bit at Mauls sudden appearance, and his brother Savage backing him up. This was his first encounter with both the Nightbrothers together, and he learned much from this first and failed fight. He was being ragdolled by the brothers until Ventress saved the day, but nonetheless escaped and evaluated himself against the pair. Ventress was capable of choking two Jedi’s simultaneously, and had tutored under Count Dooku, so she actually evened the odds slightly..despite Kenobis protest to being out matched. They were ultimately out matched, but managed to turn the tables on the brothers in the long run. But it wasn't sheer skill and tactics that led him to defeat Maul and Savage on Florrum. In his second encounter with the horned crazies Kenobi was accompanied by another Jedi Master, Adi Gallia. He had learned from the previous encounter not to be too hasty, but Gallia was no match for Savages ferocity. After retreating, and again assessing his odds, he uses Pirate leader Hondo Ohnaka and his reformed gang, to assist him. Leading the pair away to a more secluded area he skillfully attacks in the same spot on Savages leg, like Gallia did, and lands a critical blow. This enables him to sever Savages arm and completely disrupt the fight. He also used Gallias lightsaber to fight in a more aggressive defence style. This enabled him to keep both attackers at bay more, and calculate counter strikes. The brothers only chance at victory was to now retreat themselves, which Kenobi had forced them into..much like they'd done to him on Raydonia. Somehow I also think that the death of Gallia spurned Kenobi into greatness, much like we witnessed him do much later on Mustafar, after the death of the Jedi Order. Kenobis resolve was incredible, which led him to his abilities being enhanced under great pressure.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How did non-Clone Navy officers react to Order 66?
Answer: Order 66 was an order like every other one..on every other day of the Clone Wars. It just so happened that this order, to non-Clone Navy officers, may have appeared a little ‘stern’..but nonetheless these human officers would have complied with the clonetroopers executing Order 66. Remember..the penalty for not being totally complicit with the order was the same as treason, and could warrant an immediate on site military execution. This is evident in events witnessed in The Clone Wars Season 7. Even though non clone officers may have been shocked by the clonetroopers willingness to follow such an order, given the long loyalty demonstrated by their Jedi superiors, they still would have complied and gone along with it just like every other day; but in the case of some future Imperial Officers, like Crix Madine and Jan Dodonna, the seeds of dissent had already been planted. Below top; Crix Madine as a Rebel Alliance head commander, and beneath is a picture of himself as an Imperial Officer. Below; Jan Dodonna, Senior Rebel Alliance General, who was once one of the first Imperial officers to take command of the new Imperial Star Destroyers, before he defected. Both the aforementioned men would defect from the Galactic Empire, as would many more, due to the bare boned, murderous ideals of their new Emperor. Other former Republic Navy stalwarts, such as Wullf Yularen, wouldn't question Imperial orders, just as they didn't disobey Order 66 back on the last day of the Republic.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How was General Grievous able to kill so many Jedi when they could easily defend themselves using Force powers?
Answer: Yes..the Jedi could easily defend themselves using their force powers, but that's easier said than done when you're actually staring down the good general. Grievous designed himself to be a pure weapon against the Jedi in every respect. Before he became a cybernetic monstrosity Grievous was a general during the ‘Huk Wars’, but the Jedi intervened and cruelly made millions of his own people starve to death by blockading Kalee. By slowly transforming himself into an invincible Jedi slaying machine, Grievous took it upon himself to start purging the Jedi Order long before Darth Sidious issued Order 66. He took killing Jedi as something very personal. Slowly upgrading himself, and then becoming completely cybernetically dependant, Grievous’ ‘improvements’,..as he called them to his personal medic droid, made him extremely formidable and capable of taking on the Jedi with their force power advantage. Personally tutoring under Count Dooku, one of the greatest lightsaber duelists in history, afforded Grievous to become proficient in each lightsaber form. This allowed him to best the Jedi in almost any situation. He could engage the Jedi in combat and take a considerable battering. His metal exoskeleton consisted of hardy duranium, his droid legs allowed him to leap great distances, his four cybernetic arms gave him a greater advantage than just two, and his lightsabers made him a whirling dervish of impenetrable spinning blades. He could be bisected and still rip his enemy to pieces, and the good general could even survive for short periods in the vacuum of space. When Grievous abandoned his former organic body he did so in a bid to become superior than the Jedi. After being first unleashed on the unsuspecting Order, in the Stalgasin Hive catacombs on Geonosis, Grievous cut a bloody swathe through the Jedi, with unconfirmed reports that his kill count was in the hundreds. Grievous was able to murder so many Jedi simply because he had extremely enhanced his body to do as such.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What happened to General Grievous’ lair after Order 66?
Answer: Near the Outer Rim world of Vassek, on the third moon, General Grievous had his personal fortress built into the side of an enormous canyon. This castle served as the generals personal lair, and was perpetually surrounded in a thick fog due to the moons eery climate. Grievous had all sorts of amenities from an operating theatre, a central command hub, and even a hangar for his ship, the Soulless One. Dotted with booby traps and Magnaguards, his castle even had personal statues of the general, a trophy room with fallen padawan braids and artifacts, and the generals personal guard dog; a massive, cybernetically enhanced Rogwart named ‘Gor’. The castle was maintained and serviced by Grievous’ personal medical droid and assistant, EV-A4-D. On a whole..this place was full of horrors..and the home to monsters. In 22 BBY a Jedi strike force, led by Masters Kit Fisto and Nahdar Vebb, stormed the castle with devastating consequences. Needless to say Fisto and his astromech were the only survivors, but after the Clone Wars what became of this evil edifice? More than likely Grievous’ lair fell back into the hands of Palpatine and his newly created Galactic Empire. The Separatist Alliance was just a concoction created by Palpatine to help him achieve his goal of intergalactic domination. They were all dead and Palpatine ruled supreme, so Grievous’ Castle probably just became another Imperial outpost, or the home to some Imperial douche bag.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Can only Palpatine execute Order 66?
Answer: No. After the Great Purge of Order 66 Jedi survivors spread far and wide across the galaxy, in a bid for freedom, and to escape the Empire that destroyed the Republic..and the Jedi Order. Ferren Barr was one of these Jedi who escaped the carnage of the Clones and fled off world. Palpatines Jedi assassins, the Inquisitorious, wasn't far behind,..with Vader in tow. When confronted by the gang of murderous Inquisitors Barr uses a Jedi mind trick on the clones in the Purge Trooper squadron accompanying the assassins..and actually uses Order 66 to fool the clones into thinking that the Inquisitors were Jedi. Order 66 takes immediate effect, stunning the suprised Inquisitors, and gives Ferren Barr enough time to escape them. But unfortunately his bold actions would amount to nothing…as Vader cuts him down like so many other Jedi.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What do you think of Star Wars Sith Momin as an artist?
Answer: An artist!!! This sick and twisted individual was as much an artist as Hannibal Lector. Darth Momin, before he became one of the most depraved Sith Lords to ever live, was a sculptor that employed very “questionable” subject matter. This psycho would kill animals, and worse, and sew them together, like the Creeper in Jeepers Creepers!! His controversial art pieces began from an early age..where his mother discovered his horrific secret after seeing it first hand. When he got older he just got more sick and more *&#@ed up. One day he created an immense sculpture, complete with skulls, wings and the entrails of murdered creatures, and upon publicly unveiling it he was immediately jailed for his crimes against nature. This is when he was freed by Lady Shaa..and became a Sith Lord. But his desire to create more twisted sculptures didn't die when he was reborn as a powerful Sith. After killing his master he built a deadly superweapon..designed to freeze his victims in an eternal moment of horror; captured in time forever as just another one of his sick art pieces. Eventually he was killed, and his spirit lived on in his mask. Palpatine gave it to Vader upon his journey to Mustafar, and Vader gave Momin a physical form by way of Momin possessing a local Mustafarian. Afted 9 unsuccessful attempts at creating Fortress Vader he finally succeeded, and was ultimately the one who created the final castle for Vader. This was probably his only successful piece of art, and in the end he had created a massive edifice in honour of the darkside. Vader killed him by crushing him with an enormous chunk of rock, thus ending the reincarnated Sith Lord, and his ‘art’.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What did Jan Dodonna do prior to joining the Rebel Alliance?
Answer: Prior to joining the Rebel Alliance Jan Dodonna had an illustrious military career..on both sides of the conflict. Hailing from the planet of Commenor Dodonna began his impressive career as a bridge officer aboard a Venator- class Star Destroyer. He had enlisted in the Republic Navy, and by the time the Clone Wars had erupted he had already established himself as a respected and gifted Naval officer. His services to the Republic would not be forgotten..when the Galactic Empire took the reigns of the galaxy. For his outstanding service to both the Republic, and the Empire, Dodonna was awarded one of the first ever positions of Captain aboard the new Imperial Star Destroyers. Dodonna was once the thing that he would later swear to destroy, and so becoming totally disillusioned with the Emperor and his tyrannical reign Dodonna proudly defected to the Rebel Alliance. This is where his tactical genius became instrumental in devising the attack that destroyed the Death Star.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who has the worst anger issues in the whole Star Wars?
Answer: Now a lotta people are gonna point fingers at characters like Vader or Maul, but in this case I'm giving the accolade to the bounty hunter Cad Bane. Now normally this guy is a pretty cool customer, but he has ‘anger issues’ that run pretty deep too. Bane had a thing for wide brimmed, leather cowboy hats, and it had to be the exact style. When he bust out of prison with Moralo Eval, and an undercover Obi-Wan, Bane immediately began the search for the perfect headpiece. The first hat he finds, on Nal Hutta, doesn't quite meet his tastes, and he even roughs up the poor old man who ran the shop. Then out of spite, and the desire to get a bigger share of the reward, he sprays his so called fellow bounty hunter in the face with a noxious, knockout spray! Then when he arrives at Dookus pad on Serenno he starts getting all shitty about hats again. He eyes off a prospective hat, but it was owned by an Ithorian bounty hunter. The dude starts intimidating the hunter, then before it can be sorted civilly Bane shoots the Ithorian dead! He takes the deceased hunters hat, and acts like it's as casual as buttering toast. Oh yeah,..and later he becomes so frustrated, and impatient, that he ‘accidentally’ tortures a Rodian Jedi to death. Anakin Skywalker may have had extreme anger issues…but Cad Bane had a mean streak that made his temper totally unpredictable.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: If Dathomire rooted with Darkside, why didn’t the Empire set up a base there?
Answer: Once Palpatine had declared himself Emperor of the galaxy he had access to almost every planet that he desired. By allowing his henchmen, such as Vader, Tarkin and Thrawn, to run his ever expanding empire meant Palpatine was free to immerse himself in studying and learning more about the darkside. Planets aligned with the darkside of the force, such as Malachor, Moraband, and the Sith homeworld of Korriban where his to explore at will. Palpatine didn't care about setting up huge bases on Sith planets, such as Dathomir, rather he cared about obtaining the knowledge of the force from each planet. It was knowledge that could elevate the Siths power over the galaxy. Knowledge was what Palpatine sought, not a hold on the planet itself. Besides,..Dathomir wasn't a place where one just “set up a base”. Bathed in a crimson glow due to its sun, and covered in thick, hostile, impenatrable and treacherous terrain, Dathomir was nicknamed “The Rancor Planet”. Home to living, breathing horrors..such as the Rancors themselves.. Dathomir was also home to nightmarish creatures such as giant, winged Chirodactyls, enormous snakes, tentacled Versonks and..Bane Back spiders. These spiders were enough reason to steer clear of Dathomirs jungles and forests, with these enormous arachnids spitting toxic, poisonous saliva at its prey, and pulling them screaming into underground burrows. If these things, the Rancors, or the poisonous, stinging, thorny, plants don't messy up your day, then something else on Dathomir most definitely will.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What would have happened if Count Dooku ordered General Grievous to kill Chancellor Palpatine after he was captured?
Answer: What would have happened? Most likely a Separatist victory at the Battle of Coruscant, and possibly the fall of the Republic to the Confederacy of Independent Systems. So let's just say that Grievous had a bomb, or something just as effective, in Palpatines ‘restraining chair’..and when Dooku gave the thumbs up the good general actually disintegrated Darth Sidious! What would happen to the fate of the galaxy now? Dooku would use this opportunity to seize leadership over the galaxy..and become the Sith Lord master himself. Already having a competent enforcer in Grievous, and being privy to most of his late masters grand plan, Dooku would not be hindered by Sidious’ meddling. He could produce as many battle droids and ships as necessary to win the Clone Wars, because after all..Palpatine was just holding back the might of the Separatist Alliance. Dooku still had Order 66 up his sleeve, so he could rid himself of the Jedi this way and continue his assault on the Republic. The Jedi would be painted as war mongering instigators, and without them the Republic would crumble. The CIS would eventually swamp the Republic with overwhelming battle droid numbers. Just remember..it took the Kaminoans 10 years to pump out a single, battle ready, clonetrooper..and a single droid foundry could smash out thousands of battle droids every day. Towards the end of the Clone Wars the Republic was facing odds of 100 to 1..in the Separatists favour. Without Sidious pulling the strings Dooku could increase these odds to completely saturate the galaxy. The Jedi would be all but extinct, and the Republic without their precious peacekeepers would soon bow to Separatist rule.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did Dooku hate Darth Maul for killing Qui-Gon?
Answer: Yes he did. It was this event in itself, which would lead to Dooku's tipping point..and his ultimate fall to the darkside. Palpatine was aware that Dooku had been Qui-Gons master in the Jedi Order, and he also knew that if he used this information to his advantage then he would claim a powerful and influencial apprentice. After he left the Jedi Order, and Maul killed his apprentice, Dooku later lamented that the sadness for Qui-Gons death sealed his fate and fall to the darkside of the force. Dooku didn't get his chance to confront the monster who killed his former apprentice until events in the Son of Dathomir comics. Maul actually captures Dooku and Grievous, and actually offered to strike a partnership with the Count..but Dooku declined, vowing allegiance to Darth Sidious. Dooku hated Maul for a few reasons; killing Qui-Gon for starters, but the fact that his master had once called Maul his apprentice also added to the hatred towards the former Dathomirian Sith apprentice. Dooku felt himself superior than Maul, and viewed the fact that Maul still lived and breathed as an insult to himself..and the Sith Order. Meanwhile Dooku conducted himself without really contemplating that betrayal was an inherent trait of the Sith.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why did the Kaminoans not use Cad Bane for the clone template?
Answer: Because it wasn't the Kaminoans choice on who would be the clone template, for the order that was placed on behalf of the Jedi. The Kaminoans were just the ones creating the army on behalf of someone else. They were just like any other company, taking a specific order from a client. Even though infamous bounty hunter Cad Bane may have been an excellent choice for the clone template, Count Dooku and his master already had another superior candidate in mind. Prior to his death, during the Battle of Geonosis, Jango Fett was the number one hunter in the entire Star Wars Universe. His death left a void that Cad Bane filled with pleasure, and it was only after the Clone Wars that the son of Fett would resume the mantle of top hunter again. But because Jango was the number one in the galaxy this didn't mean that this was the idea why he was chosen for the template. When he was still a Jedi Knight Count Dooku spearheaded the Battle of Galidraan, where the Jedi battled a large group of Mandalorian warriors. During the carnage Dooku witnessed Jango Fett kill 5 Jedi Knights with his bare hands! The Sith wanted an army of soldiers who,..when the time was right, could easily subdue and kill the Jedi. Jango was shaping up to be a perfect match. Bane had proven himself a worthy contender, particularly in the ‘killing Jedi business’, but it was Jango who impressed Dooku more. Besides, the whole thing cost Dooku and the Kaminoans 20 million credits to pay out Jango for his DNA. Cad Bane would probably want more! On the bright side, the millions of clonetrooper outfits fitted both Fett and Bane perfectly, so the Kaminoans didn't really care who wore them.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What happened to General Grievous' family?
Answer: Believe it or not, but in Legends General Grievous had ten wives, and was father to thirty sons and daughters!! We know that when he was a child he was taught to fire a Czerka Outland Rifle by his grandfather, but the rifle had been passed down by his great grandmother..who had been a great warrior herself. Grievous was born during a time of great conflict between his species the Kalee, and the war mongering insects, the Yam’rii. During this time he fell in love with a fellow warrior named Ronderu lij Kummar. At the height of a vicious battle Kummar was murdered by the Yam’rii, and her body desecrated by being dumped and lost in the ocean. To fill the void of his beloved ones death the warlord takes ten wives and ends up fathering thirty children. He fought many battles, and would return home every time for his family to heal him. But most of this family ends up starving to death, and being forced to endure sheer hell after the Republic and the Jedi annex Kalee. After Grievous’ supposed death in a shuttle crash his wives and children took him for being dead. In Canon not much is said about Grievous’ actual family, save that he was born “to a family of his flesh and blood father and mother.” This couldn't be any more vague, but I'm assuming that Grievous was from a large Kalee family, with many brothers and sisters. Maybe one of them still survived until the Empire arose, or maybe Grievous had children from his previous relationship, and they've just been waiting to exact revenge on the Jedi.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Do you think Owen and Beru Lars will be confronted by an inquisitor in the Kenobi series?
Answer: Yes. At some point in time I believe curiosity got the better of Vader, and eventually he despatched one or more of his Imperial Inquisitors to Tatooine, to spy on his late step father's house near Mos Eisley. Whether it was the force whispering something to him, or whether it was out of a twisted sense of ‘checking up’ on the only family he thought he had left..at some point after the Empire seized power he had to know what the Lars couple had been doing all these years. I think it might play out something like in the 2005 Star Wars graphic novel ‘Visionaries’. Seeing as how geniuses like Jon Favreau, of The Mandalorian fame, are incorporating elements of the Expanded Universe into current Canon, I think they might be heavily inspired by events that happened in this old EU comic. In the story Maul comes to Tatooine and attempts to attack the Lars homestead, knocking Owen Lars temporarily unconscious. Then Kenobi springs from the sand, where he had been hiding in anticipation of Mauls attack, and confronts his old nemesis. I believe that in the upcoming Kenobi series it won't be Maul coming to the Lars homestead, because his canon story arc ends differently with Kenobi, but instead it will be one of the members of the Imperial Inquisitorious. Undoubtedly the Inquisitor will confront Owen and Beru, possibly about a ‘force sensitive child’, but how Kenobi deals with him/her remains the mystery.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: In Revenge of the Sith, when Obi-Wan fought General Grievous, why did Grievous tell the droids to "back away"? Couldn't Grievous have easily killed Obi-Wan if he had ordered the droids to shoot?
Answer: General Grievous gave the order to back away to his droids because he wanted Kenobi all for himself. Kenobi had kindly taken the liberty to leap straight into into the middle of Grievous and his battle droids..and challenge the general directly; no stuffing around! Grievous simply couldn't resist, and he also couldn't look weak in front of his forces. This is why General Grievous ordered his droids to stand down. Besides, Kenobi had already made his intentions clear by effortlessly doing away with Grievous’ Magnaguards, so now the general would oblige the other general, and come to a temporary gentlemans agreement. Kenobi and General Grievous had become sworn enemies near the beginning of the Clone Wars, and throughout the three year struggle for intergalactic power the two opposing generals had faced each other in combat on several occasions. Each time they met it ended up in a duel, with either Grievous escaping at the end, or outside military intervention disrupting the pair. Grievous had let Kenobi slip through his hands many times before, but as the war progressed towards an end the cyborg Separatist leader wanted to finally add Kenobis lightsaber to his own collection. Grievous knew that by himself Kenobi wouldn't stand a chance if he ordered his droids to kill the Jedi, so by ordering his men to back away signalled for the general once again.. “..I will deal with this Jedi slime myself.”

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did many people miss something in Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace?
Answer: Yeah,..like how R2-D2 actually fits inside the Naboo N-1 Starfighter. When I first watched the movie this didn't even register in my mind, but over the years as I've watched The Phantom Menace again and again I couldn't help but wonder how R2 fitted inside the N-1. When he is seen sitting behind Anakin you can clearly see that there's no room for his legs inside the ship. It's just his head poking out, with no possible way of his body fitting inside the impossibly narrow space. But then I did a bit of research, and discovered a startling piece of information that I have missed for all these years. To fit inside an N-1 Starfighter an astromech has its head all but removed from its body!! Yeah, that's right! When an astromech, such as R2 is lifted into the N-1 its body remains in the lower part of of ship..while it's head is removed upwards, and extended into the flying position. So everytime a droid goes aboard one of these things it has its head elongated and telescoped..and then screwed back on again! Above; taken from ‘Episode 1: Incredible Cross-sections.’ 1999. Actually, astromechs have a real world problem of fitting into several of the starships that we see them in. In Revenge of the Sith we see R2 again, but this time he's on board the Aethersprite, which the Jedi had upgraded from their previous ships, the Delta-7's. When we see actual production shots of the movie it is painfully obvious that astromechs are too big to actually fit inside the ships they were supposed to navigate. I completely missed this everytime I watched the movies.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How did Imperials get around the Death Star? By walking?
Answer: Remember General Grievous’ massive Subjugator-Class heavy cruiser, The Malevolence?It was one of the largest vessels in the Separatist Navy during the Clone Wars, and measured at nearly 5 kilometres long;..which was over 5 Venator-Class Star Destroyers in length! To ferry droids around the colossal ship the heavy cruiser had an internal shuttle train system. This was essential to deploying all of the 900 droids, in the ships crew complement. The Death Star operated similar systems throughout the cavernous battle station, which was far more enormous than The Malevolence. To walk the 120 kilometre diameter of the Death Star would take well more than a whole day, while non stop walking! Officers, Stormtroopers and the millions of men and women who operated the Death Star used a myriad of elevators to go up and down inside the station, but when it came to traversing across the enormous Imperial structure shuttle systems were utilised.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Are Jedi allowed to use guns?
Answer: There's nothing in the rules that says a Jedi can't use a blaster, rifle or any other type of firearms. When the Clone Wars erupted upon the galaxy the Jedi Knights were assigned as military generals by the Republic, and as such it would be pretty silly if an active wartime general couldn't fire a gun! The Jedi were a monastic order of force wielders, and this meant their primary weapon was the force..second to their lightsabers. The Force, and their lightsabers, were a Jedi’s sole defensive measures usually, but ‘guns’ were just another tool in a Jedis environment, to utilise if no other means was left available to solve a problem. When the Galactic Empire claimed power over the galaxy the Jedi survivors of Order 66 were spread far and thin. To blend in, and avoid suspicion of being caught, many Jedi became accustomed with, and carried blasters. The Jedi Kanan Jarrus was one such Jedi, and his padawan, Ezra Bridger, created a lightsaber/blaster hybrid. In the EU, Jedi wannabe, Kyle Katarn, used both blasters and his lightsaber during combat, and in addition to his blaster Katarn wielded a variety of weapons including thermal detonators and rocket launchers. During his Jedi training Luke Skywalker slung a blaster, and was prepared to use it. He had it with him on Bespin when he fought Vader, and when he went to Dagobah he even pointed it at Jedi Grand Master Yoda! Obi-Wan Kenobi, though he deplored the use of blasters, had no other option but to use General Grievous’ own sidearm to defeat the good general on Utapau. Once during the Old Republic it was shunned upon for a Jedi to use a blaster, but as the times changed for the worse it became more practical for a Jedi to resort to carrying a holstered firearm.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Do swords exist in Star Wars?
Answer: Of course they do. What do you think that the Jedi based their lightsabers on? They do refer to it as a “laser sword” in the Star Wars Universe. Many thousands of primitive or rudimentary planets still employed the use of swords, and many species still took pride in crafting these ancient yet effective weapons. Twi'leks, Kaleesh, Kyuzo, Dathomirians, Nightsisters, Mandalorians and other cultures still use swords in combat occasionally, while keeping ceremonial swords and daggers as reminders of their people's past. Above; a pre-cyborg General Grievous The Kaleesh are a very warlike and Spartan culture, who still use swords, spears and daggers as weapons of war. Before he brandished quadruple lightsabers, and became a psychopathic cyborg, General Grievous used swords to vanquish his enemies, such as the Huk species, who had invaded and enslaved Kallee. As a Warlord, back on Kallee, he used to behead his opponents with his blood stained sword. Below; Qymaen Jai Shelal beheads his enemy. The Toydarian people have curved bladed swords, that are still carried as weapons, and their ruler, King Katuunko, had a beautiful custom one of his own. Below; King Katuunko, the Toydarian ruler, brandishes a Ceremonial sword. The Kage warriors use ancient electro swords to engage their enemy the Belugans, and even the Sith are partial to brandishing a sword from time to time. Above; Naga Sadow and Ludo Kressh duel with dark imbued Sith Swords. Ludo Kressh preferred to use a sword, rather than a lightsaber, and his Sith imbued sword was an extremely deadly, double edged weapon. Another Sith Lord, Naga Sadow, used a Sith sword, which he actually fought Ludo Kressh with, and the Dathomirian Nightsister leader, Mother Talzin, could conjure a dark imbued sword out of thin air. Below; Mother Talzin conjures a Nightsister sword.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What weapons are illegal in Star Wars?
Answer: When Darth Vader explicitly instructed Boba Fett “No disintegrations”..he was talking about a specific type of weapon. Besides all the big weapons of mass destruction that could level half a city, there was one particular weapon that even the Empire itself banned from being sold; And if the Galactic Empire thought it was so bad to warrant a ban on this particular type of rifle,…then thats saying something! I introduce to you the T-7 Ion Disruptor. Coming in at a cost of 8,000 credits, and manufactured to cut through nearly anything, the T-7 packed one hell of a punch. Its primary function was to cripple starships and take out multiple opponents simultaneously, but the T-7 had a darker secret which led the Imperial Senate to propose a bill making the Ion Disruptor Rifle completely illegal to possess or use. Firing a charged burst of ionised plasma the weapon was capable of bringing down a large Starship,..but this isn't the reason why it was banned from use. Its use against Starships proved extremely useful, but when fired at living beings it was a whole other story.. The horrible way in which individuals died was highly unethical to keep this weapon service active, but it was at the Battle of Lassat that the weapon gained its infamy. The T-7 was employed by the Empire against the Lassat species, pushing it to the brink of total extinction. Later it was concluded by the Empire that the T-7 Ion Disruptor was far too dangerous to be utilised again..and had the weapon made illegal through the Imperial Senate. Source; Wookiepedia: T-7 Ion Disruptor.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who were the only people allowed to see Darth Vader without his suit?
Answer: There was one guy who was definitely allowed to see Darth Vader without his suit; Vanee..who was Darth Vaders personal assistant and keeper of Fortress Vader on Mustafar. Vanee was originally an inspector for Imperial Command, and was sent to Mustafar by Moff Seward. Several of the stationed Stormtroopers assigned to Mustafar had gone clinically mad, and so Vanee was sent to get some answers. In the beginning Vanee protested to Vader that the lava fumes throughout the castle were toxic, but Vader ignored him. Eventually Vanee became delusional and mad himself, saying that he heard voices telling him to serve Vader. The Sith Lord offered Vanee the position of being his personal attendant, and so Vanee accepted. At this point his cheese had sliden well and truly off his cracker, but nonetheless Vanee served Vaders bidding and became his loyal servant. Vader actually needed him in the beginning to assist with him his tasks around the castle..which included helping Vader without his suit. Vanee was Vaders personal attendant, but why were there a pair of the Emperors Royal Guards in attendance also at Fortress Vader? You'd assume they were there to guard Vader while he was in his bacta tank, or act as personal bodyguards..but I think they were actually there to spy on Vader in his new house. After all..they were the Emperors Royal Guards… Reference; Wookiepedia: Vanee, Canon, and ‘Star Wars Adventures: Shadow of Vaders Castle #1

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did Darth Sidious expect Maul to die?
Answer: He certainly did not. By the time Obi-Wan Kenobi defeated Darth Maul on Naboo, Darth Sidious had already done away with his master, Darth Plagueis. At this point in time Palpatine had seized the mantle of Sith Lord Master for himself, and promoted Maul to full Sith Lord apprentice. He needed Maul to act as his assassin, scout, representative and more, so for his apprentice to be defeated at such a crucial stage in the Sith Grand Plan was a genuine loss for Palpatine. Darth Sidious trained Maul in secret as a Sith assassin, then presented him to his master as an idea to help further their plans. Unbeknownst to Plagueis, his apprentice was attempting to deceive him. Palpatine had kidnapped Maul after deciding that he had more force potential than his mother, Talzin. Sidious originally intended to make Mauls mother his secret apprentice, until he sensed that her son was a far superior candidate. Even at this stage during his apprenticeship under his master Darth Sidious was already making designs on taking the throne, but rather than do all the hard work he waited until the plan was at the right stage before doing away with Plagueis. Maul was his Sith apprentice waiting in the wings, and was privy to much of Palpatines grand plan. But Darth Sidious did take into account that his Dathomirian apprentice could be defeated, and had already begun fostering ill will towards the Jedi in the mind of another prospective apprentice;..Count Dooku. Sidious used the death of Qui-Gon Jinn, at the hands of his Sith apprentice, to tip the Count over to the darkside. But had Dooku known that he was intended to be just a Sith ‘stand in’ for as long as was convenient for Palpatine, he may have reconsidered his offer. Sidious didn't intend for Maul to be defeated on Naboo, but he also didn't hedge his bets by solely relying on Maul. The plan must continue regardless.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Does the character of Darth Vader represent a tragedy?
Answer: The Tragedy of Darth Vader the Chosen One is one of the saddest and most tragic stories in all of modern science fiction. His very conception was one of retribution and sadness, for to bring balance to the force,..as it was prophesied for centuries, Anakin Skywalker had to lose everything he held dear in his life, in the most deceitful and also the most heartbreaking of ways imaginable. Then he had to die to fulfil a Jedi prophecy; but not before becoming both galactic saviour…and then the face of its doom. His entire existence was a tragedy at every stage he turned in his sad life. Born into slavery, his mother Shmi was abused and sold off by Hutt gangsters to a seedy Toydarian Junk dealer. Then in a fate of circumstances he was promised and granted freedom on the provision that he left his childhood home,..and more importantly his mother, which he shared a very strong bond with. Then he was whisked away to be inducted into a monastic order of magical monks, who in no way emotionally supported him with his inner turmoils. Forced to abandon his mother, and to forget the very meaning of love, he is taught to be a child soldier for a group of crusading zealots, blindly taught to never show any signs of emotion..and to supress his negatively impacting emotional state. The boy was brainwashed from the beginning by the fanatical Jedi Order, and to make it even worse he was groomed in secret for years by a sadistic megalomaniac, to be his lapdog and unquestioning servant. The Jedi, or any of their compassionate affiliates, make no offer to free Anakin's mother from slavery, then the boy receives prophetic nightmares about both his mother and wife dying..and they come true! His mother dies in his arms, after being tortured to the brink of death, his fellow Jedi die in a pointless and unnecessary war, and then his wife dies in childbirth. He is hideously burned and dismembered by his former master, then forced to wear a painful and restricting survival suit. His own children are kidnapped, hidden and estranged from him, and by the time he wants to make repentance for a life of misfortune and misdeeds, and know his adult children..it's too late to repair the time lost. If this story isn't tragic enough then you must be a glutton for punishment. At every point in his life Anakin Skywalker was subject to pain, loss, sadness and despair. It went from one tragedy to the next, with promises of hope that were only dashed or manipulated by both the bad guys..and the good ones. His mother, his wife, his children and everyone else he held dear were systematically ripped out of his life, transforming him into a sad, remorseless shadow of his former self. He was then resigned to serving evil up until the day that he died. According to the light side of the force he was redeemed for this horrible actions, but the tragedy that was his life must have still echoed forever, long after living had passed for him.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: In Star Wars: ESB, why did Luke and Han’s sensor sweep for life signs not pick up the Wampa who was apparently right next to Luke?
Answer: Wampas are highly stealthy creatures, but not only due to their shaggy, white fur color, and incredible speed, but due to something else entirely. There was a very good reason why Han and Luke couldn't detect the Wampas life signature on their equipment, as well as the Rebel Alliance when they first established Echo Base on Hoth. Above; an enormous Wampa located shortly after the construction of the new Rebel base. Wampas were officially classified as reptomammals, and as such shared the best of both creatures worlds. They had adaptive characteristics associated with mammals, but more importantly the amazing survival and defence mechanisms of reptiles. Below; a Wampa making a stealthy surprise attack. Wampas were adapted so that they could conserve heat due to a defensive layer of skin and blubber. They also had a self regulating metabolism, and were capable of lowering their body heat to such a degree that it barely registered on scanning equipment. This was enhanced by the Wampas extremely long hair, and their layer of durable outer skin. Above; Wampas behaving in their natural habitat. R2-D2 even had trouble detecting the Wampas life or heat signatures! When the Rebels first established Echo Base on the icy planet it became apparent immediately that the Wampas were going to be a continual problem for the base. Above; A gigantic Wampa terrorises Echo Base. Wampas made frequent and coordinated attacks on the Rebel personnel at Echo Base, dragging them off screaming into the cold night, and still remained undetectable to droids and the most sophisticated scanning devices alike. Above; Han Solo operating the CryonCorp manufactured EnhanceScan multi purpose scanner. Eventually the Rebellion had to purge the surrounding area of the Wampas, yet still they stealthily crept up, hidden by their defence characteristics, and continued to terrorise the isolated base. Below; Wampas continue their sustained attacks on Echo Base despite the Rebels taking further precautions. After the Battle of Hoth the Rebel Alliance fled this accursed planet, and the Empires brief occupation began their horrific documentation of confronting the deadly creature that had plagued Echo Base. Both the Rebellion and the Empire had greatly misjudged these abominable apex predators. Below; images of Wampas during the evacuation of Echo Base. (note the Wampas coordinated attacks.) Another species that shares this uncanny ability to remain undetected from lifeform scanners are the Talz, native to the icy planet of Alzoc III. The Talz were able to perform eerily similar attack tactics on the Clones, Battle droids and Pantorans during the Clone Wars. Below; the Talz attacking a Battle droid despite its inbuilt sensor equipment, attacking and killing the Pantoran Assembly Chief, Chi Cho.., and a Talz befriending Obi-Wan Kenobi. A group of Talz settled on Hoth, due to it having a similar climate to their homeworld, and the Wampas showed no hostile intentions towards the Talz. The Wampas believed that themselves and the Talz were one in the same. Maybe it had something to do with this amazing physiological similarity. Reference; Wookiepedia: Wampa (Legends)

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Do the stun batons in the new Star Wars movies (and JFO) block lightsabers because of some special material in them, or is it just the electricity?
Answer: Upon further inspection it is only the powerful electrical current that enables the Z-76 Riot Control Baton to block a lightsaber. Seen in debut film of the sequel trilogy, The Force Awakens, and manufactured by the First Order to be utilised in their non lethal weapons program, the Z-76s prime function was to “batter their opponents into submission.” The two long contact conductor vanes, which were connected by the central shaft, were made of alloys that a lightsaber blade could easily cut in two given enough exposure. Its handle had an inbuilt adhesion grip that magnomatomically paired with the Riot troopers gloves. Once activated the Z-76 delivered a powerful charge capable of withstanding the plasma blade of a lightsaber. The conductor vane was useless against a lightsaber by itself. The vanes only acted as a wide surface area for the electrical charge to spread along. The Purge Troopers from Jedi: Fallen Order are equipped with similar weapons to allow them to take on the Jedi. These troopers used a variety of stun weaponry including electobatons, electrostaffs and electrohammers, however unlike the First Orders batons the Purge Troopers weapons were highly lethal; just like Grievous’ Magnaguards weapons, which could also block lightsabers, and stop the heart with enough charge. The Electrohammer could be charged up and slammed into the ground, creating a devastating shock wave that sent opponents flying, or if it was angled could create a ripple capable of knocking any Jedi off their feet.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did the Grand Inquisitor know that Darth Vader was Anakin Skywalker?
Answer: I don't believe the Grand Inquisitor did know Vader was Skywalker. Not at least while he was alive anyway. When Vader and the 501st Legion stormed the Jedi Temple during Order 66, he slaughtered all the Jedi and the Temple Guards. But one of these guards was a traitor to the Jedi Order, and was rumoured to have murdered his fellow temple guards in the massacre. Later he defected to the darkside and became the Grand Inquisitor. But when the Sith Lord met the Grand Inquisitor he nearly killed him. Vader wasn't unaware of the Imperial Inquisitorious until the Emperor revealed his new dark acolytes to him. Prior to the actual introduction the two met one another, with Vader attempting to kill the Utapaun darksider. Even though the Grand Inquisitor was totally aware of the attack on the temple by the Sith and the Clones, he may not have been aware that it was a pre suit Darth Vader that led the attack. Otherwise he'd definitely have known. But after the Grand Inquisitor died during his duel with Rebel, and Jedi Knight Kanan Jarrus, his dark spirit was captured by Vader. Then the Sith Lord bound his spirit to an old Jedi Temple to act as a guard. The Inquisitor sacrificed himself during the final duel with Jarrus, possibly thinking it might redeem his corrupted spirit,..but he was wrong. It's possible that as a twisted darkside spirit he finally became aware of Darth Vader's secret identity, but I doubt that he worked it out while he was still in the land of the living.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How can a bunch of drunk pirates capture and keep a Sith lord and 2 powerful Jedi hostage (Star Wars: The Clone Wars S1E12)?
Answer: Because Hondo Ohnaka was a very clever pirate. The Ohnaka gang operated in the Outer Rim, with a pirate stronghold on Florrum. Now a gang of pirates is about as good as a bunch of clones, ..and we all know what happened to the Jedi during Order 66 at the hands of the Clone troopers, so a very large group of heavily armed and well organised pirates are going to easily subdue Count Dooku, Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi. Remember when Maul and his brother Savage fought the same pirates after the “crimelords” divided Ohnakas gang, and both came off worse for wear!? Well these two extremely dangerous Sith Lords get their limbs blown off by these pirates, so even if the troubled trio broke free of the stuncuffs they'd have some very stiff opposition threatening their escape. They didn't even have lightsabers to defend themselves, and were outgunned in a confrontation. These pirates were so crafty that they managed to pickpocket Count Dooku's lightsabers without him even knowing! Not even invisible Nightsisters with poison darts could do this!

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Did the Jedi have a division of assassins that operated outside the order, but were still bound by the same principles?
Answer: Well, there were these guys,..and they were actually called The Jedi Assassins in the Expanded Universe fandom. They even had their own Jedi symbol. These mysterious Jedi were carefully selected padawans that were trained in both the lightside..and the darkside of the force, but not known if they were bound by the same principles as the Jedi. Because the Jedi Councils views clashed with using the darkside to fulfil the peaceful purpose set forth by the Jedi, these padawan learners were trained in absolute secrecy. Their existence was only known to a select handful of Jedi. Above; Darth Verraeter. During the time in which the Jedi Assassins operated they were under the threat of the Sith Lord, Darth Verraeter, and covertly trying to sabotage his efforts. The Sith of the era launched terrible attacks on the Republic and the Jedi, and one such incident of the period was the great Battle of Calox III. This battle saw the fall of the Republic, and the Jedi Temple in which the Jedi Assassins were trained. Many were killed by Darth Verraeter himself.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Would Papitine dueling Yoda inside the packed senate building attract unwanted attention and reveal that he is a Sith Lord when he uses his force powers and lightsaber?
Answer: This is very good question. You'd think that with all the surveillance cameras, droids, guards..and even sanitation operators working in the Senate building, that at least one of them wouldn't have seen or even recorded the epic duel between Palpatine and Yoda. I mean, in earthly terms..it was kinda like the leader of NATO having a sword fight with the Pope or something. Someone must have seen..or heard something..right??!! The final clash between Grand Master Yoda and Sheev Palpatine was a pretty noisy affair! It began as a lightsaber duel that turned into a full blown clash of the titans. I know that Palpatine turned off all the surveillance equipment in the Senate Chambers, after the building was cleared of all personnel in an attempt to cover up his tracks, but the building was very big, around two kilometres in diameter, and their clash must have arroused some suspicion within the enormous facility. When Sidious and Yoda arose into the massive auditorium, and started spewing force lightning and flipping Senate Pods around the place, someone must have heard something..even in the slightest. What about a service droid? Or what about something else with independent functioning optical processors capturing a glimpse of the lengthy duel? The damage that was created as a result of the clash created rumours that fuelled Palpatines accusations against the Jedi. When returning senators heard what had happened during their absence it only fuelled rumours; Rumours that Yoda lead a strike force against the Chancellor, where Palpatines forces defeated the Jedi, and the Jedi Grand Master was possibly killed in the confrontation. Was this how Palpatine got hideously deformed? Look..at the end of the day Palpatine was the senate, and obviously had the place locked down tight. At this moment in time the shift of galactic power had already occurred. If anyone did see anything, and say something, then I'm betting the Emperor would just have them swiftly killed.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why did Ewoks: The Battle for Endor come with a parental warning?
Answer: I'd say it definitely had something to do with the first five minutes of the movie. In the prequel to this Star Wars movie, Caravan of Courage: An Ewok Adventure, the Towani family find themselves marooned on the strange forest moon of Endor. Immediately the parents of Mace and Cindel Towani are kidnapped by the planets towering apex predator.. the gigantic Gorax, and taken captive to his mountain fortress. Needless to say, Cindel, Mace, Wicket the Ewok (and many of his tribe from Return of the Jedi), help and accompany the Towani children to rescue their parents, and save the day. Happy endings all round! Yub nub!! Then in the first 5 minutes of The Battle for Endor Mace, and the children's two parents are viciously gunned down by Sannyassan pirates, who crash landed on the same moon. For a Star Wars movie it was pretty confronting for young audiences, considering the first movie was so kid friendly. This is what probably prompted the movie to have a parental warning. After young Cindel watches her entire family murdered by alien marauders herself and Wicket flee terrified into the deep, dark woods;…and find Wilford Brimley… Just another reason to give this movie a parental warning. Did anyone see this guy in John Carpenters The Thing?! Dude scared the ever loving crap outta me for years!

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How did the Jedi Council react to Pong Krell’s treason?
Answer: The Jedi Council would view the treason of Pong Krell as something they'd rather sweep under the rug, for if word got out about a Jedi General going rogue, and falling to the darkside of the force..then it would create great unease, uncertainty and doubt; not only amongst the Jedi Order, but throughout the vast ranks of the Grand Army of the Republic. Pong Krell said that he had sensed a power shift encroaching on the Republic, during a premonition that he had. He sensed a dark power rising and jumped ship for Dooku's camp. Krells carnage on Umbarra changed many an opinion, and rightly so. Once legendary amongst the Jedi Order, Count Dooku fell to the darkside and became one of the worst traitors in the galaxy. If Krell was following suit it could set a very dangerous precedent. If Dooku and Krell could fall with such ease then what chance did every other Jedi have? Could this spark a wave of doubt over the Jedi and their teachings? Would more Jedi leave the Order because of this treacherous two? Towards the end of the Clone Wars Mace Windu lamented on Pong Krells treason, only this time it was in regards to a third powerful Jedi defecting over to the enemy camp. Quinlan Vos had joined forces with Dooku, and once again shattered the very fabric that held the Jedi together. The Jedi Council hated this kind of thing, because it was bad for the Republic. Once the galaxy became aware of more than one Jedi becoming a force for evil it would question everything that they stood for. Dooku and Krell had completely undermined the Jedi and the Republic in the eyes of the entire galaxy.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: How did the Galactic Empire expect to police so many people?
Answer: When Darth Sidious pulled off Order 66, he secured his position as Emperor of the newly created Galactic Empire. With this came the tremendous responsibility of keeping thousands of planets in line. The Emperor knew he didn't have anywhere near the numbers to police every planet and territory, but he already had a plan in motion. One of his most trusted individuals was Wilhuff Tarkin. Palpatine and him were friends during the Clone Wars, and the Sith Lord knew that Tarkin would become instrumental in maintaining his new empire. That's when during the year 18 BBY Tarkin made a proposal to his Emperor, that would solve the problem of how to police such a vast and expansive kingdom. It was called the ‘Tarkin Doctrine’, and with it came a philosophy that would effectively keep the grasp that Palpatine had on the galaxy. This Imperial philosophy would become the Empires leash and muzzle,..which would further tighten around the citizens of the galaxy. Tarkins main principle of his design was in the way he planned to police the multitude of star systems under the Empire. Rather than ruling through fear, he planned on ruling with the threat of fear and force itself. After the completion of the Death Star he had the perfect weapon to uphold his philosophy. He would basically wave a bigass gun around the galaxy, and threaten everyone into submission. Those that didn't comply would face the wrath of the Death Star and the entire might of the Galactic Empire, and after that all nearby systems would fall in line out of the threat of their world being blown to oblivion. This is how the Empire expected to police so many people.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is your favorite scene from all of the Star Wars universe?
Answer: Mine is when Palpatine executed Order 66, during the events of Revenge of the Sith. As a child I grew up with the original trilogy, that left so many questions unanswered. Then in the late 90’s Lucas started introducing the sequel trilogy, and all my questions started getting answers in a big way. But the question of exactly how Darth Sidious would rid himself of the Jedi from the galaxy was still teetering on my mind. Then it all happened before me, as I sat in the movie theatre with my eyes completely glued to the screen. When Palpatine uttered the phrase.. ..and then Commander Cody began the great Jedi purge I couldn't believe what I was witnessing. This was the moment that I had been waiting for many years to witness..and I wasn't disappointed. I was not prepared for Anakins march on the Jedi Temple, and when he began the extermination it all started clicking in my head. This was how the old bastard did it! It began with Obi-Wan Kenobi, and after his plunge into an Utapau sink hole it cycled through other Jedi throughout the galaxy being executed. Ki Adi Mundi, Stass Allie, and Ayla Secura all fall in the most treacherous of ways, all leading up to Yoda. I knew the Jedi Master wasn't going to die that day on Kashyyyk, but when he simultaneously decapitated the clone troopers trying to execute him it blew my mind. That whole scene has always stuck in my mind, and remains a moment of pure mixed emotions every time I see it! The sadness, the excitement and the beautiful music all seamlessly create this one epic scene, where fans and non fans alike will never forget what they witnessed.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Anakin is raised by Jango Fett. How does this change him?
Answer: It just means that Anakin Skywalker would have been a Bounty Hunter, instead of a Jedi Knight, before he became Palpatines apprentice. It was already long prophesied that Anakin, The Chosen One, was the individual who would bring balance to the force;…but the Jedi prophecy never said that he had to be a Jedi. If Jango took Anakin from Tatooine and made him his son, like he did with Boba, then Anakin would be loyal to the Mandalorian Creed. Anakin would be a foundling, and as such Jango would be like his father. Anakin would learn quickly and become even more skillful than Boba ever was, but Anakin had a strong bond with his mother, and after losing her, the loss of Jango at the hands of Mace Windu would tip him over the edge. There's a slight chance Skywalker may even kill Windu that day in the arena, but regardless..the young Skywalker will greatly resent this loss. He will sorely want revenge; the same way he exacted revenge on the Tuskens who kidnapped and tortured his mother in episode II. But this revenge will come. If Anakin remained a bounty hunter his services would have eventually come under the attention of Palpatine. The Sith Lord was known for hiring the top bounty hunter in the galaxy from time to time, and Anakin would definitely achieve the number one title thanks to his unprecedented skill in the force. This is when the Sith Lord would offer Anakin the chance at revenge,..by offering Skywalker to become his secret apprentice. Anakin was always preordained by the force to restore balance to it, so it was only a matter of time before he fell under Palpatines spell. The rest is history.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Would clones be more loyal to the Galactic Empire than regular soldiers?
Answer: Of course they would. Whether it was the Republic, or the Galactic Empire, the clones of Kamino would be completely loyal to the Empire..given the right level of genetic manipulation altered within the clone soldiers. The clones of the Grand Army of the Republic were completely loyal to the Republic, and if it hadn't been for the bio chips, with Order 66 contained within them, they would have remained loyal to the end. The Kaminoans who engineered the clones used all kinds of inhibitors, enhancers, and mind conditioning to make the clones as subservient or aggressive as possible. They could bio engineer entire batches of clones to meet the tailored and specific needs of any client. That is why the Sith used their services until they were duped, and all but eliminated except for a handful of Kaminoan scientists. Until the Galactic Empire completely destroyed Tipoca City, and the rest of the Cloning facilities on Kamino, the cloners did business as usual. They were known, in the right circles, to create a very fine breed of clone. If the Galactic Empire had not destroyed the Kaminoans, to cover the secrets of the Emperor, then a clone army would have been more loyal than conscripted or recruited soldiers. The level of loyalty engineered into the GAR Clones was unparalleled, with soldiers following orders and dieing without question. Darth Sidious approved the clone army because of two reasons; firstly he knew how incredibly skillful the template Jango Fett was, and his inbuilt hatred for the Jedi;..and secondly, because the Kaminoans tasked with creating the army could tailor the clones to his specific needs. Order 66 being that one specific need. Then they were disposed of just like most other pawns in Palpatines plans.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is the most practical spacecraft in Star Wars?
Answer: I'm surprised nobody mentioned this old, but highly practical spacecraft before. The Rebel Transports, that we seen frantically ferrying evacuated soldiers from Echo base on Hoth, are the most practical ships in the Rebel Alliance..if not the entire galaxy. The GR-75 Medium Transports were the backbone of the Rebel fleets equipment and personnel logistics, and even though they're ugly, cumbersome, unimaginative vessels, the Rebel Medium Transports were invaluable to those that possessed them. They could transport huge amounts of vital equipment, supplies, and Rebel operating personnel, to anywhere in the galaxy. Under civilian use they could be used for moving just about anything. Above; the underside of the GR-75 Medium Transport, detailing the storage areas. These things were basically an enormous storage unit, providing bulk storage space underneath, and cheap passenger room elsewhere in giant lifepods. It was no frills design, no fancy paint job, no souped up modifications, and looked like a giant fishing lure. It was purely designed to fulfill the very general purpose of moving goods and personnel from one point in the galaxy to the next. Very mundane..but highly practical in regards to fulfilling a very, very important intergalactic need.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What is the most realistic technology in Star Wars?
Answer: Do you remember the scene when Aunt Beru is clearly cooking fennel, in a very earthly looking food processor, at the start of A New Hope? That tin pot thing looks like the most realistic piece of kitchen equipment in any science fiction movie. In fact the whole kitchen, at the Lars homestead looks suspect; with items staight out of some Martha Stewart cooking demo. But the thing is, in Star Wars we have planet killing superweapons the size of small moons, lightsabers, hyperspace travel, and a droid manufactured for every conceivable occupation,…yet they still had to cook food like my mom in the 1980’s?! Heck,..my mom still cooks like this now! Take sci-fi works such as The Fifth Element and the Star Trek franchise. Their kitchen appliances were light years ahead of any Star Wars culinary equipment. In the Star Trek franchise replicators have been common place since time immemorial for most people, and at the simple usher of a voice command to the ships computer you can have a Tandoori chicken, or dry vodka martini in mere seconds. No mixing, no shaking, and it comes complete with a replicated cup or glass. Now that's some futuristic shit right there! In The Fifth Element Leeloo uses a similar device where once the food replicators recieve a small dehydrated pill of the chosen meal..the device instantly creates a full size chicken dinner for 5 in a whoosh of electronics! …And this movie is set on Earth in the year 2259! What the hell Star Wars!! In a galaxy set far, far away from here they still have to cook relatively similar to us on good old planet Earth; and that ‘Blue Bantha Milk’ dispenser in the corner is soo Coruscant 7-11! If this surprisingly rudimentary Star Wars technology isn't the most realistic, compared to Earthly kitchen appliances,..then I don't know what is!!

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What if a Zillo beast showed up on Tatooine just outside Jabba's palace?
Answer: Then we are likely to see Jabba move faster than anyone has seen a Hutt move ever before. Unless he had around a dozen RX 200 Falchion Class assault tanks at his disposal, Jabba would be making a hasty retreat to his Sail Barge or personal Starship,..and getting the heck out of Dodge! A Zillo Beast is one of the most terrifying creatures to be spewed forth from the Star Wars Universe, and was something that Jabba and all of his many minions couldn't repel. If the Zillo Beast gave Darth Sidious a hard time, then Jabba wouldn't stand a chance. Hailing from Malastare, the ancient Zillo beast was a monolith of a monster. Standing at a height of around 100 metres, and weighing in excess of 60,000 metric tons, the Godzilla of the SWU could destroy Jabba's Palace with a bout of bad flatulence. When one of its kind escaped its confines on Coruscant the creature caused utter pandemonium, and created billions of credits worth of damages in its destructive wake. Jabbas Palace would become one bigass parking lot in the desert, once this thing rocked up at the front door. No, sadly on this occasion Jabba would be flying his fat ass back to Nal Hutta, and assessing the damage done by the Zillo beast once it moved on. The only thing killing it, short of the chemical weapon that killed it in The Clone Wars, would be a Mandalorian and a Bantha strapped with 200 kgs of explosive charges jumping down its throat and messying up its day.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who is the most beautiful female character in Star Wars?
Answer: For myself it's a tie between two characters from the Expanded Universe. I'm lovestruck between two gorgeous blondes,..each from two very different backgrounds in the SWU. My first candidate for most beautiful female character in Star Wars is Imperial Officer Juno Eclipse. She took my breathe away when I first seen her in the PS3 video games ‘The Force Unleashed’ 1 & 2. She was personally chosen by Darth Vader to be his secret apprentices pilot, and ferry him around on his missions. Starkiller, Vader's darkside apprentice, eventually falls in love with the blonde bombshell,..and I can't blame the guy. Eclipse was quite possibly the most beautiful woman to ever serve the Empire. My second candidate is another blonde, but she's more than meets the eye. Guri was a human replica droid, worth 9 million credits, and was owned by the Black Sun crimelord, Falleen Prince Xixor. Not only was she stunning, and one of the most beautiful characters in the Star Wars Universe, but she was virtually a Terminator. Made from the hardest and most durable materials, and programmed in weapons, tactics and unarmed combat Guri may have looked like a gorgeous cabaret singer, but was capable of unleashing pure chaos. Guri could destroy droids with a single punch, or rip a mans throat out in a heartbeat. She could also speak more languages than C-3P0, and operate any vehicle or weapon at her disposal. She was designed by a pair of ex Imperial scientists, the Thrumble brothers, and actually had living skin, grown in a laboratory just for her. The only thing that gave her up as a droid was her body temperature, being at least 10 degrees cooler than an actual human. What can I say? I'm a sucker for blondes..

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why did Vader go ahead of the stormtroopers when attempting to board the Tantive IV in Rogue One?
Answer: Because it was his own mission to find the relayed Death Star plans, stolen and transmitted from Scarif Base. Once Vader had docked and come aboard The Profundity with his boarding party, he found the Rebels with the pilfered plans, and..y’know.. But as the last Rebel trooper passed the plans through the door, which Vader held closed with the force, his hopes of retrieving the detailed plans revealing the stations crucial flaw dashed away. As the Tantive IV “LAAUUUUNCHED!“ Vader proceeded past his boarding party, which had caught up with their commander, the Sith Lord did so hoping that he could still retrieve the stolen plans in a last ditch attempt. Once the Tantive IV escaped it was only a matter of time before Vader and his men caught up with the Rebel scum. The Rebel Blockade Runner, containing the plans, left a distinct trail of emissions that allowed the Imperial Star Destroyer to track and relocate the vessel. Vader allowed his men to thin the Rebel ranks down, he then did the same thing by going ahead of his men. Vader then located Captain Antilles, but due to his anger in having the plans elude him,..then Antilles deliberately trying to stall him..Vader killed the good captain. His only lead now lay in a jettisoned escape pod that launched just after his ‘arrival’ on the Rebel ship, and the captured Alderaanian Princess who had become a bothersome annoyance for the Empire. Just a thought, but as Vader stood watching the Tantive IV escape him temporarily, why didn't he just reach out with the force and pull the vessel back?

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What are some amazing facts about the Death Star in Star Wars?
Answer: The DS-1 Orbital Battle Station was a legendary triumph of engineering, that ultimately created a moon sized, planet annihilating superweapon; devised by giant termites and powered by gargantuan lightsaber crystals. This marvel of multispecies ingenuity took years to build, and was destroyed in seconds by a lone X-Wing pilot. Here's some amazing facts about the Death Star.. 1 - Before it was top secretly designated ‘Project Stardust’ by the Empire, the project was initially named ‘Project Celestial Power’. 2 - Its main purpose was to enforce the ‘Tarkin Doctrine’, where Grand Moff Wilhuff Tarkin created an Imperial philosophy based on ruling through the threat of fear, rather than ruling with fear itself. 3 - The idea for the Death Star was first concieved thousands of years before Palpatine completed its construction. Some of the earliest designs for the first Death Star date back many millennia, and were dreamed up by ancient Sith Lords. 4 - It was designed by Geonosians and actually began its initial construction phase in orbit around Geonosis. Because the flying Geonosians designed it, they didn't have a flightless species in mind when building it, therefore it didn't have any safety railings. 5 - Because the Geonosians were the creators and designers of the Death Star, the Empire went to the extraordinary length of exterminating the entire Geonosian species. This was done in an attempt to eliminate all witnesses privy to the Emperor's big secret. 6 - The Death Star only measured 100 miles in diameter, had an impressive surface area of over 45,000 square kilometres and 357 internal levels. It had a habitable crust several kilometres deep, but everything else in the entire interior space was uninhabited. 7 - Abandoned construction equipment including enormous cranes and autonomous worker droids were found in its cavernous storage spaces. 8 - Its outer hull was constucted out of hardy Quadanium steel plates, and the Death Star had its own wholly man made atmosphere, contained to the battle station by powerful magnetic fields. 9 - The enormous crater sized area in the northern hemisphere, that housed the superweapon, was knick named ‘The Dimple’. 10 - In a display of power and tyranny the Death Star destroyed the peaceful planet of Alderaan. Darth Vader used to send pieces of Alderaan as state gifts to planets that needed reminding not to upset the Emperor. 11 - Forbes Magazine estimated that in the real world it would come at the astronomical cost of 825 QUADRILLION DOLLARS to build a real Death Star. There is roughly only $40 Trillion dollars in total on Earth.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What if Sidious didn’t steal Maul from Mother Talzin? How would the movies and shows be different?
Answer: If Darth Sidious never kidnapped Maul from Mother Talzin then he would have found another apprentice elsewhere; or he would have just taken Talzin as his acolyte..which was his initial plan from the beginning. It was only when the Sith Lord realised that the Dathomiri witch had a son that Sidious altered his plans. He sensed much more raw potential in Talzins son, and so he stole the Zabrak child and indoctrinated him into the Sith Order. This is what began the blood fued that spanned for years between the Sith and the Nightsisters. During Darth Sidious’ tutelage under his master Darth Plagueis, his intergalactic travels took him far and wide. One of his places of interest was Dathomir, for he had heard rumours of a powerful witch, and struck an unlikely accord with the Nightsister. Together they traded secrets of the force, with Sidious trying to gather all the knowledge he could from Talzin, but upon discovering young Maul the darkside apprentice himself made designs on the boys future. If he didn't take Maul he would have taken his mother, and if he didn't take her he would have searched elsewhere. Sidious knew that his master had planned to all but virtually end the rule of two by instating himself and Palpatine as eternal Sith rulers, but Palpatine also wanted the unlimited power that Plagueis had concocted for himself. It was just the inherent Sith nature of killing one's own master that drove him to think like this. This is why Sidious wanted his own apprentice, so he could become the master and Maul could step into his shoes. Palpatine would have always found a prospective alternative to Maul, and he had one with Count Dooku slowly falling to the dark. The only difference to the shows would be another unfortunate soul being bisected on Naboo and the rest, except Maul maybe chosen by Ventress during her and Talzins plan to gain vengeance on Dooku. The entire Dathomir arc would be different, or not even take place due to the non existent fued between the Sith and the Nightsisters. Just thinking about it at this point now makes my head spin…

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What if Palpatine had investigated Padme's funeral and found out that Bail Organa was involved in sending the body back to Naboo?
Answer: Palpatine thought that he didn't have anything to worry about after Padme died, because his spies attended her Royal funeral procession. What he witnessed was an embalmed Padme Amidala who still appeared to be quite pregnant. In his mind that meant Skywalker had no child, heir or sucessor. No one to challenge his rule, or come back to bite his ass in the distant future. Bail Organa of Alderaan, Mon Mothma of Chandrilla and Padme Amidala of Naboo were all Senators in the Galactic Republic, and were close friends all. Palpatine may have been a little suspect on Organa, but he and Padme were coworkers and acquaintances. He had nothing to suspect in this regard, and after witnessing Padme's body his mind would have been alleviated upon believing Skywalkers heir had died with its mother. Above; Padme's personal handmaidens. The thing was that Padme's handmaidens had dressed Padme's body to give the appearance that she was still with child. They knew that if anyone, like Palpatine, suspected that the former Queen of Naboo had secretly given birth then the child would be hunted relentlessly by Palpatine and his Empire. Their trick worked for 19 years, and they had cleverly fooled two Sith Lords who had just taken over the galaxy.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Why were female Twi'leks so popular as slaves?
Answer: Because for centuries the Twi'leks homeworld of Ryloth has been subject to manipulation and servitude at the hands of intergalactic filth such as the Hutt Cartel, and the slave trading Zygerrian Empire. Because of the planets population being exposed to crime such as slavery, sex trafficking, extortion and more, the Twi'leks have suffered greatly at the hands of these criminal empires; especially the Twi'lek women who have been sold, used and exploited so popularly as slaves. Sitting at grid coordinates R-17, Ryloth sat near the Corellian Run, which was an important intergalactic trade route. Because of this the Hutts, and other powerful criminal syndicates, used the shipping routes to distribute illegal Glitterstim spice and other potent narcotics. The Twi'leks served as slaves in the drug trade manufacturing, and also as sex slaves, exotic dancers and as domestic slaves. Syndicates such as the Hutts and the Pykes had been exploiting the Twi'leks for untold years, as well as the brutal Zygerrian Empire who captured and traded in slaves. At one time in the galaxy slavery was Zygerrias prime source of revenue and wealth, and their Empire flourished under the profiteering on slavery. This was until the Jedi criminalised it, forcing the Zygerrians to trade slaves via the underworld. Twi'lek women, as I stated, have copped the raw end of the stick. Because of scum like the Hutts, Zygerrians, Pykes and other criminal empires the woman have been exploited and abused the most. Typically sold as domestic slaves, many end up as dancers, waiters and sex workers. Exploited by their masters, and abused by the employees and patrons of their ‘owners’ seedy establishments, Twi'lek woman are sold, abused and treated as objects of entertainment and as an unpaid labour source. From Coruscant, where untold numbers of Twi'lek women work as slaves, to Nevarro where they work in the very questionable ‘Twi'lek Healing Baths’, their sad plight is seen in thousands of planets the galaxy over. Even after 5 ABY, when the New Republic disbanded the Galactic Empire and slavery under its yoke, Twi'lek women would still be abused as slaves thanks to the influence of vile gangsters and criminal syndicates. It's so unfortunate that Anakin Skywalker wasn't in charge of dissolving intergalactic slavery, given the fact that his mother and himself were sold by the Hutts, and the very dim view he took on the Zygerrians and their evil slave empire.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: What are the markings on Boba Fett's armor?
Answer: Firstly his helmet has some markings that are rather mysterious in origin. In The Empire Strikes Back there are 14 yellow stripes, and by the time The Return of the Jedi there are 18 red and orange ones. Canon doesn't give us a definitive reason, whereas fans have speculated that the stripes represent anything from kill counters to mourning or tribute marks. He also has two sideways orange triangles on the forehead area, possibly representing something similar to do with his internal, HUD and sensor array equipment, much like the electronic glowing window on his chest by the time he gets his armor back in The Mandalorian. He adorns the Shoulder Sigil of the Mythosaur, a gargantuan Mandalorian super apex predator that became extinct, and an iconic symbol of Mandalore. It was an image seen on other Mandalorian warriors, as well as inside places of interest in Mandalorian warrior society. The chest patch is a tributary piece to Jangos master, and in Legends Jango paid homage to his fallen family member by painting it on his ship. When Boba inherited Jangos armour, after the Battle of Geonosis, he too paid tribute to his father's mentor by sporting the Mereel Sigil on his chest. In addition to these symbols and markings Fetts outfit used to have the braids of killed Wookiee bounties draped from his left shoulder. These were obviously taken by the Sarlacc, or when the Jawas stripped him of his armour afterwards. Curiously though, when Fett was in the initial stages of design and concept phases he had much more symbols on his helmet. One of these concept designs was used decades later in the final design for Captain Rexs helmet in The Clone Wars, and one was the Hawkbat symbol used by the Mandalorian splinter faction Deathwatch, and adorned on it's leaders cape.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Who is your favorite stormtrooper from the star wars franchise (Finn is allowed)?
Answer: My favourite Stormtrooper is from the Expanded Universe, and was the original inspiration for the Darktroopers, as seen in The Mandalorian. Long before Moff Gideon and his Imperial Remnants unleashed the Darktrooper droids on baby Grogu, their was a General in the Imperial Army who firstly had the idea of cybernetically enhanced suits for his stormtroopers.
