Rom Mohc was a decorated war hero of the Clone Wars, then turned hero of the Empire after the fall of the Republic. He eventually overseen production of the revolutionary Dark Trooper Project. This top secret project was developed to create the ultimate evolution for the standard Stormtrooper. Below; Darth Vader himself gives his approval at General Mohcs work. The Empire had already designed a Darktrooper soldier, resulting in the Phase Zero Darktroopers, which were more a macabre zombie version of a Stormtrooper. It's purpose was to produce a soldier that had all the on field skills and initiative of a clone commando, coupled with the immense firepower of a B-Series Battle Droid. They eventually evolved into the Phase 1 and 2 versions of the Stormtrooper suit, but Phase 3 was something else entirely. Above;(from left to right) Darktrooper Phase I, Phase II, and Phase III. Using remnants left over from the technology that transformed Anakin Skywalker into a cybernetic monster the Empire concieved cybernetic warriors, who initially were clone veterans. This was the initial phase,..but by the time the project had gone into its third phase of suit development and design, the latest Phase III Darktrooper exosuit was classified as a ‘bipedal tank’. Above; General Rom Mohc in his own Phase III Battle suit. General Mohc even had a colossal, customised variant of his own. Not many of these hulking battle suits were produced, but the final glorious result was a mechanical monster, standing at over 2 and a half metres tall. A Stormtrooper to instil dread and fear into the heart of the Rebel Alliance. It boasted an impressive weaponry complement consisting of an overkill arsenal of rocket launchers, missiles, laser canons, frag grenades, thermal detonators and worse. This behemoth became a mobile weapons platform, created by the Empire to eradicate the Rebel pestilence permanently. Above; One Phase III Darktrooper crash landed on Tatooine, and was trapped there for three years, creating havoc for the locals; especially Jabba's swoop gangs. The outer shell of the Darktroopers extremely durable robotic exterior was made from the nearly indestructible material, Phrik, which could withstand a lightsaber strike. Skywalker would have shit his pants after realising his blade was virtually useless against one of these these Imperial wrecking balls. Above; Phase III Battle Suits ready for operation, standing in front of their forebears. Under General Mohcs command a squadron of stormtroopers, decked out with these nightmarish exosuits, slaughtered every single Rebel Alliance member during the bloody massacre of the Attack on Tak Base. Needless to say a high ranking Rebel agent defeated the good general shortly afterwards destroying not only Mohc but a valuable Imperial ship. This incident irrevocably led to the shutdown the Imperial Project, until Moff Gideon and his Imperial scientists discovered the problem with the suit was always the trooper. Below; the attack on Tak Rebel Base by Phase III Darktroopers. Could you just imagine being one of the terrified Rebel troopers at the base, seeing one of these giant mechanoid monstrosities pour out of lingering smoke of your grenade..as you realise that your fate is sealed? The fear, fury and destructive capabilities produced by these revolutionary exosuits makes these guys my pick for favourite Stormtrooper today.

Name: John Bambrook
Question: Was Han Solo Boba Fett's most difficult bounty?
Answer: In terms of ‘acquiring’ the bounty..no; but in terms of actually delivering the bounty..most definitely. When Jabba became so furiously irate at Han Solo, and put the astronomical sum of exactly 224,190 credits on the smugglers head, every bounty hunter worth his name wanted the reward. Fett simply got lucky because firstly Vader did the bounty hunting and froze Solo for him, and secondly..because Fett and Vader were buddies. After that, when Vader gave Fett his gift wrapped prize, it was a gauntlet of extremely deadly and lethal hunters for Fett to contend with, in his attempt to just deliver Solo to the Hutt. Bossk, 4-LOM, Zuckuss, IG-88 and a host of the galaxies most impressive bounty hunters, all contended with Fett for Solo..and the riches it would bring them. Fett already had Solo, safely encased in carbonite and tucked away in the vessel's cargo hold, so it was just a matter of intercepting Slave I, wasting Fett, and taking the Corellian to Jabba for themselves. That was easier said than done, as Fett stuck to his old addage of.. “Many have tried. None have succeeded.”, as he eliminated and eluded each of his competitors in a frantic and chaotic dash to Tatooine. Boba Fett had already cemented himself as Jabbas top bounty bounty hunter, but delivering Solo would be a cake topper for his reputation under the Hutt. The acquisition of the bounty had already been provided, courtesy of Fetts old pal Vader. The difficulty of couriering the Corellian was the hard part. Unlike most jobs other hunters were vying for the same valuable reward, only in the most treacherous of ways. The arduous task of Fett having to either elude, injure or kill his competitors made Han Solo one of the bounty hunters most difficult paydays. A payday where he eventually recieved nearly a quarter of a million credits from the Hutt for his troubles. Images courtesy of; Dark Horse Comics ‘Shadows of the Empire’ graphic novel, 1997.

Question: How do Jawas and Tuskens feel about each other?
Answer: Jawas and Tuskens share many things in common. Both are native to the desert planet of Tatooine, both live nomadic lifestyles, both have interesting relationships with technology, but both actually share more in common than any of these things. Both Jawas and Tusken Raiders are actually related as a species, and canon lore states that both are descendants of the one species who lived on Tatooine nearly 25 millennia before the Battle of Yavin. Below; the Rakata enslave the Kumumgah, before reducing Tatooine to a barren wasteland. The Kumumgah were a race of beings who lived on Tatooine thousands of years before episode I, when the entire planet was a lush teaming world full of jungles, forests, oceans and life. When they became extremely technologically advanced, and rebelled against the dominant force in the galaxy at the time, the vicious Rakata, their world was punished. Tatooine was orbitally bombarded by the Rakata, reducing its once teaming surface into a slagged glass parking lot. The glass gradually disintegrated into sand, and the Kumumgah formed into two separate factions. The devastation dished out by the Rakata irrevocably transformed the indigenous Kumumgah into both the Ghorfa's (Tuskens), and the Jawas. Tuskens are only named such after their attack on an early human settlement named Fort Tusken. Both evolved to survive on their destroyed homeworld. Temperatures on Tatooine had drastically changed for the worse, creating blistering desert like conditions. As the Kumumgah evolved into two separate races they did so out of sheer necessity. To protect themselves from the twin suns overbearing heat both draped their bodies in robes, and covered their faces in masks. Both appeared intolerant to sunlight, so each race covered their eyes with face coverings. Tuskens wore goggles of sorts, while Jawas sewed yellow crystals into a head cowl to act as protective eyewear. Apparently the Jawas also developed a more hairy appearance, perhaps as an extra defence against the suns rays. After the planetary cataclysm each race coveted water, with the Tuskens treating it like a precious treasure, and even killing for it. Over thousands of generations the two ultimately coexisted in a tentative but relatively peaceful relationship. Jawas tended to avoid their larger brethren the Tuskens, due to their violent, unpredictable behaviours, and sometimes did clash resulting in territorial disputes. The Jawas eventually acquired massive Sandcrawler vehicles, abandoned by mining corporations. These gigantic vehicles then served as enormous, mobile fortresses to the diminutive desert dwellers. Jawas embraced technology, whilst Tuskens rejected and despised it. This is interesting given that it was advanced technology that lead to the obliteration of Tatooines surface in the first place. Although they share the same ancient ancestor, I wonder if after more than 25 thousand years the Jawas and the Tuskens even remember.

Question: Am I the only one who considers Star Wars: The Clone Wars a masterpiece?
Answer: I'm with you all the way on this! Beginning in 2008 The Clone Wars introduced 7 seasons of the best Star Wars storytelling to ever be seen. It truly is a masterpiece, and spawned Rebels, and The Bad Batch, which are other excellent extensions to The Clone Wars Universe. Debuting with a feature length movie, that then went on to introduce us to every unanswered question from between Attack of the Clones and Revenge of the Sith, TCW is a masterpiece because it has reached and connected with so many new and existing fans. TCW introduced us to characters such as Ahsoka Tano, Asajj Ventress, Captain Rex and a plethora of other new individuals that instantly became cult favourites. It breathed life and depth into already existing characters, such as Darth Sidious and Count Dooku, which enhanced the overall experiences of Revenge of the Sith, and even newcomers to the franchise like The Mandalorian and The Book of Boba Fett. Even SW novels such as Dark Disciple, Ahsoka and A New Dawn can be appreciated much more by immersing yourself in TCW series. It completely revived the saga and introduced an entirely new generation of fans to the fold. With each passing season the animation quality, and calibre of storytelling, grew and evolved, becoming an epic tale in its own right. Today it stands as an essential component to understanding the entire saga,..whether some fans like it or not. Some grown ups may say “Well I'm not watching a kids cartoon.”, which I've heard plenty of times, but the joy of Star Wars is letting our imaginations run wild. It is far more than just a kids cartoon, and the CGI work and animation by the final series is breathtakingly beautiful. It can be appreciated by so many audiences on so many levels. The dynamic between the main characters is a joy to watch, as the Clone Wars spans its entire length. We watch these individuals evolve more than any SW movie ever provided, and by the end of the series it becomes quite emotional. The seriousness of situations, like death, romance and betrayal span well past a kids rated, saturday morning cartoon. There is the regular Star Wars banter and humour, that provides entertainment and curiosity for younger audiences, but by the time the series enters the fourth season there are some very dark moments, which spark more of an interest to the older fans. The way Lucas and Filoni executed the entire series was, in my opinion, the best Star Wars experience I've ever had. I mean, I loved Rogue One, Revenge of the Sith, The Empire Strikes Back and even dare I say.. Solo, but The Clone Wars is the most overall epic and immersive experience of the whole drama. To call it anything short of a masterpiece would be doing yourself a great injustice as a Star Wars fan.
